methods.description: The two-timepoint ctDNA risk rule of van den Ende et al., J Pathol 2023;261:286-297 (DOI 10.1002/path.6175): 111 patients with resectable stage II/III oesophageal adenocarcinoma on neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (CROSS, n=71) or nCRT plus anti-PD-L1 (PERFECT trial, n=40), plasma at baseline (n=111), post-nCRT (n=68) and pre-surgery (n=92), each sample assayed by a custom 23-gene amplicon panel (baseline and pre-surgery cfDNA plus WBC for CHIP filtering; Ion Reporter + Oncomine Extended filter chain, pathogenicity databases) and by shallow whole-genome sequencing run through ichorCNA for copy-number tumour fractions (MD:254-270, MD:335-362; mutation-based ctDNA positivity 44.3% (47/106), ichorCNA-based 10.5% (11/105), combined detection 50.5% (52/103), MD:548-583). The rule is an OR of two independent ctDNA signals at each of two sequential draws: BASELINE call ctDNA+ = the patient's maximum baseline ctDNA-derived variant VAF > 1% OR the baseline ichorCNA tumour fraction > 3% (TTP HR 2.23 (95% CI 1.22-4.07), log-rank p = 0.007, MD:671-674), PRE-SURGERY call ctDNA+ = a baseline ctDNA-derived variant is detected in the pre-surgery sample (mutation tracking / non-clearance, MD:358-362) OR the pre-surgery ichorCNA tumour fraction > 3% (TTP HR 4.58 (95% CI 2.22-9.46), p < 0.001, MD:675-683); both calls were independently associated with TTP in multivariable Cox (HR 2.35 and 6.10, Table 2, MD:937-1009). The wrapper takes exactly three markers (the per-draw max VAF of ctDNA-derived variants, the per-draw ctDNA detection status, and the per-draw ichorCNA tumour fraction; identified by marker name, positional fallback M1/M2/M3), applies the pre-surgery rule at the landmark's last complete post-baseline draw (the paper's paired mutation+ichorCNA sample) and falls back to the baseline rule when no complete pair exists but a post-baseline draw does, and writes call = 1 for ctDNA+ (the paper's high-risk stratum, treatment judged failing) and risk = the stronger of the two arms in threshold units (max VAF / 1% vs tumour fraction / 3%, plus the 0/1 tracking arm; higher = worse - the paper defines no per-patient score, so the wrapper writes the quantity the rule thresholds; no probability is defined and TxResBench converts the risk). The fit record reproduces the paper's evaluation layer (univariable Cox HR with 95% CI and log-rank test of the call on the training fold) and quotes the paper's cohort results; the paper's pathological-response analysis is NOT implemented (response was tested but not predicted, MD:591-649).

methods.description: The CONNECTOR functional-data workflow of Cordero, Ferrero, Pernice et al. (HemaSphere 2026;10:e70375, DOI 10.1002/hem3.70375) applied to one repeated-measurement marker's whole trajectory: at fit, the model-based functional clustering of James & Sugar 2003 (JASA 98:397-408) - cubic-spline basis (p = 7 basis functions), cluster memberships treated as missing and estimated by an EM algorithm, Gaussian random effects - is estimated on the training curves with the paper's chosen free parameters (G = 4 clusters, p = 7, 50 seeded EM repetitions, h chosen automatically), and the four fitted clusters are named A-D from the lowest to the highest mean curve exactly as the CONNECTOR package does; the paper collapses A+B into favorable MRD kinetics (rapid, sustained negativization) and C+D into unfavorable MRD kinetics (persistent or fluctuating MRD, TTP HR 4.18 BM / 5.71 PB). At predict, each patient's trajectory draws an orthonormalised basis by interpolation from the fitted grid and the posterior membership probabilities are computed by Bayes' rule under the fitted model (the package's ClassificationNewCurves, the paper's model-abstraction module); a curve is assigned to the maximal-posterior cluster, or 'Unclassified' when the posterior is not confident (entropy >= 1 and max probability <= 0.6, the paper's md:126 rule) - unclassified and degenerate curves abstain with a note. The wrapper writes risk = P(unfavorable) = P(C) + P(D) (higher = more likely failing) and call = 1 for C+D, 0 for A+B; a curve with fewer than two on-treatment draws (the classifier's intrinsic minimum; the paper's analyses also classified two-point trajectories) or outside the fitted grid abstains. Nothing is learned from the outcomes: the clustering is unsupervised ('CONNECTOR conducts an unsupervised longitudinal data analysis', md:25), so the probability conversion of the benchmark is fitted on the method's own training risks. Differences from the paper: the exact RQ-PCR value -> Observation transform of the MCL data (log10 of the RQ values, NEG coded 0, PNQ coded 2) is not published ('?', S1.1 'The RQ PCR values used in the analysis were transformed as log in base 10' only), so like the published MCL Explorer's user-data path the wrapper takes the marker values as reported and refits the model on that scale each run; the published BM/PB models were fitted with the CONNECTOR report pipeline on the MCL0208 cohorts (117 BM / 95 PB profiles with >= 3 / >= 4 points), which cannot be replicated without the raw MRD values of two trials, so the wrapper fits the paper's model form (G = 4, p = 7, 50 runs, seed 2404) on the benchmark training curves - the paper's selection indices gave p = 7 and G = 4 for both tissues. The wrapper follows the published MCL Explorer code for every entry point (app/server.R:1112-1115, 1630-1633: ClassificationNewCurves(newdata, model, Cores = 2) and app/server.R:147-149: A+B -> favorable, C+D -> unfavorable).

methods.description: The CONNECTOR landmark-based minimal residual disease (MRD) classification of Cordero et al. (HemaSphere 2026;10:e70375, DOI 10.1002/hem3.70375 - the FIL-MCL0208 + MCL Younger mantle cell lymphoma research). A James & Sugar (2003) model-based functional clustering model (the CONNECTOR tool; G = 4 clusters, p = 7 spline basis functions, h chosen automatically, 50 runs) is estimated ONCE on the full training marker trajectories, unsupervised - the model never reads the training outcomes, exactly like the paper ('the unsupervised stratification of patients into distinct groups without relying on clinical assumptions or outcome data'). At the benchmark's landmark day L the trajectory of each patient is truncated at L and classified under that fixed model by maximal posterior membership probability (connector::ClassificationNewCurves with the paper's entropy >= 1 / maximal probability <= 0.6 'Unclassified' rule). The clusters are ordered A-D from the lowest to the highest mean curve (the CONNECTOR tool's own naming: 'the name the cluster with A->Z from the lower mean curve to the higher'), so the paper's clinical read-out applies: clusters A and B = favorable (rapid, sustained MRD negativization), C and D = unfavorable (persistent or fluctuating MRD, TTP HR 4.18 BM / 5.71 PB). The wrapper writes risk = the model's posterior probability of the unfavorable kinetics (P(C or D | history up to L)) - higher = more likely failing - and call = 1 when the assigned cluster is C or D, 0 when it is A or B; a curve the classifier cannot confidently classify (the paper's 'Unclassified' group, which its landmark analysis drops) gets no risk and a note. The paper's landmark survival analysis (KM/log-rank on the risk set of patients still event-free at L) is the benchmark's downstream evaluation, not part of the method. The wrapper differs from the paper where the paper is silent: the model is refit on each training set (the paper's model was fitted on FIL-MCL0208 and shipped for the landmark reclassifications), the baseline draw is excluded (the paper counts no baseline time point), and curves with 2 points are classified (the app's landmark plots keep only curves with more than 2 points, but the classifier's own floor is 2 and the paper's robustness section analyses two-time-point trajectories).

methods.description: The paper's method 5, 'Slope' (van Delft et al., Heliyon 2022;8(10):e10932; NSCLC immunotherapy, non-response at 6 months): at every consecutive measurement pair of one serum tumour marker (the paper fits each of CYFRA 21.1, CEA, CA-125, NSE and SCC separately), the slope between the two measurements on the raw values is computed; a patient is called a non-responder when two consecutive measurements both exceed an upper threshold of relevancy (UTR), or when the largest slope among pairs whose current value is at or above a lower threshold of relevancy (LTR) exceeds the test-condition threshold (the logical-test outcome, used at an upward UTR crossing as well as in the relevant range; positive results below the LTR are ignored). The three thresholds are fitted on the training cohort to maximize sensitivity at 95% specificity (the paper's anchor), with the paper's data cleaning (consecutive measurements less than 5 days or more than 30 days apart are excluded, and a baseline measurement with more than 2 values in the window is required; min_draws 3). The wrapper writes the largest LTR-gated slope as risk (the quantity the rule thresholds, higher = failing) and the 0/1 call, and no probability (the paper defines none; the benchmark converts the risk). It takes one marker, uses the draws on or before the landmark as the observation window, and the paper's exact slope formula, threshold search and decision boundaries are not published - the inferences (raw-value slope per day, the LTR/UTR/crossing reading, the search grid and tie-breaks) are documented in the README and run.json.

methods.description: Cox proportional-hazards regressions of progression-free and overall survival on each marker's BASELINE value (continuous) and its one-month change Delta = T1 - T0 dichotomised at a cut-off (the per-marker 'two-variable' models), plus a multivariable Cox per survival outcome with all markers' baseline and Delta terms and every cov_* column, reduced by stepwise selection using AIC (Guida et al., J Transl Med 2022;20:193, DOI 10.1186/s12967-022-03359-x: 272 BRAF wild-type metastatic melanoma patients on first-line checkpoint inhibitors; complete blood counts WBC/neutrophils/lymphocytes/platelets and the derived NLR and PLR at the start of treatment and one cycle later; hazard ratios in Tables 3-4 and direct adjusted survival probability curves from the multivariable Cox models in Figs 1-5; the analysis was carried out in SAS 9.4 and no code is published). The wrapper refits the published specification on the benchmark fold: for every marker the benchmark passes it takes T0 = the last value at day <= baseline_max_day and T1 = the last value up to the landmark, derives each marker's Delta cut-off from the ROC curve of the training patients' OS (the paper's 'cut-off values assessed by ROC curve' using OS as the classification criterion, md:92/md:101) maximising Youden's J (the paper's optimality criterion is not stated, '?'), and the Delta term marks the OS-worse side, so the 'Delta above cut-off' direction (WBC, neutrophils, platelets, NLR, PLR) and the 'Delta below cut-off' side (lymphocytes, Delta below -300) are both covered; it fits the per-marker two-variable Cox models (their hazard ratios are recorded in run.json) and the multivariable Cox model per survival outcome the training data give (progression from PFS, death from OS) with all baseline/Delta terms and the cov_* columns when covariates are passed, reduced by stepwise AIC. Predictions: the final multivariable model's linear predictor as risk and risk_<outcome> (higher = treatment more likely failing) and p_progression_H<h> / p_death_H<h> = 1 - S(h - landmark) from the fitted model (P(event by day h | event-free at the landmark); the fitted clock is the residual clock, which gives the same partial likelihood as the paper's treatment-start clock on the at-risk set). The paper publishes no code (SAS 9.4, no procedure named, no code-availability statement) and no coefficients, so every fitted number is the benchmark fold's own estimate of the published model structure; a patient whose model terms are not all available (no baseline or one-month draw, missing value, missing covariate) gets no prediction with a note.

methods.description: Cox proportional-hazards regression of progression-free and overall survival on clinical factors plus, per systemic inflammatory factor k in {NLR, PLR, SII, LMR}, the BASELINE value dichotomised into low/high at a fixed ROC-derived cut-off (NLR 3.87, PLR 156, SII 824, LMR 2.37) and the CHANGE of the factor (value after 6 cycles of bevacizumab with chemotherapy minus the value before treatment), with one univariate model per predictor and ONE multivariate model per endpoint containing all predictors with univariate p < 0.1 (Li B et al., J Cancer 2019;10(21):5082-5089, DOI 10.7150/jca.30478: 161 advanced non-squamous NSCLC patients treated with bevacizumab plus standard chemotherapy at Shandong Cancer Hospital, June 2011 - February 2018; 74 deaths; HRs and 95% CIs in Tables 2-3 and Kaplan-Meier confirmation plots of the retained factors in Figure 3; survival analyses in SPSS 24, no procedure named and no analysis code published, so the wrapper reimplements the stated model in R). The wrapper refits the published specification on the benchmark fold: per marker it takes T0 = the last value at day <= baseline_max_day and T1 = the last value up to the landmark (the benchmark's draws; the paper's change is before treatment vs after 6 cycles, md:32), codes the baseline term as 1 = value > the marker's cut-off (low = <= cut-off, Table 1) when the marker is one of the four named ratios and 1 = the OS-worse side of a per-training-fold Youden ROC cut-off when the marker identity is not identifiable (synthetic gate markers; the paper's ROC endpoint and optimality criterion are not stated, '?'), codes the change term as 1 = increase (T1 - T0 > 0, the two-group reading its Figure 3 plots; no change cut-off is published, '?'), runs one univariate Cox per term (recorded in run.json, the paper's Table 2/3 analogue) and one multivariate Cox per survival outcome (progression from PFS, death from OS) with all univariate p < 0.1 terms plus every cov_* column standing in for the paper's clinical factors (univariate p < 0.1 too), dropped constants aside and an intercept-only fallback. Predictions: the final model's linear predictor as risk and risk_<outcome> (higher = treatment more likely failing) and p_progression_H<h> / p_death_H<h> = 1 - S(h - landmark) = P(event by day h | event-free at the landmark, terms). The paper publishes no code and no coefficients, so every fitted number is the benchmark fold's own estimate of the published model structure; a patient whose model terms are not all available (no baseline or on-treatment draw, missing value) or a patient the package skipped (no baseline draw / no draw during treatment / fewer than min_draws draws) gets no prediction with a note.

methods.description: Multivariate Cox proportional-hazards models of real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS) and real-world overall survival (rwOS) with the on-treatment ctDNA tumor-fraction (TF) feature - molecular response (MR = at least a 90% [or 50%] decrease in TF from enrollment to the on-treatment draw, cohort B) or on-treatment detection (detected [D] vs not detected [ND], cohort A) - adjusted for the baseline clinical covariates, with risk-set adjustment for left truncation (patients enter the at-risk population at the day of their second liquid biopsy), the association analysis of Chiang et al., JTO Clinical and Research Reports 2025;6:100829, DOI 10.1016/j.jtocrr.2025.100829 (PCG NCT04180176 real-world NSCLC + extensive-stage SCLC; covariates per md:61 with missForest imputation for <25% missingness, a missing category included at >=25%, covariates with <5 observations excluded, md:61; outcome clocks rwPFS/rwOS from treatment initiation, md:59; per-patient discrimination by Harrell's C-index, md:68). The wrapper refits the published models per benchmark survival outcome on the event-free-at-landmark fold, on the paper's absolute clock with the counting-process Surv(entry, time, event) and entry = the day of the on-treatment draw (the paper's risk-set adjustment, md:59; on the benchmark's event-free-at-landmark cohort every patient has entered before every event, so the fit coincides with the residual-clock Cox - recorded); one model per outcome per cohort, the MR model (>=90% primary) scoring cohort-B patients (both draws detected, enrollment within the paper's two weeks before start, quantifiable change) and the detection model scoring the others; the >=50% sensitivity model and every per-term HR are recorded in run.json. Risk and risk_<outcome> are the scoring model's linear predictor (higher = treatment more likely failing; the paper's coding kept: MR/ND are the favourable strata with HR < 1), p_progression_H<h>/p_death_H<h> = P(event by day h | event-free at the landmark, model) from the same model; the paper prints group HRs and C-index comparisons but no per-patient scores, so the linear predictor and probabilities are the contract's association-only convention and all fitted numbers are the benchmark fold's own estimates of the published model structure. No published analysis code exists (job.code = []), so the exact coxph/missForest calls are the wrapper's, with package defaults (ties 'efron', missForest ntree/maxiter defaults) flagged as reference-only; a term constant in the at-risk training fold is replaced by the paper's continuous parent quantity (recorded fallback), then dropped, then intercept-only (constant_ok); a patient without both a detected enrollment draw and a detected on-treatment draw is scored by the detection model when an on-treatment draw exists (the paper's cohort-A scope: 'irrespective of ctDNA levels at enrollment', md:50), and a patient without an on-treatment draw is never scored (note).

The paper was analysed in SPSS 26.0 / R 4.1.2/4.2.1 with no function named and no code published, so the wrapper reimplements the published structure in R survival, sets detection_threshold = 0 (the paper's assay cut-off) and the level = max(value, 0) (no log transform: the paper keeps the non-detect group at its level), and on the benchmark clock applies the paper's separate timepoint analyses as T0 = the last marker draw at day <= baseline_max_day and T1 = the last marker draw at baseline_max_day < day <= landmark; the primary (risk) model is the paper's multivariable structure at T1 - the on-treatment analysis the landmark asks about - with every cov_* column entering when covariates are passed (complete-case, backward LR elimination of covariate blocks while p > p_remove, the ctDNA term kept; the paper's Table-2 and Table-3 rows at both timepoints are reported in run.json). methods.description: Cox proportional-hazards regression of overall survival on two per-liquid-biopsy ctDNA parameters, anchored at the time of each liquid biopsy (Dietz et al., EBioMedicine 2020; DOI 10.1016/j.ebiom.2020.103103: 73 ALK+ metastatic NSCLC patients, 277 serial plasma samples during ALK-TKI therapy; Table 3 reports univariable Cox HR 2.70 [1.82-4.02] for ctDNA detectability by capture-based targeted NGS (tumour-naive panel, 'only mutations included in both AVENIO kits were considered') and HR 1.39 [1.23-1.57] per unit of the t-MAD score (trimmed median absolute deviation from copy number neutrality) from shallow whole-genome sequencing, and a bivariable Cox with HR 2.31 [1.54-3.49] and 1.30 [1.14-1.49] showing both as independent predictors of shorter OS from the time of sample collection; the strata are displayed by Kaplan-Meier curves with log-rank tests (detectable vs not: median OS 14 vs 40 months, P < 0.001; t-MAD above vs below the sample median 0.0078: 25 vs 33 months, P = 0.0125). The analysis was performed in SPSS version 24 (Cox regression) and GraphPad Prism 7 (KM/log-rank), both proprietary, with no published code or syntax, so the wrapper reimplements the published Cox models in R survival. The wrapper consumes one binary ctDNA detectability marker (0 = no reported alteration, 1 = any reported alteration among the variants common to both AVENIO kits) and one continuous t-MAD marker, both per plasma draw; per patient it takes the draws up to the landmark day, pairs the two markers by draw day, fits the univariable and bivariable Cox models on the training patients' per-sample observations with each observation's own OS-from-that-sample clock (os time minus the sample day, the paper's 'OS from the time of sample collection'), and writes the bivariable model's linear predictor as risk (higher = treatment more likely failing; the univariable model is used when a term is degenerate on the training fold, and risk 0 when no term is estimable. The paper defines no per-patient risk score or probability - only association-level HRs and stratum KM curves - so TxResBench converts the risk into probabilities). The paper's KM/log-rank strata (detectability; t-MAD above vs below the training observations' median) are reproduced at fit and reported in run.json.

methods.description: Cox proportional-hazards regression of survival on the ABSOLUTE change of a serum marker from baseline to day 7, with the log baseline value as adjustment covariate - the 'GMI vs survival' analysis of Toebben et al. (Int J Infect Dis 2026;163:108272, DOI 10.1016/j.ijid.2025.108272; 66 invasive-aspergillosis patients on antifungal treatment in the FungiScope registry; 'A Cox proportional hazards model was used to regress the survival on GMI changes from baseline to day 7, and another one with baseline log GMI as covariate. Survival was censored at 42 days to model the mortality in a short-term manner.'; reported fit: 'each > 0.25 GMI unit increase from baseline to day 7 was associated with a 15% higher risk of death, although the association was not statistically significant (HR 1.151, P = 0.33)'; R 4.5.1 + IBM SPSS Statistics 30 environment statement only, no package/function named, no code published - the structure is specced from the paper text, the wrapper is its own reimplementation). The wrapper takes exactly ONE marker (the paper's serum galactomannan index, GMI in optical density units by the Platelia Aspergillus assay, is the application; the change + log-baseline Cox structure is marker-generic, so no required_markers), takes the baseline as the last detected value at day <= baseline_max_day (the research's initial positive baseline, OD >= 0.5, is required), takes the day-7 value as the observed draw within day7_window_days of the day-7 timepoint when present, and otherwise IMPUTES it from the paper's longitudinal submodel log(GMI + 0.001) = beta0 + beta1 t + U0 + U1 t + U2 t^2 + eps fitted on the training draws up to the landmark (the paper's shared-random-effects joint model with the same submodel is the imputation tool - no software named '?' - so the wrapper fits exactly the longitudinal submodel with nlme::lme and predicts day 7 per patient by the empirical-Bayes random-effects estimate; the paper's quadratic -> slope -> intercept fallback ladder is the wrapper's own); change = GMI(day 7) - GMI(baseline) (absolute GMI units; the reported HR is per 0.25 GMI unit increase). It fits ONE Cox per survival outcome the training data give (progression from PFS, death from OS - the paper's endpoint is day-42 mortality) on the patients event-free at the landmark on the residual clock (same partial likelihood as the paper's clock on the at-risk set), and writes risk and risk_<outcome> = the fitted model's linear predictor (higher = treatment more likely failing; the paper defines no per-patient score, publishes no coefficients - every fitted number is the benchmark fold's own estimate of the published model structure) and p_progression_H<h> / p_death_H<h> = 1 - S(h - landmark) from the fitted model = P(event by day h | event-free at the landmark). The paper's 42-day censoring and its day-0 = diagnosis-confirmation clock are the paper's cohort conventions, NOT reproduced: the wrapper fits on the benchmark's outcome data and clock (recorded; horizons are the benchmark's). A patient without a positive baseline value (the research's OD >= 0.5 eligibility), without an on-treatment draw, or whose day-7 value cannot be formed gets no prediction with a note. The paper's published values (HR 1.151 P = 0.33; the companion baseline-GMI >= 1 vs < 1 HR 2.107 P = 0.19; AUC 0.656 for the day-42 survival ROC of the change) are recorded in run.json next to the fold-fitted estimates.

methods.description: Kaplan-Meier/log-rank and Cox proportional-hazards regression on the per-patient DIRECTION OF CHANGE of one serial blood marker from the baseline draw to an on-treatment draw, with backward stepwise selection for the multivariable model (de Miguel-Perez et al., J Exp Clin Cancer Res 2022;41:187, DOI 10.1186/s13046-022-02379-1; plasma extracellular-vesicle PD-L1 in advanced NSCLC on ICIs). The published analysis groups each patient by Delta = value(T2)/value(T1) (increase if > 1, decrease if < 1; the wrapper assigns the exact-1 equality to the decrease side), runs per-cohort univariate Cox of PFS and OS on the group, and a pooled multivariable Cox (57 ICI patients) with the direction group plus clinical characteristics (age, gender, line of treatment, histology, tissue PD-L1 TPS, etc. - the exact list is in Supplementary Tables S3/S4, not in the provided text) selected by backward stepwise selection; the reported per-decrease hazard ratios are PFS 0.45 (p = 0.008) and OS 0.35 (p = 0.004). The wrapper takes the one marker the benchmark passes (required_markers: PD-L1 = CD274 / UniProt Q9NZQ7), takes T1 = the last value at day <= baseline_max_day and T2 = the last value at baseline_max_day < day <= landmark, fits one Cox per survival outcome the training data give (progression from PFS, death from OS) on the patients with a computable direction group who are event-free at the landmark on the residual clock, enters every cov_* column when covariates are passed and runs backward selection among them only (joint Wald, removal while p > p_remove = 0.10; the direction group is forced - its HR is the paper's reported quantity), and writes risk and risk_<outcome> = the fitted linear predictor (higher = increase group = more likely failing; the paper's per-decrease HR is exp(-beta)) plus p_progression_H<h>/p_death_H<h> = 1 - S(h - landmark) from the fitted Cox. A patient with no usable (T1, T2) pair or a baseline value <= 0 gets no prediction with a note. The paper publishes no code, no package for the Cox fit and no per-patient score, so the wrapper is its own reimplementation in survival and the fitted coefficients are the benchmark fold's estimates, not the paper's numbers.

methods.description: Univariate and multivariate (forward step-wise) Cox proportional-hazards regression of progression-free and overall survival on three early-kinetics predictors of an EGFR-TKI treatment course in advanced NSCLC, plus the clinical covariates (Zheng et al., Thoracic Cancer 2022;13(19):2764-2772, DOI 10.1111/1759-7714.14668: 51 advanced NSCLC patients with EGFR driver mutations on osimertinib/gefitinib/icotinib, Daping Hospital 2016-2021; Table 2 reports per-predictor HRs per endpoint, e.g. multivariate PFS ctDNA not-clear HR 4.633 [2.322-9.242] and cfDNA decrease HR 3.739 [1.923-7.271]; the analysis was run in SPSS version 20 with the baseline-ratio cutoff computed by the X-Tile tool - both proprietary, no code published). The wrapper takes the two markers of the paper's pair - the maximum MAF (%) in ctDNA (168-gene capture NGS panel) and the cfDNA amount (ng/ml, Qubit 2.0) - and derives the paper's three features per patient: the baseline ctDNA/cfDNA ratio (the baseline maximum MAF; ctDNA amount = MAF x cfDNA makes the MAF the ratio) dichotomised at a cutoff (low <= cutoff vs high > cutoff; the paper's X-tile-derived 2.2% is data-derived in its own sample in its own assay units, so the wrapper re-derives the cutoff per training fold as the candidate maximising the two-sample log-rank chi-square, and keeps the 2.2% available as the literal 'fixed' mode), ctDNA not clear vs clear at cycle 1 (the first on-treatment draw up to the landmark; the <marker>__detected companion row when present, else value > 0), and cfDNA decrease vs increase from baseline to cycle 1 (the paper's higher-risk arms, per its Results text md:134). It then fits one univariate Cox per candidate (the three features plus every cov_* column when covariates are passed) and one multivariate Cox per survival outcome the training data give (progression from PFS, death from OS) on the patients event-free at the landmark on the residual clock, with forward step-wise variable selection (score-test entry p < 0.05, Wald removal p > 0.10 - the SPSS defaults; the paper's criteria are not published) over the univariately significant candidates; the univariate HRs and the final formula are reported in run.json (Table 2 analogues). The paper defines no per-patient risk score or probability (cohort-level association only), so the wrapper projects the fitted Cox: risk and risk_<outcome> = the final model's linear predictor (higher = treatment more likely failing) and p_progression_H<h> / p_death_H<h> = 1 - S(h - landmark) from the fitted model = P(event by day h | event-free at the landmark); a patient without a baseline or cycle-1 value of a needed marker, or with a missing covariate, gets no prediction with a note. The paper's clinical covariate cutoffs (age <=60, CEA <=5.0 ng/ml, tumor size <=3.6 cm) are cohort-specific and are not applied to another unit's covariate columns, and its Table 2 label order ('clear vs. not clear', 'increase vs. decrease') is the opposite of its own Results text risk direction - the wrapper follows the Results text. Every fitted number is the benchmark fold's own estimate of the published model structure; the paper's reported HRs are recorded in run.json.

methods.description: Multivariable Cox proportional-hazards model of progression-free survival on three M-protein DYNAMIC features computed from the baseline-normalised longitudinal M-protein curve within a fixed time cutoff - the maximum percent reduction from baseline (the signed % change at the point of deepest reduction), the last observed percent change from baseline, and the rate of M-protein change (% per week, the slope of the trajectory after the nadir) - with baseline clinical covariates selected by stepwise screening on the Bayesian information criterion (Yan X et al., Clin Transl Sci 2020;13(6):1345-1354, DOI 10.1111/cts.12836: 569 POLLUX and 498 CASTOR relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma patients on daratumumab-combination vs active control; the three features per cutoff with univariate and multivariable Cox analyses on PFS, per-research BIC-selected covariate sets (POLLUX 7, CASTOR 9), per-cutoff models (1, 2, 3, 6 months and all data up to the clinical cutoff), time-varying ROC AUCs ~0.8/0.85 with the first 2 months; 'Cox proportional hazards (PHs) analyses were performed on PFS using the survival package in R 3.5.3' (md:39); no analysis code is published (job.code = []) and the paper's calls are not published, so every fitted number is the benchmark fold's own estimate of the published structure). The wrapper refits the published specification per benchmark fold: one marker (the M-protein channel, required_markers LOINC 33358-3), MP0 = the marker's last value at day <= baseline_max_day and percent change on every later draw up to the cutoff (the paper's cutoff, the model's landmark; cutoff_months reproduces the paper's 1/2/3/6-month analyses, default = all data up to the landmark, the paper's 'all data up to the clinical cutoff dates'); maximum reduction and last observed enter as signed % change from baseline (the paper's table note gives the hazard ratio per 10-unit increase of these features, so deeper reduction = a lower value = lower hazard), the slope = the regression (least-squares) line through the points from the nadir (point of maximum reduction) to the last observation (the Figure S1 note, sup:250-251; the main text says the last two observations - param slope_points, recorded), % per week; a stepwise BIC screening (direction both from the full set) selects the baseline covariates among the cov_* columns, the three features are then added without further selection, and the final Cox is fitted on the training patients at risk at the landmark (the benchmark's conditional cohort; the paper's main analysis is unconditional, recorded deviation, and its landmark analysis is a separate sensitivity analysis) with the residual clock (identical partial likelihood). Outputs: risk and risk_progression = the final model's linear predictor (higher = treatment more likely failing), p_progression_H<h> = 1 - S(h - landmark) = P(progression or death by day h | event-free at the landmark); the paper's per-10-unit hazard ratios, predicted PFS curves and time-varying ROC AUCs are evaluation display, not per-patient outputs. The paper models PFS only, so death and the response outcomes are not fitted here (TxResBench converts the risk for them).

methods.description: The paper's method: a multivariable Cox proportional-hazards regression of 48-week interferon response (IR) in chronic hepatitis B under pegylated-interferon-alpha-2b (Pegbin 180 ug weekly, 48 weeks) on exactly three continuous predictors - baseline HBsAg (log10 IU/mL), the 12-week HBsAg change (Delta-HBsAg, log10 IU/mL) and the 12-week ALT change (Delta-ALT, U/L) - with the predictors fixed by the intersection of LASSO Cox, Random Survival Forest and CoxBoost (lambda.min 0.021 / node size 3, Mtry 7, 30 trees / 61 steps, penalty 500), rendered as a nomogram mapping total points to the 48-week IR probability (Xi et al., BMC Gastroenterology 2026;26:348, DOI 10.1186/s12876-026-04813-6: 242 CHB patients, training n = 194 / validation n = 48 at a random 8:2 split, prospective RNA cohort n = 98; AUROC 0.922/0.938/0.933, Fig. 3A; no code published, only R 4.3.1 named as the environment, and the Cox coefficients, the nomogram point weights and the baseline survival are not published). The wrapper takes exactly two markers (serum quantitative HBsAg and serum ALT, roles resolved by name), computes per patient the three features from the last baseline draw (day <= baseline_max_day) and the last on-treatment draw by the landmark (the paper's week-12 visit), refits the published Cox structure on the training patients per benchmark fold with the paper's own event (IR, time = the 48-week endpoint = 336 days; the time/event encoding is the benchmark's, recorded as a deviation because the paper publishes none), and writes risk = p_no_response = P(N-IR at 48 weeks) = the failure reading of the paper's IR probability, learned per fold from the training no-response label (the package converts the risk into the progression/death/progressive-disease probabilities). No call: the paper defines no probability threshold - the 'optimal population' criteria (baseline HBsAg < 2.43 lg IU/mL, Delta-HBsAg > 1.26 lg IU/mL, Delta-ALT > 8.00 U/L) are a separate per-variable Kaplan-Meier characterization (cutoff_provenance 'derived in this sample'), not a threshold on the model's output. Differences from the paper (each recorded in run.json): the refit is the only possible route to per-patient probabilities (no published coefficients); the ML variable selection is antecedent and not rerun; the benchmark landmark substitutes the week-12 visit; the delta sign convention follows the extraction (x1 - x0) while the paper's own Table 1 medians are mutually inconsistent, so the direction of every feature is learned from the data; a below-detection HBsAg draw takes LOD/2 (the paper states the 0.03 IU/mL LOD but no below-LOD rule).

methods.description: Per-endpoint (PFS, OS) multivariable Cox pipelines over the T1/T2/Delta-T2-T1 liquid-biopsy features, each categorized high vs low at bootstrap-validated optimal cut-points, reduced by backward elimination with the Bayesian information criterion, rendered as a survival nomogram (6/12-month probabilities) and stratified into three risk groups by optimal cut-points of the individual linear predictor score (Boscolo Bragadin et al., npj Precision Oncology 2024;8:236, DOI 10.1038/s41698-024-00704-9: 113 advanced EGFR-ALK-ROS1 wild-type NSCLC patients on single-agent immune checkpoint inhibitors; plasma cfDNA concentration, maxVAF and their changes from T1 to T2; hazard ratios in Tables 4-5, C-index 0.718/0.740 adjusted through 1000 bootstrap resamples; no code published, no package named beyond RStudio, md:102). The wrapper refits the published specification on the benchmark fold: for every marker the benchmark passes it takes T1 = the last value at day <= baseline_max_day (the paper's baseline) and T2 = the FIRST value up to the landmark (the paper's T2, the first post-baseline sample at +14/+21 days; the paper's T3 at the first radiological evaluation is explicitly excluded from the integrated model, md:38/md:210, so a later draw is a T3 analogue and never enters), Delta = T2 - T1 (signed; the published PFS cut-point < -0.11 excludes |change|); below-detection draws (harness value 0 with a <marker>__detected companion of 0) take the draw's own <marker>__lod/2 else the marker's reference LOD/2 (the paper's undetectable-VAF rule, md:84). Per endpoint (PFS for progression, OS for death) and per feature it re-derives the optimal cut-point by maximizing the Harrell C of the binary univariate Cox on the at-risk cohort (the estimator of the paper's 'accuracy' column is not defined, '?'; md:90 'maximizing the discriminative ability of the Cox model' and md:96 point to the concordance) with at least cutpoint_min_frac of the cohort on each side, validated with b_cutpoints bootstrap resamples (the paper's bootstrap validation, md:206, is always recorded: median in-bag cut-point, 95% interval, median in-bag accuracy); the model categorizes at the full-sample optimal (cutpoint_estimator "full_sample", the md:90 maximizer, by default - on weak-signal folds the in-bag argmaxes are winner-cursed and their median lands on a markedly weaker cut, so the md:206 median in-bag value is recorded as the published validation and the deviation is documented; "bootstrap_median" restores the strict md:206 protocol; the paper's published constants are in its own marker units and names and cannot be applied to another unit - a benchmark refits them per fold); the main-effects Cox model per survival outcome is fitted on the benchmark's at-risk cohort (event-free at the landmark, residual clock = the same partial likelihood as the paper's treatment-start clock) with the categorized features and every cov_* column as a clinical main effect when covariates are passed (the paper's nine named clinicopathological candidates have no named harness channel; the paper's PD-L1-required exclusion of patients with unknown PD-L1 is not enforceable without a PD-L1 column - recorded), reduced by backward elimination on BIC = -2 logLik + log(n_eff)*k with n_eff = the at-risk events (the paper's convention is not stated, '?'); the final coefficients carry the bootstrap shrinkage factor (mean calibration slope over bootstrap_shrinkage resamples, clamped to [0, 1]; the paper's estimator is not stated, '?'); the C-index is reported apparent, optimism-corrected over bootstrap_eval resamples (the paper's 'adjusted through 1000 bootstrap resamples', md:96) and shrunk. Outputs: risk and risk_<outcome> = the shrunk final model's linear predictor (the nomogram total score is an affine transform whose mapping the paper does not publish, '?'; the nomogram drawing is a plotting scheme), p_progression_H<h>/p_death_H<h> = 1 - S(h - landmark) of the shrunk model = P(event by day h | event-free at the landmark), and call = 1 for the HIGH three-group (the paper's three-group stratification, md:98/md:255; the contract's call is binary so the three groups project onto the failing group, 0 for low/intermediate) when the LP admits a three-group split (the LP cut-points are not published, '?': the wrapper maximizes the three-group log-rank statistic on the training LP with each group >= group_min_frac, and records group sizes and Kaplan-Meier medians). A patient with a missing term of a final model gets no prediction with the reason in note (the paper's complete-case design, md:110).

methods.description: The refit of Model-V_INTEGR, the multivariable Cox proportional-hazards model of disease-free survival from Lv J et al., 'Improving on-treatment risk stratification of cancer patients with refined response classification by integration of circulating tumour DNA phenotypes' (BMC Medicine 2022;20:266, DOI 10.1186/s12916-022-02463-5; 821 patients with locally advanced EBV-associated nasopharyngeal carcinoma on cisplatin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by concurrent chemoradiotherapy at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, 2009-2015; 280 DFS events; 5-year DFS 72.5%): the model integrates the pretreatment clinical factors (sex, age <45 vs >=45 years, clinical stage III/IV), the pretreatment plasma cell-free EBV DNA titer dichotomised at 2000 copies/mL (the authors' previous-work cutoff, md 'cut point identification'), the post-NAC biological-and-radiological response phenotype (G1 cBR+CR, G2 non-cBR+CR, G3 cBR+PR, G4 non-cBR+PR, G5 cBR+SD/PD, G6 non-cBR+SD/PD, from the post-NAC detectable/undetectable call - cBR = undetectable cfEBV DNA - combined with the post-NAC RECIST 1.1 MRI response) and the therapeutic information (NAC cycles 2/3/4, NAC regimen TPF/TP/GP/PF/other), and is displayed as a nomogram mapping total points to the 3- and 5-year DFS probability (Fig. 4B; the published fit reports a bias-corrected Harrell's C-index of 0.69 for 5-year DFS, Models I-IV 0.57/0.60/0.65/0.68). The paper publishes the nomogram figure only - no regression coefficients, no baseline survival, no analysis code (the only software named is the environment: 'The analyses were performed in R (version 3.4.4...) and SPSS (version 23.0...)'), so the wrapper refits the published Model-V structure on the benchmark training fold: per survival outcome (progression from PFS - the paper's DFS endpoint, death from OS - the benchmark's analogous endpoint; the paper has no OS model) it fits one Cox on the patients at risk at the landmark (residual clock, the same partial likelihood as the paper's treatment-start clock) with the paper's covariates matched to the benchmark's cov_* columns by name-pattern params and the G1-G6 phenotype built from the marker's post-landmark-2nd-draw detectability and the matched MRI-response columns (a cBR indicator and no phenotype when no MRI-response column exists - recorded); outputs: risk and risk_<outcome> = the fitted model's linear predictor (the nomogram total point scale is an affine transform of the linear predictor whose published weights do not exist, '?'; the affine mapping to the Fig. 4B 0-220 Total Points axis is derived per fit and recorded in run.json, the nomogram drawing being a plotting scheme) and p_progression_H<3y>/p_death_H<3y> (and 5y) = 1 - S(h - landmark | linear predictor) = P(event by day h | event-free at the landmark, the fitted features), the paper's '3- and 5-year risks of disease progression' (md 'combinations of biological and radiological responses refine risk groupings'); the paper defines no per-patient probability row, no call rule and no risk-group cut-score, so no call column is written and the response outcomes (no_response, progressive_disease) are served by the benchmark's conversion of the risk. A patient outside the paper's cohort (no detectable pretreatment cfEBV DNA - inclusion criterion 3: 'had detectable pretreatment EBV DNA (>0 copies/mL)' - or no post-NAC/MRI assessment, inclusion criteria 4-5) gets no prediction with the reason in note; the paper's cohort is complete-case and defines no prediction for such patients. The wrapper's differences from the paper - refit instead of published coefficients; the marker drawing the benchmark passes instead of the named cfEBV DNA assay; covariate coding per the benchmark column coding; the draft 0-220 Total Points affine mapping - are stated in README.md and recorded per fit in run.json.

methods.description: Standalone Cox proportional hazards regression implemented as the paper's baseline for time-to-event analysis of kidney graft failure (Salybekov A, et al., Front Artif Intell 2025;8:1682639, DOI 10.3389/frai.2025.1682639; UNOS/OPTN 2015-2021 deceased-donor kidney transplant recipients, five phase-specific post-transplant cohorts 0-3 to 39-72 months). The paper's own model sentence is two lines (md:47 'a standalone Cox Proportional Hazards Regression (Cox PHR) model was implemented as a baseline for time-to-event analysis'; md:55 'a Cox proportional hazards regression model was utilized to calculate the concordance index (CI)'), and its OWN deliverable is the concordance index - no covariates, formula, time scale, event definition, CI values, per-patient score or code are published ('?'; the only software fact is Python 3.11.5, md:55, and no Cox package is named, so nothing was substituted; the wrapper reimplements the Cox PH model in R survival 3.7-0, the benchmark's Cox engine). The wrapper reads the paper's feature set from the extraction's input list (follow-up record at one visit within the phase, chiefly recipient serum creatinine, md:42/md:132, plus the pre-operative donor/recipient waiting-list record, md:26, entering as the benchmark's cov_* columns when the dataset provides them): per patient, the markers' values at the most recent draw in (baseline_max_day, landmark_day] stand in for the paper's randomly selected visit, and one Cox PH model (Efron ties, survival defaults; the paper names none) is fitted on the training patients' time-to-event outcome - the benchmark's progression outcome from pfs_time/pfs_event when the training data carry it (the graft-failure endpoint the paper predicts), else the death outcome from os_time/os_event. It writes risk = the fitted model's linear predictor (higher = higher graft-failure hazard, more likely failing) and NO probability of its own - the paper defines no per-patient output, only the CI, so TxResBench converts the risk; the training-fold concordance index (the paper's own reported readout) and every wrapper choice are recorded in run.json. A patient with no marker draw in the on-treatment window, or missing any model term, gets no prediction with the note; a fold with no varying term falls back to the intercept-only model (risk 0) with the reason declared in constant_ok. Differences from the paper: the paper's phase-specific cohorts, three records per subject for 15-39/39-72 months, MICE imputation and months-since-transplantation clock are the paper's cohort/reporting detail, not the Cox model; the wrapper uses the benchmark's single landmark call, complete-case terms and the benchmark's days clock (recorded; the paper's Cox time scale is not stated '?').

methods.description: Cox proportional-hazards model on a static feature vector - the baseline (C1) values of every marker (the paper's baseline models) or the first-to-second-cycle differences delta = C2 - C1 (the paper's delta models) plus the baseline clinical covariates, both variants producing the per-patient probability of progression P(PFS <= t) at t = 6 (the paper's primary), 12 and 24 months from the first treatment cycle, plus a responder/non-responder call by the optimal threshold on the 6-month progression probability (Ramos-Guerra et al., Cancer Immunol Immunother 2025;74:120, DOI 10.1007/s00262-025-03966-9: 424 advanced (stage III-IV) NSCLC patients on immunotherapy from three centres; Center1 N=212 training, Center2 N=137 and Center3 N=75 testing; six models compared - multivariate (MV) and univariate NLR versions of baseline (BM, C1 only), delta (DM, C1 and C2 with delta = C2 - C1) and longitudinal (JM) variants; all models trained to predict PFS(6), i.e. progression-free survival at 6 months, responders = PFS > 6 months; the CPH baseline hazard is left unspecified, continuous variables are min-max normalised and categorical variables one-hot encoded (the ESL '?'-unknown Cox package is not substituted, R 3.6.0 only is named); features for the multivariate models are selected by stepwise selection on the validation time-dependent AUC with the null CPH AUC as reference (training split 70% tuning / 30% validation, final model refit on the whole training cohort); the call threshold is the maximally-selected-rank-statistics (standardised log-rank) cutoff averaged over a 4-fold cross-validation of the training cohort, high risk = predicted 6-month progression probability above it; the paper publishes no code (job.code = []), no Cox coefficients of its own and no Cox cutoff values (only the JM cutoffs 0.59/0.69), so the wrapper refits the published model structure and re-derives the cutoff per benchmark training fold and records every difference in run.json. The wrapper follows the published model structure on whichever markers and cov_* baseline columns the benchmark passes (the paper's 25/26/1/1 named feature lists are the paper's cohort application; the paper itself records that the multivariate approach overfits Center1 and that the PH assumption fails for MV-BM and MV-DM, which a refit reproduces). At fit the wrapper selects features by forward stepwise on the validation time-dependent AUC at 6 months (the paper's primary endpoint), refits the final model on the whole training fold, and derives the call cutoff by 4-fold CV; it writes the fitted 6-month progression probability as risk (higher = treatment more likely failing) and call (1 = high risk / non-responder), p_no_response = the same fitted 6-month non-response probability (the paper's definition of non-response: PFS <= 6 months), and p_progression_H<h> = the fitted P(event by the horizon | event-free at the landmark). Every fitted number is the benchmark fold's own estimate of the published model structure, not a paper value.

methods.description: The univariate-then-multivariable Cox proportional-hazards model of time to castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) on PSA kinetics features from Guo J, Song G, et al., 'Rapidly decreasing level of prostate-specific antigen during initial androgen deprivation therapy is a risk factor for early progression to castration-resistant prostate cancer: A retrospective research', Medicine 2017;96(36):e7823, DOI 10.1097/MD.0000000000007823 (185 hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients on first-line androgen deprivation therapy (LHRH agonist or surgical castration plus bicalutamide/flutamide) at Peking University First Hospital 2003-2014, followed every 4 weeks over the first ADT year, 121/185 (65.4%) progressed to CRPC, median time to CRPC 38 months (4-158)): from the serial serum PSA (ng/mL) the paper derives three per-patient kinetics features - PSA nadir after ADT (ng/mL), time to PSA nadir (TTN, months from ADT initiation) and velocity of PSA decline = (PSA at ADT initiation - PSA nadir)/TTN (ng/mL per month) - dichotomises TTN at <=9 vs >9 months (borrowed from a prior Japanese-cohort research, the paper's ref 15) and the velocity at >11 vs <=11 ng/mL per month (Youden-index optimum from an ROC curve, derived in the paper's sample; the 0.03 ng/mL Youden-derived PSA-nadir cutoff is used for the Kaplan-Meier/log-rank comparison only), runs one univariate Cox per candidate factor (age, BMI, T stage, N stage, distant metastasis, EAU risk group, Gleason grade group, PSA at ADT initiation, PSA nadir, TTN, velocity), includes the univariate-significant factors (P <.05) in a multivariable analysis, and reports the retained multivariable model: distant metastasis before ADT (HR 6.030, 95% CI 3.229-11.263), PSA nadir continuous per 1 ng/mL (HR 1.185, 95% CI 1.080-1.301), velocity >11 ng/mL per month (HR 2.124, 95% CI 1.195-3.750), TTN <=9 months (HR 0.276, 95% CI 0.162-0.469, printed as an 'increased risk' despite HR < 1 - recorded verbatim), with Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests for the dichotomised groups (velocity <=11 vs >11: 44 vs 24 months, P =.002; TTN <=9 vs >9: 23 vs 57 months, P =.001; PSA nadir <=0.03 vs >0.03 ng/mL: 48 vs 28 months, P =.156; with/without metastasis: 23 vs 62 months, P =.001; EAU risk low/intermediate/high: 68/56/28 months, P =.001). The wrapper refits this pipeline per survival outcome on the benchmark training fold: the three kinetics features from the informative draws up to the landmark (PSA at ADT initiation = the last informative draw at day <= baseline_max_day; nadir = the minimum over the informative draws at baseline_max_day < day <= landmark; TTN in months = the day of the first occurrence of that minimum / 30.4375; velocity as printed), the paper's clinical covariates matched to the benchmark's cov_* columns by name (params *_regex), then per outcome: the univariate screen (report) and the paper's retained 4-predictor multivariable model as the prediction model (distant metastasis when a matching covariate is present, else the 3-kinetics-feature model - recorded) with the paper's cohort-level outputs (Table 2-style univariate/multivariable HR (95% CI, P), the KM/log-rank comparisons) written per training fold into run.json. As the paper publishes no per-patient score or probability (its output is per-predictor hazard ratios and group-level KM comparisons), the wrapper writes risk = the fitted prediction model's linear predictor (higher = more likely failing) for the paper's endpoint outcome (progression from PFS; death from OS is the benchmark's analogous endpoint and serves when PFS is absent), risk_progression / risk_death per outcome model, call = 1 for the worse velocity stratum (oriented by the fitted velocity association on the training fold - the paper's published direction has the velocity >11 group progressing faster, recorded) and p_progression_H<h> / p_death_H<h> = 1 - S(h - landmark | linear predictor) from the fitted model = P(event by day h | event-free at the landmark, PSA-kinetics features) - the paper's model projected onto the benchmark horizons; a patient with no informative baseline draw or no informative on-treatment draw by the landmark gets no prediction with the reason in note. The paper names only SPSS 22.0 (proprietary; no procedure, syntax or code published anywhere - job.code = [], no code-availability statement, Tables 1-2 are images in the published article) so nothing was substituted or downloaded: the wrapper reimplements the stated Cox models and KM/log-rank comparisons in R with survival 3.7-0.

methods.description: The cutoff-stratified Cox prognostic analysis of Fiala et al., In Vivo 2026;40(2):1065-1079 (DOI 10.21873/invivo.14261; 310 metastatic RCC patients on nivolumab monotherapy, second or higher line): the ratio features are the baseline value and the early change (delta = first on-treatment blood count minus baseline, obtained at approximately 1 month) of the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte, platelet-to-lymphocyte and lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratios - six features - each dichotomised at a cut-off into a high-risk and a low-risk group (baseline NLR >= 4, PLR >= 310, LMR < 1.5; deltaNLR >= 2, deltaPLR >= 20, deltaLMR < 0 in the paper's cohort), the groups compared by univariable and per-parameter multivariable Cox (PFS, OS; complete case) with per-group Kaplan-Meier medians, and ORR by Fisher's exact test. The wrapper writes the count of the six high-risk calls (0-6, higher = more likely failing) as risk and no probability (the paper defines no per-patient score; TxResBench converts the risk). The cut-offs are re-derived on the training patients by the paper's stated procedure (Cox-Mantel log-rank p-value scan over all possible thresholds considering both PFS and OS, accepting only a significant separation at alpha 0.05; minprop 0.1), with the published constants 4/310/1.5/2/20/0 as the fallback and available through cutoff_mode 'published'; the fit record reproduces the paper's evaluation layer per parameter (univariable and, when the covariate track is on, multivariable Cox HRs with 95% CI and p for PFS and OS, KM medians, group ORR by Fisher). It differs from the paper by the declared single per-patient score (the paper's native per-patient output is six independent two-group calls), by the declared delta arithmetic (absolute difference; the paper says 'relative change' without stating the arithmetic), by re-deriving the in-sample cut-offs per training fold rather than using the Fiala-cohort constants, and by writing no combined call (the paper defines none across the six parameters).

methods.description: A Cox proportional-hazards regression of progression-free survival on the CONTINUOUS per-patient percent change in CTC count from the baseline (T0) draw to the on-treatment follow-up (T1) draw - DeltaCTC% = 100 x (baseline - post)/baseline (Lee S et al., Cancer Res Treat 2026, DOI 10.4143/crt.2025.672; 77 stage IV EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients on EGFR-TKI, n = 72 evaluable for DeltaCTC%: the five 0-at-both-draws patients were 'excluded from DeltaCTC%-based survival analyses', md:509-513). The paper reports this model only as a robustness analysis of its binary 44.4% response call - 'when DeltaCTC% was analyzed as a continuous variable in a Cox proportional hazards model, greater CTC reduction remained significantly associated with improved PFS (p < 0.001)' (md:532-535) - and publishes NO coefficient, NO hazard ratio, NO adjustment set and NO per-patient score, and no code (R ver. 4.2.2 only, md:314-316; no package named; univariable vs adjusted not stated,?). The wrapper therefore reimplements the paper's covariate exactly and fits a UNIVARIABLE Cox (the covariate set the paper prints, md:307-310, belongs to the separate multivariable model of its binary call) per survival outcome the training data give: progression from PFS (the paper's own endpoint) and death from OS (the same model structure applied to it), on the patients event-free at the benchmark landmark on the residual clock. It writes risk and risk_<outcome> = the fitted linear predictor (higher = more likely failing; the reduction feature enters with a negative coefficient, i.e. HR < 1 per percentage point of reduction, as in the paper's 'greater CTC reduction... improved PFS') and p_progression_H<h>/p_death_H<h> = 1 - S(h - landmark) from the fitted Cox. Patients the paper cannot score abstain: a baseline count of 0 makes DeltaCTC% undefined (the paper excludes the 0-at-both-draws patients and states no DeltaCTC% value for a zero baseline, md:719-723/md:781-783), and no T0/T1 pair means no feature. The wrapper writes no call and no response probability: the paper's output for this model is the cohort-level association, not a decision rule.

methods.description: Kaplan-Meier/log-rank plus univariate-then-multivariable Cox proportional-hazards stratification of progression-free and overall survival by the two-group CX3CR1 score: at least 10% vs <10% maximal percent change of the CX3CR1+ subset in peripheral-blood CD8+ T cells from baseline, assessed at 6-9 weeks (Eihab A, Long MD, Kajihara R, et al., Cancer Research Communications 2023;3(12):e-0383, DOI 10.1158/2767-9764.CRC-22-0383; 29 patients with naive or previously treated NSCLC on first- or later-line combination chemoimmunotherapy at Roswell Park, Feb 2018-Jul 2021, 12 responders (PR) / 17 nonresponders (13 SD, 4 PD), ORR 41.3%): per patient the CX3CR1 score = the maximal percent change of the CX3CR1+ subset from the baseline draw over the on-treatment draws up to the grouping window (md:76, md:91) dichotomised at the fixed published cutoff >=10% (Table 2 rows '<10% (ref)' / '>=10%', md:153-155; the 10% is the rounded value of the Youden-index optimum 9.42%-10.35% derived in this sample for the response analysis, md:91, so the wrapper does not re-derive it per fold), then (1) Kaplan-Meier curves by group compared by log-rank (PFS P = 0.0051, OS P = 0.0138, md:110), (2) one univariate Cox per candidate factor (the group plus the paper's 11 Table 2 clinical covariates, which enter as the benchmark's cov_* columns), and (3) ONE multivariable Cox per survival outcome (progression from PFS, death from OS) of the group plus the factors with univariate p < 0.10 (the paper prints the selection rule inconsistently - 'P < 0.01' in the Methods, md:76, vs '(P < 0.10)' in the Results, md:110; the printed multivariate columns match P < 0.10, so p_entry = 0.10 with the discrepancy recorded; the group is included unconditionally because the printed multivariate columns print it for both outcomes, md:110, md:153-155); reported paper result univariate PFS HR 0.28 (0.11-0.75) P = 0.011 / OS HR 0.25 (0.08-0.80) P = 0.019 and multivariable PFS HR 0.36 (0.13-1.01) P = 0.051 / OS HR 0.25 (0.07-0.91) P = 0.036 for the >=10% group (md:110, md:153-155). The wrapper refits the published specification on the benchmark fold and, as the paper defines no per-patient score (its output is the per-predictor hazard ratio and the KM/log-rank comparison, md:110, Table 2), writes risk = the CX3CR1 score itself (the quantity the >=10% group rule thresholds, oriented so higher = more likely failing by the direction of the group's fitted association on the training fold - the paper's published direction has the opposite sign, its >=10% group HR 0.28 < 1, md:110, and the paper fact is recorded), call = 1 for the worse stratum (the paper's two-group call oriented to failure) and p_progression_H<h> / p_death_H<h> = 1 - S_group(h - landmark) from the training-fold per-group Kaplan-Meier, i.e. P(event by day h | event-free at the landmark, two-group stratum) - the paper's group-level KM curves projected onto the patient (the run.json report of the fit holds the full univariate/multivariable Cox record and the per-group KM/log-rank output). The paper's cohort-level outputs (per-row univariate HR (95% CI, P), the multivariable coefficients, per-group KM medians and the log-rank comparison) are recorded per training fold in run.json; the paper publishes no analysis code (the named software for KM/log-rank is GraphPad Prism 9.4.1, proprietary, md:76; the Cox fits name no software at all, md:76, and the paper's own code repository holds only the tumor TCR-seq data, md:81), so the wrapper reimplements the stated model in R with survival 3.7-0 (coxph, survfit, survdiff) and no package or function was substituted for the paper's.

methods.description: Cox multivariate proportional-hazard regression on the baseline level and the maximum per-cent decline of one serum tumour marker (Ko, Hwang, Venook, Abbruzzese, Bergsland & Tempero, Br J Cancer 2005;93:195-199, serum CA19-9 in advanced pancreatic cancer on fixed-dose-rate gemcitabine; DOI 10.1038/sj.bjc.6602687). The paper's model has three factors - the baseline marker concentration (continuous), the research the patient was treated on (a three-research factor) and the percentage marker decline (continuous, the maximum per-cent change relative to baseline over the treatment course) - and a Cox proportional-hazard model is fitted for overall survival and for time to treatment failure; only the qualitative finding is published ('data not shown'). One Cox model per survival outcome the training data give (time to treatment failure mapped to progression, overall survival mapped to death), fitted on the patients event-free at the landmark on the residual clock, with the log (log1p default) baseline marker value and the maximum per-cent decline (0 for non-decliners, the paper's single-measurement rule) as the marker covariates and every cov_* column when covariates=True (the paper's research factor has no harness channel). It writes the linear predictor as risk and risk_<outcome> and the model's own probability of the event by each horizon; a patient without a baseline marker value gets no prediction. The paper's factor set, functional forms and coefficients are unpublished, so the wrapper's fold-fitted coefficients (run.json) are its own estimates, not the paper's.

methods.description: Multivariable Cox proportional-hazards model of progression-free survival on the per-patient risk score of the dynamic serum markers and the metastasis stage, rendered as a 1-year PFS nomogram with a maximal-rank-statistics cutoff into high/ low-risk groups (Zhang Ao et al., Cancer Cell International 2021;21:518, DOI 10.1186/s12935-021-02217-y: 160 recurrent or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients on anti-PD-1 combination therapy, serum biomarkers drawn within 3 days before the first anti-PD-1 treatment and 3 weeks later; multivariate HR 5.163 [1.889-14.107, p=0.001] per unit risk score and 2.194 [1.320-3.646, p=0.002] for M1; nomogram C-index 0.662 [0.577-0.746] training / 0.630 [0.509-0.752] validation vs TNM stage 0.536/0.513; KM log-rank p < 0.001 / 0.042 for the high-risk (total score <= 78.5) vs low-risk split). The wrapper takes exactly two markers - the per-draw serum AST/ALT ratio (markers[0]) and serum LDH (markers[1]) - recognizes the roles by name and falls back to the sorted order the package passes, computes per patient the published risk score score = (-0.242 * Delta-W3 AST/ALT) + (-0.0007 * Delta-W3 LDH) with Delta-W3 = last on-treatment draw at or before the landmark minus the last baseline draw (the paper's '3 weeks later' minus 'within three days before the first treatment'; the corpus convention of the fixed two-draw wrappers: the last draw each side, draws after the landmark never enter), and on the training patients refits the published Cox structure coxph(Surv(time, event) ~ score + metastasis) on the absolute days-since-first-dose clock the paper also uses for PFS, with PFS as the learned outcome (or OS when the training data carry no PFS), entering the metastasis stage covariate (a cov_* column recognised by name, converted to 1 for M1) when the dataset carries one, and fitting on the risk score alone otherwise (recorded, and the reason for the 'optional' declaration: the paper's model needs metastasis, but the benchmark's covariate track is dataset-dependent and the unadjusted variant is the documented fallback). It writes risk = the fitted model's linear predictor (the model's own failure-oriented score - the nomogram total score is an affine transform of it whose point scaling the paper does not publish, and the paper's total-score axis is inverted relative to the LP convention since high risk = total <= 78.5, so the published 78.5 itself cannot be ported to a refit) and call = 1 for the high-risk group split at the maximal-rank-statistics cutoff (survminer::surv_cutpoint -> maxstat LogRank, minprop 0.1, the paper's own cutoff procedure on the training cohort, md:222-225/md:446-447) of the training LP; it writes no probability of its own - TxResBench converts the risk into each outcome's probability, and the paper's C-index/KM diagnostics for the training fold are recorded in run.json. A patient without both draws of both markers, or without the metastasis value the fitted model uses, gets no prediction with the reason in note; a risk score a patient cannot be given from the markers (a non-finite delta, e.g. a missing draw value) abstains the same way.
methods.licence: wrapper calls survival (LGPL >= 2), survminer (GPL-2) and maxstat (GPL >= 2); the paper (CC BY 4.0) publishes no analysis code

required_markers.list_source: the two dynamic serum indicators the published model is DEFINED on: the per-draw AST/ALT ratio (a routine serum biochemistry ratio - one of the paper's 56 serum markers; the components are aspartate aminotransferase, LOINC 1920-8, and alanine aminotransferase, LOINC 1742-6, and the ratio is computed by the dataset pipeline as the unitless per-draw feature the lab panel reports) and serum LDH (LOINC 14804-9); the wrapper computes Delta-W3 = value at the last on-treatment draw at/before the landmark minus the last baseline draw for each, and the published risk score from those two deltas. A dataset carrying only the two aminotransferases must precompute the ratio feature for this method; if it does not, the method does not run on it (a raw AST or ALT level is not the ratio the formula's coefficient weighs).

methods.description: Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional-hazards regression of progression-free survival (and overall survival, when the training data give it) on plasma circulating-marker detection covariates as TIME-DEPENDENT variables, adjusted for baseline clinical risk factors, with the proportional-hazard assumption checked by Schoenfeld residuals (Garrido et al., LungBEAM, Cancer Med 2021;10:5878-5888, DOI 10.1002/cam4.4135: 110 stage IV EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients on first- or second-generation EGFR-TKI, plasma drawn at baseline and every 4 weeks to the 72-week follow-up, OncoBEAM BEAMing MAF; published per-covariate HRs for PFS: univariate plasma p.T790M detection 1.94 [1.48-2.54, p<0.001], confounder-adjusted 2.08 [1.58-2.74] (Table S7), and the Table 2 multivariate model with p.T790M 1.38 [1.02-1.87, p=0.038], Ex19del 2.12 [1.67-2.70], L858R 1.68 [1.27-2.22], both p<0.001, adjusted for age, sex, smoking status and number of metastatic locations; the paper publishes no analysis code - only 'R 3.5.2 statistical software' is named and no Cox package/function, so the wrapper reimplements the published structure in R survival). The benchmark mapping: every marker passed enters as a time-dependent covariate - a marker carrying the benchmark's below-detection encoding (<marker>__detected companion rows, or 0/1 values) is coded as the paper's detection covariate switching 0->1 at the first detected draw (the paper's note: 'mutations detected by the analysis of ctDNA should be regarded as time-dependent variables'; the md does not show the Table 2 coding, '?'), and any other marker as its continuous per-draw value carrying forward (the paper family's quantitative-MAF coding); the covariates are fitted as the patient's current state at the benchmark landmark. The wrapper fits per-marker univariate models (the paper's univariate p.T790M HR), per-marker models adjusted for the clinical covariates (the Table S7 analogue), and the joint model of all markers' time-dependent covariates plus every cov_* column (the Table 2 analogue) per survival outcome; the risk / risk_<outcome> is that joint model's linear predictor (higher = treatment more likely failing; the paper's detection HRs are > 1), and no own probability is written because the paper reports only per-covariate HRs and names no baseline-hazard estimator, so TxResBench converts the risk. The observed per-covariate HRs (95% CI, p) of all models and the Schoenfeld-residual PH tests are recorded in run.json (the paper's Table 2 / S7 rows are its own cohort's estimates; every fitted number here is the benchmark fold's estimate of the published model structure).

methods.description: Multivariable Cox proportional-hazards regression of patient survival on a single per-patient score adjusted for age and sex (and HPV status where the dataset provides it), with the score z-scaled within the (training) cohort, so the reported hazard ratio is per 1 standard deviation of the score (Wang B et al., 'Longitudinal liquid biopsy identifies an early predictive biomarker of immune checkpoint blockade response in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma', Nature Communications 2025, DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-63538-4: Fig. 5D reports HRs per 1-unit increase of the LiBIO score adjusted for age and sex in TCGA HNSC n=516, Foy et al. n=102 and INSPIRE n=12, plus Kaplan-Meier curves of high-score vs low-score patients split at the cohort mean of the score compared by the log-rank test; the published analysis code is scripts/figure5.R of github.com/wbb1813/Time_series_mouse_ICB and the published HRs are reproduced exactly when the score enters z-scaled - HR 0.8013 [0.69-0.92] TCGA OS, 0.7048 [0.56-0.89] Foy OS, 0.2060 [0.06-0.76] INSPIRE OS). The wrapper takes the one marker the benchmark passes as the per-patient score: the marker's last value at day <= baseline_max_day (the paper's one pre-treatment sample per patient in every cohort), z-scales it with the training cohort's mean and SD, and on the training fold fits one Cox per survival outcome the training data give (progression from PFS, death from OS) on the patients event-free at the landmark (the benchmark's residual clock; the paper's cohorts have no landmark), adjusted for the cov_* columns that name-match age, sex and HPV (a numeric column enters as is, a character column is reference-coded with the training levels; the paper always adjusts for age and sex - a benchmark fold without them runs the unadjusted model, recorded), and reports per term the hazard ratio with 95% CI and Wald P (the paper's headline output) plus the Kaplan-Meier high/low split at the cohort mean with the log-rank P, all in run.json. It writes the fitted model's linear predictor as risk (higher = more likely failing, whatever the score's own direction: the paper's higher LiBIO score means better survival, HR < 1), one LP per outcome as risk_progression / risk_death, and the model's own landmark-conditioned event probability by each horizon as p_progression_H<h> / p_death_H<h> (a fitted Cox survival probability; the paper publishes only group-level KM curves and HRs - the per-patient probability is the wrapper's projection, recorded). It writes no call: the paper's mean split is a descriptive KM grouping, not a decision rule, and its outputs are association quantities. The two-group KM split (score > training mean) is reproduced as the diagnostic the paper reports; it does not create a per-patient call.

methods.description: The landmark PFS four-group stratification of Paiva et al. (Blood Cancer Discovery 2023;4(6):470-480, DOI 10.1158/2643-3230.BCD-23-0044; KarMMa phase II, NCT03361748, 128 relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma patients treated with idecabtagene vicleucel): at each of the months 1, 3, 6 and 12 after ide-cel infusion, among the patients who at the landmark had not progressed or died, the 2x2 combination of the conventional serological response per IMWG (CR or better - conventional or stringent CR - vs less than CR; md:88, md:44) and the bone-marrow MRD status by next-generation flow (undetectable regardless of the LOD achieved, hemodiluted samples not MRD-negative, detectable >1 x 10^-6 positive; md:95) is computed, giving the groups CR/MRDneg, <CR/MRDneg, CR/MRDpos and <CR/MRDpos (md:44) - CR/MRDpos is empty at months 1 and 3 (md:47) - and the groups are compared by landmark PFS measured from the landmark, per-category Kaplan-Meier curves, per-category medians, a log-rank test across all groups and Cox models (md:104); the published ordering at months 6 and 12 is progressively worse CR/MRDneg > <CR/MRDneg > CR/MRDpos > <CR/MRDpos (md:44). The wrapper takes two markers in this order: the per-draw BM NGF MRD status and the per-draw per-IMWG serological response at the same time point; at the call's landmark day L it takes each marker's last draw after the baseline window on or before L, resolves the MRD detectable/undetectable call (the marker's <mrd>__detected rows when present, else a 0/1 status, else the value-0 below-detection convention, else the paper's positive threshold on a quantitative level with a documented median fallback for uncalibrated inputs) and the CR-or-better call (0/1 status, the IMWG categories, or a numeric cutoff), and writes the 2x2 group as risk (0 = CR/MRDneg, 1 = <CR/MRDneg, 2 = CR/MRDpos, 3 = <CR/MRDpos; higher = more likely failing - the paper's published ordering) and call = 1 when MRD is detected at the landmark (the paper's month-1 finding that the presence of MRD predicted poorer landmark PFS; the treatment is judged failing); the paper's landmark analysis (per-group counts, per-group Kaplan-Meier curves and median landmark PFS, the log-rank across all groups, the pairwise contrasts and a Cox four-level factor model) is recomputed at fit on the training patients and reported in run.json, since the paper defines no per-patient probability and TxResBench converts the risk. Differences from the paper: the paper's four landmark months are one analysis per landmark and the benchmark calls the wrapper with one landmark day (the analysis reported is the call's landmark); the paper's exact draw-to-landmark window for 'at months 1/3/6/12' is not stated, so the wrapper uses the last pre-landmark draw of each marker (the benchmark's landmark convention); the paper's log-rank stratification ('stratified by CR and MRD status') is read as the grouping definition, so the global log-rank across the groups and the pairwise contrasts are reported, not a stratified test; the MRD detection call on an input without the assay's undetectable/detectable information follows the benchmark's below-detection convention or a documented fallback, and the response marker on a continuous scale is split at the param cutoff; a patient without both statuses at the landmark gets no prediction with the reason in note.

methods.description: The Conditional Restricted Boltzmann Machine (CRBM) generative model of Fisher, Smith & Walsh (Sci Rep 2019, DOI 10.1038/s41598-019-49656-2): an undirected bipartite network with one hidden layer of 50 ReLU (lower-truncated-normal) units and the visible vector v = {x(t+1), x(t), x_static} - the adjacent 3-month time points plus the static covariates (the paper's single 3-month lag k = 1 and 90-day bucketing, 7 time points 0..18 months in the paper). It learns the joint distribution p(v_static, x(t), x(t+1)) of every marker with the static covariates, so any conditional can be sampled: training imputes missing values from p(v_missing | v_observed) (2 Monte Carlo steps), and forecasts iteratively add time points by sampling each next grid point conditioned on the previous one, so the paper's 'single CRBM model is used to predict all variables, and all time points'. The paper trains it with the combined maximum-likelihood + adversarial objective C = -gamma L - (1-gamma) A (gamma = 0.3; a random-forest adversary - 5 trees, max depth 5 - on the hidden activations, the BEAM training setup of SI ref [7]) by persistent contrastive-divergence Gibbs sampling (50 Monte Carlo steps per model-sample update), ADAM (0.9, 0.999) with the learning rate 0.005 decaying linearly to 0 over 2000 epochs, batch size 100, an L2 weight penalty of 10^-1 and temperature-driven sampling off (Table III). The wrapper reproduces this model and pipeline on the drawn marker values (every marker is a Gaussian continuous visible unit after the paper's log-and-standardize transform; the cov_* columns, when given, are the static units) and uses it exactly as the paper does: per-patient forecasts of the whole marker trajectory conditioned on the observed values (100 simulations per patient as in the paper), with the conditional expectation as the single-value prediction. Because the CRBM predicts marker trajectories and the paper defines no treatment-failure association, the wrapper fits a ridge logistic regression of the first available training failure label (no_response, else progressive_disease, else progression by the first horizon, else death by the first horizon) on the per-patient forecast trajectories and writes its fitted probability of treatment failure as risk; TxResBench converts the risk into the four outcome probabilities. Differences from the paper (the added failure link, conditioning on the draws up to the landmark rather than the t = 0 draw only, the log1p handling of non-detect zeros, the grid extent driven by the benchmark horizons) are recorded in README.md and run.json.
