methods.description: The four-group progression classification rule of the daily CRP/albumin ratio in neonates with necrotizing enterocolitis of Ghauri et al. (Cureus 2025;17(6):e87308, DOI 10.7759/cureus.87308; 66 neonates, Bell's Stage I-IIIa, Children's Hospital Lahore, July 2023 - July 2024, prospective cohort): CRP and albumin are measured on the three consecutive days of admission, the CRP/albumin ratio is calculated daily (md:27), and each patient is placed in one of four groups by the progression pattern of the ratio over that three-day period (md:29): Group A, a consistently decreasing ratio; Group B, a consistently increasing ratio; Group C, a stable ratio with less than 10% variation; Group D, a variable ratio without a clear trend (the paper's cohort: A n = 37, B n = 19, C n = 4, D n = 6, md:54). The rule's documented failure side is the increasing or variable trend: 'among those in Group B and Group D, no patient responded to conservative medical management, and all underwent surgery' (md:84) while Group A (3/37 = 8.1% surgery) and Group C (0/4) were managed conservatively - the paper itself reports the four-group classification and its cohort-level associations (Kruskal-Wallis H 41.260 / 38.295 / 37.241 on Days 1/2/3, Pearson chi-square 54.714 for conservative management and 46.958 for surgical intervention, per-group mortality A 2.6% / B 26.3% / C 0 / D 25%), not a per-patient binary. The wrapper takes the patient's first three informative draws of the marker up to the benchmark landmark (the last draw on or before baseline_max_day = the admission-day value, then the first two draws after it: with the paper's daily schedule this is exactly Days 1-3 of admission) and classifies the three-value trajectory with a declared reading of the paper's unpublished arithmetic - stable first (strictly less than stable_variation variation, the range of the three values over the Day-1 value), then consistently decreasing (no upward step and a net decrease), then consistently increasing (no downward step and a net increase), then the residual variable class (a reversal, no clear trend) - documented in the README and run.json. The wrapper writes risk = the total relative change of the ratio over the window, (Day 3 - Day 1) / Day 1 - the paper's own delta-direction reading, 'An increasing delta (change) indicates worsening inflammation and higher surgical risk, while a decreasing or stable delta suggests clinical improvements' (md:166), higher = more likely failing - and call = 1 for Group B or Group D (the predicted need for surgical intervention, failure of conservative medical management), 0 for Group A or Group C; no probability is written (the rule is a deterministic classification, TxResBench converts the risk), and the four-group cell is reported as per-class training counts in run.json. The wrapper is a fixed rule (fitted false, no training outcome is ever read); a patient without a positive admission-day value (0 is the below-detection encoding and the paper's %-change anchor is undefined), or without at least two on-treatment draws by the landmark, gets no prediction with the reason in note (the research excluded 'incomplete clinical or laboratory data', md:25). Differences from the paper, all declared: the exact arithmetic of the class boundaries is not printed in the paper, so the wrapper's reading is a declared interpretation with the alternatives exposed as settings (stable_variation, variation_reference) rather than a claim of reproduction; 'less than 10%' is read strictly; the benchmark's sparse draw schedules of the paper's 'three consecutive days' are read as the first three informative draws; and the benchmark's binary call (B/D vs A/C) is the paper's own outcome statement reduced to the per-patient decision the benchmark scores, which the paper reports only as cohort-level association.

methods.description: The 3-group on-treatment CRP kinetics classification rule of Fukuda et al. 2021 as applied in the phase III OAK trial by Saal et al. (JNCI Cancer Spectrum 2023;7(3):pkad027, DOI 10.1093/jncics/pkad027; 758 of 1225 OAK participants with analyzable CRP kinetics): each patient's serial serum CRP is grouped into CRP flare-response ('doubling of baseline CRP within first month and drop at least once within 3 months', md:21; origin: '[CRP levels] increased to more than double from baseline within 1 month after initiation of nivolumab (flare) and then decreased to a lower value than baseline within 3 months'), CRP response ('at least 30% decrease of baseline CRP without prior flare', md:21; origin: 'decreased by ≥30% from baseline within 3 months without "flare"') or CRP non-response ('the remaining patients', md:21). In the paper's atezolizumab-treated cohort the call is validated against outcome (validation only, NOT part of the call): CRP responders OR 5.3 and flare-responders OR 4.4 for objective response (CR/PR as best overall response, chi2 P <.0001 /.0001 vs non-responders, md:30) and flare-responders HR 0.52 (95% CI 0.37 to 0.75, P <.001) for death in univariable Cox (md:35), plus the 6/9/12-week re-classifications of the same rule with a truncated drop window in Table 1 (md:43-60). The wrapper takes one marker (the per-draw serum CRP concentration), reads the baseline as the last draw on or before baseline_max_day (the paper's draw before treatment start), tests the flare in the draws after the baseline within flare_window_days (default 30 days, the paper's 'within the first month after ICI start', md:21) and the drop/30% decrease within drop_window_days (default 90 days, the paper's 'within the first 3 months after the start of therapy', md:23), with both windows truncated at the landmark (the data the run has), and writes risk = the native 3-group code (0 CRP response, 1 CRP flare-response, 2 CRP non-response; higher = more likely failing - the non-response group is the paper's worse-outcome group, fivefold lower odds of objective response and the reference of the flare-responders' HR 0.52) and call = 1 for CRP non-response, 0 for CRP response/flare-response (the paper's own fivefold-likelihood contrast, md:30). It writes no probability (the paper defines none; TxResBench converts the risk). A patient with no baseline draw, a baseline at or below the detection limit (value 0 or its __detected row 0 - the ratios would be undefined and the paper excludes patients with missing CRP values instead of imputing, md:23), no on-treatment draw, no draw in the flare window (the flare test and the response class's 'without prior flare' qualifier cannot be assessed), or an observed flare with no later draw to test the 'then decreased' part gets no prediction, with the reason in note (the paper excludes such patients 'to avoid misclassification', md:23). The wrapper learns nothing from the training outcomes; at fit it reports the training group distribution in run.json. Wrapper differences from the paper (detailed in README.md): the rule has no published code (only the IDE 'R Studio (v.1.4)' is named, md:21), so the definition is implemented from the methods and origin text; the paper's calendar months are parametrized as days (defaults 30 and 90; the paper leaves the calendar-vs-4-week rule unstated and the OAK 21-day-cycle schedule puts exactly one draw in the first month at a median 22 days, md:21); the benchmark's landmark stands in for the paper's analysis time points so the windows are truncated at it (the Table 1 6/9/12-week variants are the same rule with a truncated window, md:40, md:43-60); a draw after the 3-month window never enters the rule (md:23); the origin's strict 'more than double' flare boundary is implemented (the J2023 restatement says 'doubling'; the boundary is not resolved there, and the origin's stricter wording is recorded - the >= 30% decrease boundary is inclusive in both texts); and because the paper reports per-patient only the 3-group call (no score or probability), the risk column carries the ordered group code, which is the grid's convention for a three-group rule.

required_markers.list_source: Saal JH et al., JNCI Cancer Spectrum 2023;7(3):pkad027, DOI 10.1093/jncics/pkad027 (the phase III OAK application) and Fukuda S et al., J Immunother Cancer 2021;9(2):e001564, DOI 10.1136/jitc-2020-001564 (the origin definition): the method IS the 3-group CRP kinetics rule - 'Patients were divided into the 3 CRP kinetics groups based on their on-treatment CRP levels as defined by Fukuda et al. methods.description: The refined four-group on-treatment CRP kinetics classification rule of Dächert et al. (J Immunother Cancer 2023;11:e007765, DOI 10.1136/jitc-2023-007765; discovery n=562, validation n=474, pan-cancer palliative immune checkpoint inhibition at Austrian centres, 2011-2021): from the serum CRP at ICI treatment start (which the paper defines as the research baseline and requires of every patient, md:49) and all available on-treatment serum CRP values within the first 3 months (md:51, md:53), each patient is placed in one of four groups - all-normal CRP if the baseline and every on-treatment value are at or below the upper limit of normal of 5 mg/L (the fourth group, this paper's refinement, which takes precedence over the other three per the reclassification counts md:216 and requires a baseline at or below the ULN by definition, md:228); CRP flare-responder if CRP at least doubles the baseline (>=100% increase) within 1 month of treatment start and then drops below the baseline within the consecutive 2 months; CRP responder if CRP falls by at least 30% from the baseline within 3 months; and CRP non-responder for all remaining patients, including those with only one longitudinal CRP readout (the paper's explicit default, md:53). The paper validates the call against ORR, PFS and OS (per-group ORR 41%/38%/31%/12% and median PFS 8.2/6.1/5.7/2.3 months, all-normal/responder/flare/non-responder, md:221, md:223; refined multivariable PFS HRs 0.48/0.63/0.74 vs non-responders, md:186) - validation only, not part of the call. The wrapper writes risk = the minimum on-treatment CRP divided by the baseline CRP (the quantity the 30%-response branch thresholds at 0.70; higher = more likely failing) and call = 1 for the CRP non-responder group (the paper's failing side - 'early identification of patients... with very high risk of primary treatment resistance and rapid disease progression', md:258), 0 for the other three groups; no probability is written (the rule is a deterministic classification; TxResBench converts the risk), and the four-group table of the training patients is reported at fit. The paper's windows are calendar months (1 month, 3 months) and give no day conversion, so the wrapper reads them as 30 and 90 days, both truncated at the benchmark landmark, and prints no draw after the first 3 months; the paper publishes no analysis code (Stata 16.1 only, md:60; code and data on reasonable request, md:64, md:285), so every threshold quoted here comes from the Methods/Results text.

methods.description: The 3-class on-treatment CRP kinetics rule of Nose et al. (BJC Reports 2023;1:7, DOI 10.1038/s44276-023-00005-x; 76 gastric adenocarcinoma discovery and 71 oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma validation patients on nivolumab monotherapy at Osaka University Hospital): from the serum CRP at baseline (before nivolumab initiation) and the on-treatment serum CRP draws within 6 weeks, each patient is called CRP-spike (an increase more than twofold from baseline AND >1.0 mg/dL within 4 weeks of nivolumab initiation, followed by a decrease of <1.0 mg/dL within 6 weeks), CRP-flat (maintenance at <1.0 mg/dL, or a decrease from >1.0 mg/dL to <1.0 mg/dL, during the period from before to 6 weeks after initiation) or CRP-increase (all other patients) (md:37). In the paper's cohorts CRP-spike is the favourable group (multivariate PFS hazard ratio 0.38 [0.16-0.91] in gastric and 0.28 [0.12-0.68] in oesophageal cancer, spike vs others, md:71/md:85), CRP-increase the worst (gastric DCR 3.3% vs 44.4% spike, md:64) - validation only, not part of the call. The wrapper takes one marker (the per-draw serum CRP concentration, whose values must be the paper's mg/dL scale since the 1.0 mg/dL thresholds are absolute), reads the baseline as the last draw on or before baseline_max_day (the paper's 'baseline, before the initiation of nivolumab', md:27), tests the spike in the draws within rise_window_days (default 28, the paper's 'within 4 weeks') and the spike drop / flat period within drop_window_days (default 42, the paper's 'within 6 weeks'), with both windows truncated at the landmark (the data the run has) and no draw after the window ever used; it applies the spike test first, then the flat test, then the paper's residual (the class order of md:37, the reading the per-method spec records as inferred from the text order), and writes risk = the native 3-class code (0 CRP-spike, 1 CRP-flat, 2 CRP-increase; higher = more likely failing) and call = 1 for CRP-increase (the paper's failing side: ORR 0%/9.7%, DCR 3.3%/32.3%, median PFS 1.5/2.0 months in the two cohorts, md:64/md:69/md:78/md:83), 0 for CRP-spike and CRP-flat; no probability is written (the paper defines none; TxResBench converts the risk). A patient is left unclassified (empty risk, the reason in note) when the paper's data requirement is not met and no class is defined for it (the spec's new_patient_prediction.fallback): no baseline draw; a baseline at or below the detection limit (the benchmark's value 0 / its __detected companion 0 - the >2x ratio and the absolute comparisons are undefined, and the paper states no zero handling, md:37); no on-treatment draw within the 6-week window; no draw within the 4-week rise window (the spike rise test cannot be assessed - a hidden rise would decide the class, and the spec records the paper's fallback as not defined, '?'); or an observed spike rise with no later draw by the drop window end (the 'followed by a decrease of <1.0 mg/dL within 6 weeks' cannot be assessed). The rule is quoted verbatim from the paper's Methods (md:37); the paper publishes no analysis code (job.code = []; only 'JMP Pro 14 Discovery(TM)' is named, md:47), so nothing is substituted or re-derived, and the wrapper states each reading it had to make in the README and run.json.

methods.description: The four-group combined CTC + cfDNA change risk rule of Ko JMY et al., 'Liquid Biopsy Serial Monitoring of Treatment Responses and Relapse in Advanced Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma' (Cancers 2020;12(6):1352, DOI 10.3390/cancers12061352; 57 analysed of 60 recruited advanced stage III/IV ESCC patients on palliative, mostly platinum-based, chemotherapy): each of the four specimens - CTC count at baseline (CTC1) and pre-cycle III (CTC2, cells/5 mL whole blood, size-based CTChip FR1 / ClearCell FX1 enrichment with pan-CK/EpCAM/MUC1+/CD45- immunofluorescence) and plasma cfDNA concentration at baseline (cfDNA1) and pre-cycle III (cfDNA2, copies of haploid genome (hG)/mL plasma, Qubit 2.0 after AVENIO isolation, log10-transformed) - is marked 1 (high) or 0 (low) at the paper's thresholds (CTC count > 2, i.e. >= 3 per 5 mL; log10 cfDNA1 >= 3.360; log10 cfDNA2 >= 3.2817), and the patient is assigned one of four risk groups by the 16-combination table of Supplementary Table S3: group 0 (low-risk: both changes favorable, 0-1 marks), group 1 (at-risk: one favorable and one unfavorable change, or both favorable with 2 marks), group 2 (at-risk: both changes unfavorable, 2-3 marks), group 3 (highest risk: all four marks). The four groups are independently associated with OS in the forward-stepwise multivariable Cox (HR 6.008 [1.27-28.5] / 9.520 [1.81-50.0] / 81.958 [7.95-845] for groups 1/2/3 vs group 0 reference, p = 0.002, with age HR 0.932; median OS 479/183/162/77 days, p = 4e-6; Table S2 AUROC 0.641 on the 0-3 group scale). The wrapper takes exactly two markers (the CTC count and the plasma cfDNA concentration), pairs each patient's baseline and pre-cycle III draws (last draw on or before baseline_max_day; last draw after it up to the landmark - the paper's pre-cycle III visit being after two cycles, ~6 weeks after baseline), applies the mark rule and Table S3, and writes risk = the pre-cycle III CTC count in cells/5 mL - the quantity the rule's on-treatment CTC threshold applies to, the combined rule's strongest independent axis (univariate HR 3.426 interim reassessment / 3.680 PFS / 3.576 OS for the high CTC2 group) - and call = 1 for any non-low-risk group (group >= 1; the paper's Table S2 ROC operating point 0.5 on the 0-3 group scale), 0 for the low-risk group 0. It writes no probability of its own: the paper defines none per patient (the KM medians and Cox HRs are cohort-level), so TxResBench converts the risk. Nothing is learned from the training outcomes (the thresholds were derived in the authors' own sample by ROC for OS, no code or optimum criterion published; the corpus's published-constant convention). A patient without all four usable specimens gets no prediction, with the reason in note - the paper's complete-case analysis (n = 44 of 57 with all four; 0 CTCs is a valid low mark, a cfDNA level of 0 is not log10-transformable and the Qubit quantification measured positive levels only).

methods.description: The three-group CTC change risk rule of Ko JMY et al., 'Liquid Biopsy Serial Monitoring of Treatment Responses and Relapse in Advanced Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma' (Cancers 2020;12(6):1352, DOI 10.3390/cancers12061352; 57 analysed of 60 recruited advanced stage III/IV ESCC patients on palliative, mostly platinum-based, chemotherapy): the CTC count per 5 mL whole blood (STRECK tubes, size-based CTChip FR1 / ClearCell FX1 enrichment, pan-CK/EpCAM/MUC1+/CD45- immunofluorescence enumeration) at baseline (CTC1) and pre-cycle III (CTC2, end of cycle II, ~6 weeks after baseline) is each dichotomized low (0-2 CTCs) vs high (>= 3 CTCs; the paper's '>2' per the Table S3 footnote, threshold chosen because the mean CTC1/CTC2 enumerations were 2.31/2.47 cells per 5 mL and it gave 'the higher specificity of CTC1 and CTC2', md:83, corroborated by the Table S2 ROC for OS: CTC2 AUROC 0.661, threshold 2.5, sensitivity 0.375, specificity 0.846), and the patient is assigned one of three risk groups: group 0 (low-risk: both draws 0-2 CTCs), group 1 (intermediate-risk: all other combinations, i.e. low->high or high->low), group 2 (high-risk: both draws >= 3 CTCs) (md:176). The groups were associated with TTP at interim imaging reassessment (median 98/90/57 days, log-rank p = 3.34e-4), PFS (125/105/60 days, p = 4.37e-7) and OS (302/178/77 days, p = 0.005) (Figure 3Ai-iii), with univariate OS Cox HRs 3.103 (1.11-8.65, p = 0.089) and 6.178 (1.87-20.4, p = 0.004) for groups 1 and 2 vs group 0 (Table 2C, group variable p = 0.012) and with multivariable HRs in Table S5 (age, stage at CTC blood collection, cfDNA1/2 change groups; OS group 2 HR 9.945 [1.751-56.488], p = 0.01) - all complete-case on the n = 43 patients with both CTC1 and CTC2 (group 0 n = 22, group 1 n = 16, group 2 n = 5). The wrapper takes exactly one marker (the CTC count), pairs each patient's baseline and pre-cycle III draws (last draw on or before baseline_max_day; last draw after it up to the landmark - the paper's pre-cycle III visit after two cycles, ~6 weeks after baseline), applies the per-draw dichotomy and the three-group combination, and writes risk = the pre-cycle III CTC count in cells/5 mL - the quantity the rule's on-treatment CTC threshold applies to and the rule's strongest independent axis (univariate HR 3.426 interim reassessment / 3.680 PFS / 3.576 OS for CTC2 >= 3, Table 2) - and call = 1 for the high-risk group 2 (both draws high, the paper's adverse class), 0 otherwise. The paper defines no per-patient score or probability (its medians and HRs are cohort-level), so TxResBench converts the risk; the per-patient three-group ordinal and the training cohort's group/status counts are reported at fit (run.json). A patient without both usable draws gets no prediction, with the reason in note - the paper's complete-case analysis (n = 43 of 57, no imputation stated); 0 CTCs is a valid low count (0-2), not a non-detect.

methods.description: The CTC-dynamics three-group classification rule of Liu MC et al., 'First-Line Doublet Chemotherapy for Metastatic Triple-Negative Breast Cancer: Circulating Tumor Cell Analysis of the tnAcity Trial' (Cancer Manag Res 2019, DOI 10.2147/CMAR.S208712; the prespecified exploratory CTC analysis of the randomized Phase II/III tnAcity trial, NCT01881230; 126 of 191 enrolled first-line metastatic TNBC patients on weekly nab-paclitaxel (nab-P)/carboplatin, nab-P/gemcitabine or gemcitabine/carboplatin in the main analysis): the CELLSEARCH CTC count per 7.5 mL whole blood (CellSave tube, 8-10 mL blood, Menarini Silicon Biosystems) at baseline (day 1 of cycle 1, before treatment) and on day 1 of cycles 3 and 5 (postbaseline) is each dichotomized at the cutoff (>= 1 CTC/7.5 mL for the main analysis; >= 2 and >= 5 for supporting analyses), and the patient is assigned one of three groups, verbatim (md:38): Group 1 (+ + +; CTCs elevated at baseline and both postbaseline visits), Group 2 (+ - -; CTCs elevated at baseline and cleared at >= 1 postbaseline visit [cycle 3 and/or cycle 5]), Group 3 (-; no CTCs detected at baseline - defined by the baseline draw alone; postbaseline draws do not reclassify). The grouping was associated with treatment failure in the expected direction: Group 1 (persistent elevation) had the lowest ORR (29.1%, Table 3; the running text prints 29.2%) and the shortest median PFS (4.7 months) and OS (9.8 months); Group 2 (clearance) had the best outcomes (ORR 79.6%; median PFS 8.5 months, HR 0.30 [95% CI 0.17-0.54] vs Group 1; median OS 17.8 months, HR 0.35 [0.20-0.62]); Group 3 (none at baseline) was intermediate (ORR 43.8%; median PFS 5.9 months; median OS 16.0 months, HR 0.40 [0.22-0.73] vs Group 1). The wrapper takes exactly one marker (the CELLSEARCH CTC count per 7.5 mL; declared in required_markers), reads the baseline as the marker's last draw on or before baseline_max_day and the postbaseline visits as all marker draws after it up to the landmark, and writes risk = the rule's three-group failure code (0 = Group 2 clearance, 1 = Group 3 none at baseline, 2 = Group 1 persistent elevation; higher = more likely failing - the paper's ordering of the three groups on ORR/PFS/OS) and call = 1 for Group 1 only (the paper's adverse class: persistent elevation = treatment judged failing), with no probability of its own (TxResBench converts the risk; the paper's KM/log-rank and Cox HRs are cohort-level evaluation of the grouping, not per-patient scores). A patient without a usable baseline draw, or with an elevated baseline and no usable postbaseline draw (the paper's Group-1-vs-Group-2 distinction is undefined for such a patient, md:38/md:53), gets no prediction with the reason in note; 0 CTCs is a valid 'no CTCs detected' value, not a non-detect; a postbaseline value below the cutoff marks clearance and a Group-3 patient's postbaseline draws never reclassify. No analysis code is published (job.code is empty; no software named in md:43), so the rule is implemented from the paper's text with the published cutoff as the fixed setting (params ctc_cutoff 1) and nothing is learned from the training outcomes.

methods.description: The day-14 CTC composite response endpoint of the CirCe01 trial (Cabel L, Berger F, Cottu P, et al., Br J Cancer 2021;124:1207-1213, DOI 10.1038/s41416-020-01227-3; 51 patients with >=5 CTC/7.5 mL randomised to the CTC-driven arm A of a prospective multicentre randomised trial of late-line chemotherapy for metastatic breast cancer): 'A >=70% decrease of the baseline CTC count or a fall to below <5 CTC/7.5 mL was considered to be indicative of a potential response to chemotherapy.' (md:136-140); 'CTC monitoring showed a CTC response (>=70% relative reduction or <5 CTC/7.5 mL absolute count at week 2) in 25 patients (58%)' (md:476-478), 'Patients predicted to experience early tumour progression according to CTC monitoring (i.e. no CTC response according to the above-mentioned composite endpoint) had to discontinue their third-line chemotherapy' (md:151-155). The CellSearch CTC count (CTC/7.5 mL) is read at the line baseline (before the first cycle, md:116-118) and repeated at day 14 of cycle 1 (before the second cycle, md:134-135); the wrapper evaluates the benchmark's landmark draw as the paper's day-14 draw (the last draw after baseline_max_day and at or before the landmark) and writes the composite in its Fig. 1 De Morgan form - call 1 (treatment judged failing) = no CTC response = '>=5 CTC/7.5 mL and Relative decrease <--70%' (md:199-206) = (day-14 count >= 5) AND (relative change > -70%), call 0 = CTC response = (day-14 count < 5) OR (relative change <= -70%); risk = the day-14 relative change of the count (per cent, negative = decrease - the quantity the 70% criterion thresholds; the OR-composite is not fully captured by that scalar per the spec's projection, a count <5 CTC/7.5 mL with a shallow relative decrease is still a response). methods.description: The three-class CTC dynamics rule and the univariable-then-multivariable Cox analysis of De Laere et al. (The Prostate 2018;78(6):435-445, DOI 10.1002/pros.23488; 174 mCRPC patients treated with abiraterone acetate (124) or enzalutamide (50) at nine European centres): the CellSearch CTC count per 7.5 mL whole blood at treatment initiation (baseline, day <= baseline_max_day) and the follow-up draw 'in patients who were responding for ca. 10-12 weeks' (the last draw after the baseline at or before the landmark; observed average 2.37 +/- 0.67 months, median 2.3 months) give the per-patient class 'increasing' (follow-up > baseline) / 'decreasing' (follow-up < baseline) / 'stable' (follow-up == baseline) — direction only, no 30%/50% magnitude cutoff ('decreasing CTC counts (which, except for 2 patients, was at least 30%)'); the stable-class boundary is not resolved by the paper (stable_class 'equality' by default; the 'band' reading — both draws at 0 or 1 CTC/7.5 mL — is the Supplementary Figure 4 legend's description and is available as the alternative setting). The analysis evaluates the classes against PFS (treatment initiation -> clinical symptomatic and/or radiologic progression, RECIST v1.1) and OS (baseline blood sample -> death, censored at last follow-up) by three-group Kaplan-Meier + log-rank and by one Cox per survival outcome in which the dynamics are DICHOTOMIZED as increasing vs stable/decreasing, the continuous baseline CTC count is log-transformed and used as the only baseline CTC measure, and the significant baseline variables plus the >=50% PSA-change covariate at 10-12 weeks are entered: the wrapper screens the log-transformed continuous baseline CTC count and every cov_* column at univariate p < p_enter (0.05, the paper's two-sided p < 0.05 convention) and keeps the dichotomized dynamics and an identified PSA-50%-change covariate in every model. It writes risk = the CTC count change (follow-up - baseline, the quantity the published rule thresholds; higher = an increase = more likely failing), call = 1 for the increasing group (the paper's exposed failure group), risk_progression/risk_death = the fitted Cox linear predictors and p_progression_H*/p_death_H* = 1 - S(H - landmark) of the fitted models (the model's own conditional event probabilities), and reports in run.json the cohort-level outputs the paper prints: the three-group KM medians and log-rank p, the dichotomized Cox HR for the increasing group, the univariable screening table and the multivariable coefficients per outcome. The paper names only R as the environment ('All tests were performed in R', md:245-246) and publishes no analysis code, so the wrapper is its own reimplementation in survival 3.7-0 and the fold-fitted coefficients are the benchmark fold's own estimates; the resolved differences — the stable-class boundary, the log base (log1p, natural log of value + 1; 0 CTC is a valid count and never encoded as missing), the covariate channel (the benchmark's cov_* columns, with none defaulting to the dynamics + continuous log baseline CTC only, the paper's model being covariate-adjusted), the PFS/OS origin difference (treatment initiation vs the baseline blood sample, near-coincident) and the benchmark's 'as of the landmark' pairing instead of a 10-12-week-only window — are recorded in run.json and README.md.

methods.description: Per-patient binary risk call at the t2 (6-week, post-2nd-cycle) blood draw for patients on pembrolizumab (Kakouri AC et al., Transl Lung Cancer Res 2025, DOI 10.21037/tlcr-2024-1095; prospective SWIPE trial NCT02705820, 46 analysed metastatic NSCLC patients): among patients with detectable circulating tumour cells (CTCs) and at least one PD-L1+ CTC at t2 (CTCs detected in 21/33 (63.6%) and PD-L1+ CTCs in 18/21 (85.7%), md:125), the CTC Ki67-index (iKi67 = percentage of Ki67+ CTCs over the total CTC number per patient, md:130) is compared with the fixed 30% cut-off >30% Ki67+ CTCs (high-iKi67) vs <30% (low iKi67) (md:130); high-iKi67 marks the risk-positive group - the paper reports shorter PFS (2 vs 4.45 months, P=0.03, HR =10.13) and OS (5 vs 27.2 months, P=0.003, HR =6.1). The cut-off is borrowed from the authors' previous research (ref 21, Spiliotaki et al. 2023), not derived here, and the paper publishes no analysis code (R is named as the statistics environment only), so the wrapper implements the rule from the paper text, its data table and the supplementary methodology: it reads exactly two markers (the CTC Ki67-index and the PD-L1+ CTC count/status, declared as required markers UniProt P46013 / Q9NZQ7, triple IF on PBMC cytospins), makes the call at the last paired panel draw at or before the t2 assessment (day 42 = 6 weeks; draws after it never enter), writes the iKi67 value as risk (higher = more Ki67+ CTCs = more likely failing) and call = 1 for high-iKi67, and abstains - empty risk with the reason in note - for patients without an evaluable t2 CTC panel or without PD-L1+ CTCs, because the paper's call is defined only within that subgroup (a patient with exactly 30% is assigned to the low group, the strict reading of the printed '>30%'); no probability is defined by the paper, so none is written and TxResBench converts the risk. The paper's PFS/OS log-rank and age-/sex-adjusted Cox are cohort-level validation of the two call groups, not part of the per-patient call.

methods.description: The two-group survival analysis of CTC status at the first on-treatment follow-up of Schochter F, Friedl TWP, Schaeffler H, et al., 'Efficacy, safety and circulating tumor cell dynamics in patients treated with Eribulin for HER2-negative advanced breast cancer - results from the phase II DETECT IVb trial', Breast Cancer Res Treat 2026, DOI 10.1007/s10549-026-08069-2 (DETECT IVb, HR+/HER2- and triple-negative metastatic breast cancer on single-agent eribulin, n = 109 registered, 75 with a first on-treatment CTC assessment >= 21 days after registration): the CellSearch CTC count per 7.5 mL whole blood at the patient's first on-treatment follow-up (>= 21 days after registration, per-patient variable; median 33 days, IQR 27-66, range 21-268, md:99) is categorized by one of two predefined statuses - complete CTC clearance (0 vs >= 1 CTC) as default, or the established Cristofanilli cutoff (0-4 vs >= 5 CTCs) - and the two groups are compared by Kaplan-Meier curves with log-rank tests and by univariable and multivariable Cox proportional-hazards regression of PFS (primary) and OS (secondary, both from registration), the multivariable model adding the paper's five predefined covariates (metastatic treatment line, metastasis-free interval, site of first metastasis, tumor subtype, patient age), with the likelihood-ratio test of the CTC-status addition; published adjusted HRs (n = 75): PFS 0.56 (0.31-0.98, p = 0.043) for clearance vs detectable and 0.55 (0.30-1.01, p = 0.052) for 0-4 vs >=5, OS 0.69 (0.39-1.21, p = 0.192) and 0.45 (0.25-0.82, p = 0.009) (md:105). The wrapper reads the one CTC-count marker the benchmark passes, takes each patient's FIRST draw with day >= min_followup_day (21) on or before the decision day (max_followup_day set reproduces the paper's 21-84-day sensitivity analysis), writes risk = the raw count at that draw (the quantity the status thresholds; higher = the paper's higher-risk group), call = 1 for the unfavorable group (detectable / >= 5 CTCs), and fits one Cox per survival outcome on the training patients event-free at the landmark with a status draw (univariable, plus the paper's multivariable model when its five covariates are identified by name in the cov_* channel, complete cases): risk_<outcome> = the fitted linear predictor, p_<outcome>_H<h> = 1 - S(h - L) of the fitted model - the paper defines no per-patient probability, so the response outcomes use the package's conversion of the count. A patient without a useable status draw (or without a covariate the adjusted model needs) gets an empty risk and the reason in note. The paper's analysis was run in SPSS 26 with no published code or syntax, so nothing was substituted: the wrapper is the survival package's reimplementation and its estimates are the benchmark fold's, not the paper's; differences from the paper (harness clock vs registration, fixed decision day vs the per-patient assessment time, one-level-status fallback, covariate identification) are recorded in the README and run.json.

methods.description: The two-draw CTC trend call of Fina E et al., 'Clinical Significance of Early Changes in Circulating Tumor Cells from Patients Receiving First-Line Cisplatin-Based Chemotherapy for Metastatic Urothelial Carcinoma' (Bladder Cancer 2016;2(4):395-403, DOI 10.3233/BLC-160069; single-centre pilot, 31 patients with metastatic urothelial carcinoma on first-line MVAC, Fondazione IRCCS Istituto Nazionale dei Tumori, Milano, July 2012-May 2014): tumour-cell mRNA expression of EPCAM, MUC1 and ERBB2 in peripheral whole blood after AdnaTest ProstateCancerSelect enrichment and AdnaTest BreastCancerDetect semiquantitative multiplex-PCR (ng/uL, co-amplified with ACTB as a control, md:34-36) is measured at baseline (T0, the day before starting chemotherapy) and after the second cycle (T2, with the disease restaging, md:27). Per draw the sample is CTC-positive if at least one of the three markers is at or above its cut-off (EPCAM >= 0.40, MUC1 >= 0.10, ERBB2 >= 0.20 ng/uL; ROC-derived in healthy donors, md:10, md:38); the T0-T2 status pair is then split - 'due to small numbers, CTC variation was arbitrarily split in favorable (-/-, +/- and -/+) and unfavorable (+/+) groups' (md:45). The published results: unfavorable vs favorable trend 3-year PFS 10% vs 49.2% (p = 0.006; HR 5.04, 95% CI 1.58-16.05) and 3-year OS 20% vs 63.5% (p = 0.017; HR 3.97, 95% CI 1.27-12.38), median PFS 6 vs 20 months (median OS 8 months vs more than 65% alive at 3 years), maintained in bivariable Cox models with liver metastases and MSKCC score (and with RECIST response for PFS only, md:64, md:66); the association of CTC with RECIST response was not significant (md:62) and single-timepoint T0/T2 status was explicitly NOT prognostic (md:64). The wrapper takes exactly the three panel markers (EPCAM, MUC1, ERBB2 mRNA expression), pairs each patient's full-panel draws (T0 = the last draw carrying all three markers on or before baseline_max_day; T2 = the last such draw after it and at or before the benchmark landmark - the corpus fixed-pair convention for the paper's after-the-second-cycle draw; a run at the ~2-cycle landmark reproduces the paper's pair), applies the any-of-3 cut-offs, and writes call = 1 exactly for the unfavorable +/+ pair (the paper's adverse class: 'patients with persistently positive CTC after 2 cycles of MVAC had significantly worse PFS and OS', md:87) and call = 0 for every other pair (the -/+ cell stays in favorable by the paper's own discussion argument, md:73) - the contract's failure orientation. It writes risk = the number of the three panel markers at or above their cut-off at the T2 decision draw (0-3, the per-draw CTC-positive level that the any-of-3 status thresholds at >= 1): the paper defines no per-patient score (its KM probabilities and HRs are cohort-level), so the wrapper writes the quantity the rule's on-treatment threshold applies to, per the corpus convention for fixed-pair rules, and TxResBench converts it; no probability is written (the paper defines no per-patient probability). Nothing is learned from the training outcomes (fitted false): the cut-offs are assay constants ROC-derived in healthy donors (md:10, md:38) and the trend split is the authors' fixed arbitrary rule (md:45), treated as published constants (params, user-overridable). A patient without both full-panel draws gets no prediction, with the reason in note - the paper's complete-case trend analysis (n = 26 of 31; the ACTB >= 3.0 ng/uL evaluability gate of md:40 is a pre-analytic assay QC that the benchmark's per-draw values already passed, and a patient without an evaluable T2 was excluded, md:57); a marker value below its cut-off (including the benchmark's non-detect encoding, value 0) is CTC-negative for that marker, and a non-finite or negative expression value makes the draw unusable. The per-marker statuses, the trend group and the training cohort's status-pair counts are reported at fit (run.json), with the paper's reported results.

methods.description: The per-patient (and per-on-treatment-draw) ctDNA-progression rule of van der Wel et al. (JTO Clinical and Research Reports 2025;6:100853, DOI 10.1016/j.jtocrr.2025.100853; multicenter prospective research NCT04148066, 21 evaluable EGFRm+ NSCLC patients, exon 19 deletion with or without insertion or L858R, T790M-mediated resistance, second-/third-line osimertinib 80 mg daily, AVENIO ctDNA expanded panel RUO): plasma ctDNA was analysed at baseline and serially (every 6 weeks for the first 6 months, every 8 weeks thereafter, every 12 weeks after 1 year, md:25), variants were reported when VAF was at least 0.1% (md:66), and 'any increase in VAF between two subsequent plasma samples was regarded as ctDNA progression' (md:66) - arm 1: the primary EGFR driver mutation VAF rises between two consecutive samples (no numeric threshold, no baseline or nadir reference); arm 2: a known genomically-defined resistance mechanism (RM) is detected in plasma (md:50): BRAF V600E, PIK3CA H1047L, ERBB2 amplification, ERBB2 L755P, EGFR amplification, EGFR C797S, EGFR G724S (each observed before PD, md:131), ERBB2 L755S and ALK fusion (at PD, md:131), MET amplification (protocol-monitored, md:41; none detected); amplifications per the CNV rule (CNV score >= 5 AND genomic region < 20% of the affected chromosome, 'possible' and 'probable' both counted, md:66); the call = arm 1 OR arm 2 (md:20). In the paper's cohort the driver VAF rise preceded radiologic RECIST 1.1 PD in 7/21 (33%, median interval 9 weeks, range 7-34, md:124) and at least one RM was detected before PD in 7/21 (33.3%, median 14 weeks, range 7-34, md:131); all patients with ctDNA PD also developed radiologic PD (md:126). The wrapper writes call = 1 when the rule fires on any consecutive pair or RM presence up to the benchmark landmark, risk = the largest consecutive-pair primary-driver VAF increase in the dataset's value scale (the quantity arm 1 thresholds at > 0 - the paper defines no per-patient scalar), and no probability; a patient with fewer than two observed driver draws gets no prediction with the reason in note. The wrapper's declared readings of the paper's open points are in the README: only the primary driver counts (a T790M rise is recorded but not used, md:50 vs md:124), an undetectable-to-detectable transition counts as an increase (the paper's 're-emergence', md:133/md:155), the RM arm reads presence not emergence (the reported before-PD metric counts baseline RMs, md:131), the published CNV-score/region pair cannot be reproduced from the benchmark input so amplification calls come from the dataset's own call (detected rows or a 0/1 status) or the declared amp_detection_threshold and otherwise do not fire, and the complete curated RM list is in the paper's supplementary information (md:68) so the wrapper declares the recoverable reported set.

methods.description: ctDNA clearance at any time point (Nixon et al., Scientific Reports 2026;16:14766, DOI 10.1038/s41598-026-43178-4; 24 ctDNA-evaluable of 36 KeyLargo phase II patients with metastatic HER2-negative esophagogastric adenocarcinoma on first-line pembrolizumab + capecitabine + oxaliplatin, tumour-informed bespoke NeXT Personal assay, median LOD 2.03 PPM; no analysis code published - the rule is implemented from the Methods/Results text, statistics in R 4.3.1 md:405-406). The rule groups patients by clearance, 'defined as the absence of ctDNA signal at any time point between C1D8 and C7D1' (md:424-425): clearance = the ctDNA signal below the limit of detection at ANY of the window draws (7/24 patients), persistently ctDNA-positive = detectable at every window draw (17/24); failure to clear was associated with inferior PFS (HR 19.94, p = 0.00461) and OS (HR 7.07, p = 0.0115) (md:225-229). The window is the protocol's per-draw detection status of the assay's one-tailed Poisson test (p <= 0.001, md:396-398), which the benchmark carries as <marker>__detected rows (the wrapper uses them when present, else value > 0 or a detection_threshold / training-median stand-in for the level, with a warning); the window is [window_start_day, landmark_day] in days since the first dose (window_start_day default 7 = the paper's C1D8; the baseline C1D1 draw is explicitly NOT in the window, md:424-425). It writes risk = the fraction of the patient's window draws that are ctDNA-positive (higher = more protracted positivity = worse; 1.0 = no clearance = call 1) and call = 1 for persistently ctDNA-positive (treatment judged failing), 0 for clearance; no probability is defined by the paper (TxResBench converts the risk). A patient with no window draw (the paper does not state how such a patient is called, '?') or with a window draw whose detection status is undetermined (an unknown draw could be the below-LOD one) gets no prediction, with the reason in note.

methods.description: The three-group survival risk stratum of Wang Y et al. (J Natl Cancer Cent 2024, DOI 10.1016/j.jncc.2024.01.008; 103 analysed of 128 enrolled unresectable LA-NSCLC patients on curative-intent CRT with or without consolidation ICI, two-center prospective cohort with an external 30-patient validation set; 486-gene plasma NGS of cfDNA at baseline (diagnosis), 4 weeks after completing radical CRT (post-CRT) and at progression): patients are divided into 3 groups on the basis of their post-CRT ctDNA detection status and dynamic delta-bTMB (post-CRT bTMB minus baseline bTMB) - group 1 = post-CRT ctDNA UNDETECTABLE and non-increased delta-bTMB (delta-bTMB <= 0; the longest OS/PFS), group 2 = post-CRT ctDNA DETECTABLE (residual) and non-increased delta-bTMB, group 3 = post-CRT ctDNA DETECTABLE and increased delta-bTMB (delta-bTMB > 0; the significantly shortest OS and PFS, OS median 9.0 vs 23.0 vs NR months and PFS median 3.4 vs 7.3 vs 25.2 months, P < 0.001, Fig. 5A/B; pairwise 3-group comparisons significant; DCA C-index 0.723 OS / 0.693 PFS for the combined model, Fig. 5C/D; validation PFS C-index 0.742, Fig. 6E/F). The wrapper takes exactly two markers (the per-draw ctDNA detection status and the per-draw bTMB level, identified by name or by the positional convention), reads the baseline draw (last at or before baseline_max_day) and the post-CRT draw (last after it and at or before the landmark - the paper's 4-weeks-post-CRT protocol visit has no benchmark channel), computes the detection call from the marker's data (the contract's <marker>__detected companion first, then a __lod row, then 0-coded non-detects / 0-1 status values, then the training-derived level threshold as a documented stand-in when the data carries no detection call at all) and delta-bTMB = post-CRT bTMB - baseline bTMB, and writes risk = the ordered group code (1/2/3, higher = worse - the paper's group 3 is the adverse class with the significantly shortest OS/PFS) and call = 1 for group 3 (residual ctDNA + increased delta-bTMB = the paper's treatment-failure class to be identified for therapy intensification), and no probability (the paper defines none; TxResBench converts the risk). A patient with undetectable post-CRT ctDNA but increased delta-bTMB gets no prediction with the reason in note: the paper's 2x2 combination has that cell structurally empty ('All patients with undetectable ctDNA post-CRT had non-increased delta-bTMB (delta-bTMB <= 0)', md:128) and the published rule defines no group for it; likewise a patient without both draws of both features (the paper's exclusion 'Patients whose blood plasma was not collected at prespecified time points were excluded from the final analysis.', md:37). At fit the paper's cohort-level association is recomputed on the training patients and reported in run.json (per-group KM medians, 3-group log-rank test, Holm-adjusted pairwise comparisons, Harrell's C of the stratum) - evaluation machinery, not part of the call, and the paper's DCA-computed C-index (a non-standard definition, md:57) is NOT reproduced. Wrapper differences from the paper are listed in README.md.

methods.description: The ctDNA-guided End of Treatment (cEoT) branched decision algorithm of Fabi A, Giordani E et al. (J Exp Clin Cancer Res 2026, DOI 10.1186/s13046-025-03605-2; GIM21/LiqERBcept, 43 analysed HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer patients on T-DM1, 27 cPD-positive): a ctDNA-RECIST (cRECIST) trajectory rule that, after the first ctDNA progressive disease (cPD, >= 20% Delta-ctDNA increase and/or a new ctDNA species - the default cRECIST mirror of RECIST 1.1), follows an intensified-monitoring branch and assigns a personalized End of Treatment (cEoT) at (a) the second of two consecutive ctDNA increases, regardless of magnitude, or (b) the first ctDNA absolute increase after the first post-cPD Tr drop, whichever occurs first, with the fallback (c) EoT coincides with PD per standard of care; Tr is the average of the three consecutive Delta-ctDNA values of each overlapping 3-point series (triplets), its trend increase/decreased with disappearance of a previously detected ctDNA and de novo appearance of a new one assimilated to Tr decrease/increase. The wrapper takes one or more per-draw ctDNA measurement features (any marker set: the paper's bespoke NGS/dPCR panel of 78 alterations arrives as per-draw variant/CNV features, and the wrapper sums them per draw with the paper's arithmetic - rounded absolute values, sum over the detected alterations, Delta-ctDNA % change vs the lowest positive level so far, T0 or nadir), finds the first cPD, computes Tr over the observed draws and runs the branched rules on the post-cPD draws up to the benchmark landmark (no look-ahead: draws after the landmark are never read; the paper's time-to-cEoT prediction cannot be evaluated at a landmark without outcome-time knowledge). It writes as call 1 = the cEoT trigger (a) or (b) has fired by the landmark = treatment judged failing, 0 = continue (the algorithm's no-trigger state, under the rule-(c) fallback until the unobservable PD date), and as risk the Delta-ctDNA at the last draw on or before the landmark - the paper's single per-draw ctDNA response quantity and the quantity the algorithm's cPD branch thresholds at +20% (higher = more ctDNA increase = more likely failing); the paper defines no per-patient severity score (its per-patient outputs are the cEoT timing and the branch, validated as R2 = 0.86/0.85 of time-to-cEoT vs PFS, n = 12/27), the benchmark output has no predicted-time column, and the timing is recorded in the fit report instead. A patient without a baseline draw, without a draw during treatment by the landmark, or with no ctDNA detected at baseline (the paper's ctDNA-negative exclusion) gets no prediction with the reason in note. The rule is fixed (fitted false): no threshold is learned from training outcomes - the 20% cPD cut-off is the paper's default RECIST 1.1 mirror (the 10-50% alternatives changed the cPD assignment only marginally, md:62) and nothing else is fitted; the paper publishes no code, so the wrapper re-implements the stated arithmetic and records every reading of an undefined case (Tref with the all-lost cCR state, Tr ties, the exact post-cPD Tr-drop gating, the analysis-only data-density conditions) in the README.

methods.description: The combined ctDNA + cfDNA early-dynamic four-subgroup rule of Zheng et al. (Thoracic Cancer 2022;13(19):2764-2772, DOI 10.1111/1759-7714.14668; 51 advanced EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients on EGFR-TKIs, Daping Hospital 2016-2021, plasma capture NGS of 168 lung-cancer genes): from the cycle-1 draw (the paper's cycle-1 sample, within 2-4 months of EGFR-TKI start, md:30) plus the baseline, each patient is assigned one of four subgroups by two binary features - ctDNA not detected vs detected at cycle 1 (early clearance = maximum MAF 0; 30/51 vs 21/51, md:99) and cfDNA increased vs decreased from baseline to cycle 1 (20/51 vs 31/51, md:99): group 1 = ctDNA- & cfDNA increased (maximal benefit), group 2 = ctDNA- & cfDNA decreased, group 3 = ctDNA+ & cfDNA increased, group 4 = ctDNA+ & cfDNA decreased (minimal benefit) (md:115); the paper's cohort-level validation contrasts group 1 vs group 4: median PFS 20.2 vs 8.1 months (p < 0.001), median OS 62.3 vs 25.2 months (p = 0.001), ORR 63.6% vs 16.7% (p = 0.036) (md:115). The wrapper takes exactly the paper's two markers (maximum MAF (%) in ctDNA and cfDNA amount (ng/ml); required_markers, id system other, match all - the same pair cox-early-kinetics declares, since the paper's ctDNA amount = maximum MAF x cfDNA amount makes the maximum MAF the rule's ctDNA quantity, md:30), pairs each patient's baseline and cycle-1 draws (last draw on or before baseline_max_day; last draw after it up to the landmark - the corpus fixed-pair convention and the same draws the same paper's cox-early-kinetics wrapper reads), reads the ctDNA detection call from the <marker>__detected companion row of the cycle-1 draw when present (the benchmark's below-detection encoding) else value > 0 (the paper's clear = maximum MAF 0, md:99), takes the cfDNA change sign (increased = cfDNA(cycle 1) >= cfDNA(baseline); an exact zero change is the increase side, the cox-early-kinetics convention - the paper states no equality rule, md:99), and writes risk = the cycle-1 ctDNA-axis value (the maximum MAF in %, 0 = not detected - the quantity the rule's detectability call applies to; higher = more likely failing, the ctDNA+ arm being inferior for PFS/OS/ORR, md:115, and the independent factor of the multivariate Cox for PFS (HR 4.633) and OS (HR 2.434), md:134) and call = 1 iff group 4 (ctDNA+ & cfDNA decreased - the only cell with both features on their unfavorable sides, the paper's minimal-benefit group, md:115), 0 for groups 1-3; the four-group assignment and the training cohort's group counts are reported at fit (run.json). The rule learns nothing from the training outcomes (fitted false): no code or cutoff is published (SPSS 20 / GraphPad 8 / X-Tile, md:45) and the wrapper implements the rule from the Methods/Results text; it writes no probability (the paper's per-group log-rank/chi-squared tests are cohort-level, so TxResBench converts the risk), and a patient without the cycle-1 ctDNA draw or without the baseline or cycle-1 cfDNA draw gets no prediction with the reason in note (the paper's complete-case cohort, md:30).

methods.description: The per-patient 'substantial increase' and 'molecular progression' calls of Frank MS et al. (Cancer Res Commun 2022;2(10):1174-1187; 150 advanced / noncurative locally advanced NSCLC patients, first-line systemic treatment, NCT03512847): plasma ctDNA of one selected cancer-specific mutation per patient (copies per uL by ddPCR, per-draw 95% CI based on Poisson statistics) is monitored at every treatment cycle. Molecular progression = 'an increase in ctDNA at any time during treatment or follow-up' (md:305-306) - any consecutive-draw increase; substantial increase = the Thomsen rule, 'a ctDNA value with no overlap between the 95% CI of the current and immediately preceding measurements' (md:538-540), evaluated over the serial trajectory (the paper's 28 patients qualifying at the first increase plus 21 later rises = 49 (74%) of 66 with a ctDNA increase, and the substantial group had worse PFS/OS: median 106 vs 150 days, HR 0.49, and 283 vs 603 days, HR 0.44). The wrapper takes each patient's consecutive draw pairs up to the benchmark landmark, calls substantial increase when the current draw's 95% CI lies entirely above the immediately preceding draw's 95% CI on an increase pair (no overlap requires a gap; CIs touching count as overlapping - the paper does not state the boundary, '?'), and writes as risk the largest increase ratio a/b over the increase pairs (the paper's fold change (a - b)/b shifted, so 1 = the neutral no-change boundary; higher = more likely failing) and as call 1 = substantial increase (treatment judged failing), 0 otherwise. The per-draw 95% CI is the rule's decision input but the benchmark contract's long frame has no CI slot, so the wrapper consumes per-row ci_lo/ci_hi columns or the <marker>__ci_low / <marker>__ci_high companion feature rows when present and, without them, does not invent a Poisson CI: it evaluates the paper's companion molecular-progression call (any increase) instead, records the mode in the fit record and documents the difference. No probability is written: the paper defines none, TxResBench converts the risk; the paper's KM/log-rank survival comparison is cohort-level validation, not part of the call. The wrapper is a fixed rule (no fitting, no outcomes learned).

methods.description: The DANCER ctDNA clearance call of Zhou et al. (MedComm 2025, DOI 10.1002/mco2.70402: neoadjuvant dalpiciclib plus aromatase inhibitors in 30 operable HER2-negative luminal B breast cancer patients): among the patients with detectable ctDNA ('initially ctDNA-positive', the paper's 19 of 30), the per-draw tumor-informed ctDNA positivity status classifies each patient as clear at or before a deadline - clear <= T1 (negativity at T0+ or T1, without rebound), clear <= T2 (T0+, T1 or T2), clear <= S (T0+, T1, T2 or S) - or nonclear (ctDNA-positive at T2 and/or S; among the 19, 5 nonclear vs 14 clear <= T2 were 100.0% vs 42.8% MR, OR 14.385 p = 0.045, and 80.0% vs 7.1% PEPI >= 4, OR 52 p = 0.006; with the T1 deadline, RCB III 90.9% vs 25.0%, OR 30 p = 0.006). The wrapper takes one marker (the per-draw ctDNA positivity call: the marker's __detected rows when present, else 0/1 values, else the level compared with detection_threshold, default the training median as a documented stand-in for the assay's combined p < 0.01 call, which the benchmark frame does not carry), restricts the call to patients with ctDNA detected in a baseline draw (day <= baseline_max_day) and abstains for the others exactly as the paper does, maps the paper's protocol draws onto the benchmark clock by order (T1 = first on-treatment draw, T2 = second, S = third; the postoperative PO draw is not part of the call definitions and is ignored; when the history has no third on-treatment draw S is absent and the call is read on the draws at hand), writes the four nested groups as risk (0 clear <= T1, 1 clear <= T2, 2 clear <= S, 3 nonclear; higher = worse) and call 1 for the patients not clear by the clearance_deadline (default T2, the paper's headline MR/PEPI analysis; T1 is its RCB analysis; S is the full nested reading). No probability is written. A patient with no baseline draw, no determined baseline status, ctDNA-negative at baseline (outside the cohort), fewer than two on-treatment draws, a missing slot status, or deadline S with no S draw in the history gets no prediction, with the reason in note. The deadline and detection threshold are the rule's only settings; nothing is fitted on the training outcomes.

methods.description: The three-category ctDNA clearance-pattern rule of Bando et al. (Nature Medicine 2026, DOI 10.1038/s41591-026-04428-0; the ALTAIR phase 3 trial, CIRCULATE-Japan GALAXY platform, NCT04457297): among resected stage I-IV colorectal cancer patients who were ctDNA-positive by the tumor-informed Signatera 16-plex PCR-NGS assay after curative-intent surgery plus standard-of-care therapy and had no radiological relapse, the serial per-draw ctDNA status (positive/negative) during and after post-adjuvant FTD/TPI or placebo was classified per patient into no clearance ('remained ctDNA positive at all timepoints up to a DFS event'), sustained clearance ('converted from ctDNA positive to ctDNA negative and remained negative at all subsequent timepoints', with 'at least one negative ctDNA result after treatment completion') or transient clearance (converted then reverted to positive, or converted during treatment with no post-treatment ctDNA assessment); the analysis included patients with at least one ctDNA assessment after starting treatment and before or on the day of a DFS event (235 of 243; the groups had DFS HRs 17.42 and 6.23 vs sustained clearance, P < 0.0001 and 0.0001). The wrapper consumes one marker (the per-draw ctDNA positivity call: the marker's __detected rows when present, else 0/1 values, else the level compared with detection_threshold, default the training median as a documented stand-in for the assay's call 'Plasma samples with two or more SNVs were defined as ctDNA positive', which the benchmark frame does not carry), takes the draws with baseline = 0 (after baseline_max_day, the harness 'during and after treatment' window) up to the landmark, and writes the group as risk (0 sustained clearance, 1 transient clearance, 2 no clearance; higher = worse, the paper's ordering from its DFS HRs) and call 1 for transient and no clearance (the treatment judged failing) and 0 for sustained clearance. It writes no probability (the paper defines none for the call; TxResBench converts the risk). A patient whose baseline (enrolment) ctDNA status is negative or cannot be determined gets no prediction with the reason in note (the ALTAIR population was ctDNA-positive at enrolment by trial design, and the paper's rule as printed has no category for a patient who did not convert from ctDNA-positive), as does a patient with no ctDNA status on any on-treatment draw. The paper's group-level DFS/OS hazard ratios, medians and milestone rates (the Kaplan-Meier/Cox association layer, which the deposited R analysis reproduces over the precomputed group column) are cohort-level validation statistics, not part of the per-patient call; the rule is applied by the wrapper to the draws observed by the landmark rather than retrospectively to the DFS event day (the benchmark's call time), and the per-patient treatment-completion date is not published, so the 'after treatment completion' anchor uses treatment_end_day (default 168 days = six 28-day courses per the protocol), a documented stand-in.

methods.description: The per-patient two-group ctDNA trajectory rule of Qin et al. (Blood Advances 2021, DOI 10.1182/bloodadvances.2020001637; 24 high-risk extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma patients on pegaspargase/gemcitabine-based systemic chemotherapy, prospective plasma cfDNA genotyping with a 112-gene capture panel at enrollment, after every 2-3 cycles, at end of treatment and every 3-month follow-up): FAVORABLE = rapid ctDNA clearance (mutations detected at baseline, no detection of any mutation in cfDNA within 2-4 cycles of chemotherapy) OR consistently undetectable ctDNA (undetectable at baseline and at subsequent monitoring); UNFAVORABLE = persisting detectable ctDNA (baseline detected, still detected during monitoring) OR emerging ctDNA (undetectable at baseline, detected later during therapy and surveillance). Per patient the wrapper takes one marker (the per-draw ctDNA mutation detectability status; the paper's definition is nonquantitative, md:168, so the detection call comes from the <marker>__detected companion row when present, else value > detection_threshold) and classifies the draws up to the benchmark landmark: the baseline state (last draw on or before baseline_max_day) branches the rule - baseline detected: favorable iff a draw within the 2-4-cycle window (day >= cycle_days to day < 4*cycle_days, the paper's window is in cycles and never converted to days, so cycle_days declares it, default 21) is undetectable with no detected draw later; baseline undetectable: favorable iff no monitoring draw is detected (a later detection is the paper's emerging arm, unfavorable). It writes risk = the marker value at the draw that carries the call (0 for the two favorable arms, the benchmark's undetectable encoding; the value at the last in-window draw for persisting detectable; the value at the first detected draw for emerging) - the quantity the per-draw detection call thresholds - and call (1 = unfavorable = treatment judged failing, 0 = favorable); no probability is written, TxResBench converts the risk. Patients the paper's rule leaves open get no prediction with the reason in note: no baseline draw, unknown baseline detection call, no monitoring draw by the landmark, no definite detection call in the 2-4-cycle window for a baseline-detected patient, an incomplete window or monitoring trajectory that blocks verifying the arm, or a detected draw after a within-window clearance (rebound; the paper reports no rebound in its favorable group and does not state a reclassification, md:141).

methods.description: The three-group ctDNA clearance-timing rule of Magbanua et al. (Cancer Cell 2023, DOI 10.1016/j.ccell.2023.04.008; I-SPY 2 ctDNA substudy of 283 HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer patients on neoadjuvant chemotherapy): patients who tested ctDNA-positive at the pretreatment draw (T0) with complete ctDNA data at the first three time points are grouped by the per-draw status triple at T0, T1 (3 weeks after treatment initiation) and T2 (12 weeks, after paclitaxel-based treatment and before AC): early clearance at T1 (ctDNA+/−/−), late clearance at T2 (ctDNA+/+/−) or no clearance at T2 (ctDNA+/+/+). In TNBC the groups had different pCR proportions (Fisher's exact p=0.0002) and early clearance was a significant predictor of pCR (logistic OR 13.06, 95% CI 3.54-57.95) and of RCB-0/I (OR 19.00, 95% CI 4.98-89.06); in HR-positive/HER2-negative there was no significant association (p=0.92). The wrapper consumes one marker (the per-draw ctDNA positivity call: the marker's __detected rows when present, else 0/1 values, else the level compared with detection_threshold, default the training median as a documented stand-in for the assay's call 'at least 2 of the 16 patient-specific variants detected', which the benchmark frame does not carry), reads the first three protocol draws on the benchmark clock (T0 = the last draw on or before baseline_max_day, T1 = the first draw after it, T2 = the next draw; all by the landmark; the paper's T3 draw after NAC is not part of this rule), and writes the group as risk (0 early clearance, 1 late clearance, 2 no clearance; higher = worse, the paper's ordering from its TNBC findings) and call 1 for the two non-early groups (the paper's contrast 'early clearance... compared to those who cleared at T2 or remained positive until T2'; the paper proposes switching therapy for patients who do not clear ctDNA at 3 weeks) and 0 for early clearance. It writes no probability (the paper defines none; TxResBench converts the risk). A patient ctDNA-negative at T0 gets no prediction with the reason in note (the paper's groups are defined only for patients ctDNA-positive at T0), as does a patient without the first three draws or with a status history fitting no group (e.g. ctDNA+/−/+); the paper's group-level Fisher's exact p-values and logistic-regression ORs are cohort-level validation statistics, not part of the per-patient call, and the paper runs them per subtype (the call itself is subtype-independent; the benchmark passes one marker).

methods.description: The confirmed >=50% ctDNA response rule of Goldberg et al. (Clin Cancer Res 2018;24(15):3796-3803; DOI 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-17-1341; 28 metastatic NSCLC patients on anti-PD-1/anti-PD-L1 immunotherapy): a ctDNA response is a drop in the allele fraction (AF) of the single tracked tumor-derived mutation (the one with the highest AF at baseline) to below 50% of the baseline value with a second successive confirmatory measurement; every patient starts as a non-responder, and a responder whose subsequent measurements are above the 50% threshold with a second consecutive confirmatory value is re-classified as a non-responder. The wrapper takes the tracked mutation's AF as its one marker, requires a detectable baseline (the paper's analysis set is the 28 of 49 patients with a mutation in baseline plasma), and writes the deepest percent change from baseline among the on-treatment draws by the landmark as risk and the paper's status at the landmark as the call (1 = not a confirmed ctDNA responder, treatment judged failing); it writes no probability. Differences from the paper: the benchmark has no off-treatment date, so the paper's exclusion of draws >2 weeks after it becomes the landmark truncation; a value exactly at 50% of baseline is counted in neither the entry nor the exit condition (the paper's '<50%' and 'at least 50%' wordings conflict at the boundary); an undetectable on-treatment value is a full drop (the paper's magnitude analysis reports it as -100%); a confirmed drop after a re-classification re-enters the responder state (the paper does not state the re-entry case).

methods.description: The cfDNA-defined progression rule of Ahlborn et al. (Oncotarget 2018;9(66):32570-32579, DOI 10.18632/oncotarget.25948): 16 RECIST 1.1-evaluable patients with BRAF V600E-mutated non-melanoma solid tumours (colorectal, bile duct, lung, pancreatic) on BRAFi combination therapy in the CoPPO program (NCT02290522), serial plasma cfBRAFV600E mutant allele fraction (AF) by QX200 ddPCR every four weeks from baseline (within 24 h before treatment start) until progression, 124 samples (mean 7.75 per patient). 'An increase in cfBRAFV600E AF was recorded if the AF increased from non-detectable to detectable levels (AF >= 0.001) or increased in two consecutive samples unless it was the last plasma sample collected prior to termination of treatment due to clinical progression' (md:474-479); 'we defined progression as the time point when an increase in cfDNA was observed' (md:189-193) - per patient the first draw at which an increase is recorded - and the increases preceded RECIST 1.1 progression (CT every 8 weeks) in 11 of 16 cases (median 5 weeks, range 2-17). The wrapper scans the patient's serial draws up to the benchmark landmark (nothing is fitted: the 0.001 detection limit and the two-samples condition are the paper's, the rule learns nothing from the training outcomes; `fitted` false, `uses_history` landmark) and writes call 1 = an increase recorded = cfDNA-defined progression = treatment judged failing, and risk = the strongest observed consecutive-sample rise signal (the quantity the rule thresholds; no probability is defined by the paper, TxResBench converts the risk). Every paper-open point is declared rather than guessed: 'increased in two consecutive samples' is read as the confirmed increase - rises at two successive sample pairs, `min_rising_pairs` 2 (the single-pair reading is `min_rising_pairs` 1); the terminal-sample exclusion is not applied at the landmark (`terminal_exclusion` 'off') because the benchmark gives no treatment-termination information (`last_draw` restores the structural analog, the last observed draw as the terminal sample); detectability comes from <marker>__detected rows when present else value > `detection_threshold` 0.001 (the paper's AF-fraction detection limit; datasets in percent units must supply __detected rows or set the threshold); a rise from an ND/zero draw is measured against the patient's smallest positive AF and an all-ND trajectory gets risk 0 with call 0 (the paper lists such patients - Pt 2, 3, 12 - among the no-recorded-increase group, not as excluded); equality is not an increase (the paper's unchanged-AF patient Pt14 was not counted; `rise_boundary` 'greater_equal' relaxes it); the trajectory starts at the last baseline draw (day <= baseline_max_day) then the on-treatment draws in day order, and consecutive means adjacent in day order. The rule is DEFINED for the single tracked mutation (BRAF V600E AF, `required_markers`); the same paper's >= 50% reduction survival rule, the baseline AF >= 0.05 stratification, the tumour-burden/CA19-9 correlations and the WES resistance analyses are separate methods, not this rule; the paper's lead time needs the RECIST progression date (post-call information) and is not emitted (run.json reports the wrapper's own train counts).

methods.description: The confirmed twofold ctDNA increase rule of Demuth et al. (Oncotarget 2018;9(52):30064-30073; DOI 10.18632/oncotarget.25779; 40 EGFR/ALK wild-type NSCLC patients on palliative erlotinib, targeted NGS on the pre-treatment plasma and per-mutation ddPCR on the serial monthly samples): an increase in ctDNA concentration was defined as a twofold or higher percentage increase compared to baseline, and the twofold increase had to be confirmed in a second successive sample; a patient with such a maintained twofold increase was predicted to have non-response (radiological progression) on the following imaging (10 of the 12 confirmed patients, 83%, progressed on the following imaging). The wrapper takes every marker passed as one tracked mutation's ctDNA concentration (a per-mutation ddPCR quantity, fractional abundance % or copies/mL; one quantity kind per mutation), computes the baseline-relative percent change of each tracked mutation against its own baseline draw, and combines them at the patient level the way the paper combines mutation increases elsewhere ('for at least one mutation', md:133): risk = the strongest per-mutation increase among the on-treatment draws by the landmark (the quantity the rule thresholds; >= 100% = twofold), call = 1 when a twofold-or-higher increase is confirmed in two successive on-treatment samples of any tracked mutation (predicted non-response; the paper's one-sided call with no re-classification), 0 otherwise; the total-concentration reading (the patient's ctDNA concentration as the sum of the tracked mutations, each draw against its own baseline reference) is exposed as mutation_combination 'total'. A patient with no baseline draw, no mutation detected at baseline (the paper's monitorable set: at least one alteration detected in the baseline sample, 21 of 36 sequenced patients), or no on-treatment draw gets no prediction. The wrapper writes no probability. Differences from the paper, all declared: the per-mutation aggregation to the patient concentration (unstated; 'strongest'/'at least one mutation' default, 'total' exposed), the confirmatory condition of the second sample (unstated; read naturally as itself at or above the twofold threshold at the next drawn sample), which ddPCR quantity is 'concentration' (left to the markers the caller passes), and the benchmark's landmark frame replaces the paper's monitoring until progression.

methods.description: The molecular-progression detection rule of Provencio et al. (Oncotarget 2018;9(1):488-494; DOI 10.18632/oncotarget.22470; 41 stage IIIB-IV activating-EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients on EGFR-TKI treatment, 251 serial plasma samples, median follow-up 10 months, drawn at diagnosis, then every 3 weeks for the first 3 months and every 12 weeks thereafter, md:26, md:117; cfDNA from 1 ml plasma by Maxwell RSC and array-based digital PCR with Rare Mutation Assays on the QuantStudio 3D Digital PCR System, md:124). The paper's rule (md:74): molecular progression = an elevation in the quantification of the original sensitizing EGFR mutation OR the appearance of the p.T790M resistance mutation (MAF > the assay's 0.08% LOD, md:94, md:124; never detected at baseline, md:33) in two or more consecutive serial samples with the last sample being obtained at the time of progression, evaluated against radiological PD per RECIST v1.1 on the 29-patient/70-serial-time-point subset that also carried CTC counts: sensitivity 94.4% (95% CI 73-100), specificity 72.7% (39-94), PLR 3.5 (1.31-9.15), NLR 0.1 (0.01-0.53), ahead of the CTC <5 vs >=5 cut-off (44.4%/63.6%, PLR 1.2, NLR 0.9, P = 0.021) (md:74, Table 3, md:81-86). The wrapper scans the patient's serial draws up to the benchmark landmark (nothing is fitted - the rule learns nothing from the training outcomes, `fitted` false) and evaluates the two arms with the two-consecutive confirmation; `call` 1 = molecular progression detected = treatment judged failing. The paper defines NO numeric magnitude for the 'elevation' arm (the spec records it as '?'; the only numeric thresholds in the paper are the per-assay LOD/LOQ, md:94, which are assay sensitivity limits, not the elevation rule), so the wrapper declares its reading rather than guessing: `elevation_reference` 'previous' (default - each draw against the immediately preceding sample, the paper's own binary 'increase vs unchanging or decreasing', md:9, md:39; 'baseline' and 'nadir' alternatives) with `elevation_ratio` 1.0 (any increase) and `elevation_boundary` 'greater' (a strict increase - 'increase' vs 'unchanging', md:39); the two-consecutive condition is read as attaching to BOTH arms (the extraction's reading, min_draws_required 2); the alternative parse - the condition only on the T790M appearance arm - is exposed by setting `elevation_min_consecutive` to 1 (the two arm-specific switches `elevation_min_consecutive` / `appearance_min_consecutive` default to 2, the paper's 'two or more consecutive samples', documented in the README); the last-sample-at-progression anchor is read in the benchmark's landmark frame as the run ending at the last draw observed at/before the landmark (`window_end` 'current', the current-assessment analog of the paper's PD-concurrent draw; the paper's own trajectories are outcome-contingent by design, and the wrapper's scan ends at the landmark, `uses_history` 'landmark'). risk = the strongest observed consecutive-sample rise ratio of the sensitizing mutation quantification (the quantity the elevation arm thresholds, per the contract's rule-writing convention; the T790M appearance arm is a detection state on a different scale and contributes to the call only, as the two arms live on different scales - the combined-ctdna-resistance-criteria precedent); no probability is written (TxResBench converts the risk). A patient with fewer than two serial samples, or with no quantification of the sensitizing mutation, gets no prediction (empty risk, reason in note). The paper's Table 1 per-patient anytime counts (18/26 vs 1/15 p.T790M, 24/26 vs 5/15 increase, md:42-48), the 51-day p.T790M lead time (md:51) and the Cox time-dependent-covariate analyses (Table 2, md:58-68) are separate analyses and not this rule.

methods.description: The BRAF V600mut ctDNA increase rule of Schreuer et al. (J Transl Med 2016;14:95; 36 advanced BRAF V600 mutant melanoma patients on dabrafenib/trametinib; the pair 'BRAF V600mut ctDNA copy number' and 'BRAF V600mut ctDNA fraction' by allele-specific qPCR on the Idylla ctBRAF prototype assay, 1 mL plasma). Per patient, from the serial draws up to the landmark: an increase of the copy number and fraction was diagnosed (call 1 = the paper's PD-identified-by-ctDNA call; in the paper 19/27 PD patients, 0/9 ongoing-response patients, sensitivity 70%, specificity 100%, Kappa 0.54), with the operative reference 'the first increase in the fraction, after the fraction became undetectable or was decreasing' (md:136). The wrapper reads the paper's unquantified pieces literally and records each: an increase is any strict rise of the drawn value over the previous draw (min_rise_ratio exposes a relative floor, null by default; a rise from an undetectable draw counts); the reference state is the earliest undetectable or strictly falling draw (the 'was decreasing' magnitude is unstated); a trajectory that never becomes undetectable and never falls anchors at its start (the paper's cohort always fell first, so the case is unillustrated there); the call needs both quantities to rise (require_both, the 'copy number and fraction' sentence), false = either quantity's first rise (the 'or' of md:136). It writes risk = the strongest upward movement of the fraction over the post-reference window (max consecutive draw ratio v_j/v_{j-1}, a rise from an undetectable draw measured against the patient's smallest positive fraction value; the paper's unit-free boundary 'the fraction rose' is the ratio > 1, so higher = a stronger rise = the treatment more likely failing) and the 0/1 call; no probability (TxResBench converts the risk); no call when the fraction trajectory has fewer than two drawn values by the landmark, or when the copy-number trajectory is missing or single-drawn under require_both (then it abstains with the reason in note). Undetectable is the harness encoding (value 0 with a <marker>__detected row of 0, else value above detection_threshold); the paper's 0.01% / 3 mutant copies (md:81) is its analytical sensitivity, not stated to be the report cutoff.
