methods.description: Per-patient binary risk call for detecting disease progression (PD per RECIST v1.1) of the combined ctDNA-dynamics + CTC Ki67-index combinatorial rule of Kakouri AC et al., Transl Lung Cancer Res 2025;14(6):1945-1960 (DOI 10.21037/tlcr-2024-1095; prospective SWIPE trial NCT02705820, 46 analysed metastatic NSCLC patients on pembrolizumab switch maintenance). The paper's call (md:135, md:140): risk-positive = a high-iKi67 (>30% Ki67+ CTCs, iKi67 = percentage of Ki67+ CTCs over the total CTC number per patient, md:130) at the assessed timepoint AND/OR unfavourable ctDNA dynamics - an increase or a decrease of less than 50% of the per-sample maximum VAF (%) from baseline to an early phase of treatment (the negation of ctDNA-MR = '>50% decrease or clearance', md:117; the 50% cut-off is borrowed from refs 14/46 = Goldberg 2018 / Thompson 2021, md:157, and the 30% cut-off from ref 21 = Spiliotaki 2023, md:130). The wrapper reads exactly two markers (the per-draw max ctDNA VAF and the per-draw CTC Ki67-index, declared as required_markers), makes the call at the benchmark landmark capped at the paper's t2 (6-week) assessment (draws after it - t3, 9 weeks - never enter; the paper's assessed timepoints are t0 baseline / t1 3 weeks / t2 6 weeks, md:61, and the t0 call of the paper pairs the baseline iKi67 with the early-phase ctDNA change, which a benchmark on-treatment call does not reproduce), writes risk = the minimum on-treatment/baseline ratio of the max ctDNA VAF across the early-phase draws (the quantity the >50%-decrease rule thresholds; higher = less decrease/increase = more likely failing; it is the paper's ctDNA-dynamics scale, and the iKi67 arm enters the call only - the paper defines no per-patient scalar) and call = 1 for marker-positive (high-iKi67 and/or unfavourable ctDNA dynamics). A patient without a baseline ctDNA mutation (no baseline max VAF: 25/43 patients had mutations at any timepoint, md:110) gets an empty risk and no call with the reason in note - the paper does not state how such a patient enters the ctDNA arm ('?', spec new_patient_prediction fallback (a)); an unevaluable CTC arm counts as not firing (the ctDNA arm decides, noted), and an unevaluable ctDNA arm (no baseline mutation, or no NGS-evaluated on-treatment draw) makes the patient abstain. No probability is defined by the paper, so none is written and TxResBench converts the risk; the paper's sensitivity/specificity against RECIST v1.1 PD (88.2%/30.4% FPR at t0, 70%/11.1% at t2, md:140) and the KM/multivariate Cox associations (md:135) are cohort-level validation of the call groups, not part of the per-patient call. The paper publishes no analysis code; the wrapper implements the rule from the paper text, its data tables and the supplementary methodology.

The required ids are the biological entities/quantities: for id_system 'other' the unit's feature must be keyed exactly as 'ctDNA_maxVAF' (the per-sample maximum VAF, not a per-variant series), and the P46013 marker must carry the CTC Ki67-index, not a Ki67/PD-L1 readout of another specimen.

methods.description: The ctDNA kinetic-pattern rule of Sanz-Garcia et al. (Clin Cancer Res 2026, DOI 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-25-3541; IO-KIN, NCT04606940; 15 evaluable recurrent/metastatic HNSCC patients on pembrolizumab or nivolumab monotherapy; plasma ctDNA by the tumor-informed Signatera assay, mean tumor molecules (MTM) per mL of plasma). Per patient it makes a binary call on the serial plasma ctDNA concentration: downDelta-ctDNA = a persistent decrease from day 8 onward compared with the baseline (pretreatment) value - a continuous decline with no increases at any later time point (md:46, md:124); upDelta-ctDNA = stability or an increase from day 8 onward compared with the baseline value (md:46). The rule is direction-only (no numeric threshold anywhere: any decrease counts; the distinguishing condition is the absence of any increase at any later time point), and the day-2/3 draws are not part of it ('There was no clear pattern in ctDNA kinetics on day 2 or 3', md:124). The wrapper writes risk = the strongest observed change relative to baseline over the draws from pattern_start_day (8) on up to the benchmark landmark, max((v - baseline)/baseline) - the quantity the rule's direction boundary (increase/stability vs decrease) thresholds at 0 - and call 1 for upDelta-ctDNA (treatment judged failing) and 0 for downDelta-ctDNA; no probability exists in the paper and none is written (TxResBench converts the risk). The paper's validation statistics (per-class median PFS 511 vs 77 days, P = 0.006, and OS 855 vs 442 days, P = 0.084; Cox HRs; Fisher's exact P) need the outcomes and are not part of the per-patient call; its secondary per-timepoint analysis ('any decrease at day n vs baseline' for n = 2, 3, 8, 15, 22, 29, md:129) is reproduced from the draws alone and recorded in the fit record. Points the paper leaves open, with the wrapper's declared readings (README has the quotes and reasons): the day-8 draw itself is included ('from day 8 onward', md:46, vs the Fig. 2 caption's 'beyond day 8'); a value exactly equal to the baseline is 'stability' - upDelta-ctDNA (no tolerance is stated, so strict equality); a non-detected on-treatment draw (contract encoding value 0 with <marker>__detected 0) counts as below baseline (a decrease toward the limit of detection - the paper does not state the handling, md:122); a baseline draw that is not detected has no reference value, so the patient gets an empty risk and a note (all 15 patients get a class in the paper's Fig. 2A but its handling of the two baseline-undetectable patients is never stated, md:122; its per-timepoint analyses use the baseline-detectable subset, N = 13, md:129); a missing day-8-onward draw does not contribute - the call is made from the available day-8-onward draws - and the wrapper abstains when there is no draw from day 8 onward; the baseline reference is the last draw on or before baseline_max_day ('baseline (same or prior day to first dose)', md:31 - one baseline draw is described); the paper's '>= 5 plasma time points' evaluability rule (md:83) is its cohort-inclusion criterion, not a computability requirement (the wrapper needs the baseline and at least one day-8-onward draw, min_draws = 2).

methods.description: The depth of ctDNA response as a diagnostic test for RECIST response (Anagnostou et al., Nat Med 2023, CCTG BR.36 stage 1, pembrolizumab): the fractional change of the per-sample ctDNA marker (maxMAF, or mean/median MAF of tumor-derived plasma mutations, in %) from the pre-treatment draw (C1D1) to one fixed on-therapy draw - C3D1 by default, the paper's optimal evaluation timepoint, C2D1 as the alternative - d = (maxMAF_C1 - maxMAF_Cx)/maxMAF_C1, with negative values meaning an increase in ctDNA. The paper evaluates d as a receiver operating characteristic curve against the binary 12-week RECIST response (CR/PR responder vs SD/PD non-responder) and reports AUCs of 0.77/0.81 for maxMAF at C2D1/C3D1 (pROC 1.16.2, R 3.6.1), and defines no operating cutoff, no per-patient probability and no call; this wrapper therefore writes the failure-directed score risk = -d = (Cx - C1D1)/C1D1 (higher = increase = treatment more likely failing) as risk and no call and no probability of its own (TxResBench converts). A baseline of 0 (undetectable ctDNA) makes the ratio undefined; the paper imputes the smallest d observed at that timepoint in the cohort - the greatest increase - so the wrapper imputes the training cohort's largest risk, saved with the model. It needs the baseline draw and one draw in the timepoint window; a patient without them gets no prediction, with the reason in note.

methods.description: Durable molecular clearance (ctDNA-dmCR) of Garralda et al. (Clin Cancer Res 2026;32:333-49, DOI 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-25-2312): per patient, the ctDNA detection status of every draw up to the benchmark landmark (the assay's per-draw call, consumed from the marker's <marker>__detected rows or the level against a detection threshold) is read in day order; a patient is mCR+ when at least one draw is undetected ('Molecular clearance (ctDNA-mCR): at least one timepoint with undetected ctDNA during the course of treatment'), and dmCR+ when the undetected state is observed without an intervening detected draw for at least 180 consecutive days ('durable mCR (ctDNA-dmCR), was defined as ctDNA-mCR for at least 180 consecutive days'; the longest all-undetected run spans >= 180 days, so a single undetected draw is mCR+ but never dmCR+; 180 days = the DCB duration). The wrapper writes the paper's own nested clearance group as risk (0 dmCR+, 1 mCR+ not durable, 2 never undetected; higher = worse per the paper's group ordering: dmCR+ 100% survived, mCR+ PFS HR 3.52 and OS HR 6.77 relative to mCR-), call 1 = dmCR- (did not attain durable clearance; the paper's poorer-outcome group) and no probability - TxResBench converts the risk. Differences from the paper: the published text says 'consecutive days' and the released notebook instead computes the span from the first undetected draw to any later undetected draw without checking the draws in between; the wrapper implements the published consecutive-days reading (recorded), and the benchmark evaluates the rule up to its landmark (draws after the landmark are not used) while the paper evaluated the whole course retrospectively (recorded; at an early landmark the 180-day span is unobservable and all patients are dmCR-). At fit nothing is learned: the detection-call fallback threshold is resolved from the training draws (a documented stand-in for the assay's one-tailed Poisson P < 0.001 call, median LOD 1.9 PPM, which the benchmark frame does not carry) and the training-cohort group counts are reported; the paper's published association (mCR+ n = 14 text / 16 Table 1 of 202; dmCR+ n = 8 text / 9 Table 1; PFS and OS log-rank P = 4.61 x 10^-5, OS P = 3.03 x 10^-6, 100% of dmCR+ survived) is recorded for reference.

(Mol Cancer 2022;21:117, DOI 10.1186/s12943-022-01590-0; 47 CRT/RT-treated inoperable localized NSCLC patients of the discovery cohort, serial plasma targeted NGS of 474 cancer-related genes): from the per-draw ctDNA detection status and ctDNA level, Group 0 = undetectable ctDNA in all tested samples, Group 1 = detectable at baseline and undetectable at the last follow-up before PD, Group 2 = decreased but detectable at the last follow-up, Group 3 = increased at the last follow-up compared with baseline; 'patients in Group 0 and Group 1 had better PFS and OS than those in Group 2 and 3' (KM curves, log-rank; PFS log-rank P = 0.0002 - cohort-level validation, not part of the call). Differences from the paper: the anchor is the landmark's last draw rather than the retrospective pre-PD draw; the per-draw detection call is the benchmark's (the paper's in-house threshold is not published); the decrease/increase direction is the raw level comparison (no numeric criterion is published), an unchanged detectable level is grouped with Group 2 (Group 3 is defined by an increase); a patient undetectable at both the baseline and the last follow-up but detectable in between fits no group and gets no prediction with the reason in note.

methods.description: The plasma molecular progression rule of Passiglia et al. (Cancer 2025;131(11):e35917, DOI 10.1002/cncr.35917; PMID 40184734; 32 advanced KRAS p.G12C-mutant NSCLC patients on sotorasib 960 mg once daily within the Italian Expanded Access Program, prospective PROMOLE translational research; serial plasma at baseline (day 1, cycle 1), cycle 3 (56 +/- 10 days later) and each radiologic assessment thereafter (every 3 months), two to eight collecting points per patient, md:33; the KRAS exon 2 p.G12C variant allele fraction (VAF, %) per draw by an ultra-deep customized NGS assay (SiRe panel, 568 clinically relevant hotspot mutations in seven predictive biomarkers: EGFR, KRAS, NRAS, c-KIT, BRAF, PIK3CA, PDGFRA) on the Genexus platform; variants with 500X allele coverage and quality score X20 within an amplicon coverage of at least 2000X alleles; only mutations with VAF >= 0.2% recorded; visual inspection by GenomeBrowse 2.0.7; batch-1/2 discordance resolved by the mean, md:33, md:97). Among the 28 patients with RECIST 1.1 progression at data analysis (CT at baseline, week 12, then every 12 weeks, md:26), the 24 with a valid plasma sample collected within 3 months before radiologic evidence of disease progression were evaluable for the molecular resistance analysis (md:172): a dynamic increase of the KRAS G12C median VAF was detected in 16 of 24 patients (67%; five had undetectable mutations at baseline), with a median interval of 32 days (range, 24-40 days) between the detection of plasma molecular progression and radiologic evidence of disease progression (md:172); the abstract and Discussion report the same finding as 70% of evaluable patients (md:9, md:191) - a 67% vs 70% discrepancy, recorded verbatim. The wrapper scans the patient's serial draws up to the benchmark landmark (nothing is fitted: the rule learns nothing from the training outcomes, fitted false; uses_history landmark) and writes call 1 = a dynamic increase detected = plasma molecular progression = treatment judged failing, and risk = the observed rise ratio value/reference at the detection point (the quantity the rule thresholds; the paper defines no probability, TxResBench converts the risk). The paper NEVER QUANTIFIES the rule and publishes no analysis code: no increase cutoff (the only numeric VAF threshold is the assay's 0.2% recording cutoff, md:33/md:97, a variant-calling limit, not the increase), no reference (baseline vs nadir vs earlier draws), no earliest/sustained semantics, no definition of 'median VAF' (the spec records each as '?'), and the call is anchored at the resistance time point (a valid sample within 3 months before radiologic progression, md:172; Methods say within 30 days, md:33 - a Methods/Results discrepancy). Every open point is declared and exposed as a method_params switch (README.md): quantity = the per-draw VAF with same-day rows reconciled by the mean (md:33's batch rule; 'median VAF' is read as the paper's name for the per-time-point VAF level and the wrapper does NOT collapse the trajectory to a per-patient median, where a 'dynamic increase' would be undefined); undetectable = VAF < 0.2% = level 0 (increase_reference 'previous' default: the immediately preceding draw - the serial-monitoring reading of 'dynamic'; 'baseline' and 'nadir' exposed; increase_ratio 1.0 with boundary 'greater' - any increase, the paper's unquantified 'increase'; increase_at 'end' default: the increase is assessed at the last draw at/before the landmark, the resistance-time-point analog, with 'anywhere' exposing the anytime reading; non_detect 'zero' default: an undetectable -> detectable transition IS an increase - five of the 16 detected increases had undetectable baseline, md:172/md:193, and 0 -> 0 is unchanged; 'skip' drops undetectable draws). No confirmation requirement exists (the paper states no run condition; this is NOT the two-consecutive-samples structure of ctdna-consecutive-elevation-progression, a different paper) and there is no baseline-detectability requirement (md:172, md:193), unlike the paper's separate clearance call (recorded as its own method). A patient with fewer than two serial VAF draws by the landmark (the paper's eligibility: baseline + resistance sample, md:33; spec min_draws_required 2) gets no prediction (empty risk, reason in note). The paper's reported lead time (median 32 days, md:172) needs the radiologic progression date - post-call information - and is not emitted.

methods.description: Per-treatment-line ctDNA dynamics classification of Mehta et al. (Cancer 2026, DOI 10.1002/cncr.70242; 200 recurrent/metastatic gastroesophageal-cancer patients, 584 systemic-therapy lines, 62 analysable lines from 52 patients): from the binary ctDNA status at the line's first ctDNA timepoint (the closest to treatment initiation, up to 90 days before) and at the first on-treatment timepoint (at least 4 weeks after initiation, Figure 1C: 27 days), four dynamics categories - Neg-Neg (remained serially negative; 6/6 treatment benefit), Neg-Pos (initially negative, later positive; 2/2 progressed), Pos-Pos (remained persistently positive; 27/40 vs 13/40 benefit/progression), Pos-Neg (clearance; 12/14 benefit) - and within Pos-Pos a >90% decrease in the ctDNA level (MTM/mL) at the first on-treatment timepoint vs the first timepoint (HR 3.9, 95% CI 1.13-13.5, p =.032 vs a <90% decrease or any increase), then a favourable vs unfavourable group: favourable = Neg-Neg, Pos-Neg and Pos-Pos with a >90% decrease (better PFS, HR 5.5, 95% CI 2.28-13.47, p <.0001 vs unfavourable); unfavourable = Neg-Pos and Pos-Pos with a <90% decrease or an increase; the categories correlate with the imaging-based treatment-benefit call (RECIST NED/PR/SD/CR = benefit vs PD = progression, md:42) and PFS (KM, log-rank, Cox HRs; R survival 3.7-0, md:47 - cohort-level validation, not part of the call). The wrapper takes one marker (the per-draw ctDNA level; the per-draw positivity call follows the benchmark's below-detection convention: <marker>__detected rows when present, else <marker>__lod, else a 0/1 status marker, else value 0 = not detected, else every positive level is detectable with a recorded warning - the paper's positivity call is the commercial assay's own ('at least two tumor-specific variants detected', md:37) and no numeric cutoff is printed; detection_threshold overrides), and writes risk = the 5-level cell code (0 Neg-Neg, 1 Pos-Neg, 2 Pos-Pos >90% decrease, 3 Pos-Pos <90% decrease or increase, 4 Neg-Pos; higher = worse - the paper's HR ordering: Pos-Neg similar to Neg-Neg p =.701, Pos-Pos HR 6.3 vs Neg-Neg, Neg-Pos HR 8.5) and call = 1 for the unfavourable group (treatment judged failing), 0 for the favourable group; no probability is written (the paper defines none, TxResBench converts the risk). Differences from the paper: the benchmark clock carries no per-line protocol days, so the first timepoint is the last draw on or before baseline_max_day (closest to treatment initiation) and the first on-treatment timepoint is the first draw at or after first_on_treatment_min_day (28 days = the paper's 'at least 4 weeks'; its Figure-1C '27 days' is kept as printed, boundary not reconciled) at or before the landmark; the exact percent-change formula is not printed, so >90% decrease is implemented as v1 < (1 - decrease_cutoff_pct/100) * v0 on the MTM/mL values with the >90% wording winning at the boundary (an exactly-90% decrease is on the unfavourable side); the 90% cutoff is borrowed from ref 25, absent from the provided text; a line without both ctDNA timepoints gets no prediction (the paper excludes such lines, 522 of 584); the per-line unit is the paper's own (62 lines from 52 patients), so a patient with several treatment lines must be carried as separate benchmark rows with per-line day origins.

methods.description: The three-class ctDNA dynamic profile rule of Bratman, Yang et al. (Nature Cancer 2020, INSPIRE, pembrolizumab): from the serial absolute ctDNA level (mean tumor molecules per ml plasma, MTM/ml) the patient is 'clearance' when ctDNA was zero at any on-treatment time point, 'below baseline' when without clearance all on-treatment values stayed below the baseline value, and 'above baseline' when without clearance any on-treatment value rose above the baseline value. methods.description: The 6-month ctDNA-emergence response call of Watanabe et al. (PLoS ONE 2019;14(12):e0227366, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0227366; 26 chemotherapy-naive pancreatic-ductal-adenocarcinoma patients on first-line chemotherapy): patients in whom plasma KRAS-mutated ctDNA (one targeted KRAS point mutation per patient, determined in the matched tumour tissue and monitored in blood by ddPCR, detected at the per-sample 'two or more positive droplets' threshold) was DETECTED within 6 months of chemotherapy are called emergence-positive (therapeutic-response failure: median PFS 4.8 vs 14.9 months for the favorable group, log-rank P<0.001; RECIST response-within-6-months association P<0.001 by Fisher's exact test); patients in whom it was NOT DETECTED or DISAPPEARED within 6 months of chemotherapy are called emergence-negative (favorable). The wrapper implements the paper's two-group definition on the last in-window draw (the spec's disappearance-revocation reading: a patient detected and then undetectable within the window reverts to the favorable group - the paper's example of a patient whose KRAS-mutated ctDNA 'decreased and disappeared after chemotherapy' with complete radiological response): the per-draw detection call comes from the dataset's <marker>__detected rows when present (the paper's >=2-positive-droplet assay call is made by the ddPCR layer, not recomputed), else from binary 0/1 values, else from the level against detection_threshold (default the training median as a documented stand-in for the unreported numeric droplet limit). The window is 6 months from the first dose (6 x 365.25/12 = 182.625 days, the package's month conversion), truncated at the benchmark landmark (recorded in run.json); draws after the window cut never affect the call; a patient with no in-window draw, or with an unassayable last in-window draw, gets no prediction with the reason in note. The wrapper writes the group as risk (0 emergence-negative, 1 emergence-positive; higher = worse - the paper's group that had worse PFS) and call (1 = emergence-positive = treatment judged failing, 0 = emergence-negative), and no probability (the paper defines none; TxResBench converts the risk). The paper's PFS log-rank and RECIST Fisher's-exact comparisons are cohort-level validation statistics, not part of the per-patient call, and the paper's survival-clinical validation endpoints run on a different clock (PFS from pathological diagnosis) - recorded in run.json and README.md. The rule is prespecified (fitted false): nothing is learned from the training outcomes; only the detection-threshold stand-in is derived from the training marker levels (never from outcomes).

methods.description: The per-patient favorable vs unfavorable ctDNA profile rule of Lee et al. (JAMA Oncology 2018; melanoma, anti-PD-1 +/- ipilimumab): favorable = (1) undetectable ctDNA at baseline that remained undetectable, or (2) detectable ctDNA at baseline that became undetectable or decreased by at least 10-fold during treatment; unfavorable = detectable ctDNA at baseline that remained stable or increased. The wrapper evaluates the serial plasma ctDNA (one marker, copies per mL of the patient's BRAF/NRAS mutation) from baseline to the benchmark landmark, capped at the paper's 12-week window; any draw can qualify and the first qualifying transition fixes the profile (a later rebound does not reclassify, the paper's Patient 1). It writes risk = the smallest on-treatment/baseline ratio over the window (0 for an undetectable draw, and 0 for the baseline-undetectable arm), the quantity the rule thresholds (a >=10-fold decrease is a ratio <= 0.1), and the 0/1 call (1 = unfavorable profile = treatment judged failing); no probability is written, TxResBench converts the risk. A patient whose trajectory the paper's two arms do not cover (baseline undetectable that became detectable; unknown baseline state; no usable draw) gets no prediction, with the reason in note; the paper's ddPCR detection limit (eMethods 3, not retrievable) is read from the benchmark's undetectable encoding (value 0 with a <marker>__detected row of 0, else value above detection_threshold).

methods.description: The ctDNA-based progression-detection rule of Zhang et al. (Clin Transl Med 2020;10:e254; DOI 10.1002/ctm2.254; 40 unresectable/metastatic gastric cancer patients on HER2-targeted therapy - trastuzumab + chemotherapy, JACOB, ADCs, HER2 inhibitors - with 327 plasma specimens from pretreatment baseline to disease progression, collected every two treatment cycles; cfDNA sequenced with a 425-gene targeted panel, mutations by Trimmomatic/BWA-mem/GATK/VarScan2 and CNVs by ADTEx, denoised against a WBC database and healthy-plasma background; md:28, md:40, md:45). The paper's rule (md:94): each draw's three genomic features - ERBB2 copy number, total copy number load (TCL) and tumor mutation burden (TMB) - are normalized to relative fold changes against their own cutoffs (1.4-fold amplification, TCL high >= 2, TMB high >= 8.5 mutations/Mb, md:47); if a feature is elevated beyond its cutoff for at least two time points, the patient has ctDNA-based PD, and the first of those points is the ctDNA-based PD date. The wrapper evaluates the rule on the draws up to the benchmark landmark (the paper ran it to the progression reference) and writes as risk the strongest cutoff-relative elevation signal (the maximum over the three features of the feature's k-th largest fold change, k = min_elevated_points = 2) and as call the paper's 0/1 ctDNA-based PD decision (1 = treatment judged failing). Nothing is fitted: the cutoffs and the >= 2-time-point condition are the paper's (md:47, md:94), so the wrapper never reads the training outcomes. The paper's reported result (30 patients with CT-determined progression and >= 3 plasma specimens): ctDNA-based PD ahead of CT-based PD in 12/30 (40%) with an average advancement of 38.4 days (md:94), versus 4/30 (13.3%) and 10.0 days for the CEA comparator (md:99 - not part of this rule). The wrapper's declared readings of the paper's open points, each with a method_params switch and the argument in README.md: the qualifying points are the on-treatment draws (include_baseline false - with the baseline counted, the paper's reported advancement is impossible, since the cohort's features 'recovered to the similar levels as BL at PD', md:82); the two points are of the same feature (elevated_points_same_feature true), need not be consecutive (require_consecutive false), and 'elevated beyond' is fold >= 1 (elevation_boundary greater_equal, matching the paper's explicit '>=8.5' / '>=2' high definitions, md:47); the 0.65-fold ERBB2 deletion cutoff does not participate (the rule's 'elevated' is the amplification branch; the paper states no deletion branch). The wrapper declares no probability (the paper defines none; TxResBench converts the risk) and does not emit the advancement in days, which needs the CT-based PD date - post-call information at the landmark; the fit record reports the training first-PD-day median instead.

methods.description: The per-patient two-class ctDNA response-pattern rule of Moding et al. (Nature Cancer 2020; consolidation immune checkpoint inhibition after definitive chemoradiation in unresectable stage IIB-IIIB NSCLC): from the ctDNA concentration at the pre-CICI and the early on-CICI draws, the patient is 'Increasing' (the paper's primary-resistance face: all 5 such patients progressed within 4.5 months of starting CICI) or 'Decreasing' (1-year FFP 100%, FFP P=0.007 vs Increasing) when the two measurements changed at least 2 fold OR were statistically distinguishable (non-overlapping 95% confidence intervals from negative binomial estimates); the analysis set is patients whose ctDNA was detected at either draw (the paper's 10 dynamics-evaluable patients, 5/5). The wrapper takes the last draw on or before baseline_max_day as the pre-CICI draw and the last draw after it up to the landmark as the early on-CICI draw, evaluates the 2-fold test, and for a sub-2-fold change - where the paper's CI arm would decide - falls back to the direction of the change (a rise = Increasing, a fall = Decreasing, exactly no change = Increasing, the paper's unstated middle case) because the negative binomial model behind the CI arm and the count data it is fit on are not published and the benchmark input carries only the per-draw concentration and its detection call; it writes the fold change as risk (the quantity the rule thresholds, higher = more likely failing), the paper's call (1 = Increasing, treatment judged failing) and no probability of its own (TxResBench converts the risk). Patients with ctDNA undetected at both draws (outside the analysis set), without both draws, or with a detected draw whose value cannot form a fold get no risk, with the reason in note; a rise from an undetectable pre-CICI draw is classed Increasing (the paper's analysis set and Rising class) with empty risk, the fold being undefined.

methods.description: The ctDNA surveillance rule of Lapin et al. (Clin Cancer Res 2023, DOI 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-22-3526; 56 advanced pancreatic cancer patients on first-line gemcitabine, gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel or FOLFIRINOX; plasma ctDNA point-mutation VAF (%) by HYTEC-seq, eight-gene panel, monthly draws plus draws at progression). Per patient it makes a binary call of whether the serial ctDNA trajectory detected disease progression during treatment: a >25% increase in ctDNA VAF at a follow-up draw, OR ctDNA persistence (i.e. a <10-fold reduction in VAF vs baseline, the paper's lack-of-clearance condition). The paper's monitoring set (27 patients with >= 2 draws and >= 1 radiological examination, excluding patients without follow-up samples at progression or without any positive ctDNA sample): increase alone detected progression in 17/27 (63%), increase OR persistence in 19/27 (70%), median lead time 22 days (increase) / 19 days (combined) vs 6 days for a >50% CA19-9 increase. The wrapper scans the patient's draws up to the benchmark landmark (nothing is fitted: the 25%/10-fold thresholds are the paper's, the rule learns nothing from the training outcomes) and evaluates the two arms; two paper-open points are declared rather than guessed: (1) the paper never states what the >25% increase is measured against, so `increase_reference` records the wrapper's reference - default 'previous' (each draw vs the preceding one; the paper's own paired analysis supports this reading: a significant ctDNA VAF increase from the 2-month draw to the progression draw (P = 0.003) but no increase vs baseline (P = 0.434), md:158) with 'baseline' and 'nadir' alternatives; (2) which on-treatment draw(s) qualify as 'persistence' in the surveillance analysis is not re-stated, so the wrapper reads the paper's Discussion gloss ('the lack of ctDNA clearance') as: persistent if no on-treatment draw up to the landmark reduced the VAF 10-fold - an undetectable on-treatment draw counts as cleared. risk = the strongest observed rise ratio of the VAF (the quantity the >25% arm thresholds; higher = worse); call = 1 = ctDNA detected progression (treatment judged failing), 0 = neither signal; no probability is written (TxResBench converts the risk). The paper's group-level lead-time statistics need the reference-event date (radiologically detected progression / death) and are not per-patient predictions; the lead time is therefore not emitted (the fit record reports the wrapper's own detection counts). The paper's separate ctDNA persistence survival rule (B2/B3, Fig. 3) and its baseline-status Cox analyses are other methods (relchange-threshold variant, cox-ctdna-status-level variant).

methods.description: The per-patient three-group ctDNA kinetic profile classification of Marsavela et al. (Cancers 2020;12(12):3793; 84 metastatic melanoma patients with serial plasma ctDNA within the first 12 weeks of systemic therapy - 47 on BRAF/MEK inhibitors, 37 on immune checkpoint inhibitors; patient-specific droplet digital PCR ddPCR assays, copies/mL): Group A = 'undetectable ctDNA levels at baseline and during 12 weeks of therapy or non-significant ctDNA changes'; Group B = 'detectable baseline ctDNA that became undetectable or significantly reduced during treatment'; Group C = 'ctDNA positive or negative at baseline with static or significantly increased levels during the first 12 weeks of therapy'; biological response = A + B vs C ('groups A and B represented patients that showed a biological response... group C was comprised of patients that did not show a biological response', md:218-227; ctDNA responders A+B N = 69 vs C N = 15, md:268-269). 'Significant' is decided by the Poisson test between the baseline and follow-up ctDNA levels of the same patient, 'using the minimum and maximum values plus total droplet counts as analytical variables' (md:613-615; ref [41] = Gu et al. 2008, Testing the Ratio of Two Poisson Rates), with significance at p < 0.05 (md:624-625); the paper publishes no code, no per-patient numeric cutoff and no probability. The wrapper takes one marker (the per-draw ctDNA concentration), reads the baseline as the last draw on or before baseline_max_day and the profile as the draws within the paper's 12-week window (window_days default 84; truncated at the landmark), pairs the baseline with the patient's LAST draw in the window (the paper does not state which follow-up draw pairs with the baseline) and reconstructs the Poisson test on the concentration scale - lambda_i = x_i/lod (lod from the marker's __lod rows when the dataset carries them, else the dataset median, else the declared default lod_concentration = 1.0), lambda = 1 for an undetectable draw (the below-detection convention of the close-family rule dpcr-biological-response-criteria), z = (lambda_f - lambda_0)/sqrt(lambda_f + lambda_0) (the equal-exposure score form of the ratio-of-two-Poisson-rates test of ref [41]; the exact statistic the paper used is not published (spec '?'), so this is the wrapper's recorded reconstruction). Groups: baseline undetectable and last undetectable -> A; baseline undetectable and last detected -> C (Figure 2A caption 'became detectable... without significant biological response'); baseline detected and last undetectable -> B; both detected: z below -zcrit -> B (significantly reduced), above +zcrit -> C (significantly increased), |z| <= zcrit -> A (non-significant change; Figure 2B 'NSD = Non-significant decrease'). It writes risk = z (the quantity the rule thresholds; higher = more likely failing) and call = 1 for group C (the paper's no-biological-response group - treatment judged failing), 0 for A and B; no probability (the paper defines none; TxResBench converts the risk). Patients the rule cannot classify get no prediction with the reason in note: no baseline draw, or no on-treatment draw within the 12-week window by the landmark (the paper's analysis cohort is restricted to patients with longitudinal collections within 12 weeks). The wrapper is a fixed rule (fitted false): it learns nothing from the training outcomes, and at fit it reports the training group distribution. Wrapper differences from the paper (each a choice among the md's own alternatives, detailed in README.md and run.json): the Poisson test is reconstructed (the closed form and the definitions of the min/max/droplet-count variables are not published; the benchmark contract's long frame carries no per-draw count or CI columns, so the test runs on the concentration scale with the assay LOD); the follow-up draw paired with the baseline is the last in-window draw; the two md-open boundaries (non-significant increase between A and C; the A 'non-significant changes' vs C 'static' split) are read per the group definitions and Figure 2A/B; the paper's undefined rebound case is read by the endpoint; the A/B/C group code itself is reported at fit (run.json) while the predictions table carries the contract columns (risk, call, note).

methods.description: The ctDNA molecular-response rule of the CCTG BR.36 trial stage 1 (Anagnostou et al., Nature Medicine 2023, advanced/metastatic NSCLC on first-line pembrolizumab): the per-draw maxMAF (the maximal mutant allele fraction, in %, of the tumor-derived plasma mutations remaining after the paper's WBC DNA-informed cellular-origin classification) is read at the three protocol draws - pre-treatment C1D1, C2D1 (3 weeks) and C3D1 (6 weeks, the response timepoint determined at 8 weeks accounting for treatment delays, draws dated by collection date). A patient with a detectable baseline whose maxMAF is reduced to undetectable levels at the C3D1 response draw is a molecular responder (mR, call 0); a patient whose maxMAF persists (is detected) at the C3D1 response draw is molecular disease progression (mPD, call 1, treatment judged failing), whatever the magnitude of the decrease (the >85% but <100% reduction patients are mPD). A patient with undetectable baseline ctDNA is not evaluable and gets no call (not imputed into either arm); one whose C3D1 draw is missing but who cleared at C2D1 is mR (the paper's BR360048); one whose maxMAF is still detected at C2D1 with no C3D1 draw gets no call (the paper is silent). The wrapper takes the per-sample maximum as its one marker and writes the maxMAF of the decision draw as risk (0 after clearance, higher = more residual circulating tumor burden = failing; the paper defines no per-patient score, and continuous maxMAF is its own Cox covariate) and the 0/1 call; no probability is written, TxResBench converts the risk. From the paper: the marker must be the per-draw maximum over variants classified tumor-derived (the germline/clonal-hematopoiesis filtering is upstream of the benchmark input).

methods.description: The three-group interim molecular-response rule of Kurtz et al. (Nature Biotechnology 2021, PhasED-Seq ctDNA in large B-cell lymphomas on front-line immuno-chemotherapy): at the interim landmark after 2 of 6 planned cycles the patient is 'not achieving MMR' (ctDNA detectable, log10 reduction < 2.5), 'achieving MMR but with persistent ctDNA' (a 2.5-log reduction but still detectable), or 'undetectable ctDNA' by PhasED-Seq; the groups had distinct event-free survival (not achieving MMR: especially high risk of early events; persistent ctDNA: higher risk of later relapse or progression; undetectable: overwhelmingly favorable). The same rule after 1 cycle uses a 2-log reduction (EMR). The wrapper reads one marker (the per-draw PhasED-Seq ctDNA quantity with its detection call), takes the baseline draw (last on or before baseline_max_day) and the landmark draw (last up to the landmark), and writes the signed log10 change as risk (higher = increase = worse; the quantity the paper's log-fold-change plots threshold), call 1 for the two non-favorable groups and 0 for undetectable ctDNA, and no probability. The PhasED-Seq detection algorithm is assay software and not reimplemented: the per-draw detection call and detection limit come from the data (__detected / __lod companion rows). scale 'linear' (default; the wrapper takes log10) or 'log10' (values already log10(haploid genome equivalents/mL)); mmr_log_reduction 2.5 (set 2.0 for the 1-cycle EMR parameterization). A patient with an undetectable baseline or no baseline/landmark pair gets no prediction: the paper defines no rule for it.

methods.description: The three-event ctDNA molecular-progression criteria applied by Lu C et al., Biomarker Research 2025;13:98 (DOI 10.1186/s40364-025-00809-8, letter to the editor): an exploratory analysis of serial plasma ctDNA (baseline, week 8, at progression; 52 successful samples of 21 patients - 20 baseline, 26 on-treatment, 6 at PD) in 21 Chinese patients with advanced RET fusion-positive NSCLC treated with pralsetinib 400 mg once daily (NCT03037385; 168-gene LungPlasma panel, Burning Rock, 20,000x; per-variant VAFs and the derived per-draw indices maxAF, cfDNA-normalised MTM/mL and methylation MD ratio, md:15/MOESM1). The rule (md:40, borrowed from prior research in EGFR-mutant NSCLC [3], no published analysis code): 'Molecular progression was defined with reference to prior research in EGFR-mutant NSCLC [3] and includes the following events: (1) acquisition of putative resistance mutations not present at baseline, (2) a pre-existing mutation with an allele frequency that increased by more than 10% compared with baseline, or (3) any alteration detected after ctDNA clearance (defined as undetectable ctDNA or reduction of all baseline mutations to zero at the current limit of detection of the assay, not limited to RET fusions).' The wrapper evaluates the three events per patient over the serial draws against the per-patient baseline (each variant's own last pre-treatment draw; a variant absent at baseline is not present at baseline, the panel-report convention), reads the >10% increase as RELATIVE with the boundary excluded (factor > 1.10, exposed as af_increase_ratio) and STRICTLY greater than the baseline, reads the clearance state from the per-draw ctDNA indices when the unit carries them (md:28: undetectable measured by both maxAF and MTM/mL - a draw with a positive level and no detection call is not clearance, no LOD is printed so no threshold is invented) and from the baseline-mutation-zero reading of md:40 when it does not, and fires arm 3 on any variant detected at a draw strictly after the first clearance draw. call = 1 when any event fired by the benchmark landmark (molecular progression = treatment judged failing); risk = the largest per-variant relative AF increase factor vs baseline (the quantity arm 2 thresholds; an acquired or after-clearance variant's magnitude is measured against the patient's smallest positive value of its series, else the training minimum positive, because a rise from 0 is undefined in the paper, '?'); no probability is written (TxResBench converts the risk). The paper's cohort findings (6/21 PD, three dynamic profiles x 2 patients, mean 2.2-month lead time to radiologic PD, acquired KRAS G12R/CSMD3 amplification/B2M missense/EPHA7 E239K) are descriptive validation, not per-patient output. Declared readings of the paper's open points (no fixed resistance-gene list for arm 1 - the benchmark's per-variant features are the alteration space; the two printed clearance definitions are not reconciled, the wrapper declares the index reading when indices exist; the absolute +10 percentage points reading cannot be excluded from the text '?'; the no-baseline-mutation and baseline-undetectable degenerate cases are the paper-silent cases) are in the README and run.json.

methods.description: The personalised multi-variant ctDNA detection rule of Cavallone et al., Sci Rep 2020 (26 TNBC patients of Q-CROC-03 on neoadjuvant chemotherapy; tumour-informed personalised ddPCR assays for 121 SNVs, average 5 per patient). Per variant, a detection threshold is calibrated on 3 pools of plasma from 10 cancer-free volunteers each and set as the mean of the 3 pool MAF values + 2 SD (md:37); a variant is detected in a blood sample when its MAF is above its own threshold; the patient call at a timepoint is ctDNA+ when at least 1 variant is detected and ctDNA- when no variant is detected for any gene (Table 3 footnote, md:47). The wrapper applies it at the benchmark's landmark: the decision draw is the patient's last on-treatment draw (after baseline_max_day, up to the landmark), the tested variants are those measured at that draw ('only tested variants are considered at each time point', Fig. 4), and call = 1 (ctDNA+) means residual disease predicted / treatment judged failing. It writes as risk the paper's own per-patient quantity at that draw - the average MAF with the non-detected variants assigned 0 (md:42; the paper's T4 pCR 0.017% vs non-pCR 0.55%, p = 0.0001) - higher = more ctDNA = failing, and no probability (TxResBench converts). The per-variant threshold reaches the wrapper as the variant marker's __lod rows (the benchmark's detection-limit channel carrying the normal-pool mean + 2 SD); without __lod rows the wrapper falls back, per marker, to the marker's own per-draw __detected rows (the threshold applied upstream), and without either to value > detection_threshold (0) - the benchmark's below-detection-limit encoding - each fallback recorded in run.json.

methods.description: The four-tier early ctDNA dynamics call of Hou et al. (Frontiers in Medicine 2026, DOI 10.3389/fmed.2026.1833355; 120 enrolled / 107 day-28 landmark patients with refractory metastatic colorectal cancer on fruquintinib 5 mg qd, 3-weeks-on/1-week-off; customized 425-gene hybrid-capture ctDNA panel, calling required VAF >= 0.1%, >= 3 independent mutant molecules and >= 3,000 x depth, md:64): from the per-draw maximum variant allele frequency (mVAF, % - the highest VAF among all non-synonymous somatic mutations detected in that sample, computed independently at each time point so the max at day 28 may be a different mutation than at baseline, md:71) and the mutation-level day-28 states, four tiers at the day-28 draw of the first cycle - clearance (baseline mVAF > 0 with all baseline mutations below the 0.1% detection limit at day 28 and zero independent mutant molecules detected, md:76), decrease (>= 50% mVAF reduction without clearance, md:81), stable (less than 50% decrease to less than 25% increase, md:86), increase (>= 25% increase or emergence of new high-confidence mutations, md:91); patients with undetectable baseline ctDNA are excluded from the primary stratification (md:93); the thresholds are borrowed (assay technical CV 15% and previously published solid-tumor thresholds, md:93) and the percent-change formula is not printed (the standard (mVAF_day28 - mVAF_baseline)/mVAF_baseline x 100 is the only reading consistent with the reported medians, md:204). The wrapper takes every marker passed as one mutation of the panel (per-mutation VAF features; __detected/__lod companions are stripped), reads the baseline draw as the last draw on or before baseline_max_day and the day-28 draw as the last draw in (baseline_max_day, landmark_day] - the paper's fixed day-28 window (days 26-30 of the first cycle, md:60) mapped onto the benchmark's landmark frame with the corpus fixed-pair convention (the paper prints no per-patient draw days); the day-14 application is exploratory (md:209) and never used. Detection per draw follows the benchmark's vocabulary first (the marker's __detected rows; else its __lod rows; else the paper's fixed 0.1% limit on the value_to_pct-scaled scale); a draw with no detected mutation at all is the paper's day-28 undetectable state (the 'zero independent mutant molecules' clause - the tidy vocabulary carries the assay call, not molecule counts). The wrapper writes risk = the percent change of the mVAF (the quantity the rule thresholds, higher = worse; -100 for clearance) and call = 1 for the combined stable/increase strata (the reference group of the paper's Cox and logistic models, md:118/md:123; the paper's per-stratum medians order clearance > decrease > stable > increase for both PFS, md:236, and OS), 0 for clearance/decrease; no probability is written (the paper defines none, TxResBench converts the risk). A patient without both draws, or with no baseline-detected mutation (undetectable baseline ctDNA, md:93), gets an empty risk and call with the reason in note; the paper defines no fallback call for them. The wrapper learns nothing from the training outcomes (fitted false); the paper's KM/log-rank/ROC/Cox/logistic analyses are validation of the call, not fitted here. Differences from the paper: the day-28 window is not enforced (the last pre-landmark draw is used); the new-mutation branch needs 'new high-confidence mutations' which the paper never defines beyond the calling criteria (md:64, md:91) - read here as a mutation detected at the day-28 draw but not at the baseline draw; when both the >= 50% decrease and a new high-confidence mutation hold, the patient is increase (the increase definition is an OR without exclusions and the tier orients to failure; new_mutation_priority 'decrease-first' switches to the as-printed order reading); the benchmark's binary call collapses the four tiers (the paper's native output is the four-level stratum, and its per-stratum DCR is reported for clearance/decrease/stable+increase combined, md:218).

methods.description: The per-patient molecular-progression event detector of Nixon AB, Navarro FCP, Zhou KI, et al., 'Monitoring treatment response using an ultra-sensitive ctDNA assay in advanced esophagogastric cancer patients', Scientific Reports 2026;16:14766 (DOI 10.1038/s41598-026-43178-4; the KeyLargo phase II research, 24 ctDNA-evaluable HER2-negative metastatic esophagogastric adenocarcinoma patients on first-line pembrolizumab + capecitabine + oxaliplatin; serial ctDNA PPM by the tumor-informed bespoke NeXT Personal assay, plans of up to ~1,800 somatic variants, median LOD 2.03 PPM, draws at baseline C1D1, C1D8, end of cycle 1 and each restaging cycle and around clinical/radiographic progression; imaging RECIST 1.1 every three cycles from C4D1): 'Molecular progression was defined as the earliest ctDNA increase of 20% or more from the lowest ctDNA measurement.' (md:431-432), with the reference spelled out as the running minimum of the patient's PRECEDING ctDNA measurements - 'the time gained in detecting disease progression using ctDNA analyses (20% increase in PPM from the lowest preceding ctDNA measurement) compared to more traditional imaging methods (20% increase in total diameter from the preceding lowest total diameter or death)' (md:156-158). No confirmation ('sustained') requirement is stated, and the paper's output is the per-patient event date plus the lead time against imaging progression or death: the ultra-sensitive ctDNA analysis provided a median lead time advantage of 65 days (mean 55.4 days) and all patients but one (patient 140, whose ctDNA levels were the highest in the research) progressed by ctDNA prior to or at imaging progression (md:159-167); a secondary correlation of per-time-point ctDNA ratio vs RECIST sum-of-diameters ratio gives rho = 0.58 (abstract 0.59), p = 7.3 x 10^-9 (md:168-172, md:446-451). The wrapper applies the rule as published to the patient's ordered ctDNA PPM draws up to the benchmark landmark (nothing is fitted: `fitted` false, `uses_history` landmark): the scan tracks the running minimum of strictly preceding quantitative measurements, and the earliest draw with PPM >= (1 + increase_cutoff) x that minimum is the molecular-progression event; call = 1 = molecular progression by the landmark = treatment judged failing, 0 = no draw reached the 20% threshold; risk = the strongest observed PPM/nadir rise ratio over the draws with a preceding draw (the quantity the rule thresholds; 1 = no change, below 1 = decrease = favourable, >= 1.2 = the event threshold), which TxResBench converts to probabilities - the paper defines no per-patient probability. Below-LOD (non-detected) draws carry no quantitative PPM and leave the run of measurements (the paper does not state their participation; the 100-PPM-LOD simulation shows the rule's sensitivity to very low detections, md:251-256); a patient with fewer than two quantitative draws by the landmark gets no prediction, the reason in the note. The wrapper's outputs are the event call and its risk; the paper's lead time needs the imaging progression date, which is not part of the benchmark's prediction frame (TxResBench's analysis code associates the call with the outcomes).

methods.description: The ctDNA progressive-disease (PD) detection rule of Gray JE, Markovets A, et al. (J Thorac Oncol 2024;19(11):1525-1538; DOI 10.1016/j.jtho.2024.07.008; FLAURA NCT02296125 and AURA3 NCT02151981; 146 PFS-eligible patients per trial, all with RECIST 1.1 PD; serial plasma EGFRm ctDNA by clinical-grade ddPCR, the Biodesix GeneStrat assay, C1D1/D8/D15, C2-7 D1, then every 6 weeks; LLOQ = >=30 mutant droplets). The paper's Table 1 rule (md:455-466): ctDNA PD is defined with respect to the nadir ctDNA result and its proximity to the ddPCR detection limit and lower limit of quantification, with three nadir-conditioned thresholds: (1) nadir positive above the LLOQ -> 'A 100% increase in mutant allele fraction at one time point'; (2) nadir positive below the LLOQ or non-confirmed negative -> 'Any positive result above the LLOQ'; (3) nadir confirmed negative (two consecutive negatives, may include the baseline sample, i.e. clearance) -> 'Two consecutive positive results (below LLOQ) OR any one positive result (above LLOQ)'; ctDNA PD is defined only from week 3 onwards (Supplementary Methods) and the call is on the presence of Ex19del or L858R, one of which each patient carries (the resistance mutations T790M/C797S are separate analyses, not this call). The wrapper scans each patient's serial draws up to the benchmark landmark (nothing is fitted: `fitted` false) and applies the rule per mutation with the running minimum of the allele fraction over the preceding draws as the nadir; `call` = 1 if either mutation meets its branch (molecular PD = treatment judged failing); `risk` = the strongest observed rise of the patient's ctDNA allele fraction over its nadir (the quantity the Group 1 arm thresholds; higher = worse), which TxResBench converts to probabilities. Paper-open points are declared, never guessed: no LLOQ-in-MAF value is published (only '>=30 mutant droplets', md:466), so the wrapper reads the per-draw three-state classification from a mutant-droplet-count series if the unit carries one, else from the `lloq` setting (per-dataset value via the benchmark's method-params mechanism), else - the declared fallback - treats every detected positive result as above the LLOQ (the only reading under which the rule's categorical arms are not silently disabled); 'week 3' is not mapped to a cycle day, `start_day` 14 records the wrapper's reading (the C1D15 draw of the 21-day cycle schedule); the nadir is tracked per mutation as the running minimum over the draws before the draw under test; each patient's own mutation is identified from the two series because the paper's cohorts carry one per patient (the per-patient `driver` reading); a patient without a draw in the evaluated window gets no prediction (empty risk, the reason in the note).

(md:372) plus the commercial assay layer, the Biodesix GeneStrat ddPCR assay (md:323-325); the article is CC BY-NC-ND (md:102-104) - so this wrapper implements the published rule from the Methods text, Table 1 (md:455-466) and the Supplementary Methods (suppl:4-9))

methods.description: The per-alteration ctDNA clearance rule of Kim et al. (Br J Cancer 2022;127:898-907, first-line palliative chemotherapy in 62 metastatic colorectal cancer patients, 272 serial plasmas, AlphaLiquid 100 106-gene panel): per follow-up sample, ctDNA clearance = the disappearance of ALL mutations or CNVs above the calling cutoffs that were detectable at the baseline sample (mutation VAF >= 0.3% together with the upstream >= 6 altered-read and CNV P < 0.01 criteria, which enter as the dataset's detection state; amplifications CN >= 6 and gains CN >= 4); sustained ctDNA clearance = clearance in at least two consecutive samples, whose (-) group is no clearance at all or clearance at a single timepoint. The wrapper takes every marker passed as one alteration of the panel and writes call = 1 for no clearance (the paper's 13/51 clearance(-) group with shorter PFS: median 7.5 vs 11.8 months, P < 0.001, aHR 0.22 95% CI 0.10-0.46), call 0 when the baseline alterations have all disappeared at an on-treatment draw up to the landmark; the setting call_definition = 'sustained' switches the call to the paper's sustained call (1 = not sustained). risk is the remaining extent over the patient's own baseline alteration set at the last on-treatment draw before the landmark - the mean over the set of value / per-alteration cutoff (VAF/CN in multiples of the paper's cutoff; cleared alterations 0), 0 = complete clearance at the decision draw; the paper defines no per-patient probability and no combined mutation+CNV scalar (its average VAF, md:185-187, is the mutation-only mean), so no probability is written and TxResBench converts the risk. A patient without baseline alterations abstains: the disappearance check is vacuous and the paper does not fix the call for its 6/51 baseline-mutation-free patients (Fig. 3 shows them under sustained clearance without PD while the Fig. 2b counts imply the clearance(-) group).

methods.description: The ctDNA monitoring success/failure rule of Edland et al. (Molecular Oncology 2023; DOI 10.1002/1878-0261.13472; 81 prospectively included patients with advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, 69 metastatic and 12 locally advanced, Stavanger and Haukeland University Hospitals, first-line palliative chemotherapy per Norwegian guidelines - FOLFIRINOX (36), nab-paclitaxel/gemcitabine (38), gemcitabine monotherapy (7); plasma KRAS codon 12/13-mutated ctDNA by PNA clamp PCR, level as delta-delta Cq = 11.27 - sample dCq (md:143; sample positive when ddCq > 0, ddCq < 0 set to 0 in the statistical analyses; no amplification signal in both PNA-clamp replicates = not detected; baseline, every 4 weeks during chemotherapy, CT at baseline and every 8 weeks per respRECIST 1.1, md:75). The paper's monitoring cohort = 30 patients with KRAS mutations in the baseline blood sample and at least two blood samples including at least one within 1 month of the date of radiologically confirmed disease progression (md:266). The call (md:266, Fig. 4A/B captions, md:269): Success (20/30) = 'persistently high ctDNA levels' (n = 3) OR 'initially decreasing ctDNA levels that increased again at the time of or earlier than radiological disease progression' (n = 17) - Fig. 4B: 'persistent or increasing ctDNA levels before or until 1 month after radiological evidence of progression'; Failure (10/30) = 'decreasing ctDNA levels that did not reflect disease progression' (Fig. 4A: 'ctDNA levels that only decrease', yellow curves); reported quantity: median lead time of ctDNA-based over radiological detection 23 days (P = 0.01, Wilcoxon signed rank test with continuity correction; 22 days, P = 0.02, using ctDNA increase only; md:183, md:266). The wrapper evaluates the rule per patient on the serial ddCq draws up to the benchmark landmark (nothing is fitted - the rule learns nothing from the training outcomes, fitted false; uses_history landmark): the paper's call is anchored to the (known, retrospective) radiological progression date, which a prediction at the landmark does not have, so the landmark takes the place of the radiological progression reference and the whole observed trajectory up to it is read - the current-assessment analog of the paper's 'at or before progression'; the 1-month-after-progression window and the lead time are outside the benchmark frame and are not output (README records the difference). call 1 = Success = ctDNA reflected disease progression = the treatment judged failing, call 0 = Failure (decreasing only). The paper defines NO numeric magnitude for either branch (spec records 'persistently high' and 'increased again' as '?'), so the wrapper declares its readings rather than guessing: the increase arm is any strict rise of a drawn ddCq over the immediately preceding draw (increase_ratio 1.0 with increase_boundary 'greater' - the paper's own 'increasing' vs 'only decrease' binary, Fig. 4A; increase_reference 'previous' by default, 'baseline' and 'nadir' exposed; a rise from an undetectable draw has an undefined magnitude and is measured against the patient's smallest positive ddCq, the committed increase-rule convention) and the persistence arm is every on-treatment drawn value at or above the patient's baseline ddCq (persistence_min_fraction 1.0 - 'stably high', Fig. 4A; a fraction below 1 exposes the 'never fell by more than X%' readings). Undetectability is read from the harness encoding (a <marker>__detected companion row of 0, else a value at or below detection_threshold, default 0) and an undetectable draw enters the trajectory as the level 0 (md:143), so a decrease to undetectable that does not return is 'decreasing only' (Failure) while a return above detection is the 'increased again' arm; ddCq < 0 is set to 0 (md:143, clip_negative). risk = the strongest observed rise ratio of the serial ddCq trajectory (the quantity the increase arm thresholds, per the contract's rule-writing convention; > 1 = an increase = higher risk = the treatment more likely failing); no probability is written (TxResBench converts the risk). A patient the method cannot classify gets no prediction, with the reason in note: no positive baseline draw (the paper's monitoring cohort is restricted to baseline ctDNA-positive patients, md:266), no baseline draw, no on-treatment draw by the landmark. The paper's PFS/OS Cox models (Tables 2-3), the jmbayes2 joint model (Table 4) and the CA19-9 comparator rule (> 50% increase; median lead time 9.5 days, P = 0.03; md:266) are separate analyses, not this rule.

methods.description: The longitudinal ctDNA surveillance persistence rule of Yang et al. (Signal Transduct Target Ther 2025;10:347, DOI 10.1038/s41392-025-02445-y; LS-SCLC on CCRT + consolidation serplulimab, NCT05443646): among patients with serial plasma ctDNA surveillance draws between cycle 3 (C3), month 6 (M6) and year 1 (Y1) of consolidation ICI, a patient with ctDNA-negative results at ALL those draws is 'persistently negative' (the paper's favorable group, n = 20 of the 28 with serial samples) and a patient with ctDNA detectable at >= 1 of them is 'at least one detectable' (n = 8); in the paper the groups had markedly different PFS (persistently negative prolonged: HR 0.08, 95% CI 0.01-0.42, p = 0.003, Fig. 5d; PFS from treatment initiation). The wrapper takes one marker (the patient's per-draw ctDNA result, consumed as the assay's per-draw detection status from the dataset's <marker>__detected rows when present, else above detection_threshold), reads the surveillance draws as the draws of that marker in the ICI surveillance window - after the baseline window (the paper's pre-ICI t2 draws are baseline-window draws and are excluded) up to the benchmark landmark, optionally from a surveillance_start_day - and re-evaluates the persistence call as the draws accrue (a patient negative at C3 and M6 but detectable at Y1 moves to 'at least one detectable'): call = 1 for 'at least one detectable' (treatment judged failing), 0 for 'persistently negative'. It writes risk = log1p of the highest marker level over the surveillance draws (the wrapper's own summary of the strength of the detection signal; the paper defines no per-patient score) and call; no probability (the paper defines none; TxResBench converts the risk). A patient without a surveillance draw by the landmark gets no prediction, with the reason in note. Nothing is fitted (fixed rule; the paper publishes no analysis code - the KM/log-rank/Cox HR is the paper's cohort-level validation of the call, not a per-patient output). The paper's companion analyses of the same data (Y1 detection HR 7.95; acquired detection HR 0.30; the t2-positive/C3 clearance 1/6) are separate rules and are recorded in the README, not implemented here.

methods.description: The per-patient binary ctDNA-detected-progression call of Chin et al. (Cancer Sci 2022;113:1808-1820; DOI 10.1111/cas.15304; 33 ER+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer patients on CDK4/6i + endocrine combination therapy, 178 serial plasma samples, median follow-up 12 months; serial plasma targeted NGS with the Oncomine Pan-Cancer Cell-Free Assay, 52 genes, UMTs, hg19, Torrent Suite 5.10.1 / Ion Reporter 5.10.3.0, md:100, md:105): the assay's per-draw detection criteria are (a) >= 3 same-UMT reads per functional family, (b) SNVs/indels detected with >= 2 variant-supporting functional families at VAF >= 0.2%, (c) not detected with any counts in the corresponding WBC sequencing, (d) >= 2.5-fold change between CNV target amplicons and non-CNV reference amplicons (md:105); clonal-hematopoiesis mutations (TP53, FBXW7, IDH2) excluded upstream (md:178). The rule's call (md:115): 'ctDNA levels at point of progression shows a minimum of 0.2% for SNVs and at least 2.5-fold for CNVs' - the patient is ctDNA-positive at or near the point of clinical progression (RECIST v1.1, md:90) with SNV VAF >= 0.2% OR CNV >= 2.5-fold, ctDNA-negative otherwise; published 2x2 evaluation: 15/20 (75%) of the patients who eventually developed PD were ctDNA positive vs 1/13 (8%) of those still responding -> sensitivity 75%, specificity (negative percent agreement) 92% (md:115, md:188); the paper's monitoring-marker definition (ctDNA detected within cycle 1 - within 1 month - AND >= 0.2%/2.5-fold at least once during monitoring AND not in WBC, md:115; 38 monitoring-marker alterations in 20/33 patients, 61%, md:178), the acquired-alteration definition (undetected within the first cycle: SNV count = 0 or CNV = 2.0-fold, then SNV >= 0.2% or CNV >= 2.5-fold at PD, md:115) and the lead-time analysis (>= thresholds in consecutive intervals from the initial rise until PD, from 1 month onwards; average lead time 3 months (range 1.5-6) in 8/12 responders who later progressed and 2 months in 3/8 non-responders via biweekly cycle-1 sequencing, md:115, md:188) are the method's descriptive layers. The wrapper takes exactly two serial ctDNA measurement series - the ctDNA SNV/indel VAF (%) and the ctDNA CNV fold-change (the spec's per-draw feature pair; each marker's role is identified by name cues - 'vaf'/'snv'/'indel'/'maf'/'variant allele'/'mutant allele' vs 'cnv'/'copy number'/'fold'/'amplif' - with the positional convention markers[0] = SNV VAF series, markers[1] = CNV series as the fallback for generic names, refusing a marker that matches both cues). Nothing is fitted (fitted false - the rule learns nothing from the training outcomes): at the benchmark landmark L the wrapper reads each chain's ctDNA level at that chain's most recent draw at or before L (window_end 'current', the current-assessment analog of 'ctDNA levels at point of progression' at the nearest sampling interval; window_end 'anywhere' exposes the at-any-evaluated-draw reading), applies the paper's absolute thresholds, and writes call 1 = ctDNA-positive at/near progression = treatment judged failing, call 0 = ctDNA-negative; the call is the OR of the two chains (the SNV chain and the CNV chain are the paper's two threshold channels, md:115), each chain evaluated by the literal value-vs-threshold comparison by default (detect_source 'threshold' - the paper's own rule thresholds, which coincide with the assay floors, md:105/md:115 - with 'detected'/'auto' exposing the dataset's <marker>__detected assay call instead). risk = the ctDNA SNV/indel VAF (%) at the call draw (the quantity the SNV chain thresholds - the contract's rule-writing convention; the spec's projection leaves risk derivable, not native); the CNV chain lives on a different scale (fold-change vs %) and contributes to the call only (the two-arms-different-scales precedent, cf. combined-ctdna-resistance-criteria and ctdna-consecutive-elevation-progression), with risk_source 'cnv' exposing the CNV fold-change as the risk instead and a documented cross-chain fallback when the risk_source chain has no level at the call draw. No probability is written (TxResBench converts the risk). A patient with fewer than two serial draws, or with no ctDNA level of either chain at the call draw, gets no prediction (empty risk, reason in note). The wrapper does not emit the paper's lead time (it needs the RECIST progression date - post-call information in a benchmark prediction setting; the analysis layer computes it against the outcome), it does not apply the monitoring-marker/acquired-alteration filters to the call (the paper's 2x2 uses the at-progression levels alone, md:115/md:188 - the definitions are recorded as per-chain diagnostics instead), and the WBC/clonal-hematopoiesis exclusion is upstream of the benchmark values (noted, not re-implemented).

methods.description: The five-group quantitative ctDNA response criteria of Gouda et al. (JCO Precision Oncology 2022;6:e2100512, DOI 10.1200/PO.21.00512; 204 patients / 260 systemic treatment courses in advanced solid tumors, longitudinal tumor-informed ddPCR with the ctDNA aggregate VAF = the sum of the VAFs of all detected somatic alterations): a per-patient call, made separately at the paper's mid-treatment (cycle 1, day 21 +- 2 weeks) and first-restaging (restaging between weeks 6 and 10, day of first restaging +- 2 weeks) evaluations, from the percent change of the aggregate VAF between the baseline draw and the on-treatment draw - ctDNA CR (ctDNA clearance after initial detectability), ctDNA PR (decrease of more than 10% in VAF), ctDNA PD (increase of more than 10% in VAF or de novo ctDNA detection), ctDNA SD (no increase or <10% increase or decrease in VAF), ctDNA nonmeasurable disease (undetectable ctDNA before and after treatment); the groups had different median time-to-treatment failure (Table 3: mid-treatment CR 23 weeks [P =.006], PR 12, SD 8, PD 10, nonmeasurable 16; first restaging CR 26 weeks [P <.001], PR 10, SD 10, PD 9, nonmeasurable 13). The wrapper takes one marker (the per-draw aggregate ctDNA VAF in percent; the per-draw detectability state comes from the marker's <marker>__detected companion rows when present, else the value being positive - the paper's ddPCR/QuantaSoft 1.7.4 detection call is assay software, not reimplemented), reads the baseline draw (the last draw on or before baseline_max_day - the paper's baseline window cycle 1 day -21 to +8 straddles day 0, so pre-treatment draws count) and the on-treatment draw (the last draw after it and at or before the landmark), applies the paper's rule at the benchmark landmark as the paper's mid-treatment evaluation when the landmark is within the mid-treatment window (at or before day 35, day 21 +- 2 weeks) and as the first-restaging evaluation otherwise, and writes risk = the percent change of the aggregate VAF (the quantity the rule bands; higher = increase = more likely failing), with the categorical branches recorded as the documented values -100 for ctDNA CR and +100 for de novo ctDNA PD, since the paper prints no numeric percent change at an undetectable draw - and call = 1 for ctDNA PD (the paper's failure category: increase of more than 10% or de novo detection) and 0 for ctDNA CR/PR/SD/nonmeasurable. It writes no probability (the paper defines none; TxResBench converts the risk). A patient with no baseline draw or no on-treatment draw gets no prediction with the reason in note; ctDNA nonmeasurable disease is written as call 0 with the reason in note and no risk score (the percent change is undefined at an undetectable baseline). Wrapper differences from the paper (each listed in README.md): the paper's named protocol visits have no benchmark channel - the wrapper applies the rule to the draws the run has by the landmark and picks the evaluation timepoint from the landmark day; the percent-change formula is not printed in the paper, so the standard (VAF_on-treatment - VAF_baseline)/VAF_baseline x 100 is used, the only reading consistent with the paper's categorical branches; the exactly +/-10% boundary is not covered by the printed bands (PR/PD require 'more than 10%', SD '<10%'), so the wrapper puts exactly +/-10% in ctDNA SD (the LB-RECIST application of the same criteria states 'changes within +/-10%'); and the paper's only validation is the cohort-level per-group median TTF (Table 3), so no binary failure grouping is part of the method - the call 1-vs-0 split is the wrapper's PD-vs-non-PD reading, stated here.

methods.description: The per-patient, per-evaluation-draw ctDNA-RECIST response classification of Iden CR, Ogaard N et al. (Gastric Cancer 2026, DOI 10.1007/s10120-026-01743-w; Lon-Gas trial, 86 previously treated gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma patients with baseline plasma, 77/44 evaluable by plasma ctDNA after one/two treatment cycles): the 95% confidence interval of the current plasma ctDNA measurement (copies/mL, tumor-agnostic methylation-specific ddPCR of the summed C9orf50/CLIP4/KCNQ5 markers, Poisson statistics - md:45) is compared with the CI of the reference measurement (the previous measurement - md:49 - or, for the paper's week-8 categorization, directly the baseline) and calls progressive disease (PD, current CI above and non-overlapping), stable disease (SD, CIs overlap), partial response (PR, current CI lower and non-overlapping and not overlapping 0), near-complete response (NCR, current CI lower and non-overlapping and overlapping 0) or complete response (CR, undetectable following a previous measurement with CI non-overlapping with 0) - the ctDNA-RECIST criteria of refs [18,19], which the paper borrows (md:49); overall response = CR/PR/NCR, and the paper's survival grouping is 'ctDNA PD' vs 'ctDNA non-PD' (SD/PR/NCR/CR, md:161). The wrapper writes as call 1 = ctDNA PD (or, in the point-estimate fallback when the benchmark input carries no per-draw CI, a ctDNA increase = the paper's own PD wording in the poor-responder definition, md:49), and as risk the evaluation-to-reference ctDNA ratio (the comparison quantity the five categories are ordered on: 1 = no change, above 1 = increase, below 1 = decrease; the paper defines no per-patient score - its survival quantities are cohort-level HRs and KM medians - so the ratio is the wrapper's contract projection, documented in the README). The paper's second derived call, 'poor ctDNA responders' ('high' baseline ctDNA and/or a ctDNA increase after one cycle, md:49; high = above the 80th percentile of the training baseline draws, the paper's > 1,068 copies/mL of 86 baseline samples, md:47/md:116), is available via the call_definition setting. The wrapper is a fixed rule (fitted: false): no fitting, no outcome column is read; the only training-data statistic is the 80th-percentile baseline threshold of the poor-responder call, computed at fit.

methods.description: The per-patient, per-pre-planned-on-treatment-draw ctDNA objective response (cOR) classification that mirrors RECIST 1.1, called ctDNA-RECIST (cRECIST) by Fabi A, Giordani E et al. (J Exp Clin Cancer Res 2026, DOI 10.1186/s13046-025-03605-2; GIM21/LiqERBcept, 43 analysed HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer patients on T-DM1, 38 ctDNA-positive, 27 cPD-positive): the RECIST 1.1 numeric cut-offs (SD/PD >= +20% and SD/PR <= -30%, 'default RECIST 1.1 cut-offs', md:10, md:39, md:49) are applied to Delta-ctDNA - the percent change of the summed absolute VAF (%) + CNV values (each rounded to two decimals) of all target ctDNAs present at a draw vs Tref (T0 or Tnadir, whichever the lesser, md:49) - giving 4 classes: cPD (Delta-ctDNA >= +20% or detection of a new ctDNA species), cSD (between +20% and -30%), cPR (Delta-ctDNA <= -30%) and cCR (loss of all detectable target ctDNAs, dPCR LoD 0.01% VAF) (md:39, md:49); cORs are assigned longitudinally at the pre-planned draws until the first cPD (monitoring stopped at cPD for symmetry, md:49); per patient the rule also yields the best cOR (the deepest Delta-ctDNA drop on research, md:83) and the cPD-positive vs cPD-negative grouping (presence of at least one >= +20% Delta-ctDNA increase, md:62). The wrapper takes one or more per-draw ctDNA measurement features (markers: any - the paper's bespoke NGS/dPCR panel of 78 alterations arrives as per-draw variant/CNV features, and the wrapper sums them per draw with the paper's arithmetic, md:49), and writes as call 1 = cPD-positive on the draws up to the benchmark landmark (the paper's failure-direction grouping, whose cPFS clock is T0 to first cPD, md:62, md:90) and as risk Delta-ctDNA at the last draw of the cOR series (the per-draw quantity the four classes are cut on; higher = more ctDNA increase = more likely failing; negative = ctDNA decrease = the response direction). The paper defines no per-patient probability or severity score (its cohort-level validations: cPD anticipated PD by >= 21 days in 24/27, p < 0.0001, but cPD-positive vs cPD-negative PFS/OS and best cOR vs PFS/OS/cPFS did NOT differ - md:66, md:81, md:90 - recorded in the run), so the wrapper writes no probability and TxResBench converts the risk.

methods.description: The multimodal uncertainty-range combination rule of van Wilpe et al., JCI Insight 2025;10(5):e186062 (DOI 10.1172/jci.insight.186062; 93 metastatic urothelial cancer patients on anti-PD-(L)1 ICI monotherapy - pembrolizumab n=72, nivolumab n=7, avelumab maintenance n=14 - with blood at baseline and 2-6 weeks into treatment for ctDNA (n=88) and whole-blood RNA-seq (n=79, 74 with both), split by enrollment timing into discovery/test/validation cohorts): the per-patient call combines two standalone early-response readouts - the ctDNA increase/no-increase rule on the OT/BL ctDNA copies/mL ratio (increase = predicted N-CB, no increase = predicted CB, undetectable-both = no increase, md:136) and the 10-gene sPLS immunotranscriptome model's CB probability at the 55% cutoff (md:167) - by the paper's uncertainty-range switch (md:172): the readout is the RNA model's call when the patient's ctDNA ratio falls inside an uncertainty range around the ratio cutoff 1 (the ctDNA value is then 'uncertain' and the RNA readout takes over), it is the ctDNA model's call when the RNA probability falls inside an uncertainty range around 55%, the RNA model is prioritized when both fall inside their ranges, and the wrapper completes the cell the paper leaves silent (both values outside their ranges) with the ctDNA call, the prediction the paper's description adjusts from; call = 1 means predicted N-CB (treatment judged failing - the paper's reported sensitivities/specificities are for detecting N-CB), risk = the ctDNA ratio (the quantity the rule thresholds; no per-patient score or probability is defined by the paper, so no probability is written and TxResBench converts the risk). The paper tuned the uncertainty-range values in its test cohort ('The best combination of ctDNA ratio and predictive probability cutoffs defining the uncertainty ranges was selected in the test cohort, allowing for the highest increase in sensitivity and specificity compared to the standalone RNA model performance', md:172) and does not print them (spec '?'; the checked supplement holds figure data only), so the wrapper's fit call re-derives them on the benchmark's training fold (the fit fold stands in for the paper's test cohort): a grid of symmetric half-widths around the two cutoffs, the combination maximizing sensitivity + specificity (Youden; 'the highest increase in sensitivity and specificity') of the N-CB call against the 6-month CB label from the harness PFS channel, tie-broken by higher specificity (the paper's stated clinical priority), then smaller widths (parsimony), and the paper's published operating points (test cohort n=27: 71% sensitivity at 100% specificity; independent blinded validation n=19: 79% at 100%, md:70) are recorded as the paper's own (unreproducible) values, not the wrapper's. The wrapper takes exactly two markers (the per-draw ctDNA copies/mL and the per-patient 10-gene RNA-model CB probability - the sPLS classifier is separately specced and is never refitted here; the wrapper consumes its scalar input, the rule's declared between-method dependency), pairs the baseline ctDNA draw with the earliest OT draw carrying both readouts (the paper's 'The BL sample and the earliest OT sample available were used', md:114), and abstains with the reason in note when a patient has no baseline, no paired OT readouts, or an undefined ratio (undetectable baseline with a detected OT draw - the paper does not state the single-undetectable case, spec '?'); the paper's internal discrepancy between the Results 'increase or stable' grouping and the Methods increase/no-increase dichotomy (md:43 vs md:136) is resolved in favour of Methods (strict increase > 1) and recorded, as are all wrapper readings in README.md and run.json.
