methods.description: The three-level risk stratification of Yang Y et al. (Signal Transduct Target Ther 2025, DOI 10.1038/s41392-025-02445-y) in 144 limited-stage small cell lung cancer patients treated with concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) with or without consolidation serplulimab: a per-patient risk stratum at t1 - after induction chemotherapy, before thoracic radiotherapy - from the combination of (a) the t1 ctDNA detection status by tumor-naive 139-gene panel NGS (positive if at least one nonsynonymous somatic alteration is detected after filtering out germline variants and CHIP, md:98) and (b) the radiological tumor shrinkage after induction chemotherapy (RECIST 1.1, md:103) dichotomized at 60% (the 75th percentile, md:61). Verbatim rule (md:61): low risk = tumor shrinkage >=60% AND t1 ctDNA-negative (19 patients; 4-year PFS 68.4%, 4-year OS 78.9%); mid risk = (shrinkage <60% AND ctDNA-negative; 38 patients) OR (shrinkage >=60% AND ctDNA-positive; 6 patients); high risk = shrinkage <60% AND ctDNA-positive - the mixed cells are merged into mid. High-risk patients had significantly worse PFS (HR 4.61, 95% CI 1.90-11.14, p < 0.001) and OS (HR 4.26, 95% CI 1.46-12.43, p = 0.008) than low-risk patients, and in high-risk patients consolidation ICI gave PFS HR 0.24 (95% CI 0.08-0.75, p = 0.014) and OS HR 0.06 (95% CI 0.00-0.42, p = 0.001) vs CCRT alone, while low-risk patients have a high chance of cure with CCRT alone and ICI efficacy in mid-risk patients needs further investigation (md:61, md:63, md:79). The wrapper takes one marker (the per-draw ctDNA level/detection status; the per-sample detection call is resolved from the data: <marker>__detected / <marker>__lod companions, a 0/1 status feature, the 0-coded non-detect convention, else a level threshold - the paper's mutation-calling cutoffs are in the Supplementary Methods, not in the available text) and the t1 tumor shrinkage from a cov_* column (params shrinkage_covariate / shrinkage_candidates, percentage of shrinkage, positive = smaller; the paper is silent on the exact RECIST diameter formula). risk = 0/1/2 (low/mid/high, higher = more likely failing); call = 1 for high risk only (the paper's adverse stratum that derived significant benefit from consolidation ICI), 0 for low/mid - the benchmark's binary collapse of the paper's three-level call. When the covariate track has no shrinkage column the wrapper cannot form the 2x2 and runs the paper's own t1-ctDNA-status-alone analysis (Fig. 2f-g: t1 ctDNA detection predicted worse PFS, HR 2.46, 95% CI 1.47-4.12, p < 0.001, and OS, HR 2.50, 95% CI 1.34-4.67, p = 0.004, in the CCRT-only cohort): risk = the 0/1 detection call, call = 1 if positive - reported at fit and documented in README.md.

methods.description: The two-stage unsupervised longitudinal-ctDNA clustering of Garralda et al. (Clin Cancer Res 2026;32:333-49; tumor-informed ctDNA PPM from the first baseline to the end of follow-up in patients on systemic treatment): soft dynamic time warping (soft-DTW, Cuturi and Blondel ICML 2017, arXiv 1703.01541 - the paper's cited methods reference) computes the pairwise distance between patients' ctDNA time series, partition around the medoids (PAM) identifies k = 2 clusters (chosen by the Silhouette index over k = 2-10 in the primary cohort), and the primary-trained clusters are applied to new patients by assigning each to the nearest cluster representative (the paper's 'centroid from the primary cohort was applied to the validation cohort'). The wrapper reads one marker (the ctDNA level per plasma draw), builds one log1p-transformed time series per patient from its draws in day order, fits the clustering on the training patients' full history (as the paper clusters first baseline to end of follow-up) and saves the two medoids, then assigns the test patients (draws up to the benchmark landmark) to the nearest medoid. Per patient it writes the binary cluster call: risk 1 for the failure cluster (the paper's cluster 2 - stable or increasing ctDNA with higher median levels; cluster 2 membership carried PFS HR 3.24, 95% CI 1.8-5.9, and OS HR 5.2, 2.4-11.3) and 0 for the other cluster (cluster 1 - decreasing ctDNA), and the same value as call (1 = treatment judged failing). The two found clusters are oriented with the paper's interpretation without using outcomes: the cluster whose representative trajectory is more stable-or-increasing is cluster 2 (tie-break: higher median ctDNA level). It writes no probability (the paper defines no per-patient probability or risk score; its survival quantities are group-level association statistics - TxResBench converts the risk). A patient with fewer than two usable draws gets no prediction with the reason in note (the paper includes only patients with more than one plasma timepoint). Unsupervised and deterministic: the fit never reads the training outcomes and uses no random numbers, so the same input gives the same clusters.

methods.description: The per-patient, per-draw-pair two-group ctDNA dynamics call of Lauridsen ED et al. (Int J Colorectal Dis 2026, DOI 10.1007/s00384-025-05055-w; 57 enrolled / 56 evaluable locally advanced rectal cancer patients on neoadjuvant treatment + surgery; tumour-agnostic multiplex MS-ddPCR of five methylation markers with ALB as reference, md:51): per marker, the dynamics of its ratio to ALB between the pair of draws is judged by Poisson 95% CI non-overlap - a significant increase (I) or decrease (D) is a non-overlapping CI pair, overlapping intervals are stable values (SV) (md:53, machinery 'as described by Jacobsen et al. [15]'); the per-draw ctDNA status transition of the same assay (both positive = PP, both negative = NN, negative to positive = NP, positive to negative = PN, md:53) is combined with the dynamics letter into two groups: evidence of increasing ctDNA levels = NPSV, NPI, PPI; stable or decreasing levels = NNSV, PNSV, PND, PPD, PPSV (md:53). The wrapper writes the per-patient group as call (1 = increasing ctDNA = the failure direction; 0 = stable/decreasing) and as risk the patient-level variance-weighted mean log change of the per-marker ratios (the continuous counterpart of the dynamics letter: 0 = no change, positive = increase = failure direction; the weights are the per-marker baseline-value variances of the training patients, normalised to mean 1 - unsupervised, fitted at fit, never an outcome, so the paper's rule still weighs the markers equally for the call; the paper defines no per-patient score - it reports only cohort-level AUCs of the group, 0.52 [0.39-0.65] for baseline to preoperative dynamics vs pathological response, n = 38, and 1.00 [1.00-1.00], 100% sens/spec/accuracy, for preoperative to 6-month postoperative dynamics vs recurrence within 2 years, n = 35). It takes the five panel markers (required_markers), the pair = the last baseline draw and the last on-treatment draw by the benchmark landmark (the paper analyses two fixed pairs, baseline->preoperative and preoperative->6-month postoperative), the per-draw status from the data's per-marker detection state (the paper's droplet-count LoB majority rule with its NPY+GDAP1L1-only exception, md:51 - the droplet counts are upstream of the benchmark frame, so the wrapper consumes the per-marker detection calls), and the per-marker 95% CIs from the data's ci_lo/ci_hi columns or __ci_low/__ci_high companion rows, with the documented point-estimate fallback when the benchmark frame carries neither; the cases the paper leaves undefined (CI boundary touching, the I/D/SV aggregation over the five markers, the four unlisted status x dynamics categories) are resolved as documented in the README.

methods.description: The co-primary activity-evaluation endpoint of the c-TRAK TN trial (Turner et al., Ann Oncol 2023, DOI 10.1016/j.annonc.2022.11.005): sustained ctDNA clearance 6 months after the first pembrolizumab dose = ctDNA undetectable (the paper's personalized digital PCR tracking assay, >= 2 mutant FAM droplets) at the sample collected closest to and preceding the 6-month timepoint from the first dose AND free of disease recurrence by that timepoint ('Patients must have been negative for ctDNA at this timepoint only, and also be free of disease recurrence by this timepoint.'). It is a fixed rule (nothing is fitted; the paper publishes no code). It writes risk = log1p(mutant copies/ml) at the assessment sample (higher = more MRD = worse; the paper publishes no per-patient score) and call 1 = no sustained clearance (failing): the marker arm is ctDNA-positive at the assessment sample (the paper's detection criterion, consumed from the dataset's <marker>__detected rows, with a value-above-detection_threshold fallback), and the paper's recurrence-free conjunct also makes call 1 when the patient had disease recurrence by the 6-month timepoint. The benchmark has no native slot for the recurrence status, so the wrapper takes it from a numeric cov_* column named by the setting recurrence_covariate (1 = disease recurrence by the 6-month timepoint, 0 = free of recurrence by then), given with covariates=True; without it the wrapper runs the marker arm alone (the recurrence-free conjunct is recorded as unavailable and reported in run.json). No probability of its own (TxResBench converts the risk). At fit the paper's endpoint is evaluated on the training cohort: the clearance proportion with an exact (Clopper-Pearson) 95% CI and the two-conjunct attribution, using the recurrence covariate when given, else the benchmark's progression outcome as the recurrence surrogate; a patient with no assessment draw or (in the full-rule arm) no recurrence status gets no prediction, with the reason in note.

methods.description: A per-patient call from the serial plasma ctDNA trajectory of the first 60 days of a FOLFIRI-based first-line treatment (Lyskjær et al. 2019, Scientific Reports; 24 enrolled / 22 ddPCR-evaluable / 21 analysed metastatic colorectal cancer patients, one patient-specific mutation quantified by ddPCR per patient): the patient's ctDNA levels of the drawn samples are put in order (pre-treatment C10 at day 0, then C17 day 7, C20 day 14, C27 day 21, C414 first radiological status evaluation day 60), each sample is compared with the previously drawn blood sample, and each strictly higher level is one occurrence of a temporary increase; the call is 'two temporary increases in ctDNA' when the count is two or more, vs 'less than two' otherwise (Fig. 3C: 7 called vs 14 not; the group had a shorter PFS, p = 0.01, HR 4.11 [1.27-13.36], and OS, p = 0.06, HR 3.63 [0.87-15.25]). Nothing is fitted (the count threshold and the 60-day window are the paper's; the wrapper never reads the training outcomes). It writes the count as risk (0 to 4 with the paper's five draws; higher = more temporary increases = the patient's group in the paper had the shorter PFS/OS) and the 0/1 call (1 = count >= 2 = treatment judged failing), and no probability. The wrapper's declared readings of the paper's open points, each with a method_params switch and the argument in README.md: the window is the first 60 days with the day-60 draw included, truncated at the benchmark landmark (the rule cannot use later draws); 'two occurrences' is read as count >= 2 (the Fig. 3 groups are 'Two temporary increases in ctDNA' vs 'Less than two') with an exactly-two alternative; 'a higher ctDNA level' is strict (an equal level is not an occurrence) with an equal-alt counts alternative; a below-LOD draw is the level 0 in the comparison (the harness's non-detect encoding and the literal 'higher than' reading of an undetectable-to-detectable transition), with a skip-draw alternative; a patient without a detectable pre-treatment ctDNA draw is not analysed (the paper excluded the two such patients from all ddPCR analyses) unless require_detectable_baseline is false; and a patient with fewer than three drawn samples in the window gets no prediction (only at most one comparison, and the paper excluded the patient with only C10 and C414).

methods.description: The two-stage EGFR-ctDNA turnover / Weibull progression-free-survival model of Janssen et al. (Clin Transl Sci 2022;15:1916-1925): stage 1 fits the on-treatment plasma EGFR ddPCR allele concentrations (copies/ml) with a joint nonlinear mixed-effects turnover model - zero-order growth kin minus first-order elimination kout times a time-dependent resistance R(t), dy/dt = kin - kout*y(t)*R(t), with R(t) = exp(-lambda*t) for the driver mutations (L858R and exon19del combined under shared parameters) and R(t) = exp(-lambda*y(t)) for the T790M resistance mutation; the pre-treatment baseline is unobserved, so an additional baseline parameter is estimated per patient; interindividual variability (exponential; the paper's Table 1 CV%) is on the baseline and progression factors only, with separate proportional residual errors. Stage 2 predicts the individual driver trajectory and fits the parametric Weibull time-to-event model h(t) = lambda*t^(alpha-1)*exp(beta*DriverREL) for progression-free survival, where DriverREL is the relative change in the predicted driver concentration from the estimated baseline (the paper's only retained covariate; the drug, the mutation type and all other concentration covariates were tested and rejected). The published analysis software (NONMEM 7.3, FOCE-I/Laplacian) is commercial and no control stream or code was published, so the wrapper estimates the same structural equations in Python: population parameters by pooled nonlinear least squares with proportional residuals, per-patient driver parameters (baseline, progression factor, asymptotic concentration) by a bounded search anchored on the patient's observed trajectory with the paper's IIV priors, and the Weibull by maximum likelihood. It writes the per-patient risk (the Weibull linear predictor, higher = failing) and the model's own probabilities P(event by day h | event-free at the landmark) = 1 - S(h)/S(L) for progression and death; the paper's binary-response outcomes are not modelled and their probabilities are converted by TxResBench from the risk.
methods.licence: MIT (this wrapper; the published analysis was performed in the commercial NONMEM 7.3 / PsN 4.4.8, no control stream or code was published)

methods.description: The ctDNA-positive disease-progression rule of Guan et al. (Frontiers in Oncology 2022;12:926260; DOI 10.3389/fonc.2022.926260; a prospective cohort of 40 metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma patients on first-line chemotherapy, S1 plus nab-paclitaxel in 92.5%: tumor tissue and pretreatment plasma from 40 and 35 patients; plasma ctDNA by 425-gene targeted NGS at ~30,000x depth, mutations by VarScan2 after BWA-mem/GATK; followed every 2 months with CT and blood collections until CT-confirmed progression). The paper's longitudinal rule (md:139): 'a more than 2-fold increase in MAF values for any of four primary driven genes compared with the previous test result or a change from negative to positive in any gene was considered to indicate ctDNA-positive disease progression', applied along the serial draws (pretreatment and every 2 cycles) of the four primary driver genes KRAS, TP53, CDKN2A and SMAD4; the first trigger yields the patient's ctDNA-positive PFS, which the paper compares with the radiological PFS in the 24 of 35 pretreatment-sampled patients with at least two on-treatment samples (mean 4.6 vs 5.5 months, 0.9 months earlier, p = 0.004 paired t-test / two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank; earlier in 11 patients, inconsistent in 1). The wrapper scans the patient's serial MAF trajectory up to the benchmark landmark (nothing is fitted - the rule learns nothing from the training outcomes, `fitted` false) and evaluates both branches per gene: the magnitude branch (current MAF more than 2x the previous test result, strictly greater per 'more than 2-fold') and the detection-status branch (a change from negative to positive). `call` = 1 = ctDNA-positive disease progression detected = treatment judged failing; `risk` = the geometric mean over the four genes of the gene's median observed adjacent-test fold factor (per-gene factor; the strongest-pair reading is exposed as gene_factor 'max') (the quantity the magnitude branch thresholds, the F2016 combined-criteria precedent for turning an any-gene rule into one scalar; a gene that is negative at both ends contributes factor 1 = unchanged, a detected-to-negative step contributes a decline factor below 1, an undetectable-to-detectable transition contributes the ratio to the smallest positive value with the branch firing as a flag); the strict max-over-genes reading is exposed as gene_aggregation 'max'. A patient with never a current-and-previous test result of any gene gets no prediction (empty risk, reason in note). The paper's companion analyses - the pretreatment mutation-status Kaplan-Meier/log-rank and Cox regression (md:98, Table 3), the >= 3 driver genes in tumor tissue OS association (md:90), the CA19-9/CEA/NLR/PLR associations (md:55) and the SPSS 25.0 statistics - are separate analyses and not this rule.

methods.description: The three-category Guardant360 ctDNA tumor-response-map rule of Liao et al. (JTO Clinical and Research Reports 2021;2(2):100099, DOI 10.1016/j.jtocrr.2020.100099; 15 EGFR T790M-positive advanced NSCLC patients starting second-line osimertinib 80 mg/day, prospective baseline - week-4 - progression plasma draws, Guardant360 digital NGS, no analysis code published - the rule is implemented from the Methods/Results text). At the week-4 on-treatment draw the paper classifies each patient by the map (md:50, verbatim): category 3 = 'detectable EGFR T790M or increasing EGFR-activating mutation AF at week 4' (the two criteria: T790M detectable at week 4; the EGFR-activating mutation AF - exon 19 deletion or L858R, % - increased vs the baseline draw, a DIRECTION call with no numeric cutoff, e.g. patient 15 '48.5% at baseline, 66.5% at week 4', md:46); category 2 = 'no detectable EGFR T790M and no increase in EGFR-activating mutation AF at week 4, with or without mutations in other genes' (TP53, PTEN, CDKN2A, EGFR amplification, MET amplification feed only the category-1-vs-2 distinction); category 1 = 'undetectable mutations of any kind at week 4' (a subset of category 2: no mutation of any kind implies no T790M and no AF increase). The validated call is category 3 vs combined categories 1 and 2 = early disease progression within 16 weeks of the first osimertinib dose (2/3 vs 0/12 in the paper's cohort, Fisher's exact p = 0.03, md:50, md:71; ORR 53%, median PFS 7.3 months, md:10). The wrapper takes the per-draw ctDNA series (marker-specific: required_markers - the T790M series, the EGFR-activating-AF series, the other-gene panel or a precomputed week-4 any-mutation flag), pairs each patient's baseline draw (last on or before baseline_max_day) with the evaluation draw (last in the baseline_day..landmark window, the corpus fixed-pair convention for the paper's fixed week-4 schedule), and writes risk = the paper's category ordinal (1 -> 0, 2 -> 1, 3 -> 2; higher = more likely failing; only the 3-vs-1+2 contrast is validated by the paper, so the 1-vs-2 step is the map's Fig. 3A/B/C order, documented) and call = 1 for category 3 (treatment judged failing). No probability is defined by the paper (TxResBench converts the risk). A patient the map cannot read - no usable baseline/week-4 pair of the EGFR-activating series, no week-4 T790M call and no baseline pair - gets no prediction with the reason in note; an unevaluable arm counts as not firing (two-arm OR per md:50); undetectable is a category of the map, not a missing value (below-detection = 0 and/or the <marker>__detected rows), and a week-4 undetectable activating AF is not an increase (md:44).

methods.description: The week-4 ctDNA rise-or-emergence response call of Wang et al. (The Oncologist 2020;25(8):e1188-e1194, DOI 10.1634/theoncologist.2020-0161; 18 refractory MSS colorectal cancer patients on regorafenib + nivolumab/pembrolizumab, 13 with paired Guardant360 plasma ctDNA at baseline and after cycle 1). Per patient, from the two draws: criterion A = the panel's highest mutation allele frequency (MAF, %, Fig. 2E/F) at the 4-week draw vs the baseline draw - rise or decline (direction only, the paper states no numeric cutoff); criterion B = emergence of new clones at 4 weeks - any alteration present at the 4-week draw that was not present at the baseline draw. Call: rise OR emergence = predicted progressive disease (PD) at the 2-month imaging point (call 1); decline = predicted radiographic disease stabilization (call 0); in the paper's 13-patient cohort this is 10/10 and 3/3. The wrapper takes the marker set of the per-draw panel result (rate one as the summary highest-MAF readout; every other marker is an alteration) and writes risk = the signed change of the highest MAF (baseline -> 4-week draw; the quantity the direction rule thresholds, higher = stronger rise = more likely failing) and the 0/1 call; no probability (TxResBench converts the risk). The paper leaves several cases open, each fixed by a recorded convention (README.md): flat highest MAF = not a rise (call 0); baseline non-detect read as 0; a 4-week non-detect = the extreme decline; a new clone with a declining highest MAF = the OR reading (call 1); detection of an alteration comes from its <marker>__detected row when the dataset has one (the commercial assay's own reporting limits), else from the value above detection_threshold (default 0 = the benchmark's below-detection encoding); the on-treatment draw is the last draw on or before the landmark and the baseline draw the last on or before baseline_max_day (the paper's 'after cycle 1', day 28 of the 28-day cycle). With no per-alteration marker passed the emergence arm is not evaluable and the rule falls back to criterion A, recorded in the fit report. The paper was a single 13-patient cohort with no statistics and no published code; the rule is deterministic and learns nothing from the training outcomes (fitted false).

methods.description: The per-patient week-8 ctDNA-favorable call of Lu C et al., Biomarker Research 2025;13:98 (DOI 10.1186/s40364-025-00809-8, letter to the editor; exploratory analysis of the prospective single-arm NCT03037385 cohort: 21 Chinese patients with advanced RET fusion-positive NSCLC treated with pralsetinib 400 mg once daily; plasma at baseline (within 7 days before the first dose), every 8 weeks - the first on-treatment draw = the first radiographic assessment at week 8 - and at disease progression; 52 successful samples: 20 baseline, 26 on-treatment, 6 at PD; 168-gene LungPlasma panel (Burning Rock), NovaSeq 6000, 20,000x; per-draw indices maxAF (%), cfDNA quantity-normalized MTM/mL and methylation MD ratio, md:15/MOESM1; no published analysis code - R 4.1.0 named for the statistics only, MOESM1, data on reasonable request md:80). The rule (md:28): 'Patients with extremely low ctDNA levels (maxAF < 0.1%) or ctDNA clearance (undetectable tumor-specific variants in cfDNA measured by both maxAF and MTM/mL) had significantly longer PFS [P < 0.001 (Fig.S4); P = 0.002 (Fig. 1f), respectively].' The wrapper reads each patient's baseline draw (last on or before baseline_max_day; the paper's change-from-baseline comparator, md:23) and the evaluation draw (last maxAF-series draw in (baseline_max_day, landmark_day] - the corpus fixed-pair convention for the paper's fixed week-8 first-visit schedule, md:23, MOESM1) of the per-draw ctDNA index series. Roles are identified from the marker names: maxAF/MAF/VAF/allele-frequency-like names are the maxAF series, MTM/molecules-per-mL-like names the MTM/mL series, MD-ratio/methylation names the MD ratio (identified but NOT consumed by the call, md:28); a name set identifying no role at all (e.g. the gate's M1/M2) is read positionally as the spec's marker order: markers[0] = maxAF, markers[1] = MTM/mL. call = 1 (treatment judged failing) when the patient is NOT ctDNA-favorable at the evaluation draw: favorable = (a) 'extremely low' - maxAF < 0.1% (strict, md:28; the cutoff is exposed as extralow_maxaf_percent, values read on the paper's % scale, md:15) - OR (b) clearance - the draw is undetectable by BOTH maxAF and MTM/mL (an AND, md:28); 'undetectable' reads the unit's own per-draw state (the <marker>__detected companion 0, else value 0, else value <= the draw's <marker>__lod when the unit carries a declared limit - the paper prints no numeric LOD, md:15 '?', so no threshold is invented), a positive value without a detection call is NOT undetectable, and a metric not measured at the evaluation draw is unknown (never counts as undetectable). risk = the evaluation-draw maxAF in % (the quantity the 0.1% arm thresholds; 0 for an undetectable maxAF, the favourable state): the tiering 0 (undetectable) < < 0.1% (extremely low) <= >= 0.1% (not favourable) is the rule's own order, higher = more residual ctDNA = more likely failing; the paper defines no per-patient score (its output is the group PFS/ORR association, md:28) and no probability is written (TxResBench converts the risk). A patient without the baseline or the evaluation draw gets no prediction with the reason in note (the paper defines no call for a missing week-8 draw, '?'; its ORR comparison covers 17 of 21 patients, md:28); where maxAF is flagged undetectable but its value is >= 0.1% and MTM/mL was not measured at the evaluation draw, the clearance AND is unknown and the patient is abstained (never imputed as not favourable, no LOD to resolve the value, '?'). Baseline-undetectable patients are not excluded (md:28 'All patients demonstrated a reduction in ctDNA levels by week 8'; the paper does not exclude them, '?'); the paper's two stratifications (clearance: median PFS not reached vs 4.8 months, P = 0.002, Fig. 1f; maxAF < 0.1%: P < 0.001, Fig. S4; ORR 10/14 vs 0/3, md:28) are the paper's validation, not per-patient output.

methods.description: The dCLABs-XGBoost classifier of durable clinical benefit (DCB = the confirmed absence of disease progression or death within 6 months after initiation of therapy; patients otherwise no durable benefit, NDB) from first-line immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-containing therapy in advanced gastric cancer, of Nie, Song, Xu, et al. (Gastric Cancer 2025;28:1213-1231): a gradient-boosted decision tree (xgboost 2.0.3 XGBClassifier, the paper's named package and version) on 10 dynamic clinlabomics features (dCLABs) - baseline_LDH, C2_NLR, C2_PLR, C2_ALC, C3_ALC, deltaC2_ALC, deltaC2_Eosinophil, deltaC3_LMR, deltaC3_ALB, deltaC3_ALP, where deltaCLABs = (value at the respective time - value at baseline) / value at baseline - built from 8 peripheral-blood laboratory analyses (absolute lymphocyte, monocyte, neutrophil and eosinophil counts, platelet count, lactate dehydrogenase, albumin and alkaline phosphatase) at the baseline (prior to cycle 1), C2 (prior to cycle 2) and C3 (prior to cycle 3) draws, with NLR and PLR and LMR ratios derived per draw. The model was selected as the best of nine ML algorithms (md:981-988) and fine-tuned by grid search with 10-fold cross-validation maximising AUC (md:627-631); the published optimal hyperparameters (Supplementary Table S4) - reg_lambda 0.5, min_child_weight 4, max_depth 4, learning_rate 0.3 - are the ones the wrapper fits, everything else at the package's defaults (objective binary:logistic, n_estimators 100), and the final model was retrained on the whole discovery cohort as a locked model (md:635-637). The wrapper re-implements it because no analysis code is published (the paper's code URL is a deployed Streamlit app, not a repository; codes on reasonable request): per benchmark training fold it derives the paper's DCB label from the training PFS (no durable benefit = progression or death within dcb_days = 183 days of the first dose), builds the continuous 10-feature vector from the baseline draw, the first and second on-treatment draws by the landmark (the paper's C2/C3 draws; days per cycle are not published), and fits XGBClassifier on the patients with a known label; it does NOT reproduce the paper's 70/30 training/validation split (the benchmark's own cross-validation replaces it), the unpublished grid search, the unnamed ComBat harmonization, multiple imputation and Youden dichotomization steps (each recorded in README.md and run.json), and its cohort was assembled from eleven hospitals with standardized units, which the benchmark's single-unit datasets match. risk and the own p_no_response carry the fitted P(no durable benefit), failure-oriented, so the published Youden cutoff of 0.434 applies directly: call = 1 (failing) when the probability is above it, the paper's high-risk group; the paper reports no survival calibration, so the progression/death probabilities are TxResBench conversions of the risk. Missing values are not imputed: they travel to the trees' built-in missing path (the paper's multiple-imputation implementation is unnamed); a patient without a baseline draw or without a draw during treatment by the landmark gets no prediction with the reason in note.
methods.licence: n/a (the paper publishes no analysis code - the trained model is a deployed Streamlit web application and the codes are on reasonable request; the wrapper is the author's own work, implemented from the paper and supplement; the named xgboost 2.0.3 package is Apache-2.0 per its PyPI metadata)

NLR = neutrophil-to-lymphocyte, PLR = platelet-to-lymphocyte and LMR = lymphocyte-to-monocyte (md:949-952) are derived per draw from the counts; the ratio markers are not separate input markers. methods.description: The three-category dynamic bTMB survival stratification rule of Wang Y et al. (J Natl Cancer Cent 2024, DOI 10.1016/j.jncc.2024.01.008; 103 analyzed of 128 enrolled unresectable LA-NSCLC patients on curative-intent CRT with or without consolidation ICI, two-center prospective cohort with an external 30-patient validation set; 486-gene plasma NGS on cfDNA at baseline (diagnosis), 4 weeks after completing radical CRT (post-CRT) and at progression): the patient's bTMB (mut/Mb) at the post-CRT draw minus the baseline bTMB gives dynamic delta-bTMB, and the patient is one of three categories by its sign - 'Decreased delta-bTMB (delta-bTMB < 0) represents effective treatment response after CRT, stable delta-bTMB (delta-bTMB = 0) represents the same bTMB level before and after CRT, and increased delta-bTMB (delta-bTMB > 0) indicates worse post-treatment scenarios' (md:111), with no magnitude cutoff (the paper's baseline bTMB cutoffs at 10/16/20 mut/Mb and across 4-20 mut/Mb all failed to predict OS/PFS, md:109; median delta-bTMB -1.6 mut/Mb). The category was associated with treatment failure in the expected direction: increased delta-bTMB had the significantly shortest OS (median 9.0 vs NR vs NR months, P < 0.001, Fig. 4C) and PFS (median 3.4 vs 21.0 vs 23.9 months, P < 0.001, Fig. 4D), while decreased vs stable did not differ (OS P = 0.950; PFS P = 0.900); in the external validation set increased delta-bTMB had shorter PFS (median 12.3 vs 50.8 months, P = 0.006, Fig. 6D). The wrapper takes exactly one marker (the per-draw bTMB level; declared in required_markers), reads the baseline draw (last at or before baseline_max_day) and the post-CRT draw (last after it and at or before the landmark - the paper's 4-weeks-post-CRT protocol visit has no benchmark channel; the corpus fixed-pair convention), computes delta-bTMB = post-CRT - baseline, and writes risk = the ordered category code (1 decreased / 2 stable / 3 increased, higher = worse - the paper's increased class has the significantly shortest OS/PFS) with call = 1 for increased delta-bTMB only (the paper's adverse class, 'indicates worse post-treatment scenarios'), and abstains (empty risk + note) when the baseline or the post-CRT draw is missing or its value is not usable (the paper excluded patients whose blood plasma was not collected at the prespecified time points, md:37); no per-patient probability exists (the paper defines none; the benchmark converts the risk) and nothing is learned from the training outcomes (fitted false - the category cutoffs are the prespecified zero boundary).

(md:37), with bTMB (mut/Mb) = absolute mutation count x 1,000,000 / panel exonic base num (md:47), and the call is the sign of the within-patient change between the baseline and the post-CRT draws, 'Dynamic bTMB after CRT (delta bTMB) = post-CRT bTMB level - baseline bTMB level' (md:47) categorized 'decreased delta bTMB (delta bTMB < 0)... stable delta bTMB (delta bTMB = 0)... and increased delta bTMB (delta bTMB > 0)' (md:111). bTMB is a panel-derived score, not a gene analyte: no HGNC/UniProt/LOINC/miRBase/HMDB term exists, so the id is the project's canonical marker name (cf. the bTMB id of Chen2024_EC-CRT-001 and of ctdna-btmb-combined-three-group); matching is case-insensitive. methods.description: The Cox proportional-hazards association of the DIRECTION of the change in the cancer-specific methylation score (CSM) between the baseline (SB) and the cycle-3 day-1 (C3B) cfMeDIP-seq draws with OS and PFS (Stutheit-Zhao EY et al., Cancer Discovery 2024;14(3):454-469, DOI 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-23-1060; 53 patients with both draws in the INSPIRE pembrolizumab pan-cancer cohort, 5 histology cohorts INS-A..E): per patient the change direction is coded 'Increase' (C3B > SB) / 'Decrease' (SB > C3B) / 'Same' (equal, dropped as NA - Rmd:905-918) by the RAW sign of the difference (the paper's Delta CSM = log10(0.01 + score) difference, Rmd:395, is sign-identical), and one Cox proportional-hazards model per endpoint, coxph(Surv(time, event) ~ change + cohort) (scripts:91-93; 'All survival analyses were undertaken with a Cox proportional hazards model incorporating the parameter(s) of interest as well as the research cohort as a categorical variable.', md:193), reports the adjusted hazard ratio per CSM DECREASE ('changeDecrease', levels order Increase first): OS aHR 0.40 (0.21-0.75) P = 0.005, PFS aHR 0.35 (0.18-0.69) P = 0.003 (Fig. 3B), and the multivariable variant (cohort + PD-L1 fraction = pdl1_percent/100 + log TMB, Rmd:1180-1191) gives OS aHR 0.45 (0.23-0.88) P = 0.019 and PFS aHR 0.37 (0.19-0.74) P = 0.005 (Fig. 3C). The wrapper (the paper's own published R/Rmd code reimplemented in survival 3.7-0) takes the one marker the benchmark passes (required_markers: the CSM score), x0 = the last baseline value (day <= baseline_max_day, the paper's SB) and x1 = the last on-treatment value up to the landmark (the paper's C3B, cycle-3 day 1 ~weeks 6-7; the harness carries no cycle labels), forms the direction factor, and fits one Cox per survival outcome the training data give (progression from PFS, death from OS - the paper's two endpoints) on the patients event-free at the landmark on the residual clock (identical partial likelihood; the paper's clock runs from the patient's own cycle-3 draw, os_since_C3/pfs_since_C3), adjusted for every cov_* column when covariates are passed (the paper's cohort factor is the column naming 'cohort'; without covariates the model is fitted unadjusted - the recorded deviation) - and reports the paper's multivariable variant when the covariates carry recognizable cohort/PD-L1/TMB columns. It writes risk and risk_<outcome> = the fitted Cox linear predictor (higher = the Increase group = more likely failing; the paper reports an association, not a per-patient score, so the LP is the contract's association-only convention) and p_progression_H<h> / p_death_H<h> = 1 - S(h - landmark), the model's own conditional event probabilities; the per-fold aHR (95% CI, P) per CSM decrease per outcome, the group counts and the MVA aHRs are reported in run.json. A patient with no baseline CSM value, no on-treatment draw by the landmark, or an unchanged CSM (the paper drops 'Same') gets no prediction with a note; the paper's additionally required matched bespoke-ctDNA (CMC) stream has no harness channel and is recorded.

methods.description: The joint two-feature Cox proportional-hazards model of Stutheit-Zhao et al. (Cancer Discov 2024;14(3):454-469, DOI 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-23-1060; INSPIRE, 87 patients with various metastatic cancers on pembrolizumab; 55 with both markers at both timepoints): per patient, the two change-direction factors between the baseline (SB) and cycle-3 (C3B) cfMeDIP-seq draws - CSM-change = factor(if_else(C3B - SB > 0, 'Increase', 'Decrease'), levels c('Increase','Decrease')) on the raw CSM difference (zero change coded Decrease, the authors' rule) and FLS-change = the same direction factor on the raw FLS difference - one Cox model per survival endpoint, coxph(Surv(time, event) ~ `FLS change` + `CSM change` + cohort) (OS: both terms significant, reproduced aHR per Decrease FLS 0.471, CSM 0.455; PFS: only CSM, reproduced 0.663 / 0.394; Fig. 4B/C). The wrapper takes exactly two markers (markers[0] = the per-draw CSM score, markers[1] = the per-draw FLS; roles also recognised by name, declared in required_markers with the positional fallback documented in the README), maps SB = the last value at day <= baseline_max_day and C3B = the last value by the landmark (day > baseline_max_day, day <= landmark) per marker, fits one Cox per survival outcome the training data give (progression, death) on the patients with a complete direction pair who are event-free at the landmark on the residual clock, with every cov_* column when covariates are passed (the paper's cohort adjuster has no harness channel) and none otherwise, and writes risk and risk_<outcome> = the fitted linear predictor (per level pair, so Increase in either biomarker is the higher-risk side, matching the paper's aHR per Decrease < 1) and p_progression_H<h> / p_death_H<h> = 1 - S(h - landmark) from the fitted Cox. The paper reports the cohort-level adjusted hazard ratios (no per-patient score or probability), so the per-fold fit reports them in run.json and the per-patient columns are the wrapper's projection of the published model.

methods.description: The delta-CTC-score direction-of-change rule and the stratified multivariable Cox analysis of Hong et al. (PNAS 2018;115(12):3094-3099, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1719264115; 49 metastatic-melanoma patients on ipilimumab or pembrolizumab, prospective): the per-draw CTC-19 score is built from the fixed 19-marker melanoma CTC RNA signature — sum over the 19 markers of (Transcript_i - (HD median_i + 2 x SD_HD,i)), floored at 0 (SI:143-151); at the 7-wk conditional landmark the delta-CTC = (7-wk measurement - baseline) is divided by direction only into 'reduced' (<= 0) and 'increased' (> 0) (SI:75-77, SI:137-139), and the group is the predictor of stratified multivariable Cox models of PFS, TTNT and OS adjusted for the candidate clinical set (baseline CTC-score high/low at the prespecified 14,732 cutoff, gender, age > 65, disease stage, brain metastasis, primary site, <3 vs >=3 metastatic sites, prior metastatic therapy, treatment; SI:91-107) and STRATIFIED by baseline LDH (SI:95-97), fit with backward/forward/stepwise selection in SAS 9.4 (no published code; the paper reports PFS HR 0.17 (0.05-0.62, P = 0.008), TTNT HR 0.22 (0.06-0.79, P = 0.02), OS HR 0.12 (0.02-0.91, P = 0.04), leave-one-out jackknife in Table S4). The wrapper computes the score over the markers it is given (the required 19-gene panel identified by name; when the names do not match, every passed marker is used, recorded), takes the baseline as the last draw on or before baseline_max_day and the 7-wk measurement as the last draw after it and at or before the landmark (the SI's latest at or before 7 wk), writes risk = the delta-CTC score (the quantity the published rule thresholds; higher = increase = more likely failing) and call 1 = increased / 0 = reduced, and fits the Cox per survival outcome the training data give (PFS -> progression, OS -> death; the paper's TTNT has no benchmark outcome channel) on the patients event-free at the landmark with the delta-CTC group and the baseline CTC-score category plus every cov_* column when covariates are passed, stratified by a cov_* column naming LDH when one is given; it writes risk_<outcome> = the Cox linear predictor and p_<outcome>_H* = 1 - S(H - L) of the fitted model, reports the group hazard ratios and the leave-one-out jackknife in run.json, and records the documented differences: the per-marker 36-HD background values are not published (marker_background parameter, default 0 = no subtraction), the paper's selection criteria and retained covariate sets are not published (the wrapper fits the full candidate set, keeping the delta-CTC group in every model), the baseline CTC high/low category uses the published 14,732 cutoff, and the Cox is unstratified when no LDH covariate is given.

methods.description: Per-patient prognostic association of the change in the fragment-length score (FLS) between the baseline and cycle-3 cfMeDIP-seq draws with progression-free and overall survival in the INSPIRE pembrolizumab cohort (Stutheit-Zhao EY, Sanz-Garcia E, Liu Z, et al., Cancer Discovery 2024;14(3):454-469, DOI 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-23-1060; 87 patients, 204 samples; 55 patients have both baseline (SB) and cycle-3 (C3B) FLS draws): per patient Delta FLS = FLS(C3B) - FLS(SB) on the raw FLS scale, grouped by direction only into a two-level factor (Increase when Delta FLS > 0, Decrease otherwise - an exactly-zero change is coded Decrease by the paper's if_else > 0 rule), and a Cox proportional-hazards model fitted as coxph(Surv(time, event) ~ change + cohort) per survival outcome, where the paper reports the adjusted hazard ratio per FLS DECREASE: OS aHR = 0.40 (0.20-0.77), P = 0.006 and PFS aHR = 0.51 (0.26-1.00), P = 0.0503 (Fig. 4A; aHR < 1 = decrease is favourable; the multivariable variant of Supplementary Fig. S16 adds PD-L1 and log TMB: reproduced OS aHR = 0.465 (0.238-0.906) P = 0.024, PFS aHR = 0.566 (0.286-1.118) P = 0.101). The wrapper takes the one marker the benchmark passes (required_markers: the fragment-length score) and exactly two draws per patient: x0 = the last FLS draw at day <= baseline_max_day (the paper's baseline SB) and x1 = the last FLS draw after it and at or before the landmark day (the paper's cycle-3 day-1 draw, C3B, around weeks 6-7 on treatment; the harness carries no cycle labels), forms the direction group at the fixed published rule (the paper's if_else > 0), and fits one Cox per survival outcome the training data give (progression from PFS, death from OS) of the group plus every cov_* column when covariates are passed - reference-coded for categorical columns, continuous for numeric ones - on the patients event-free at the landmark on the residual clock (the paper's own clock is months since the patient's cycle-3 draw; the benchmark's day-since-first-dose times minus the landmark reproduce the same estimand), and writes risk and risk_<outcome> = the fitted linear predictor (higher = more likely failing: the paper's 'Decrease' level, the favourable one, carries a negative coefficient - its aHR is 0.40 for OS), and p_progression_H<h> / p_death_H<h> = 1 - S(h - landmark) from the fitted Cox, the model's own conditional event probabilities. The paper's reported cohort-level quantity - the aHR (95% CI, P) for the FLS-decrease direction per outcome - is reported per training fold in run.json together with the group counts, the coefficients, the fitted formula and the documented differences. The paper reports no per-patient score, probability or call (its Fig. 4A output is the two-group KM curves and the aHR), so the per-patient risk is the wrapper's own projection of the published model, and the paper's cohort adjustment is realised by the benchmark's cov_* columns when they are passed (with no covariates the model is unadjusted - a recorded deviation from 'All survival analyses were undertaken with a Cox proportional hazards model incorporating the parameter(s) of interest as well as the research cohort as a categorical variable', md:193); the paper's method also computes KM curves per group (survfit/ggsurvplot) which the wrapper reports in run.json and does not write as curves.

methods.description: DIREct-On (Nabet et al., Cell 2020): a Bayesian probit classifier of durable clinical benefit from the early on-treatment change in one ctDNA marker (first on-treatment value divided by the pre-treatment value), optionally with baseline covariates such as normalised bTMB and CD8 fraction. The probit prior comes from subsample fits on the training patients, the posterior from Gibbs sampling, and the score is the median posterior probability of benefit. It writes risk and p_no_response (one minus that probability) and a call at the Youden threshold derived on the training patients. A patient with a zero baseline, or without an early on-treatment value, gets no prediction.

methods.description: The paper's method 4, 'Doubling time' (van Delft et al., Heliyon 2022;8(10):e10932; NSCLC immunotherapy, non-response at 6 months): at every consecutive measurement pair of one serum tumour marker (the paper fits each of CYFRA 21.1, CEA, CA-125, NSE and SCC separately, with per-marker thresholds), the marker's doubling time is computed as DT = (day2 - day1) x ln(2) / ln(value2 / value1) (Figure 1C). A patient is called a non-responder when two consecutive measurements both exceed an upper threshold of relevancy (UTR), or when the test score - the smallest positive doubling time among the pairs whose current value is at or above a lower threshold of relevancy (LTR) - is below the test-condition threshold (positive test results below the LTR are ignored; the logical-test outcome is used at an upward UTR crossing). The three decision thresholds are fitted on the training cohort to maximize sensitivity at 95% specificity (the paper's anchor), with the paper's data cleaning (consecutive measurements less than 5 days or more than 30 days apart are excluded, and a baseline measurement with more than 2 values in the window is required; min_draws 3). The wrapper writes the per-day log fold change of the marker (g = ln2 / DT) as risk - the quantity the rule thresholds, re-oriented so that higher = failing (the paper's DT is anti-oriented: a shorter doubling time means faster growth and failure, and negative for falling markers) - and the 0/1 call, and no probability (the paper defines none; the benchmark converts the risk). It takes one marker and uses the draws on or before the landmark as the observation window; the paper's threshold search, the direction of the doubling-time test and the boundary conventions are not published - the wrapper's reading and search are documented in the README and run.json.

methods.description: The per-patient four-class biological response call (bR/bS/bP/NE) of digital PCR ctDNA kinetics at the first on-treatment monitoring point, as defined and validated for metastatic BRAF/NRAS-mutated melanoma on anti-PD1 by Herbreteau et al., Cancers 2021;13:1826 (DOI 10.3390/cancers13081826; 49-patient validation cohort, pooled 102; criteria prespecified in the derivation research Herbreteau et al., Oncotarget 2018;9:25265-25276, DOI 10.18632/oncotarget.25404). ctDNA (BRAF or NRAS mutated copies/mL of plasma) is quantified by digital PCR at baseline and at the first follow-up point (week 2, or week 4 when no week-2 sample); the two concentrations are compared by a one-sided Z test at alpha = 2.5% on the PROPORTION of dPCR mutation-positive microcompartments - i.e. the change must exceed the assay's own measurement imprecision ('The repeatability of the measurement can be estimated from the standard error of this proportion', md:182-183) - with an undetectable point entered as 'below 1/total number of microcompartments' (md:188-190). Classes (Table 1, md:128-155): biological Response (bR) = significant decrease vs baseline; biological Progression (bP) = significant increase vs nadir (with the two points evaluated here the nadir is the lower of the two); biological Stability (bS) = neither, with baseline high enough to identify a bR if ctDNA became undetectable; Non-evaluable (NE) = no bP and undetectable/too-low baseline. An initial bP identifies primary resistance: pooled n = 12/102 bP patients had ORR = 0%, 4-month PFS = 0%, 1-year OS = 13% (md:856-858), HR vs bR 12.74 [3.81-53.25], p < 0.0001 (md:737-738); the whole cohort had 64/102 NE (63%). The wrapper takes the one marker the benchmark passes (the ctDNA concentration series of the tracked mutation), reconstructs the microcompartment proportions with the Poisson law and the papers' own conversion constants (1 mutated copy per assay = 4 mutated copies/mL, the detection limit; 20,000-well chip - the derivation research; the 2021 paper says 'several thousand microcompartments'), writes the Z statistic as risk (higher = more likely failing), call = 1 for bP (the paper's primary-resistance call; bR/bS/NE = 0, the paper's own Fig. 3 grouping), and no probability; the closed form of the Z test is not published in either paper, so the wrapper's reconstruction is a recorded deviation (README), and the NE 'too low' bound is implemented as the paper's own operational statement (the baseline must significantly exceed the undetectable-boundary proportion).

methods.description: The pre/post-treatment dynamic change of the two LASSO-selected plasma small RNA features as a monitoring biomarker of response to combination immunotherapy in advanced gastric cancer (Fang, Sun, Yu, et al., Cancer Medicine 2025;14(21):e71339, DOI 10.1002/cam4.71339): from the paired plasma sRNA sequencing values (TMM-normalised CPM, md:72) of 49 discovery patients (34 responders / 15 non-responders, all with paired baseline + post-two-21-day-cycle samples, md:40/md:157), differentially expressed sRNAs were screened (paired Wilcoxon p < 0.05, subgroup re-test, concordant-direction removal, md:74), LASSO feature selection retained the non-zero features hsa-miR-320c and hsa-miR-26b-5p (md:223), and each of the two per-patient CHANGES was used ALONE as a response discriminant (ROC AUC 1.00, 95% CI 0.73-0.92 for hsa-miR-320c and 0.81, 0.68-0.93 for hsa-miR-26b-5p, Figure 4B, md:223: 'responders demonstrated a significant downregulation of hsa-miR-320c (p = 0.006) and a significant upregulation of hsa-miR-26b-5p (p = 0.007)', md:223) and patients were further stratified by the DIRECTION of the change with Kaplan-Meier/log-rank PFS and OS (decreased hsa-miR-320c: median PFS 9.17 vs 3.03 months, p < 0.001; OS 16.43 vs 10.23, p = 0.115; elevated hsa-miR-26b-5p: PFS 9.17 vs 3.03, p = 0.382; OS 21.17 vs 12.88, p = 0.229; md:225; the model was assessed on the training set only and was NOT validated, md:158/md:238). The wrapper takes exactly the two sRNAs (required_markers: the miRBase v21 mature accessions; the LASSO selection that produced them is upstream and not reproducible from the benchmark's two-marker input, so this is a fixed-list rule): roles by the marker names when they identify the sRNAs (hsa-miR-320c = the risk marker - the paper's headline monitoring sRNA with the significant PFS split and AUC 1.00 - and hsa-miR-26b-5p = the companion), else by sorted order, markers[0] = the risk marker (the corpus fixed-list convention; the gate's M1 plays it); per patient and marker the change is Delta = CPM(post) - CPM(baseline) with the baseline draw = the marker's last draw on or before baseline_max_day and the post draw = its last draw after that and at or before the landmark (the paper's after-two-cycles sample at the benchmark's landmark; draws after the landmark never enter; a non-detect participates as its recorded 0); the wrapper writes as risk the Delta of the risk marker, signed so that higher = more likely failing - the sign is oriented at fit from the training patients' failure label (the paper's own R-vs-NR group comparison, reproduced with a two-sample Wilcoxon on the training fold; the paper's published direction, decrease favourable for hsa-miR-320c / increase favourable for hsa-miR-26b-5p, md:223, is the recorded fallback when the fold cannot orient it), and writes no call and no probability of its own: the paper defines no decision cutoff (the per-feature ROC AUCs are cohort evaluations; the direction split's 'decreased'/'elevated' reference group is not stated, '?') and no per-patient probability, so the roster group response-probability is recorded as a deviation and the contract classification is static-risk, one score at the landmark (the same resolution as the sibling per-feature wrappers c3-two-spot-delta-roc and cd8-delta-polyfx-psi). The paper's published cohort outputs - the two AUCs with their CIs, the four median PFS/OS pairs and the four log-rank p-values - are reported in run.json as printed, never fitted; the fit also records the training-fold per-feature direction-group Kaplan-Meier summaries on the harness clock as diagnostics. A patient without a scorable baseline + post-baseline pair of the risk marker gets no prediction with the reason in note (all 49 discovery patients were paired, md:40; the paper defines no imputation).

methods.description: DynPG - Dynamic prediction of Patient and kidney Graft survival (Chabeau et al., Clin Epidemiol 2026;18:572750, DOI 10.2147/CLEP.S572750, reusing the model of Fournier et al., Nephrol Dial Transplant 2019;34:1961-1969, DOI 10.1093/ndt/gfz027, externally validated in Lenain et al., Transplantation 2021;105:396-403): a shared-random-effects joint model of log serum creatinine and the time to patient and kidney graft failure, whose equations and parameters the 2019 paper publishes - a linear mixed-effects submodel (log marker, random intercept and slope, no baseline covariates) linked to a Weibull proportional-hazards survival submodel by the current value and the current slope of the marker trajectory (the two alphas), with the six DynPG baseline variables (recipient age at transplantation, graft rank, history of cardiovascular disease, pretransplantation anti-HLA class I immunization, 3-month serum creatinine, acute rejection episode during the first year post-transplantation) and the before-2008 period adjustment in the survival submodel; the per-patient dynamic prediction is the probability of being graft-failure-free from the landmark time s to a chosen horizon (paper: the 5-year sliding window, pi = S(s+5)/S(s); Chabeau also the 11-year final horizon, pi = S(11)/S(s)), conditioned on being event-free at s and on the marker trajectory known at s. The published model was fitted once on the DIVAT learning set (n=2,749) whose data are not a benchmark unit and whose random-effects/residual variance components and standardization constants are not published, so the wrapper refits the published specification on the training set (the benchmark's standard for fitted methods) and evaluates the fit on the marker history up to the benchmark's landmark (contract 2.0: long_full at fit, long at predict, last.time = landmark, JM::survfitJM Monte Carlo); the paper's graft-failure composite endpoint is mapped to the benchmark's progression outcome (pfs_time/pfs_event), risk = the fitted model's probability of failure by the first horizon, p_progression_H<h> = its own probability at each horizon (death and the response outcomes are converted by TxResBench from the risk). The wrapper's readings of the paper's open points (the benchmark clock origin and absolute-horizon per call vs the paper's post-transplantation landmark grid; the name-mapped cov_* columns carrying the six variables with numeric ones standardized on the training patients like the paper; non-detected values excluded from the log; the documented covariate-free slice when no mapped covariate is present; 2008-period term only when a transplant-year column is named; the fallback above) are in method.json params, README.md and run.json.

methods.description: The early PD-1+ CD8 T-cell response rule of Kamphorst et al. (PNAS 2017, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1705327114), from two flow-cytometry markers on peripheral blood: markers[0] is the frequency of Ki-67+ cells among CD8 T cells (%), markers[1] the frequency of PD-1+ cells among Ki-67+ CD8 T cells (%). Per patient, the fold increase of the Ki-67+ CD8 T-cell frequency from the baseline draw is computed at every on-treatment draw; a maximum fold increase of at least 1.5 is an immunologically responsive patient; the response is early when it is first detected within 4 weeks of treatment initiation (the paper's delayed class is a response first detected after 6 weeks); an early response is PD-1+ when the responding Ki-67+ CD8 T cells are predominantly PD-1+ at the best early response draw (the wrapper reads 'predominantly' as a strict majority, > pd1_predominance_cutoff_pct = 50%, because the paper states no numeric cutoff). An early PD-1+ CD8 T-cell response is call 0 (the paper's favorable group, 57% vs 15.4% partial response); absent, delayed or PD-1neg responses are call 1 (treatment judged failing). It writes the maximum fold increase as risk (the quantity the 1.5-fold condition thresholds, so higher risk = larger proliferative response) and no probability; a baseline Ki-67+ frequency of zero leaves the fold undefined and the patient gets no prediction, with the reason in note.

methods.description: Univariable Cox proportional-hazards regression of progression-free survival on the per-patient 'early CRP decline' feature (EarlyDeltaCRPmax = the maximum per-cent decline of plasma CRP from the baseline value to the lowest value within the first 8 weeks after anti-PD-1/PD-L1 initiation, patients with CRP increase set to 0) - the exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis of Riedl et al. (Cancers 2020;12(8):2319, DOI 10.3390/cancers12082319; 90 advanced NSCLC patients on ICI monotherapy in Graz; analysis n = 74 with observed baseline and 8-week CRP data; 'each 10% reduction in CRP predicted for a 0.9-fold reduction in PFS risk (HR = 0.91, 95% CI: 0.83-0.99, p = 0.036)', md:214 - plus the binary early-decline grouping at a 15.6% cutoff 'derived using Youden's Index' used for the paper's Figure 6 (md:217; sample-derived grouping cut, not a prediction threshold). The wrapper takes exactly one marker (the per-draw plasma CRP value as reported; required_markers LOINC 1988-5), takes the baseline as the last draw on or before baseline_max_day, takes the feature as the maximum per-cent decline from that baseline to the minimum value over the draws after the baseline up to min(landmark, feature_window_days) (the paper's first 8 weeks = 56 days; the benchmark's landmark truncates), clamps it to [0, 100] with increases set to 0, and fits ONE univariable Cox per survival outcome the training data give (progression from PFS, the paper's own endpoint, and death from OS, the same model structure) on the patients event-free at the landmark on the residual clock. It writes risk and risk_<outcome> = the fitted linear predictor (higher = more likely failing; the decline feature enters with a negative coefficient, like the paper's HR < 1) and p_progression_H<h>/p_death_H<h> = 1 - S(h - landmark) from the fitted Cox, the model's own conditional event probabilities. The paper publishes no code (Stata 15.0 environment only, md:53) and no per-patient score, so the wrapper is its own reimplementation in survival, the fold-fitted coefficients are the benchmark's own estimates (the published HR per 10% reduction 0.91 is reported in run.json for comparison), and the Figure-6 15.6% cutoff is recorded in run.json as the paper's grouping constant, not emitted as a call (the ROC outcome of the Youden derivation is not stated in the paper).

methods.description: The T0/T1 cfDNA EGFR mutation-status-pair three-group rule of A2021 (Journal of Cancer Research and Clinical Oncology 2021, DOI 10.1007/s00432-021-03658-8; 30 EGFR-mutated NSCLC patients, ASUI Trieste 2016-2019, 22 on EGFR-TKIs): the EGFR mutation detection state of the plasma cfDNA sample (real-time PCR, Diatech Easy EGFR / EasyPGX ready EGFR kit, exons 18-21, sensitivity up to 0.5%) is read at two draws - T0 at the same time of diagnosis or before starting the target treatment (md:29) and T1 during anti-EGFR-TKI therapy, proposed for patients on therapy for at least 4 months and/or with early signs of clinical disease progression, taken at the same time as the CT scan (md:31) - and the patient is assigned one of the three observed status-pair groups: group A = mutation at T0 and T1 (n = 9), group B = mutation at T0, no mutation at T1 (n = 4, the negativization group), group C = no mutation at T0 and no mutation at T1 (n = 6* in Table 3; n = 5 in the survival analysis); the remaining pair (no mutation at T0, mutation at T1) is unobserved and unassigned ('No change from no mutation to mutation has been detected during the two time points', md:102). The paper's evaluation of the grouping - per-group 12-month Kaplan-Meier PFS (22.2% / 50.0% / 66.7%) and OS (55.6% / 75.0% / 100%) with log-rank tests (md:38, md:117, md:122, md:136) and Fisher's exact test of the PD/SD association (9/0, 1/3, 2/4 PD/SD; all 9 mutation-on-T1 patients in PD, p = 0.003, md:104) - is cohort-level and not part of the per-patient call. The wrapper takes the pooled cfDNA EGFR mutation detection state (required_markers, HGNC EGFR; per-variant series pooled per draw, T790M included), pairs each patient's baseline draw (last on or before baseline_max_day, the paper's T0) and on-treatment draw (last after it up to the landmark, the corpus fixed-pair convention for the paper's variable T1), reads each draw's detection call from its <marker>__detected companion row when present (else a documented value rule: 0/1 status, else value 0 = not detected, else a quantitative level against detection_threshold, defaulting to the training median for uncalibrated input), and writes risk = the group ordinal 0/1/2 (C/B/A - the paper's own ordering, higher = worse) with call = 1 for group A only (both draws mutation-positive, the paper's adverse class: 100% PD, p = 0.003, shortest 12-month PFS/OS). No probability is written: the paper defines no per-patient probability, so TxResBench converts the risk. A patient without both usable draws, or with the paper's unobserved (no mutation at T0, mutation at T1) pair, gets no prediction with the reason in note. Nothing is learned from the training outcomes (fitted false: the per-draw call is the assay result and the groups are fixed by the paper, which publishes no analysis code); the per-group KM/log-rank and PD/SD results are recomputed on the training cohort and reported in run.json.

methods.description: The per-draw EpiScore diagnostic of Espi-Bastien et al. (Sci Rep 2026, DOI 10.1038/s41598-026-62035-y; 14 EGFR-mutant metastatic NSCLC patients on first-line erlotinib (n=9) or osimertinib (n=5) TKI, plasma ELISA at diagnosis and at disease progression, md:434-437): 'an integrated EpiScore was calculated as the sum of m1A-cfRNA, 5mC-cfDNA, H3K23Ac-cfnucleosome, and H4R3me2-cfnucleosome levels measured at diagnosis and at progression' (md:442-444) - an UNWEIGHTED raw sum of the four plasma epimark global levels at one draw, evaluated by ROC/AUC against the within-patient sample-timepoint label (diagnosis vs progression; 14 paired samples each): 'ROC curve analysis demonstrated that the EpiScore accurately distinguished diagnosis from progression (AUC=0.9541), with no significant difference compared to m1A-cfRNA alone (p=0.4982).' (md:445-447). The wrapper takes exactly the four fixed markers (required_markers, match all - the method IS this four-term sum; the same paper's methyl-cfRNA score m1A+m6A+m5C+m7G, md:411-415, is a different score), computes the per-draw sum for the patient's LAST on-treatment draw (day > baseline_max_day) at or before the landmark carrying all four finite non-negative values (a day is one draw, the max over the day's rows; a below-detection value of 0 participates as 0 - the paper states no LOD/undetectable handling and no imputation, so none is invented), and writes it as risk with identity orientation: higher EpiScore = the progression side = the failure direction (the paper's raw sum discriminates progression on the high side, md:440-447; no sign transformation is described for the sum and none is applied, with the 5mC-cfDNA decrease at progression recorded as a caveat of the raw sum). The paper defines NO operating cutoff, NO per-patient call and NO per-patient probability (the AUC 0.9541 and the comparison p=0.4982 are cohort-level statistics; md:445-447), so the wrapper writes risk only - no call, no own probability (TxResBench converts the risk per outcome) - and, like the sibling ROC/score wrappers, the contract classification is static-risk (one score at the landmark) even though the survey/roster group of the method is response-call: recorded as a deviation, not silently. The paper publishes no analysis code (GraphPad Prism Version 10.5.0 only, md:363-364; data on request, md:1048-1050), so the wrapper is the deterministic rule and the score's value is the data's own assay readout (the paper states no units for any of the four ELISA kits, md:202-225 - a raw sum across different kit scales may be dominated by the largest-scale marker, which the paper does not address). A patient with no on-treatment draw by the landmark, or none carrying all four epimarks with valid levels, gets no prediction with the reason in note (the paper defines no fallback for a missing marker or draw). Nothing is learned from the training outcomes (fitted false): the fit step records the marker roles, the draw convention, the training counts and the paper's reported statistics.

methods.description: The per-case therapy-response call of Keup et al. (Cells 2021;10(2):212, DOI 10.3390/cells10020212; 27 HR+ HER2- metastatic breast cancer patients, blood at disease progression (TP0) and two subsequent 3-monthly staging points (TP1, TP2), cfDNA targeted NGS on a 17-gene QIAseq panel, per-variant VAFs in Supplementary Table S3): for each case (patient x consecutive staging draw pair with an ESR1 or PIK3CA cfDNA variant DETECTED at both endpoints, n = 15) the delta-VAF = VAF(current draw) - VAF(immediately preceding draw) is computed ('For samples with variants detected at two consecutive time points (n = 15), the difference between the VAFs at the two time points was computed.', md:217), and the direction is the call: VAF increase -> non-response (progression, treatment judged failing, call 1), VAF decrease -> response (call 0) - the association was significant jointly for ESR1 OR PIK3CA (two-tailed Mann-Whitney U p = 0.014 on the continuous delta-VAF; two-tailed Fisher's exact p = 0.007 on the increase/decrease, accuracy 87%, md:217); neither gene alone was significant (md:217). The wrapper writes risk = the per-case delta-VAF (the quantity the sign call thresholds, in percent-of-VAF units via value_to_pct; higher = more increase = more likely failing) and call = 1 for a strict increase, 0 for a decrease. It learns nothing from the training outcomes (fitted false): the rule is exactly the paper's two-draw direction inspection. Per the paper's exclusion of non-detected variants ('we refrained from including non-detected variants for VAF difference calculation, since we could not rule out false negative results', md:263), a variant not detected at both endpoints does not enter the case and 0-imputation is never applied; a patient whose current consecutive pair has no qualifying variant gets no prediction (empty risk, reason in note), exactly as the paper's analysis set is only the detected-at-both-endpoints cases. The wrapper takes one or more ESR1/PIK3CA per-variant VAF series (each variant a marker, the tidy per-mutation convention): roles are resolved by name (esr1/pik3ca cues) with the positional fallback markers[0] = ESR1 series, markers[1] = PIK3CA series for generic names such as the gate's M1/M2; several variants are combined per patient-case by case_agg ('sum' (default): the case's delta-VAF is the change of the cumulative allele frequency of the detected ESR1/PIK3CA variants - the only multi-variant per-time-point numeric treatment the paper itself uses, the Figure 7 index-patient display, md:242; 'max_abs': the strongest delta-VAF development is the case's value - the paper's per-case aggregation for polyclonal patients is not defined, md:217 '?'; mean/max/min are the other declared readings), the case is the pair ending at the last draw by the landmark (case_window 'current' - the second time point of a pair carries the RECIST label, md:220; 'any' evaluates every consecutive pair and reports the strongest). It writes no probability (the paper defines none per patient; p = 0.014 / p = 0.007 / accuracy 87% are cohort-level test results, md:217), so TxResBench converts the risk.

methods.description: The per-patient EV-KRAS MAF dynamics classification of Chopra A et al., 'KRAS Mutation Allele Frequency Dynamics in Plasma Extracellular Vesicles: Association with Survival in Localized Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma' (Annals of Surgical Oncology 2026, DOI 10.1245/s10434-025-18633-7; 44 patients with tissue-confirmed KRAS-mutant localized pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma on neoadjuvant therapy followed by curative-intent surgery, UPMC biorepository STUDY19060127, enrolled 2019-2021): EV-associated KRAS mutation allele frequency (EV-KRAS MAF, %) is measured by single-plex ddPCR (validated detection threshold 0.01% MAF) at three fixed clinical time points - (1) at diagnosis before any cancer therapy, (2) on the day of surgery (completion of NAT, before resection) and (3) one month after curative resection - each draw is called detectable/non-detectable, and the patient is assigned one of three groups, verbatim (md:26-28): ND = no detectable EV-KRAS MAF at any of the three time points; DD = detectable EV-KRAS MAF, either at diagnosis or after completion of NAT, that decreased to non-detectable levels after curative resection; ID = detectable EV-KRAS MAF that exhibited increasing levels after completing NAT or curative resection; fluctuating patients are categorized by the final time point, one month post-surgery (md:28-30), and the paper grouped all 44 patients (ND/DD/ID = 29/8/7, md:55), so every one of the eight detectability permutations belongs to a group (ND = all three non-detectable; DD = non-detectable at the one-month draw with detectability before it; ID = detectable at the one-month draw - persistence or increase, md:17 - 4 permutations including (d,d,d), recorded as the wrapper's reading of the printed definitions, since the complete logic table (Supplemental Table 1) is not provided). The classes were associated with survival: rmDFS 31.2/27.8/9.8 months and rmOS 40.3/35.7/17.7 months for ND/DD/ID (p = 0.010/0.012), multivariable ID HR 6.95 (2.00-24.16, p = 0.002) for OS and 6.14 (2.04-18.41, p = 0.001) for DFS adjusted for surgical margin status and LN involvement, Harrell's C 0.840 (OS) / 0.794 (DFS) (md:65, md:69) - the survival statistics are the paper's cohort-level validation of the call, recorded in the fit report and not reproduced by the wrapper. The wrapper takes exactly one marker (the EV-KRAS MAF %; declared in required_markers), reads the three draws as the last baseline draw (diagnosis), the last on-treatment draw before the final one (day of surgery) and the last draw by the landmark (one month post-surgery - the benchmark's classification time), and writes risk = the EV-KRAS MAF (%) of the final (one-month-post-surgery) draw - the level the rule's final detectability call is made on (the benchmark's below-detection encoding reports a non-detectable draw as value 0, so the risk is 0 after clearance; higher = more likely failing, the paper's direction: ND longest, ID shortest rmDFS/rmOS, md:65) - and call = 1 for ID only (the paper's adverse class and multivariable ID indicator), no probability of its own (TxResBench converts the risk); the paper's three-level group (ND/DD/ID) itself is not carried in the predictions table (the benchmark keeps one risk per patient; the group is reported per cohort in the fit report, the corpus convention of a rule writes the quantity it thresholds as risk). A patient missing any of the three draws, or with an unknown detectability call at one of them, gets no prediction with the reason in note (the paper's complete case, md:22). The per-draw detection call is taken from the marker's __detected rows when present (the benchmark's below-detection encoding), else value >= detection_threshold (method_params; set 0.01 for the paper's validated 0.01% MAF on the percent scale), else 0/1 values, else the training median of the levels as a documented stand-in (the corpus detection-threshold convention, with a warning) - nothing is learned from the training outcomes (fitted false).

methods.description: The Feature-wise Transformer, one of the competing deep-learning models of SHERLOC (Mamann et al., bioRxiv 2026.06.04.730097), a framework for survival analysis of longitudinal on-treatment ctDNA in the IMpower150 metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC cohort (atezolizumab-based therapy). The input is a short ctDNA matrix (the paper: C = 21 channels - 17 gene-level VAFs mutated in >= 5% of the cohort plus 4 panel-level features - by T = 4 clinical timepoints); each longitudinal feature is one token of dimension T; a BatchNorm over the feature axis and a single-head scaled dot-product self-attention weight the feature tokens; the attention output is concatenated with a frozen 2-dimensional-per-timestep genomic-interaction embedding (the paper pretrains an MLP on the 22,068-patient pan-cancer MSK-CHORD solid-biopsy cohort with a Cox loss) and baseline clinical covariates, passed through Dropout(0.4) and one linear layer whose sigmoid output is the Cox log-risk, trained by the negative log-partial likelihood. The wrapper fits that model on the benchmark training patients and writes the fitted per-patient risk (the paper's risk score; TxResBench converts it into the benchmark's probabilities). Recorded differences from the paper: the benchmark's marker set replaces the fixed 21 channels (C = the markers handed to the method - the channel construction, not the channel identities, is the paper's definition); the frozen encoder is pretrained on the training patients because MSK-CHORD itself is not redistributed (the encoder architecture and the paper's pretraining hyperparameters are kept); the paper's T = 4 protocol visits become the draws by the benchmark landmark (baseline token + latest T-1 on-treatment draws, carry-forward padding); the final sigmoid of the authors' code is kept (the risk is sigma(eta) in (0,1)); with covariates = true every cov_* column enters the clinical branch, without it the branch is omitted; when the training data has no overall survival the Cox structure is fitted on progression-free survival; the benchmark's fold and seed replace the paper's 100-seed Monte Carlo cross-validation (an evaluation protocol). The paper's Table 2 reports for this model iAUC 73.74 +/- 3.01, C-index 66.49 +/- 2.20, IBS 19.00 +/- 0.56 (C4D1 landmark, n = 386).

methods.description: The sparse-data generalized functional linear model of Muller (Scand J Statist 2005;32(2):223-252): the one marker's sparsely and irregularly observed trajectory up to the landmark is the predictor process; its mean function, covariance surface and measurement-error variance sigma^2 are estimated by the PACE smoothing steps of Yao et al. (2005a) - run here with the same-group CRAN implementation fdapace 0.5.9 (dataType Sparse; the paper's bandwidths: 300 d for the mean and [370 d, 370 d] for the covariance, taken relative to the run's observation window exactly as the paper's were relative to its 910-day window) -, the surface's eigenfunctions give the basis of K = 2 components (the paper's choice by one-curve-leave-out CV / AIC / BIC), each patient's draws are reduced to the predicted functional principal component scores by conditional expectation E[xi_k | U_i] = lambda_k phi_ik' Sigma_Ui^-1 (U_i - mu_i), and a binomial regression with the logit link on the K scores (stats::glm; the score equation the paper solves with 'generally available software') gives the probability of the outcome. The wrapper retargets the paper's binary long-lived-group label to the benchmark's failure labels: one binomial regression per binary outcome in the training data (no_response, progressive_disease, else the event-by-horizon label of the first horizon), risk = the fitted failure probability and the model's own p_no_response / p_progressive_disease; TxResBench converts the risk for the survival outcomes. The paper's scale is log(bilirubin), so the observed marker value is log-transformed (raw lab values in the benchmark); values at or below zero (the benchmark's non-detect encoding) are replaced by half the smallest positive observed training value - the paper states no rule for them. The wrapper is deterministic and evaluates the PACE score formula itself from the fdapace fit object; the paper's class-assignment threshold (behind its leave-out misclassification rate) is not stated, so no call is written.
