methods.description: The modelled CA-125 kinetics prognostic classification (KELIM-B) of Carrot A, Corbaux P, Colomban O, You B, Freyer G et al. (CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol 2025;14:e70025, DOI 10.1002/psp4.70025; GINECO BOLD phase II, NCT04015739, bevacizumab-biosimilar + olaparib + durvalumab in 74 relapsed high-grade ovarian cancer patients, 50 CA-125-K-PD-assessable, first 100 treatment days; the KELIM-B rule itself stems from reference [1], Freyer G et al., Nat Commun 2024;15:1985, DOI 10.1038/s41467-024-45974-w): a population nonlinear mixed-effects kinetic-pharmacodynamic (K-PD) semi-mechanistic model of log-transformed serum CA-125 during the first 100 treatment days - three compartments (treatment central C1 with AMT fixed to 1, transit C2, CA-125 C3), zero-order CA-125 production KPROD (kU.mL-1.day-1) regulated by an indirect effect EFFECT(EC50) = 1 - C2/(EC50 + C2), first-order elimination KELIM (day-1), initial condition CA-125_0, and the platinum-sensitivity cohort (PRR vs PSR) as a baseline covariate on CA-125_0 and KELIM; the fit ran in the commercial NONMEM 7.5.0 with SAEM (no control stream, no dataset, no code published; the equations are published only in Supporting Information S1), so the model is specced from the paper + S1 and this wrapper uses the published final population estimates of Table 2 as a fixed population (K 1.16 day-1, KPROD 1.06 kU.mL-1.day-1, EC50 0.29 AU, CA-125_PRR,0 559.00 / CA-125_PSR,0 141.00 kU.mL-1, KELIM_PRR 0.01 / KELIM_PSR 0.02 day-1, log-scale residual W 0.29, log-normal diagonal IIV: omega^2 K 1.26, KPROD 2.92, EC50 0.31, CA-125_0 2.75, KELIM 1.67). Per patient the five individual parameters are the maximum a posteriori estimates (theta = theta_pop x exp(eta), the Table-2 diagonal prior; the NONMEM empirical-Bayes EBE is the mode of the same conditional distribution; the ODEs are solved analytically - the two K-PD compartments are closed form, the CA-125 equation via the integrating factor on a fine grid, so no ODE library is needed); the individual KELIM-B (day-1) is standardized by the training-fold median KELIM-B (per platinum-sensitivity cohort when the covariates table carries cov_cohort - the paper's 'standardizing KELIM-B by the platinum-sensitive and resistant median KELIM-B' of reference [1], and 'standardized and dichotomized by their median' in the origin paper md:94 - pooled median otherwise, a recorded deviation), and the call is 1 (treatment judged failing, unfavorable KELIM-B) when Std KELIM-B < 1, 0 otherwise (the paper: favorable KELIM-B, HR 0.35 [0.14; 0.84] PFS p=0.019 and HR 0.34 [0.12; 0.99] OS p=0.047 vs unfavorable, at the 100-day landmark). risk = -log(Std KELIM-B) (higher = slower CA-125 elimination = failing), so it writes no probability: TxResBench converts the risk per outcome. It takes one marker - serum CA-125 (declared required_markers: LOINC 10334-1, so the runner only runs it on units measuring CA-125) - and needs at least 3 detectable draws in [0, min(100, landmark)] (the paper's inclusion rule md:47); below-detection values (value 0 with <marker>__detected rows) are excluded from the likelihood (a log of 0 is undefined; the paper addresses CA-125 nondetects nowhere, '?'), and a patient with fewer than 3 detectable draws, all draws on one day, or a failed MAP gets no prediction with the reason in note. Differences from the paper: the population would not be re-estimated by SAEM in NONMEM 7.5.0 but uses the published Table-2 estimates (the fit is not reproducible - no control stream, no dataset); the per-patient individualization is the MAP with the table's diagonal log-normal IIV in place of the NONMEM EBE; residual W = 0.29 is read as the log-scale SD (the table prints 'W (kU.mL-1)'); dosing events are not published ('?') so the wrapper doses AMT = 1 every 21 days x 5 (days 0, 21, 42, 63, 84; the q3w interval of the bevacizumab-similar component of the BOLD regimen; the model's K part also does not separate the three drugs); the medians are derived per training fold (the paper's medians are sample-derived); the wrapper does not reproduce the survival stage (Kaplan-Meier/log-rank/Cox at the 100-day landmark with the BRCA/FIGO/lines multivariate analysis) - the per-patient output is the standardized KELIM-B and its favorable/unfavorable call.

methods.description: The combined KELIM-B + TIS two-group rule of Freyer G et al. (Nat Commun 2024;15:1985, DOI 10.1038/s41467-024-45974-w; GINECO BOLD phase II, bevacizumab-biosimilar + olaparib + durvalumab in relapsed high-grade ovarian cancer; the companion KELIM-B model paper Carrot et al., CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol 2025, DOI 10.1002/psp4.70025, is the second reference): markers[0] carries the longitudinal serum-analog marker (CA-125 in the paper), markers[1] the single baseline tumor-inflammation score (the 18-gene Tumor Inflammation Signature, TIS, from baseline FFPE tumor RNA in the paper; a baseline-only marker). Component 1 (KELIM-B): the individual elimination rate constant K (day^-1) of the population kinetic model of the log-transformed marker over the first 100 treatment days (>= 3 marker values required; log1p transform) is standardized by the training-fold median K (per cov_cohort cohort when that covariate is present) and is favorable when K >= the standardizing median, unfavorable otherwise - the benchmark reading of the paper's 'std KELIM-B >= 1 favorable / < 1 unfavorable' after 'standardizing KELIM-B by the platinum-sensitive and resistant median KELIM-B'. Component 2 (TIS): the baseline marker value is favorable when at or above the training-fold median (per cov_cohort cohort when present), unfavorable below - the paper's 'TIS >= median favorable / TIS < median unfavorable'. The combined call is 0 (combined favorable, treatment judged working) when BOTH components are favorable and 1 (combined unfavorable, treatment judged failing) when BOTH are unfavorable; discordant patients (one favorable, one unfavorable) get no prediction with the reason in note, because the paper's combined contrast (Fig. 4e/f: PFS log-rank chi-square 4.215, OS 8.797 on 1 df) compares the both-favorable vs both-unfavorable groups only. risk = -K (higher = slower marker elimination = failing; the KELIM-B scale, the rule's only continuous component; the paper defines no continuous combined score, so a patient's combined risk is its group, and no probability is written - TxResBench converts the risk per outcome). Deviations (all recorded in the README): the published KELIM-B is a semimechanistic K-PD nonlinear mixed-effects model fitted in commercial NONMEM 7.5 with no published code (the benchmark's approved simplification - the population log-linear mixed model, nlme::lme REML, of the benchmark's kelim method - replaces it); the TIS is a proprietary NanoString IO360 18-gene score (no public computation script), so the wrapper reads its value from the dataset's baseline marker; the standardizing medians and the TIS cutoffs are training-fold medians (per cohort when cov_cohort is present) instead of the paper's sample-derived PRR/PSR cohort medians, and the paper's 100-day landmark for the survival analyses is not part of the per-patient call (the benchmark's landmark and horizon machinery handles it).

methods.description: The modeled CA-125 ELIMination rate constant of the JOINT K-PD model (KELIM-joint) from Carrot, Corbaux, Colomban et al. (CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol 2025;14, DOI 10.1002/psp4.70025; BOLD phase II GINECO NCT04015739, bevacizumab-biosimilar + olaparib + durvalumab in relapsed high-grade ovarian cancer; the joint-model structure of Wilbaux et al., Br J Cancer 2014;110:1517-1524): a nonlinear mixed-effects population K-PD model with four compartments - treatment central C1 and transit C2 (dose fixed at 1), tumour size C3 (zero-order proliferation KPROL with the EC50 indirect treatment effect, first-order reduction KREDUC) and serum CA-125 C4 (basal production KPROD1 plus tumour-driven production KPROD2*exp(K2*VARTS), VARTS = dC3/dt, first-order elimination KELIM), C1(0)=C2(0)=0, C3(0)=TS0, C4(0)=CA125_0 with cohort-specific (PRR vs PSR) typical values for CA125_0 and KELIM only - was fitted in the population by SAEM in COMMERCIAL NONMEM 7.5.0 (no control stream, no analysis code published), and the individual KELIM-joint (day-1) was standardized and dichotomized by the median into favorable/unfavorable groups whose 100-day-landmark PFS/OS prognostic value was assessed (PFS HR 0.29 [0.12; 0.72] p=0.0073; OS HR 0.24 [0.08; 0.74] p=0.013; the continuous KELIM-joint Cox coefficient -1.23 (SE 0.46) PFS / -1.45 (SE 0.58) OS, S1 Table S2). The wrapper implements the published joint model in base R following the benchmark's convention for this K-PD family (kpd-ca125-tumour-response, psa-kelim): the published Table-2 population estimates are a FIXED population (never refit - the SAEM population fit is commercial-NONMEM-only and not reproducible), the per-patient individual parameters are maximum-a-posteriori estimates with the table's diagonal log-normal IIV, the CA-125 data enter log-transformed with the published additive residual W CA = 0.29, and the risk is -log(KELIM-joint / training-fold median KELIM-joint) (higher = slower CA-125 elimination = the treatment judged failing), with call = 1 (unfavorable, treatment judged failing) when Std KELIM-joint < 1. No probability is written: TxResBench converts the risk per outcome. The benchmark carries no serial tumour-size channel (the paper requires >= 2 tumour-size measurements), so the tumour compartment runs on the baseline sum-of-diameters from the cov_* column named by ts0_covariate (below-LOQ 10 mm -> LOQ/2 = 5 mm) when present, else on a MAP-estimated latent TS0; the PRR/PSR covariate is read from the cov_* column named by cohort_covariate (cohort-specific CA125_0/KELIM typical values and cohort-specific training-fold medians), and without it the wrapper uses the paper's two cohorts' pooled (geometric-mean) typical values and the pooled training-fold median - all recorded as deviations in run.json and the README.

methods.description: The LSTM model of Zhao et al., Sci Rep 2019;9:717 (DOI 10.1038/s41598-018-36745-x): a recurrent neural network with LSTM units on the tensor of per-one-year-slice features of the 7-year EHR observation window, with an auxiliary demographic input fed into a multilayer perceptron (MLP) with two hidden layers, for 10-year cardiovascular disease event prediction (published AUROC 0.784 +/- 0.011, AUPRC 0.276 +/- 0.014). The wrapper maps the paper's frame onto the benchmark: the observation window is the draws' span up to the landmark day, cut into one-year slices (at most 7 - the paper's 7 one-year slices), every marker passed is one of the paper's measures, and per slice and marker it builds the paper's summarized data (min, max, median, SD with the paper's >5-SD outlier removal and closest-date replacement of missing slice measures, plus an imputation dummy); the cov_* columns are the paper's demographic auxiliary input and are used whenever the cohort has them (covariates: optional - a cohort without cov_* columns feeds the auxiliary branch a constant zero vector, so the wrapper stays runnable on covariate-free cohorts; the paper's model always has the demographic input, README records the difference). Whether the demographic input merges before or at the MLP, the exact merge point of the tensor, the number of LSTM layers, the epochs and the batch size are not published (the LSTM row of Supplementary Table 3 names only LSTM 41 units, 1 hidden dense layer of 128, learning rate 0.0001, recurrent dropout 0.2, dropout 0.3); the wrapper implements one LSTM layer of 41 units followed by one 128-unit dense layer, a two-hidden-layer MLP of 128 units on the covariates, concatenation, a sigmoid output, binary cross-entropy and Adam at 0.0001, and the paper's 8:1:1 validation split with early stopping - every such wrapper choice is recorded in the README and run.json instead of being silently invented. The paper's 40 per-slice binary diagnosis/medication code indicators are not representable in the marker frame and are not built. One classifier is fitted per benchmark outcome and horizon (the response labels directly; the event-by-horizon label for progression and death); the wrapper writes each classifier's probability as its own p_* column and risk_<outcome>, with the primary risk = the first-horizon progression probability (else death, else the response labels), and no call - the paper reports discrimination only and defines no threshold.

methods.description: The kernel-weighted landmark Cox model of Li, Luo, Hu and Greene (Statistics in Biosciences 2017;9:60-78, applied to the African American Research of Kidney Disease and Hypertension) for dynamic prediction from irregularly spaced repeated measurements: every marker measurement time is both a landmark and a prediction time, the derived residual survival time is artificially censored at the horizon tau1, and, at the prediction time s, the coefficients and the cumulative baseline hazard are estimated from the whole landmark data set by a Gaussian-kernel-weighted partial likelihood and the matching weighted bivariate Breslow estimator (case weights W_ij(s) = h^-1 K((t_ij - s)/h); the paper implemented the fit with survival::coxph and the weight argument). Two markers: the first is the trajectory marker (current value at the prediction time and its history-window slope, estimated as the BLUP of a kernel-weighted landmark random intercept-slope linear mixed model, the paper's eGFR procedure; per-subject least-squares slope is the documented fallback), the second is the level marker (most recent history-window value, log-transformed by default, the paper's log urine protein-to-creatinine ratio). Any cov_* column enters as a predictor (the paper's age at the prediction time; cov_age is aged forward; the paper's hospitalization indicator is not representable in the benchmark's baseline-covariate data model and is omitted). One model per survival outcome the training data give (progression, death) and per horizon (tau1 = horizon minus landmark): it writes the linear predictor as the risk per outcome and the model's own probability P(event within tau1 | event-free at the landmark, X(landmark)) = 1 - exp{-exp(beta(landmark) X) Lambda0(tau1, landmark)} per horizon. Response outcomes get no own probability (the paper has no binary-response model) and are converted from the risk by TxResBench.

methods.description: The kernel-weighted landmark sub-distribution hazard (Fine-Gray) model of Wu Cai, Liang Li and Ruosha Li (Statistical Methods in Medical Research 2020;29:3179-3191, applied to the African American Research of Kidney Disease and Hypertension, AASK) for dynamic cause-specific cumulative-incidence prediction from irregularly spaced repeated measurements: every marker measurement time is both a landmark and a prediction time, the derived residual times are artificially censored at the horizon tau1, and, at the prediction time s, a separate SDH model per cause is estimated from the whole landmark data set by an Epanechnikov-kernel-weighted local-linear estimating equation (equation 4) whose covariates are the predictors Z~ stacked with the landmark-time interaction Z~ (t_ij - s), whose beta-hat(s) is the local-constant component, and which the paper implements by translating the competing events into a counting process (Geskus 2011, ref 40) and calling survival::coxph; the inverse-probability censoring weights use the kernel-weighted Kaplan-Meier G(t|s) and the baseline is the matching kernel-weighted Breslow-type plug-in estimator. Prediction (md:58): 1 - exp(-Lambda~10(tau1, s) exp(beta-hat(s)'Y~_o(s))). The cause mapping to the benchmark: cause 1 = the progression outcome (PFS event), with death strictly before it as the competing cause; cause 2 = the death outcome, with progression strictly before it as the competing cause (the paper's semi-competing exclusion); a patient whose PFS and OS event times coincide is a case in both cause models. Two markers: the first is the trajectory marker (current value at the prediction time and its history-window slope, estimated as the BLUP of the kernel-weighted landmark random intercept-slope linear mixed model, the paper's eGFR procedure, with per-subject least-squares slope as the documented fallback), the second is the level marker (most recent history-window value, log-transformed by default, the paper's log urine protein-to-creatinine ratio). Any cov_* column enters as a predictor (the paper's age at the prediction time; cov_age is aged forward; the paper's hospitalization indicator is not representable in the benchmark's baseline-covariate data model and is omitted). It writes the linear predictor as the risk per outcome and the model's own cause-specific CIF P(cause event within tau1 | event-free at the landmark, history) per horizon for progression and death. Response outcomes get no own probability (the paper has no binary-response model) and are converted from the risk by TxResBench.

methods.description: The per-patient two-group KM survival stratification of Pereira et al., 'Treatment Monitoring and Outcome Prediction in Invasive Aspergillosis Using Immunologic Markers', J Infect Dis 2026; DOI 10.1093/infdis/jiag140 (ECMM multicenter prospective research, 51 enrolled / 39 post-QC probable/proven invasive aspergillosis patients with hematological malignancies, Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel serum NPX, serial samples T1/T4/W2/W3): the NPX values of ONE serum inflammation protein at ONE on-treatment timepoint (Week 2 or Week 3 after antifungal treatment initiation) are stratified into low vs high by the Jenks natural breaks optimization method - OneR::bin(x, nbins = 2, method = 'clusters') (Supplementary Material 1: 'NPX values were stratified into low and high with the Jenks natural breaks optimization method using the OneR package (von Jouanne-Diedrich, 2017)', n = 25 survival subset), and the two groups' Kaplan-Meier overall-survival curves are estimated 'until last follow-up, which was censored at 6 weeks' (42 days from diagnosis) and compared (P <.05 convention; the 6-week threshold per other IA trials); the paper's four instances differ only by protein and week: CXCL6@W2 and MMP-10@W2, MMP-10@W3 and MCP-3@W3 (the 2 proteins with the highest limma differential-expression significance per week, comparing day-30 improvement vs worsening cases; only low CXCL6@W2 was significant, W3 a trend). The wrapper takes the ONE marker the benchmark passes (the paper's protein; the limma protein-selection step is NOT re-run - the spec fixes the instances), reads the marker's last on-treatment draw up to the benchmark landmark as the week value, derives the Jenks breakpoint on the training fold with OneR 2.2 (nbins = 2, the paper's low/high; OneR's own default 5 is NOT used), forms the low (value <= breakpoint) and high groups, and on the training fold fits one per-group KM curve per survival outcome in the training data, on the residual clock with the patients event-free at the benchmark landmark (the benchmark's conditioning - the paper's KM starts at diagnosis; recorded deviation). It writes risk = the week NPX value itself (higher = more likely failing: low expression is the favorable group, md:120), call = 1 for the high-expression group (0 low), and the training-fold group KM event probability by each horizon as the model's own p_progression_H<h> / p_death_H<h> (group-level, no per-patient heterogeneity in the paper); a patient without a week value up to the landmark gets no prediction with the reason in note. A group with fewer than 2 patients or no event, a degenerate split (<= 2 distinct values - OneR returns the raw values without clustering; kmeans may also fail) projects the pooled training-fold KM (recorded fallback; the paper defines none). The paper publishes no analysis code (verified in the PMC fullTextXML: no code-availability statement, job.code = []) and no breakpoint value (figure-only); the wrapper uses OneR 2.2 and survival as named, and the KM/log-rank diagnostics are its own output.

methods.description: Sliding-window group-level risk stratification of short-term radiographic progression from serial ctDNA %VAF measurements: every ctDNA measurement is treated as an initial timepoint and the binary outcome is radiographic progression within the following 100 days; the timepoints are stratified by three criteria (detectable vs undetectable %VAF; %VAF at or above the training-fold 75th percentile; Delta %VAF/month at or above its training-fold 75th percentile, the velocity derived by the wrapper from consecutive measurements), and each stratum is compared by Kaplan-Meier PFS curves (PFS at 50 and 100 days), a log-rank test and a univariable Cox hazard ratio of the high- vs low-risk stratum - Miller et al., 'Development of a Nomogram to Predict Therapeutic Resistance in Metastatic Melanoma Using Longitudinal ctDNA Kinetics', Mol Diagn Ther 2026;30:515-527, DOI 10.1007/s40291-026-00840-x (33 metastatic melanoma patients on systemic therapy, 325 clinic visits, 214 ctDNA measurements of BRAF V600E/V600K or NRAS Q61 by droplet digital PCR, 100-day windows, per-stratum HRs 22.0 / 22.2 / 9.0). The wrapper reads the one marker the benchmark passes (the paper's %VAF), derives the per-measurement velocity from the draw chain up to the benchmark landmark, derives the two 75th-percentile thresholds in the training fold (the paper's 4.83% and 0.2754%/month are this-cohort values), fits the paper's per-stratum KM / log-rank / univariable Cox on the training-fold 100-day windows, and writes the %VAF at the patient's latest scorable measurement as risk (higher = more likely failing, the paper's direction); the benchmarks' per-horizon probabilities are obtained by the package's conversion of that risk, because the paper's own output is a 100-day-window group-level KM and hazard ratio, not a per-patient probability.

methods.description: The population K-PD semi-mechanistic model of Wilbaux, You, Tod et al. (Br J Cancer 2014;110:1517-1524, CALYPSO, DOI 10.1038/bjc.2014.75): a four-equation nonlinear ODE system - two-compartment K-PD drug kinetics (dA1/dt = -K*A1; dA2/dt = K*A1 - K*A2; dose = 1 per chemotherapy cycle), tumour dynamics (dTS/dt = KPROL*(1 - A2/(A50+A2)) - KREDUC*TS) and an indirect-response CA-125 compartment (dCA/dt = KPROD1 + KPROD2*exp(K2*VARTS) - KELIM*CA with VARTS = dTS/dt; initial conditions A1(0)=A2(0)=0, TS(0)=TS0, CA(0)=CA0) - predicts the chemotherapy-induced tumour-size response of an individual patient from the patient's serial serum CA-125 (Box-Cox transformed, lambda = -0.16) and the baseline radiological tumour size, using the paper's published learning-set population parameters (Table 2: K 0.019/day, KPROL 0.869 mm/day, A50 0.162 a.u., KREDUC 0.013/day, KPROD1 0.452 U/ml/day, KPROD2 0.615 U/ml/day, K2 21.4 day/mm, KELIM 0.037/day, TS0 57.8 mm, CA0 167 U/ml; log-normal IIV from the table's %CV; additive residual 0.165 on the Box-Cox scale) and a per-patient maximum-a-posteriori Bayesian individualization (diagonal log-normal prior, the paper's IIVs; the paper reports no inter-parameter correlations, so none are used). The wrapper's risk is the predicted relative change of the (latent) tumour size at the horizon day = landmark + 200 days - the paper's predicted 'variations of tumour sizes... over a period of 200 days' read as the 200-day window after the decision point (md:70, md:188; Figure 4 plots the relative change of the predicted tumour size), so a higher risk = a bigger predicted tumour = the treatment is judged failing. The model cannot be fitted on the benchmark's training folds: the joint population estimation consumes serial tumour-size observations (md:32, md:56), which the benchmark does not carry, so the wrapper uses the paper's published learning-set population parameters as a fixed model (never re-estimated; trained from the paper, fitted: false). When the patients table carries the column named by the ts0_covariate setting, that value is used as TS0 (the paper's measurable-disease prediction, md:70); without it the wrapper runs the paper's non-measurable-disease route: the latent TS0 is estimated with the published logit-below-steady-state constraint (md:46, Supplement 3) together with the other individual parameters. Deviations (all recorded in the README and run.json): population parameters fixed from Table 2 instead of a training-fold SAEM fit (no tumour-size data in the benchmark); the paper's >= 4 CA-125 values per patient becomes the benchmark's minimum 3 draws (the gate world carries at most 3 draws by the landmark); the per-cycle dose times are not published ('?'), so doses are every cycle_days = 21 days (the CALYPSO 3-week cycle) and the k-PD schedule is the same for both arms (a tested-not-kept difference in the paper, md:44); the per-cycle dose amount = 1 (md:44); non-positive CA-125 values (non-detects, value 0 with the __detected rows) cannot be Box-Cox transformed - the paper states no undetectable-value rule ('?'), so they are excluded from the likelihood and a patient with fewer than 3 positive draws abstains with the reason in note; the latent-mode TS0 is bounded below the tumour steady state KPROL/KREDUC by the logit link (Supplement 3).

methods.description: The modeled-early-PSA-kinetics prognostic classification of Carrot, Elaidi, Colomban, Maillet, Tod, You, Oudard et al. (Cancers 2022;14:815, DOI 10.3390/cancers14030815; post-hoc analysis of the phase III NCT00764166 trial, ADT +/− docetaxel 70 mg/m2 q3w in 250 rising-PSA prostate cancer patients after radical prostatectomy or radiotherapy, 177 K-PD-assessable): a population nonlinear mixed-effects kinetic-pharmacodynamic (K-PD) semi-mechanistic model of log-transformed serum PSA during the first 100 treatment days - three compartments (treatment central C1 with AMT fixed to 1, transit C2, PSA), zero-order PSA production KPROD (ng.mL-1.day-1) regulated by an indirect effect EFFECT(EC50) = 1 − C2/(EC50 + C2), first-order elimination KELIM (day-1), initial condition PSA0E (4.220 ng.mL-1; the equations are published only as the Figure 1 image; the fit ran in commercial NONMEM 7.5.0 with FOCEI + Laplacian and the M3 method for the PSA LLOQ = 0.1 ng/mL, no control stream or dataset published, so the model is specced from the paper + Supplementary Table S2: K 2.130 day-1, KPROD 0.002 ng.ml-1.day-1, EC50 0.357 AU, PSA0E 4.220 ng.mL-1, KELIM 0.081 day-1 with log-normal diagonal IIV (the table's IIV column is the random-effect variance; BSV %CV = sqrt(IIV)×100 exactly: 25.259, 206.398, 38.079, 129.615, 35.214)) - the five parameters are estimated per patient and KPROD and KELIM 'were standardized and dichotomized by their median' (sample medians: KPROD 0.002, KELIM 0.081 day-1), and the favorable/unfavorable calls' prognostic value for PSA-PFS and OS was assessed at a 100-day landmark by Kaplan-Meier/log-rank and multivariate Cox (KELIM favorable vs unfavorable HR 0.63 (0.43-0.92) PSA-PFS / 0.57 (0.43-0.92) OS; KPROD 0.65 (0.45-0.96) / 0.53 (0.3-0.89); KELIM and KPROD not different across treatment arms, so prognostic, not predictive of docetaxel benefit). The wrapper: published Table-S2 population parameters as a fixed model (the NONMEM population fit is not reproducible; fitted: false), per-patient maximum a posteriori individual parameters with the table's diagonal log-normal prior (the wrapper's analytic solution of the ODEs; base R stats::optim), training-fold KELIM/KPROD medians for the paper's standardization (Std = X/median, the A2024 follow-up convention; this paper's formula '?'), and risk = −log(Std KELIM) oriented to failure - the paper's KELIM is prognostic for both PSA-PFS and OS (favorable = Std ≥ 1, the longer-survival group; the call is 1 when Std KELIM < 1, i.e. the paper's 'unfavorable KELIM'), with the per-patient KPROD, its median-standardized value and its call recorded in run.json for the analysis (the paper's KPROD OS axis; its favorable/unfavorable direction is '?', and from at most 3-4 sparse draws the per-patient KPROD is weakly identified - BSV 206.4% - so it is not used as the benchmark risk). It writes no probability: TxResBench converts the risk per outcome. Documented deviations: population fixed from Table S2 instead of the NONMEM refit; residual σ = 0.25 on the log scale (the paper publishes no residual error); below-LLOQ PSA (0.1 ng/mL; value 0 with _detected rows) excluded from the likelihood instead of NONMEM's M3; the paper's >10% PSA-rise patient exclusion is not applied (fixed published population model, outcome-informative selection; a rising trajectory is scored through a low KELIM/high KPROD MAP); ≥3 detectable draws from the paper's ≥3-assays rule (min_draws 3); dosing AMT 1 every 21 days × 5 (times not published; q3w regimen); window = [0, min(100, landmark)].

methods.description: The paper's method: a pooled-landmarking multivariable Cox proportional-hazards model in counting-process form, one 100-day interval per clinic visit (start = the visit time t, stop = min(t + 100 days, progression time), event = 1 iff progression occurs in (t, t + 100]), with the visit's ctDNA percent variant allele frequency (%VAF) and its velocity since the previous measurement (Delta %VAF/month = (v_t - v_prev)/(days/30)) as the only, time-varying, predictors; the final model is refitted on all intervals and its 100-day progression probability (model-based baseline survival at 100 days, Breslow estimator, logistic-recalibrated with an intercept and a slope) is what the paper's rms point-based nomogram and its total-points axis encode, with the cohort split at the median recalibrated probability (Miller H.A. et al., Mol Diagn Ther 2026;30:515-527, DOI 10.1007/s40291-026-00840-x: 33 metastatic melanoma patients, 325 visits, 214 ctDNA measurements, 174 paired %VAF/velocity values, 102 evaluable intervals, BRAF V600E/V600K or NRAS Q61 ctDNA by ddPCR; repeated stratified 5-fold CV x 100 with logistic recalibration; mean CV AUC 0.883 [0.642-0.991], C-index 0.77, 100-day AUC 0.88; no published code, no published coefficients - the wrapper fits the published structure per benchmark fold). The wrapper takes exactly one marker (the ctDNA %VAF series; the velocity is derived from it), refits the counting-process Cox on the training fold's intervals from full histories (long_full), and writes the fitted model's 100-day progression probability as risk and as p_progression_H<h> for each framework horizon (landmark-anchored: P(progression by h | event-free at the landmark), the same mapping the paper uses from a visit); the paper's rms::nomogram figure (standardized predictors) is the point-scale rendering of the same linear-predictor-to-probability mapping, its per-standard-deviation effect sizes recorded in run.json; no call and no low/high category are written - the paper's low/high split is a sample-derived median cutoff, its 0.5 threshold is a lead-time-cohort analysis rule, neither is a published prediction rule. Differences from the paper (each recorded in run.json): no published coefficients or code, so every fit is a refit; the paper's visit-anchored window is read by the benchmark's landmark-anchored evaluation (a patient's current visit is the latest draw at or before the landmark, and the framework's horizons are days since the first dose); the fit uses the benchmark's event-free-at-landmark training cohort; the velocity formula (v_t - v_prev)/(days/30) is not published anywhere (the ESM's Supplementary Table 1 values verify it exactly, e.g. subject 1: (35.19-11.26)/(35/30) = 20.51); the absolute-clock pooled model of the ESM's (start, stop) encoding is implemented, and the paper's §3.3 prose 'days from the initial timepoint' (a relative-clock model, the only one with a single S0(100) for the nomogram axis) is recorded as the alternative reading, not implemented; the survival 3.4-0 version named by the ESM is recorded, the wrapper pins survival 3.8-12; markers are generic - the benchmark passes the ctDNA %VAF marker, its scale (percent) and below-detection encoding (0) are used as reported, no log transform.

methods.description: The paper's method 7, 'Landmark model' (van Delft et al., Heliyon 2022;8(10):e10932; NSCLC immunotherapy, non-response at 6 months): a landmark-analysis Cox proportional hazards model on three summary covariates of one serum tumour marker's history up to the landmark timepoint - the most recent biomarker measurement, the average biomarker value, and the average of all positive increments between consecutive measurements (md:53; one fit per marker, per-marker analysis like the paper's CYFRA 21.1, CEA, CA-125, NSE, SCC). The model is fitted on the training patients still at risk at the landmark (the paper's landmark population: patients reaching the event or censor time before or at the landmark are removed, cutLM semantics), with administrative censoring at the 6-month horizon, and the hazard on the time-to-non-response-event scale; the paper's event is progressive disease (RECIST), clinical progressive disease, or death (md:37), mapped to the harness's progression outcome (pfs_time/pfs_event; OS fallback), because the paper publishes no time-to-event or censoring definition ('?' in the spec). The per-patient output is the class probability of non-response at 6 months after treatment initiation (absolute horizon, conditional on being at risk at the landmark), thresholded into a 0/1 call at the training cohort's 95%-specificity ROC cutoff (md:27, md:53). The wrapper writes that 6-month probability as risk (the quantity the paper's threshold uses) and the thresholded call; it writes no p_* column because the paper's own probability is the response-call risk and the benchmark's per-outcome probability conversion serves the four harness outcomes. The paper's landmark timepoint value, its exact time-to-event framework, its prediction route (dynpred::cutLM + survival::coxph + survival::survfit package facts) and the two-vs-three covariate discrepancy between Supplemental T 1 and the main text are not published - the wrapper's readings are recorded in the README and run.json (it follows the main text: three covariates). A patient whose kept sequence is left with fewer than two measurements by the paper's gap filter (<5 or >30 days between consecutive measurements excluded) gets no prediction, with the reason in note.

methods.description: The landmark dynamic prediction model of Yao, Astor, Yang, Greene and Li (BMC Med Res Methodol 2024;24:324) for kidney-transplant graft health: at each landmark time, three sub-models are fitted on the patients still at risk (alive with a functioning graft) - a cause-specific Cox model for graft failure with death as censoring, a cause-specific Cox model for death with a functioning graft with graft failure as censoring, both on residual survival times from the landmark, and a working-independence GEE (geepack) model of the marker measured between the landmark and the horizon with the time gap as a covariate. The two failure probabilities within a horizon are combined from the two Cox cumulative hazards in the Wolbers et al. 2009 closed form; the future-marker expectation at the horizon is the GEE linear predictor. The marker is the longitudinal eGFR analogue and is double-role: up to the landmark it is the time-varying predictor (the paper's 'current eGFR at the landmark', estimated by a per-subject Gaussian-kernel local linear regression because not every patient is measured at the landmark), after the landmark it is the GEE response (training only). The paper's backward selection (drop the largest p until everything is below 0.05, always retaining the marker and, when present, the age/KDPI/living-donor covariates; a predictor selected for one sub-model is retained for all) is run at the landmark of the fit. Baseline cov_* columns (when given) enter as the paper's time-invariant predictors; the paper's hospitalization and rejection histories are not representable in the benchmark data model and are omitted. The wrapper maps graft failure to the progression outcome and death to the death outcome; a patient whose PFS and OS event times coincide is a case in both cause models. It writes the Cox linear predictors as risk and risk_<outcome> and the model's own p_progression_H* / p_death_H* per horizon, plus the per-patient predicted horizon marker value in a side file (the contract's predictions cannot hold it).

methods.description: Two-group landmark survival stratification by the personalized tumor-informed ctDNA status at a fixed landmark (6 and 9 months after anti-PD-1-based therapy initiation) in advanced melanoma - Martinez-Vila et al., Cancers 2025;17:3804, DOI 10.3390/cancers17233804, 28 analyzed patients on ICI, serial plasma ctDNA by the 16-plex mPCR-NGS Signatera assay (Natera), ctDNA-positive = >= 2 SNVs detected, levels as mean tumor molecules per mL plasma (MTM/mL): at the landmark, patients with a ctDNA-negative status or demonstrated clearance (negative at the landmark, including patients positive earlier who cleared) are compared with ctDNA-positive patients by Kaplan-Meier survival distributions with the log-rank test or a Cox proportional-hazards model, patients with a PFS event within the landmark window excluded, PFS (primary, from ICI treatment initiation) and OS (secondary, restricted to first-line metastatic patients); published 6-month landmark (N = 19; 9/19 = 47.4% negative/clearance): PFS HR 10.0 (95% CI 1.2-84.0, p = 0.03), median PFS not reached vs 11.6 months, 2-year PFS 89% vs 30%, OS p = 0.045; 9-month landmark: HR 3.7 (0.6-22.0, p = 0.16), OS p = 0.13. The wrapper takes the one ctDNA marker the benchmark passes (its below-detection encoding: value 0 with a <marker>__detected 0 row = ctDNA-negative; the assay call otherwise), assigns each patient the status of the last draw in (baseline_max_day, landmark] (the paper reports no exact draw-window rule, '?'), writes risk = 1 for ctDNA-positive, 0 for negative/clearance (the paper's failure orientation: positivity = inferior PFS/OS) and call = 1 = ctDNA-positive (treatment judged failing), abstains with a note when no useable on-treatment draw exists by the landmark (the paper includes only patients with a landmark sample and no PFS event within the window; the harness already restricts the outcomes it hands over), and writes no probability of its own (the paper defines no per-patient probability - only group-level HR/KM summaries; TxResBench converts). No analysis code is published (only STATA v16.1 and R version 4.3.1 named; data-only availability statement), so the wrapper reimplements the published analysis structure in R survival (the KM/log-rank/Cox estimator choices - Efron ties, Wald CI, absolute KM clock from treatment start - are recorded as the wrapper's choices, never as paper facts), and the paper's group-level layer (per-group KM medians, 2-year PFS, Cox HR and log-rank p) is computed on the benchmark training fold at fit and reported in run.json together with the paper's published values. When the landmark status is one-level in the training fold (the two-group comparison degenerates; e.g. all draws detected), the wrapper's risk falls back to the ctDNA level at the landmark (higher = more ctDNA = worse, the paper's MTM/mL quantification) - recorded in run.json; the paper defines no such fallback.

methods.description: The landmark linear transformation model for dynamic prediction of Zhu, Li and Huang (JRSS-C 2019;68:771-791, applied to the African American Research of Kidney Disease and Hypertension): g[P{T_i - s > u | Z_i(s)}] = H(u; s) + Z_i(s)'beta(s) at any landmark time s, with the link fixed by the error hazard exp(t)/(1 + r exp(t)) - proportional odds at the paper's cross-validated r = 1 - and H an unspecified increasing step function. Because measurement times are irregular, beta(s) and H(u; s) are estimated from pth-order local-polynomial (p = 1, local linear) kernel-weighted martingale estimating equations: every training visit in the Epanechnikov bandwidth neighbourhood of s contributes with weight K_h(t_ij - s), its own covariate value and its own residual event time X_i - t_ij (the paper's eqs. 8-9; solved by the Chen-Jin-Ying 2002 iterative algorithm of the paper's Web Appendix A, which no package implements - the wrapper's solver is verified to reproduce the paper's named R function TransModel on the unweighted special case). Prediction is made at each patient's own most recent measurement time before the landmark (eqs. 10-11): the wrapper writes the method's own P(event by each horizon day | event-free at the landmark, history) and the centred linear predictor as the risk of each survival outcome the training data give; the response outcomes are converted from the risk. Missing after the paper's rules: the first marker given is the eGFR-role biomarker (current value and, at prediction times later than three years, its 3-year slope), the last marker is the BP-role biomarker (current value and 3-year volatility), other markers contribute their current value, cov_* columns are the paper's gender/baseline predictors, and prediction times at or before three years use the reduced model (current values only, as in the paper).

methods.description: The two-stage landmark linear transformation model with separate univariate functional principal component analysis (FPCA) of Zhu, Huang & Li (Biometrical Journal 2020;62:1371-1393, DOI 10.1002/bimj.201900112; applied to the African American Research of Kidney Disease and Hypertension). Stage 1: each intermittently observed marker process is denoised by FPCA (R package refund, fpca.sc, PVE 0.99) fitted on the draws up to the landmark day of the at-risk training patients only, and the fitted (denoised) current value of each marker at the landmark is taken as a predictor; per the paper, the first marker ('eGFR' in the paper) also contributes the slope of its trajectory over the past 3 years (the Li et al. 2017 random intercept-slope model, kernel-weighted BLUP, per-subject least-squares slope as the documented fallback), and the last marker ('SBP' in the paper, the frequently observed one) is used at its actual value with the 3-year volatility (mean absolute difference of consecutive observations). Any cov_* column enters as a fixed predictor (the paper's gender and age at prediction; cov_age is aged forward). Stage 2: a landmark linear transformation model g[P{T_i - s > u |...}] = H(u; s) + V'alpha(s) + Z'beta(s) is fitted per landmark on the at-risk patients with residual event times X_i - s by the Chen-Jin-Ying (2002) martingale estimating equations, solved with the R function TransModel; the link hazard exp(x)/(1 + r exp(x)) uses the paper's cross-validated r = 1 (proportional odds). Per survival outcome (progression, death) and per horizon the wrapper writes the model's own probability P(event by day h | event-free at the landmark) = 1 - pi-hat(h - landmark; landmark) and the linear predictor as the outcome's risk; the response outcomes get no own probability (the paper has no binary-response model) and are converted from the risk by TxResBench. Where the paper's per-marker FPCA cannot be estimated (too few subjects or measurement times, constant marker) the wrapper falls back to the last-observed value (the paper's LVCF comparator) for that marker and records the warning; the paper's own code is not retrievable (badge only, Wiley 403), so the wrapper is built from the paper's equations (5)-(7) and the named packages.

methods.description: The last-value-carry-forward (LVCF) comparison of the two-stage landmark linear transformation model for dynamic prediction of Zhu, Huang and Li (Biometrical Journal 2020;62:1371-1393, DOI 10.1002/bimj.201900112; applied to the African American Research of Kidney Disease and Hypertension, AASK, and reported as the LVCF approach of its Table 10). Stage 1: each marker's current value at the landmark day is imputed by the most recent observation at or before it (last value carried forward, the paper's 'most recent observation prior to the landmark time s'), plus two history summaries; the slope of the first marker over the past 3 years (the paper's Li et al. 2017 random intercept-slope model, a kernel-weighted linear mixed model on the at-risk training patients with BLUP slopes; the per-subject least-squares slope is the documented fallback) and, when at least two markers are given, the volatility of the last marker over the past 3 years (mean absolute difference of consecutive observations, the paper's SBP volatility). Any cov_* column enters as a fixed predictor (the paper's gender and age at prediction; cov_age is aged forward). Stage 2: a landmark linear transformation model g[P{T_i - s > u |...}] = H(u; s) + V'alpha(s) + Z'beta(s) is fitted per landmark on the at-risk training patients with the residual event times X_i - s by the Chen-Jin-Ying (2002) martingale estimating equations, solved with the R function TransModel; the error-hazard link exp(x)/(1 + r exp(x)) uses the paper's cross-validated r = 1 (proportional odds). Per survival outcome (progression, death) the wrapper writes the model's own probability P(event by day h | event-free at the landmark) = 1 - pi-hat(h - landmark; landmark) and the linear predictor as the outcome's risk; the response outcomes get no own probability (the paper has no binary-response model) and are converted from the risk by TxResBench. The paper's own analysis code is not retrievable (open-data badge only, no URL printed; the Wiley article and supplement return HTTP 403), so the wrapper is built from the paper's equations (5)-(7) and Appendix A and the named packaged solver (TransModel 2.3; the paper references version 2.1). It is the LVCF twin of landmark-ltm-fpca: the stage-2 model is identical, only the stage-1 current values differ (LVCF instead of an FPCA fit).

methods.description: The two-stage landmark linear transformation model with multivariate functional principal component analysis (MFPCA) of Zhu, Huang & Li (Biometrical Journal 2020;62:1371-1393, DOI 10.1002/bimj.201900112; applied to the African American Research of Kidney Disease and Hypertension). Stage 1: the intermittently observed marker processes (all markers but the last, the paper's eGFR / log(UPRO) / albumin) are denoised jointly by multivariate FPCA (Happ & Greven 2018, R package MFPCA, univariate PACE step with PVE 0.99, M multivariate components, default 9 as selected by Monte-Carlo cross-validation in the AASK analysis) fitted on the draws up to the landmark day of the at-risk training patients only, and the fitted (denoised) current value of each marker at the landmark is taken as a predictor; per the paper the first marker ('eGFR' in the paper) also contributes the slope of its trajectory over the past 3 years (the Li et al. 2017 procedure: a kernel-weighted random intercept-slope model, BLUP slope; per-patient least-squares slope as the documented fallback), and the last marker ('SBP' in the paper, the monthly-observed one) is used at its actual value with the 3-year volatility (mean absolute difference of consecutive observations). Any cov_* column enters as a fixed predictor (the paper's gender and age at prediction; cov_age is aged forward). Stage 2: a landmark linear transformation model g[P{T_i - s > u |...}] = H(u; s) + V'alpha(s) + Z'beta(s) is fitted per landmark and per survival outcome on the at-risk patients with residual event times X_i - s by the Chen-Jin-Ying (2002) martingale estimating equations, solved with the R function TransModel; the link hazard exp(x)/(1 + r exp(x)) uses the paper's cross-validated r = 1 (proportional odds). Per survival outcome (progression, death) and per horizon the wrapper writes the model's own probability P(event by day h | event-free at the landmark) = 1 - pi-hat(h - landmark; landmark) and the linear predictor as the outcome's risk; the response outcomes get no own probability (the paper has no binary-response model) and are converted from the risk by TxResBench. Where the paper's MFPCA cannot be estimated (too few subjects or measurement times, a constant marker, a degenerate covariance estimate), the wrapper falls back to the observed last value carried forward for that marker and records the fallback; a patient with no draw of a marker by the landmark gets no prediction.

methods.description: The dynamic landmark prediction framework of Lin et al. (Cancers 2026;18(16):2582, DOI 10.3390/cancers18162582): follow-up after PD-1 inhibitor initiation is divided into consecutive 28-day windows; at the end of the landmark window the patients who remained free of PD or recurrence form the risk set, and a regularized (L2-penalized, ridge) logistic regression on the pooled patient-window records predicts the probability of the first PD or recurrence during the subsequent 28-day window (the paper's M0 baseline model, M1 clinical-dynamic model and M2 immune-integrated model nest the longitudinal clinical and flow-cytometry lymphocyte-subset features). The wrapper builds the paper's dynamic features for every marker passed (baseline value, current value carrying forward, relative change from baseline, adjacent-window change, temporal slope - the paper's four constructions, md:45; the cov_* baseline variables when the run uses them), fits one ridge logistic regression on the patient-window records of the 28-day window grid covering the horizon range (from the training full history, long_full.csv; imputed by the training-record median and standardized by the training-record mean/sd, md:45), and scores the record at the landmark window, writing the fitted next-window PD/recurrence probability as risk, higher = the treatment is more likely failing. TxResBench converts the risk into the four outcome probabilities: the paper's quantity is the one-window-ahead event probability (md:35) and it publishes no probability for other horizons and no risk cut-off (md:55, md:239), so the wrapper writes no own p_* column and no call. The paper publishes no code (md:334) and names no estimator or penalty strength (md:50, md:236), so the wrapper's implementation choices (scikit-learn L2 logistic with C = 1.0, the feature definitions, the landmark-anchored window grid, medical-record median imputation) are documented deviations in README.md and run.json; the exact pooled W1-W7 training of the paper (711 records, md:108) cannot be reproduced because the harness exposes only the outcomes of the training patients still event-free at the landmark.

methods.description: Landmarking with a competing-risk random survival forest (Christiadi et al., Frontiers in Medicine 2024, dynamic survival prediction of end-stage kidney disease): at the landmark time L one forest is fitted per event outcome on the training patients still at risk at L, with the outcome administratively censored at L + horizon_window_days; the predictors are the last observed value of each marker at or before L (LOCF, the paper's primary feature construction) plus every cov_* column when covariates are used. Each forest is tuned with randomForestSRC::tune.rfsrc (the paper's nodesize grid and ntreeTry) and fitted with ntree = 1000 and the Gray's-test weighted log-rank split rule (logrankCR) when the data carry both causes; prediction reads the per-cause cumulative incidence function at the horizon (the paper's dynamic-plot readout) as the probability of the event by that horizon for progression and for death separately, and the per-cause integrated mortality is written as the risk; death is the competing cause for progression and progression the competing cause for death (an event at equal times counts for both). A patient with no marker value at or before the landmark gets no prediction. The wrapper implements the standard LOCF path; the paper's LME/LME-poly feature variants and its research-level cohort filter are not reproduced.

methods.description: Two-stage landmark model (Super Learner base learners M3 and M5 of van Gerwen et al. 2026, arXiv:2602.19761, 'standard Cox two-stage landmark models' for dynamic predictions in primary biliary cholangitis): at the landmark time t, stage 1 fits one linear mixed model per biomarker on all training measurements up to t with subject-specific linear time trends (random intercepts and slopes; M3) or with a nonlinear time specification through natural cubic splines with 3 degrees of freedom (M5), and stage 2 fits a standard Cox proportional hazards model on the patients still at risk at t (time zero = t) with the model-predicted expected biomarker trajectory at t of each marker as covariates (measurement-error-free, the paper's f(y_im) = eta_hat_im(t)) plus the baseline covariates; the conditional survival probability pi(u | t) comes from the Breslow estimator. The wrapper fits one such two-stage landmark model per survival outcome the training data give (progression and death), writes 1 - pi(h | L) as the outcome's own probability by the horizon day, the Cox linear predictor as its risk (higher = worse), and abstains with a note only for a patient it cannot score. The wrapper's choices where the paper is silent: per-marker LMMs fitted separately, nlme as the LMM engine (the paper names no LMM package), REML, natural-spline knots at the R default data quantiles, Cox ties by the coxph default (efron), and empirical-Bayes predicted expected trajectories at t for new patients.

methods.description: The landmarking gradient-boosting (LGBM) dynamic survival model of Shabani, Yaseri, Alimi, Nazemian and Zeraati (BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making 2025;25:368) for kidney-transplant recipients, named in the spec's title as 'a landmarking-gradient boosting approach': at the landmark time s a gradient-boosted survival tree ensemble (xgboost R package, objective survival:cox, the logarithm of the partial Cox likelihood as the loss, Table 1 applied values eta = 0.001, nrounds = 1000, max_depth = 2, min_child_weight = 5, eval_metric cox-nloglik) is fitted to the subjects at risk at s - those without the event or censoring until s - with the event time administratively censored at the horizon s + w, and the seven baseline covariates X plus the two longitudinal markers' values y(s) at the landmark as predictors; y(s) is imputed by a per-marker linear mixed-effects model (fixed and random intercepts and slopes of time, the paper's simulation LMM; the LMM is fitted on the training draws at or before s and the value at s is the empirical BLUP) after the paper's logarithmic transform of serum creatinine and BUN, with the last-observation-carried-forward arm as the documented comparison (setting marker_imputation). The wrapper's reported quantity is the paper's conditional survival probability Pr(T* >= s + w | T* > s, y(s), X) turned into the benchmark's failure orientation as its own p_progression_H<h> / p_death_H<h> = 1 - that probability via the risk-set Breslow baseline hazard at s + w (the paper publishes no code and never states how the boosting output - hazard ratios - was converted to its reported probabilities: this conversion, the LMM specificity and the unstated xgboost settings are the documented wrapper choices in the README), the centered linear predictor as risk and risk_progression / risk_death, and the Gain-based variable importance per landmark in run.json. The method is a survival model (the paper's endpoint is graft failure); the response outcomes are not modelled by the paper and their rows use the primary risk, converted to a probability by TxResBench. Two markers exactly (the paper's two log-transformed markers); a patient with fewer than two draws by the landmark, with an unimputable marker value (no draw of that marker, or a missing baseline covariate under complete-case analysis) gets no prediction, with the reason in note.

methods.description: The PD early-detection model of Xia S et al., Transl Lung Cancer Res 2019;8(6):1016-1028 (DOI 10.21037/tlcr.2019.12.09): 8 stage IV EGFR T790M+ lung adenocarcinoma patients on osimertinib 80 mg qd (AURA17 sub-cohort), 85 longitudinal plasma samples, capture-based targeted DNA sequencing (168-gene Lung Plasma panel, 273 kb, ~10,000x; variant calling by proprietary computation algorithms). The paper's model and call are each one sentence - 'a PD prediction model based on somatic mutations frequently detected in lung cancer for early detection of PD was generated using Lasso' and 'the early detection model predicted PD based on the elevation of the AF of certain mutations in 7 patients' (average lead time 3.0 months, as early as 8.0 months) - and the paper publishes no code and states nothing else: no feature set (the panel is not itemized), no response variable, no lambda, no coefficients, no threshold, no reference draw, no persistence requirement, no Lasso software (all recorded as '?' in run.json). The wrapper therefore refits the model with declared readings: every marker passed is one per-draw somatic-mutation allele-fraction (AF; %) series - or a per-draw maxAF summary when a marker carries 'maxaf', the paper's 'highest fraction of mutant allele detected in a particular sample' (otherwise the per-draw maxAF is derived as the max of the passed series, always over the markers passed; AF 0 = no somatic mutation detectable, never missing, never log-transformed). Per patient, per series, the features are the pre-treatment AF (last value on or before baseline_max_day), the last on-treatment AF (between baseline_max_day and the landmark), the absolute elevation (x1 - x0) and the relative elevation (a rise from an undetectable baseline is measured against the patient's smallest positive value of the series - the corpus convention, since the paper's own quantitative anchor is relative: maxAF 'reached the maximum level of twice as much as the baseline level at radiological PD'). The Lasso (l1-penalized least squares, Tibshirani 1996 - the canonical meaning of the paper's named model; scikit-learn's LassoCV stands in because the paper names no software) is fitted on the standardized features (training-fold per-feature mean and SD) against the benchmark failure label, in the order progressive_disease (the paper's call is radiological PD), no_response, first-horizon progression, first-horizon death; the penalty is chosen by cv_folds-fold cross-validation (mean squared error, lambda.min) because the paper reports no lambda. The wrapper writes the fitted value minus its intercept as risk - the elevation signal, higher = the Lasso-selected mutations' AFs rose more = treatment judged failing (the model's intercept, the training fold's PD rate, is not an elevation and is kept inside the call) - and call 1 when the full fitted value is at or above call_threshold (0.5, the midpoint of the 0/1 label scale; the paper publishes no threshold). The Lasso's nonzero coefficients are the paper's 'certain mutations' (recorded in run.json); no probability is written (the paper defines a binary call + a retrospective lead time as its output, and the lead time is not reproduced - it is an outcome-comparison statistic). The paper's cohort result (7 of 8 patients, Table 2) is a 8-patient exploratory series; on a training fold with no two-class label, too few complete-case patients, no feature aligned with the label or a penalty that shrinks everything to zero, the wrapper writes the declared constant fallback (risk 0, call 0, run.json records the reason), and a patient with a missing feature (no value of a series in the baseline or on-treatment window) is abstained with the reason in note - the paper's cohort is complete-case and defines no imputation.

methods.description: Per-prognosis Cox nomogram models for pediatric RUNX1::RUNX1T1-positive (t(8;21)) AML patients who achieved morphological complete remission after one induction course on the AML-CAMS-2009/2016 regimens (Chen X, Zhang L, Zheng Y et al., Frontiers in Oncology 2026;16:1744352, DOI 10.3389/fonc.2026.1744352; 136 patients, 22 deaths, 28 relapses; only internal 500-bootstrap validation, C-index 0.842 OS / 0.789 RFS; no analysis code published, job.code = []). The published pipeline (Methods md:255-292): candidate covariates prespecified a priori (demographics, blood counts at diagnosis, EMI, regimen, transplantation status, BM blasts by morphology/flow cytometry, LDH, cytogenetics, KIT/RAS mutations, and the RUNX1::RUNX1T1 RT-qPCR transcript quantification at diagnosis and subsequent time points, md:186-218); the serial transcripts are summarized by the prespecified binary High-Risk MRD composite (Yes iff the post-induction transcript reduction is <3 logs AND the MRD after two consolidations is >=0.01%, md:206-212); variables with <10% missingness were imputed by random forest (mice package, md:258-260); LASSO regression with L1 penalty, optimal lambda at lmin by ten-fold cross-validation (md:260-265, md:796-799); the selected variables entered multivariate Cox regression (md:276-279), and the independent (P<0.05) factors formed the nomograms predicting the 1-, 2- and 3-year OS and RFS probabilities (Table 2 md:857-923: OS - High-Risk MRD 13.983, regimen AML-CAMS-2016 0.172, WBC >=20x10^9/L 2.928; RFS - BM blasts [FCM] 1.018/%, EMI 5.148, High-Risk MRD 9.633, regimen 0.343, WBC group 2.553); total scores were stratified at X-tile v3.6.1 cutoffs (OS 0-160 vs 161-194; RFS 0-240 vs 241-350, md:760-767). The wrapper refits this pipeline per benchmark fold: from the serial marker draws it derives the composite (baseline = last draw at day <= baseline_max_day, post-induction = first on-treatment draw, post-two-consolidations = last on-treatment draw by the landmark; the paper's labeled phases have no day offsets, '?'), the LASSO candidate set is the composite plus every cov_* column (the paper's named covariates) - and, as the declared degeneracy fallback only (method_param degenerate_feature_fallback), the continuous log10 transcript levels at the three draws when the composite is one-level in the training fold (the paper's candidate set includes the transcript quantification at diagnosis and subsequent time points, md:203-206) - features with >=10% missingness are excluded and the rest imputed by mice random forest (one imputation, the paper states neither m nor the seed, '?'), LASSO lmin by 10-fold CV (glmnet, the paper names no package: '?' - declared choice), one multivariate Cox on the selected variables (survival::coxph, the hazard estimator not named, '?': declared efron default), the final model retaining the selected terms with P<0.05 (the Table-2 note 'Values in bold indicate statistically significant variables (P < 0.05) that were retained and entered into the multivariable model', md:923, and the text naming the independent factors as the nomogram basis, md:351-354/md:360-363), per endpoint (OS for death, RFS for the progression outcome) on the benchmark's event-free-at-landmark cohort with the residual clock Surv(time - landmark, event); risk and risk_<outcome> are the final model's linear predictor (higher = more likely failing; the nomogram total score is an affine transform of the linear predictor whose point scaling the paper does not publish, '?'), p_death_H<h> / p_progression_H<h> = 1 - S(h - landmark) of that model (the paper's 1/2/3-year probabilities on the benchmark's conditional-at-landmark clock; the two endpoints' different origins - diagnosis for OS, CR date for RFS, md:247-250 - and the covariates measured after the RFS origin are recorded as traps; no landmark re-origin is invented). The wrapper writes no call: the published X-tile risk-group cutoffs are on the paper's nomogram total-score scale, which the paper does not publish numerically ('?'; only the HRs in Table 2), so they cannot be applied to the wrapper's score scale - abstaining with the reasons in run.json rather than inventing a cutoff (the paper's two-group stratification remains an unsupported output; see README). A patient without the three draws (package-level, method.json min_draws 3), or with a missing needed covariate/feature value, gets no prediction with the reason in note (no imputation for new patients - the paper's imputation is its cohort protocol, and no new-patient path is described, '?').

methods.description: The paper's LASSO-logistic classifier of anti-PD-1 efficacy in recurrent or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (Zhang Ao et al., Cancer Cell International 2021;21:518, DOI 10.1186/s12935-021-02217-y: 160 RM-NPC patients on anti-PD-1 combination therapy at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, serum markers drawn within 3 days before the first anti-PD-1 treatment and 3 weeks later, random 2:1 split training n=106 / validation n=54): a one-stage LASSO logistic regression on the 56 per-patient Delta-W3 serum-marker changes ('The differences between the 56 serum markers... were calculated' md:383-385) whose endpoint was disease control (DC = PR + SD) at the first scan 8-12 weeks after treatment initiation (md:193-194, md:209-211); the LASSO (10-fold CV, 1-SE rule, md:200-203) retained two predictors and the published, executable model is the per-patient risk score = (-0.242 * Delta-W3 AST/ALT) + (-0.0007 * Delta-W3 LDH) (md:395-397), the logistic linear predictor of P(DC): AUC 0.737 training / 0.723 validation (md:399-412). The wrapper takes exactly two markers - the per-draw serum AST/ALT ratio and serum LDH, the fixed list the published score is DEFINED on (required_markers; roles resolved by name with the sorted-order fallback) - and per patient computes the two Delta-W3 changes (last draw at or before the landmark minus the last baseline draw; the corpus convention for the paper's fixed baseline/week-3 pair, draws after the landmark never enter) and the published linear combination. The paper does not publish the logistic intercept (only the two coefficients, md:395-397), so the wrapper estimates that single parameter on the training fold - a logistic regression of the progressive_disease outcome (the benchmark's encapsulation of the paper's DC-vs-PD first-scan label, PD = not DC) on the offset risk score, keeping the published slopes, link and label - and writes risk = +0.242*Delta-W3 AST/ALT + 0.0007*Delta-W3 LDH, the failure-oriented mirror of the published score (the published score is the logit of P(DC), i.e. higher = more likely disease control, so the benchmark's higher = more likely failing orientation is its negative; the ranking, AUC and probability conversion are sign-invariant), with p_progressive_disease = sigmoid(theta0 + risk) as its own probability; TxResBench converts the risk for the other three outcomes. No call: the paper reports no cutoff for the logistic risk score (the 78.5 cutoff belongs to the same paper's nomogram survival method, cox-risk-nomogram). A patient without a baseline and an on-treatment draw of both markers gets no prediction with the reason in note; the wrapper refuses at fit when the training data give no progressive_disease outcome (the paper's DC-vs-PD label is not observable; no_response = SD+PD is a different partition and is not substituted).
methods.licence: CC BY 4.0 (the article's licence; the paper publishes no analysis code - 'Analyses were performed with either the GraphPad Software or R Foundation for Statistical Computing' (md:230-232) names no LASSO/logistic package and the only availability statement is data-only, RDD system RDDA-2021724080 (md:671-673); the wrapper is written for this benchmark on the base image's pinned numpy/pandas)

required_markers.list_source: the two dynamic serum indicators the published model is DEFINED on: the per-draw AST/ALT ratio (one of the paper's 56 serum markers; the components are aspartate aminotransferase, LOINC 1920-8, and alanine aminotransferase, LOINC 1742-6, and the ratio is computed by the dataset pipeline as the unitless per-draw feature the lab panel reports) and serum LDH (LOINC 14804-9); the wrapper computes Delta-W3 = value at the last on-treatment draw at/before the landmark minus the value at the last baseline draw for each, and the published risk score from those two deltas. A dataset carrying only the two aminotransferases must precompute the ratio feature for this method; if it does not, the method does not run on it (a raw AST or ALT level is not the ratio the formula's coefficient weighs).

methods.description: Per-patient probability that a PLA2R-related primary membranous nephropathy patient will NOT achieve remission (non-remission, NR: neither CR nor PR per md:46) 12 months after initiation of rituximab (four weekly 375 mg/m2 infusions, md:39), from the published final logistic model of Wang C, Hu C, Zhang M, Li R, 'Predicting membranous nephropathy remission: a nomogram based on early dynamic biomarkers', Frontiers in Medicine 2026 (DOI 10.3389/fmed.2026.1783016; 144 patients, 86 remission / 58 non-remission, md:10; extracted text cited below as md:<line>): logit(p) = 2.317 - 0.057 x (1-month antibody decrease rate) + 0.318 x (1-month 24-h urinary protein excretion) - 0.034 x (1-month albumin increase rate) (md:127, Table 2 md:133-138), where the three features are the relative percentage decrease in anti-PLA2R antibody from baseline to 1 month, the RAW 24-h urine protein quantification at 1 month (g/24 h), and the relative percentage increase in serum albumin from baseline to 1 month (md:51-61). The three were selected by the paper's LASSO regression (10-fold cross-validation, lambda at the minimum-error value; 7 variables retained, md:100, Figure 1 md:103), established as independent predictors by a 7-variable multivariate logistic regression (Table 1, md:110-120, hypertension p=0.304, age p=0.509, eGFR p=0.129 and relative % decrease in urine protein p=0.602 NOT independent) and refit as the final 3-predictor model (md:125-127); the paper presents it as a nomogram (Figure 4, md:166-169) and reports AUC 0.905 (95% CI 0.855-0.956, md:171), bootstrap C-index 0.906, 10-fold CV C-index 0.898, HL chi2 = 7.924 p = 0.505 (md:171, md:176); no probability cutoff is published (md:171, md:198) and no per-patient scores or probabilities are tabulated. The wrapper computes the two percentage changes on the baseline and 1-month draws (the corpus fixed-draw convention: last baseline draw at day <= baseline_max_day, last on-treatment draw at baseline_max_day < day <= landmark_day - the paper's draw dates are not published, '?'), applies the published coefficients verbatim (fitted: false - nothing is estimated; the paper publishes no analysis code (job.code = []) and the patient-level data have no accession), and writes risk = the published linear predictor (higher = more likely non-remission) and p_no_response = logistic(logit) = the method's own P(non-remission at 12 months), the failure view of the paper's remission-vs-non-remission label read as the harness's no_response outcome; TXResBench converts the risk for the progression, death and progressive_disease outcomes. The LASSO + multivariate-logistic screening pipeline is NOT refit (a refit on benchmark data would be a different model and the lambda, CV scheme and candidate pool are '?'), there is no call (no threshold published), and a patient without the complete three-feature draw pair (or with a baseline value of 0, which makes the paper's percentage undefined) gets no prediction with the reason in the note - complete case, no imputation (md:70).
methods.licence: n/a for the paper's model (the article licence is not stated in the provided markdown and the paper publishes no analysis code - job.code = [], code_url null; the only software facts are environments: R 4.4.3 and SPSS 27.0, md:66, and no package/library/function is named for the LASSO step, the logistic fit or the nomogram); the wrapper is an original reimplementation with the base image's pinned numpy/pandas and the txrmethod contract helper (MIT)

methods.description: Per-patient probability of major pathological response (MPR) failure after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NCIT) plus surgery in locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) - the fixed 2-predictor logistic score of Shen, Liang, Yan et al., Frontiers in Immunology 2026;17:1681959, DOI 10.3389/fimmu.2026.1681959 (29 stage II-III ESCC patients, 9 MPR incl. 3 pCR / 20 non-MPR, md:393-397; model inputs complete for the 24 P3-evaluable patients, 7 MPR / 17 non-MPR, md:667-668): Score = 19.6326542096909 + (2.89037175789617) x NOTCH1 + (-21.4244136789189) x P3 MRD (md:773-775), where NOTCH1 (baseline tumour mutation status, 1 = present) and P3 MRD (post-NCIT plasma MRD status, 1 = positive) are the two predictors the paper's LASSO step selected from {baseline NOTCH1, CIS, P3 MRD} (md:767-772) and 'A higher score indicates a greater probability of achieving MPR' (md:776-778). The wrapper computes the published formula verbatim; risk = p_no_response = P(non-MPR) = 1 - 1/(1+exp(-Score)) (the logistic link of the paper's 'multivariable logistic regression model... fitted to predict the probability of major pathological response', md:336-338 - the paper never states the score's scale and publishes the nomogram only as Figure 5C, so the link is declared as a deviation), the failure complement of the paper's own MPR probability; the binary group call applies the published Youden-index threshold 21.07784009 (md:778-780): Low-score (call 1, treatment judged failing) = Score < 21.07784009, which on the published formula's four values is exactly 'NOTCH1 = 0 or P3 MRD = 1' (computed; the paper reports only the two groups, md:800-803). Nothing is fitted: the paper publishes the exact intercept and coefficients (md:773-775) and no analysis code (md:942-944), so the wrapper never refits the LASSO screening or the logistic (re-running the selection would fit a different model per fold and the lambda/CV scheme is not published, '?', md:870). The two features enter as the benchmark reports them (the dataset's binary status markers; a continuous level is read as-is, never binarised by an invented threshold - the paper defines no LOD conversion beyond the assay call, md:308-310); the wrapper uses the corpus fixed-draw convention for the anchored reads (NOTCH1 = the marker's last value at day <= baseline_max_day, else its first value by the landmark - the feature is a time-invariant baseline tissue status; P3 MRD = the marker's last value at baseline_max_day < day <= landmark - the paper's labeled draws have no day numbers and P3 is the post-NCIT draw, md:229-231/md:388-390); a patient without either feature (e.g. no P3 draw: 5 of 29 in the paper, md:388-390) gets no prediction with the reason in note - the paper defines no missing-data path ('?'). TxResBench converts the risk into the other outcomes' probabilities.

methods.description: Per-patient probability of pathological complete response (pCR) failure after neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy plus surgery in resectable NSCLC (clinical stage IIA-IIIB, AJCC 8th) - the 4-predictor multivariate logistic nomogram of Li, Gong, Yan et al., Journal of Inflammation Research 2025, DOI 10.2147/JIR.S542102 (113 patients, 50 pCR / 63 non-pCR, md:63): P(pCR) from smoking history (Yes/ever vs No), degree of differentiation (Poor or undifferentiated vs Moderate), dALP (post-treatment minus baseline ALP, U/L) and dNLR (post-treatment minus baseline NLR; both negative predictors, ORs 0.976 and 0.975 per unit, md:68), the predictor set reached by the paper's three-stage selection (LASSO via glmnet on 20 candidates at the optimal -log(e)lambda = 3.57 -> 9 non-zero, md:68; univariate logistic; multivariate; md:53, md:68). The paper publishes no analysis code (the only artifact is the deployed Shiny dynamic nomogram, md:73), no coefficients and no intercept (Table 2 prints ORs labelled 'HR' only, md:68), so the wrapper refits the published final structure per benchmark fold with base R stats::glm - binomial logit of the harness's no_response outcome (best response SD or PD, or responder 0: the failure reading of the paper's pCR-vs-non-pCR label, md:41) on the two marker deltas plus the two clinical covariates resolved from the cov_* columns by name (smoking history, degree of differentiation; a channel a run omits is recorded and the model falls back to the narrower set, never invented - method.json covariates optional per the benchmark convention, analysis-plan 8). risk = p_no_response = P(no pCR) = 1 - P(pCR), failure-oriented by construction; the two deltas use the corpus fixed-pair convention (last draw on or before baseline_max_day, last draw after it and by the landmark; the paper's labeled baseline/preoperative draws, md:34, and raw values without transformation, md:34/spec hyperparameters) and TxResBench converts risk for the other three outcomes. No call: the paper publishes no probability cutoff for the nomogram (the dALP -21.2 / dNLR -4.5 cutoffs belong to the SEPARATE EFS grouping by Maximally Selected Rank Statistics, md:78, not to the pCR model). The paper's LASSO screening stage and its univariate stage are NOT refit or re-selected: the published final 4-predictor set is the method's definition (md:68: 'we selected smoking history, degree of differentiation, dALP and dNLR for the further multivariate analysis'), the 20-candidate list is not tabulated ('?'), the lambda-selection rule is not stated (the 'optimal -log(e)lambda = 3.57' is reported without a CV scheme, '?'), and re-running the selection per fold would fit a different model each fold; the screening history is reported verbatim in run.json.
