methods.description: The paper's composite plasma-proteomic signature for response to first-line PD-1-inhibitor-based immunochemotherapy (SOX or XELOX, md:391-399) in advanced GC/GEJC - Meng E, Cheng X, Wu X, et al., Molecular Biomedicine 2026;7:106, DOI 10.1186/s43556-026-00510-8 (31 patients, prospective single-centre; plasma at baseline T0 and at the end of cycle 2 T1, Olink Target 96 Immuno-Oncology panel, NPX log2) - a signature built on THREE per-patient features: the baseline NPX of IL-15 and the T0->T1 absolute NPX differences of MUC-16 (CA-125) and MMP12 (the authors' published Analysis.script.R, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.18297346 v2, script:719-762; the paper's Statistics text defines dynamic change as a relative percentage, md:814-816, but the model block of the published script uses the absolute difference T2 - T1 of the NPX values, script:735-737 - the code is authority, discrepancy recorded). The published model is a binomial logistic regression whose linear predictor is the printed and published Risk Score = -5.948 + 1.287 x IL15_baseline + 0.021 x (Delta)MUC-16 + 0.064 x (Delta)MMP12 (probability of RESPONSE; positive coefficients, md:530-531, script:781-784) and, in the same block, a LASSO logistic regression (glmnet::cv.glmnet, family='binomial', alpha=1, type.measure='auc', nfolds=5, set.seed(123), lambda.min; script:804-808) whose per-patient probabilities produced the reported apparent AUC 0.865 (95%CI 0.724-1.000) and cross-validated AUC 0.799 (95%CI 0.640-0.958) (md:524-527) and the calibration/DCA figures (script:819-847); no operating cutoff is published (no call written). The wrapper's benchmark reading: the authors' fit procedure is fully published (function, family, alpha, lambda rule, folds, seed), so the wrapper refits BOTH models on the benchmark's training patients per fold - the published constants -5.948/1.287/0.021/0.064 are recorded in run.json but never reused: they are the fit on the authors' 31-patient NPX cohort, the paper never states whether they are the plain-glm or the shrunk LASSO coefficients (spec trap), and the formula's positive IL-15 coefficient contradicts the paper's own single-marker result (responders have LOWER baseline IL-15, md:423-425) - a small-sample artifact the wrapper does not import. The per-patient risk is the LASSO probability (params primary_model = 'lasso', the model the paper's reported AUC/calibration/DCA come from; primary_model = 'glm' selects the published-formula logistic, always fitted and reported either way), written failure-oriented: risk = P(no response) = 1 - P(responder), p_no_response the same quantity - the paper's CR/PR-vs-SD/PD partition (script:748) is exactly the harness's no_response outcome, so no sign conversion is invented and the fitted model's direction is learned per fold. Feature construction per patient: x0 = the marker's last draw at day <= baseline_max_day (the paper's baseline T0) and x1 = the marker's last draw at baseline_max_day < day <= landmark_day (the paper's labelled end-of-cycle-2 T1 under the benchmark's unlabelled clock - the corpus fixed-two-draw convention, a recorded deviation; draws after the landmark never enter); Delta = x1 - x0 on the values as reported, NO transform (NPX is already log2 and can be negative; a below-detection value arrives as 0 with its <marker>__detected companion and enters as the recorded 0, counted in run.json; the paper's QC excludes failed proteins instead, md:797-799, and defines no LOD rule for the model features, '?'). The paper's response model is complete case (na.omit, script:752): a patient needs both draws with all three proteins plus a response label, so min_draws is 2 and any incomplete patient is abstained with the reason in note - never imputed. Degenerate folds get declared fallbacks (single-class label: boundary constant; no varying feature: intercept-only at the training no-response rate; LASSO shrunk to zero: the plain-glm probability, else the intercept-only rate - each recorded; constant_ok). No call: the paper publishes no probability cutoff for the response model (the 161.9% MUC-16 relative-change cutoff belongs to the separate survival-rule analysis, md:458-460). The paper's PFS arm (coxph on the same three features, script:765-774, median-split KM, multivariable Cox HR 3.35 [1.56-7.20] P=0.002, md:34-35) is the paper's validation arm, not the response classifier - it is reproduced report-only in run.json when the training data carry PFS (the multivariable HR is not reproducible: the script's covariate list is example-only, script:870, and the deposit lacks the produced values).

methods.description: The paper's combined two-cohort 15-gene signature of TB treatment response - Eckold C, van Doorn CLR, Ruslami R, et al., Impaired resolution of blood transcriptomes through tuberculosis treatment with diabetes comorbidity, Clin Transl Med 2023;13:e1375, DOI 10.1002/ctm2.1375 - a fixed, published per-sample classifier ('Gene expression signature predicting month 6 versus diagnosis', Table 2 title, md:135): 'we identified signatures with the highest classifying power to discriminate between patients at diagnosis and end of TB treatment irrespective of diabetes/glycaemia by pooling all TB patients, using logistic regression with lasso regularisation' (md:132, the South African TB-DM 19 / TB-preDM 28 / TBrel-IH 32 / TB-only 17 / HC 27, md:114, + Indonesian TB-DM 41 / TBrel-IH 19 / TB-only 20, md:119, dcRT-MLPA cohorts, 'the datasets of both cohorts were pooled, and a combined two cohort 15-gene signature developed', md:132; 176 TB patients; venous blood PAXgene 2.5 mL at TB diagnosis W0 and through treatment W2/4/8/16/26 up to W52, md:38, first-line TB treatment per WHO guidelines for 6 months, md:30). The model is the published Table 2 logit (md:139-155), an exact linear combination of the GAPDH-normalised log2 dcRT-MLPA expression of the 15 genes in ONE blood sample: logit p = -14.99967 + 0.07841*BLR1 + 0.40415*CCL13 + 0.66015*CCL4 + 0.2371*CD19 + 0.35071*CD3E + 0.00263*CD4 - 0.48224*FCGR1A - 0.1725*FPR1 - 0.16957*GBP5 + 0.0172*IFIT5 + 0.3498*NLRP1 + 0.6625*PTPRCv1 - 0.51107*TAP1 + 0.06539*TNF + 0.06389*ZNF532, where p is the probability that the sample belongs to the end-of-treatment (month 6) class; derivation 'Signatures with the best discriminatory capability were identified using logistic regression with lasso regularisation (glmnet R package)' (md:52) with LOOCV and 70/30 train-test split and cross-cohort validation (md:52, md:127); published performance of the pooled signature: AUC.88 TB-only /.96 TBrel-IH /.85 TB-DM (md:132); per-signature training AUC 0.73-1.0, validation.69-.92 (md:132). The wrapper applies the fixed published coefficient vector (no refit: the fit procedure's glmnet call, lambda and standardisation are not published, md:52, and the coefficients ARE the executable artifact, the position of the lasso-logistic-pcr/lasso-logistic-dc-npc wrappers) - 'the spec treats the coefficient vector as the method (fixed score, no refit)'; as a classifier it is a fixed-STATE classifier of one sample, so per patient the wrapper scores THE LAST DRAW on treatment and at or before the benchmark's landmark (the corpus convention; each draw independently with the same vector, no updating mechanism per md:52), with the paper's noise floor (below log2 peak area 7.64 assigned 7.64, md:50 - never missing) and an abstention (empty risk + note, never an invented value) when the chosen draw does not carry all fifteen genes or a value is non-finite (the paper defines no missing handling for the signature genes, md:52; the only stated rules are the >90%-detection gene exclusion at the panel level and the 7.64 floor). Risk orientation: the published logit is the probability of the RESOLVED (month 6, end-of-treatment) transcriptome - the benchmark's responder class is the month-6 class per the spec's projection (unresolved transcriptome = treatment response failure), so the wrapper writes risk = -(published logit) = logit P('at TB diagnosis' class) (higher = more likely still diagnosis-like = more likely failing) and the calibration below; no call (the paper defines no probability cutoff; evaluation is ROC/AUC per clinical group only, md:52, md:132). Probabilities: the paper's own class probability is a transcriptome-state probability, not a benchmark outcome, so the wrapper reports p_no_response and p_progressive_disease as the published score re-anchored to the training outcomes - one intercept-only logistic of the outcome on the offset risk per outcome (the published slopes held fixed; Newton with backtracking, |theta0| <= 30; the paper's intercept -14.99967 gives the baseline p = P(diagnosis class) that the intercept shift calibrates to the benchmark outcome; fitted = true, the only learned quantities; TxResBench converts the risk for progression/death). Marker contract: the method takes exactly the 15 signature genes (markers 15, required_markers match all) - a dataset carrying fewer is not the signature (the classifier needs all 15, and no published handling of a missing gene exists); a different marker count stops with the package's message. The wrapper aligns gene name -> coefficient BY NAME (case-insensitive: the paper's probe name, the current HGNC symbol - e.g. CXCR5 for BLR1, PTPRC for PTPRCv1 - and the numeric HGNC id); markers whose name identifies no signature gene (the benchmark gate's synthetic M1..M15) are assigned to the remaining signature positions in the required_markers declaration order (sorted by HGNC id) - a wrapper convention recorded in run.json, never a paper claim, and only reachable when the names carry no identity (real runs match by name). Differences from the paper, each recorded: (1) no refit of the lasso selection - the published coefficient vector is the model (the glmnet call, lambda and standardisation are not published, md:52); (2) the benchmark label mapping (which class = responder) is fixed by the wrapper as month-6 class = responder per the Table 2 title reading (md:135) and the paper's own framing ('resolved' transcriptomes; the spec's projection 'risk = P(at TB diagnosis class) = 1 - P(month-6 class) in the benchmark's failure-oriented convention; direction NOT verified'), the class-1 encoding of the authors' fit being unpublished (?); (3) the two own probabilities are per-outcome re-anchorings of the published score, not paper-published quantities (the paper reports only ROC/AUC per clinical group, md:52, md:132); (4) the per-patient score uses the benchmark's landmark date, not the paper's month-6 evaluation draw (the signature's classes are the two sample states; the benchmark asks for a current-state risk at the decision day); (5) the paper's pooled-cohort signature was validated per clinical group (TB-only, TBrel-IH, TB-DM, md:132) while the benchmark uses one joint response label; (6) the coefficients appear in the paper without leading zeros ('.07841', md:141), recorded verbatim (0.07841).

methods.description: The IMBT (Integrated Multi-Biomarker Trajectory) two-stage pipeline of Cheng et al., J Hepatocell Carcinoma 2026, DOI 10.2147/JHC.S622498 (379 HCC patients on systemic therapy; AFP, D-dimer, ALC measured at diagnosis and every 21 days): stage 1 fits one lcmm::hlme latent-class mixed model of the log-scaled serial marker trajectory per marker (classes 2-5 evaluated, the single-class solution as starting values, many random starts, class number by lowest BIC with a minimum class size of 5% of the cohort), each patient's trajectory class = the modal posterior assignment; stage 2 fits one survival::coxph multivariable Cox model per survival outcome (PFS for progression, OS for death) with the class variables of every marker plus the baseline clinical covariates (the paper's ascites, age, maximum tumor diameter and BCLC stage = the benchmark's cov_* columns), reduced by bidirectional Akaike-information-criterion stepwise selection; the individual risk score (the final model's linear predictor) is stratified into low/intermediate/high tertiles and the fitted model's own PFS/OS event probabilities are predicted at 12/24/36 months absolute from treatment initiation (the paper's calibration horizons; survival::survfit). The wrapper refits this specification on the benchmark fold for every marker passed (the pipeline is per-marker symmetric; the paper's AFP/D-dimer/ALC trio is its cohort result, not a definition of the method): per marker the log-scale transform (log1p; the paper log-transforms AFP only), the class search (gridsearch random starts from the converged ng=1 fit) and the BIC/class-size rule are re-derived on the training data; the paper's 100 random starts are the setting gridsearch_rep (the default 12 keeps a benchmark fit bounded; recorded), its exact hlme formulas are not published so the wrapper uses a class-specific intercept and slope with no subject random effects (hlme's default random = ~ -1; the classes are the group-based mean trajectories the paper describes, tested on the benchmark's synthetic world), and its 400 ng/mL AFP baseline stratification is a marker-specific rule that the per-marker pipeline does not apply. Risk and risk_<outcome> = the final model's linear predictor (higher = treatment more likely failing), call = the HIGH tertile of the primary outcome's risk (the paper's three tertile strata projected onto the contract's binary failing call), p_progression_H<h> / p_death_H<h> = 1 - S(h - landmark) of the fitted model on the benchmark's at-risk clock; the response outcomes have no own column (the package converts risk; the paper reports PFS/OS models only). The paper publishes no code and no package versions (job.code = []; data on request md:181/md:207), so every value fitted here is the benchmark fold's own estimate of the published structure; the differences are in README.md and run.json.

methods.description: The two-predictor linear discriminant analysis of Garbuglia AR, Visco-Comandini U, Lionetti R, et al., PLoS ONE 2016;11(8):e0158989, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0158989 (23 chronic HCV genotype 1 patients on telaprevir/PEG-IFN/RBV triple therapy; the paper publishes no analysis code - 'The routine LDA from MATLAB was used to classify patients on the basis of the viral HCV RNA at T1 (day one) and T4 (day four).' md:78, with no routine, version, prior, covariance type or coefficients published '?', so this wrapper re-implements the published recipe and the fitted model is the wrapper's, not the paper's): linear discriminant analysis on the two per-patient predictors log HCV RNA at T1 (day 1 after the start of TPV treatment, md:38) and T4 (day 4, md:64/md:158), classed per patient as SVR vs no-SVR (Fig 5B; SVR = 'serum HCV RNA not detected at 24 weeks post treatment', md:31) - the paper's fitted classifier for the treatment-success question, whose published result is negative ('since the resubstitution error is 43% (6 out of 14 patients), it cannot be concluded that the HCV RNA at days T1 and T4 are able to predict SVR' md:191). In the benchmark the paper's SVR/no-SVR dichotomy is read from the training label no_response (1 = SD/PD = the paper's no-SVR side, 0 = CR/PR = the SVR side, failure-first - the benchmark's closest response outcome; the paper's label is a 24-week-post-treatment undetectability status, not a RECIST call), risk = the LDA plug-in posterior of the no-SVR class (failure-oriented; the paper reports only class calls and resubstitution errors, never a score), and call = 1 when the LDA classifies the patient as no-SVR (treatment judged failing). The wrapper's T1 and T4 are the patient's first and second on-treatment draws by the landmark (the fixed-pair convention for the paper's protocol days 1 and 4, which in the paper's own 14-patient kinetic series are the first and second post-baseline points, md:158; later draws - T5, T14, T28, T1m/T2m/T3m - never enter, spec traps.post_landmark_draws), with log10 as the log transform (the paper's plots are 'Log IU/ml' md:161 and the slope definition is y(ti)=log(x(ti)) md:64, but the log base is not stated '?'); MASS::lda with default prior = observed class proportions is the LDA engine (the paper names no MATLAB routine or prior). A patient whose T1 or T4 value is a non-detect (benchmark encoding value 0 with a <marker>__detected row 0, i.e. 'detected <12 IU/ml' (ART) or 'not detected' (US, <1.2 IU/mL)) gets no prediction with the reason in note - the paper never states the numeric coding of these values in the log-scale predictors (md:40, md:161, spec traps.log_of_zero), and the wrapper does not invent one. The wrapper surfaces the paper's negative result rather than presenting a working SVR predictor: run.json records the paper's reported resubstitution errors for both of its fits (21% = 3/14 EVR-vs-RVR Fig 5A and 43% = 6/14 SVR md:191) as the paper's numbers, and the README states that the paper's second LDA (EVR vs RVR, Fig 5A) is not reproduced as a benchmark output because its class labels - the on-treatment virological response states EVR/RVR, whose definitions the paper does not even print (md:123, '?') - are not among the benchmark's four outcomes.

methods.description: The four-category risk stratification of Guida et al. (J Transl Med 2022;20:193, DOI 10.1186/s12967-022-03359-x; 272 BRAF wild-type metastatic melanoma patients on first-line checkpoint inhibitors, 11 Italian centres): basal serum LDH (normal < ULN vs elevated > ULN, md:90) combined with one-month changes of blood parameters, Delta = value(T1) - value(T0) (md:243), each dichotomised at its ROC-derived cut-off - DeltaNLR <= 0.86 vs > 0.86 (the PFS four-group rule: median PFS 20 / 7 / 5 / 5 months for (LDH low, DeltaNLR low) / (LDH high, DeltaNLR low) / (LDH low, DeltaNLR high) / (LDH high, DeltaNLR high), md:247/md:250); DeltaLymphocytes >= -300/mm3 vs < -300/mm3 (the OS four-group rule: median OS 52 / 28 / 20 / 11 months, md:250/md:252); DeltaWBC <= 1920/mm3 vs > 1920/mm3 (combined with DeltaLymphocytes: 45 vs 7 months OS extremes, md:257). The wrapper reads T0 = the last draw on or before the baseline day and T1 = the draw at 21 +/- 7 days (the paper's pre-second-cycle draw, 21 days for pembrolizumab/ipilimumab and 28 days for nivolumab, md:92), resolves the four marker roles from the feature names (names carrying units are converted to the paper's cells/mm3), and writes per patient: risk = the one-month DeltaNLR (higher = worse, the quantity the PFS cut-off thresholds); risk_progression = the ordinal position (1-4) of the PFS four-group cell; risk_death = the ordinal position (1-4) of the OS four-group cell; call = 1 for DeltaNLR > 0.86 (median PFS 5 months, the paper's failing side), 0 otherwise; no probability (the paper's 2x2 rules are deterministic classifications; its per-category medians come from the companion multivariable Cox models, spec cox-baseline-delta). The cut-offs are the paper's published constants (in-sample ROC-derived, no external validation, md:92/md:101); the wrapper re-derives nothing and learns nothing from the training outcomes. The paper's ULN is its centres' local reference range (no numeric value published): the wrapper's ldh_uln setting (default 250 U/L, a commonly cited adult serum LDH upper limit) supplies it; the 22 LDH-missing patients (md:58) and patients without the baseline or the one-month NLR get no prediction, with the reason in note.

methods.description: The interval serum-LDH ratio threshold rule of Huang, Sim, Wu et al. (Therapeutic Advances in Medical Oncology 2020;12:1-10, DOI 10.1177/1758835920970050; 158 patients with biopsy-proven recurrent or treatment-naive metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma, first-line platinum-based doublet/triplet chemotherapy at Guangxi Medical University Cancer Hospital; LDH measured prior to CT and before each cycle by enzymatic spectrophotometric assay, ULN 240 IU/L, md:53; tumour response assessed after every two cycles of CT by RECIST v1.1, md:48): the per-patient ratio of serum LDH at a CT cycle to the immediately preceding cycle draw (LDH_CTn: LDH_CTn-1, n = 1..6, CT0 = pretreatment pre-CT, md:139) is paired with the response assessment after the pair's interval - LDH_CT1:LDH_pre-CT -> PD at CT2, LDH_CT3:LDH_CT2 -> CT4, LDH_CT5:LDH_CT4 -> CT6 (md:149, md:151) - and a ratio > 1.0 (any increase in LDH) calls progressive disease at the next RECIST v1.1 assessment, while a ratio <= 1.0 does not ('Choosing a cut-off of 1.0 is therefore practical and intuitive, as a ratio of >1.0 equates to any increase in LDH as being predictive of PD', md:151; reported sensitivity 0.79 / specificity 0.62 at the cut-off and AUC 0.74 (CT1: Pre-CT), 0.69 (CT3: CT2), 0.70 (CT5: CT4), pooled 0.73 with 95% CI 0.65-0.80, md:9/md:151; median per-group ratios across CT1-6: PR 0.738-0.988 vs PD 1.039-1.406, md:144). The wrapper takes the benchmark's one marker (serum LDH, IU/L), applies the paper's general consecutive-pair ratio to the LAST TWO draws of the marker at or before the landmark (the pair preceding the next response assessment - the corpus fixed-pair convention, because the benchmark carries days since the first dose, not the paper's cycle labels, and the paper prints no day-level grid; the paper's odd-cycle pairing is reproduced whenever the landmark sits before an assessment, and the deviation when it does not is recorded in run.json), and writes risk = the ratio (larger = more likely PD, the quantity the 1.0 cut-off thresholds) and call = 1 when the ratio > ratio_cutoff (1.0, PD predicted at the next assessment), 0 otherwise (ratio exactly 1.0 is not a call, md:151). No probability is defined by the paper (TxResBench converts the risk). The rule learns nothing from the training outcomes (fitted false): the cut-off is the authors' chosen operating point from the sensitivity/specificity trade-off of their cohort (not a Youden data-derived optimum - cutoff provenance 'derived in this sample', md:151), and the wrapper never re-derives it. A patient whose pair cannot be formed (fewer than two draws by the landmark, a missing draw, or a value of 0/below detection - 0 is the benchmark's below-detection encoding and serum LDH is a positive continuous enzyme activity with no undetectable state, md:53) gets no prediction with the reason in note; the paper's rule has no imputation ('a missing draw of a pair makes that assessment's call impossible', candidate spec).

methods.description: Two-stage semi-mechanistic prediction of time to progression under chemotherapy from serial plasma LDH and NSE, the model of Buil-Bruna et al. (AAPS J 2014;16(3):609-619; 60 SCLC patients, first-line platinum/etoposide +/- radiotherapy): Stage 1 fits - jointly on the two markers - the paper's population pharmacodynamic model: a K-PD chemotherapy exposure CT(t) (unit dose per 21-day cycle, six cycles, first-order elimination KDE = 1.16/week), the cumulative exposure, the latent disease level D(t) (D(0) = 1, linear growth lambda, drug effect EDrug = -alpha*CT(t)*D(t) with the resistance scaling 1 + gamma*AUCCT(t), gamma = 0.377/week, and no radiotherapy/G-CSF term because the benchmark data carry no such covariate), and per-marker turnover models of the log-transformed concentrations (zero-order synthesis Kin_m + KD_m*D(t) minus first-order loss Kout_m, Kout fixed at the paper's 3.2/week from MRT 0.311 weeks); the observations are log-transformed and each marker has its own residual error. Random effects (per the paper's Table I) on lambda, alpha and the two marker levels at time zero, with their covariance; the paper's NONMEM v7.2 SAEM/Laplacian or MONOLIX are commercial and no control stream is published, so the wrapper fits the population parameters by pooled nonlinear least squares and the individual parameters by penalised empirical-Bayes estimates, alternated for a few rounds (recorded in the README). Each patient's covariate is Dji = predicted relative change of the disease level between the first and the last of their draw times at or before the benchmark landmark (their CT-time proxies - CT data are not an input of the benchmark; the paper's Dji is the change in disease level between CT-scan times about 8 weeks apart). Stage 2 is the paper's time-to-progression model h(t) = h0(t)*exp(delta*Dji) with the log-logistic baseline h0(t) = mu*psi*t^(psi-1)/(1 + mu*t^psi), fitted by maximum likelihood on the training patients still event-free at the landmark with the likelihood truncated there (the paper's Laplacian method/NONMEM is not available); mu, psi and delta are fitted on every training fold, never the paper's one-cohort numbers (mu = 4.91e-6/week, psi = 3.66, delta = 0.593). The wrapper writes each patient's own probability of progression by every horizon, P(T <= h | T > landmark) = 1 - S(h)/S(landmark) with S(t) = exp(-H(t)) and H(t) = exp(delta*Dji)*log(1 + mu*t^psi), and risk = that probability at the first horizon (the paper reports no per-patient score); the model has no random effects in stage 2 - interpatient variability enters through Dji, exactly as in the paper. Only progression is predicted by the model (the paper's time-to-progression endpoint); the death, no-response and progressive-disease outcomes use the benchmark's conversion of the risk. Dji is winsorized to [-0.9, 2.0] (the stage-1 fit can produce extreme latent changes; the paper's own changes are reported near +23.5% Youden cut-off with a ~74% median disease reduction), and a patient with fewer than two usable draw days by the landmark gets no prediction with the reason in note; the wrapper's deviations from the paper (K-PD origin at the first dose instead of diagnosis, draw times as CT-time proxies, first-to-last-draw Dji, resistance scaling form, estimation method) are listed in the README.

methods.description: The semi-mechanistic NLME population model of Buil-Bruna et al. (AAPS J 2014;16(3):609-619) for two serial serum markers driven by a latent, unobserved disease level: each marker follows a turnover model (zero-order physiological synthesis Kin plus a disease-driven term KD*D(t), first-order elimination Kout), D(t) is the latent disease level (D(0)=1) which grows linearly at lambda, is reduced by chemotherapy through a K-PD exposure CT(t) (normalised dose 1 per 21-day cycle, KDE fixed from the combination half-lives), with the second-order drug effect -alpha*CT*D, loses effect with cumulative exposure (resistance gamma*AUCCT) and grows slower under radiotherapy (1 - beta*RT); the paper fits the joint model to log-transformed LDH and NSE with SAEM in NONMEM v7.2 (tumour data were NOT used for model development) and classifies the change in the predicted disease level between consecutive CT scans (Dji, ~8 weeks apart) as disease progression vs non-progression at the Youden cutoff (+23.5%) - the ROC/AUC is the evaluation, not a probability. THE WRAPPER (every difference in README.md): NONMEM is commercial and no control stream is published (job.code empty; the supplement is author-only), so the full structure above is estimated in base R - per-patient posterior-mode (MAP) estimates of the two disease parameters (lambda, alpha) by weighted least squares of the joint two-marker model with the paper's between-subject variability as log-normal priors (deterministic grid + BFGS, reproducible without a seed), the per-marker turnover parameters re-expressed in the cohort's own marker scale (median baseline, the paper's MRT and Kin/(Kin+KD) share), the marker's physiological floor (the D=0 steady state) taken from the low tail of the training data because another marker cannot be assumed to stay above the SCLC LDH floor, the paper's parameter values for the disease kinetics and K-PD, and the G-CSF covariate effect on the physiological LDH synthesis and radiotherapy when cov_rt / cov_gcsf are supplied; risk = the per-patient predicted disease-level change (percent) between the last draw at or before the landmark (the previous assessment; in the paper biomarkers were sampled at the CT times) and the next assessment 56 days later; call = 1 at the Youden cutoff derived on the training fold (the paper's +23.5 as the fallback); no probability is written (TxResBench converts); a patient with fewer than 2 draws by the landmark or a degenerate fit gets no prediction, with the reason in note.

methods.description: The landmark flexible-hazards cure (LFHC) model of Xie, Huang, Li, Tsodikov & Bhalla, Ann. Appl. Stat. 18(4) 2024, 2796-2817 (DOI 10.1214/24-aoas1906): at the landmark, an FHC (promotion-time) cure model is fitted on the patients still event-free, with the event clock reset to the time since the landmark; the covariates are the baseline and the most current (last observation carried forward) marker values plus any baseline covariates, and the conditional survival is S(t | L) = exp(-exp(beta0 + z'psi) F0(t)^exp(x'gamma)) with a nonparametric baseline cumulative hazard F0 and a flexible short-term part X that allows non-proportional-hazards covariates (the paper's real-data model has the marker in Z and the age group in X). The model's own conditional probability of the event by each horizon (1 minus the conditional survival, conditioning on being event-free at the landmark) is written as risk (first horizon) and as p_progression_H<h> / p_death_H<h>, one LFHC per learned survival outcome, shared when the outcome data coincide. The paper's other output, the conditional cure probability, has no column in the benchmark predictions table: it is summarised in run.json. The wrapper fits with fhc::fhcmodel on the residual clock as paper eq. (4) requires (the published curedynpred::pred_landmark_model fits on the original scale, which makes its conditional-survival output degenerate; see README); when the flexibility estimate or the marker terms are degenerate it falls back to a Cox model of the post-landmark clock, recorded in run.json.

methods.description: The LiBIO (Liquid Biomarker of Immunotherapy Outcomes) score and fixed-threshold immune-checkpoint-blockade response call of Wang B et al., 'Longitudinal liquid biopsy identifies an early predictive biomarker of immune checkpoint blockade response in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma', Nature Communications 2025, DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-63538-4: the signature scores of the 164-gene effector-memory CD8+ T cell (Tem) and 137-gene B cell signatures (published as Supplementary Data 1) are computed for one sample by the single-sample GSEA (ssGSEA) algorithm on the sample's transcriptome (bulk RNA-seq TPM or single-cell pseudobulk), and the LiBIO score is their mean; the sample is called a responder when the score is at or above the paper's fixed threshold (0.201 for bulk RNA-seq HNSCC - the wrapper default; 0.424 single-cell HNSCC; 0.196 melanoma; 0.632 NSCLC; 0.383 breast cancer - threshold and the ssGSEA alpha are method parameters). The scores were derived from the Day 9 (time point 2) mouse 4MOSC-HNSCC blood single-cell data and are applied to human cohorts without retraining (fitted false). The paper publishes the rule and the gene lists but not the score computation (the repository holds only figure/evaluation scripts and pre-computed per-patient scores), so the wrapper implements the ssGSEA random walk of Barbie et al. 2009 exactly as the R package GSVA 2.0.7 (alpha = 0.25, the Barbie range normalization es/(max-min) over the cohort; the range is learned on the training side and applied at predict), applies no transform to the reported marker values (the paper states none beyond TPM/pseudobulk), and treats a gene absent from a sample's measured vector as not in that sample's universe (the paper's per-cohort 'genes not expressed were filtered out' reading). It scores the patient's latest scorable on-treatment draw on or before the landmark (the paper scores one sample per subject, pre- or on-treatment; recorded). It writes the risk of the spec's projection for this method: the LiBIO score itself (the paper's native continuous score, higher = responder-favourable) and the contract's call orientation, 1 = treatment judged failing = score below the threshold, 0 = responder (score >= threshold; the paper states no boundary convention and its analogous cutpointr use is '>='); no probability is written (the paper defines none per patient; TxResBench converts the risk). Marker -> signature-gene assignment is by name: normalised marker names matched against the published human symbols or the panel genes' Ensembl ids; markers carrying the authors' pre-computed score columns (the repository's 'filtered_t2_Effector memory CD8' / 'filtered_t2_B cell' / 'mean_score' and close spellings) are used directly when present (the authors' own arithmetic, not recomputed); a unit whose markers match neither (no published list ambiguity: the wrapper is DEFINED for this fixed 294-gene list) is scored by the declared generic role convention (markers[0] = Tem score, markers[1] = B score; one marker = the combined score) with the reading recorded in run.json. A patient with no on-treatment draw by the landmark, or a query draw that does not yield both signature scores, gets no prediction with the reason in note. The seven genes present in both published lists (EEF1A1, EEF2, ETS1, NACA, PTPRCAP, RACK1, RPS13) are counted in both signatures (the panel's unique gene set is 294).

methods.description: The per-patient predicted-trajectory suppression call of the UK Collaborative HIV Cohort (UK CHIC) Writing Committee, 'Predicting virological decay in patients starting combination antiretroviral therapy', AIDS 2016;30(11):1817-1827 (DOI 10.1097/QAD.0000000000001125; 9562 antiretroviral-naive UK CHIC patients starting first-line cART after 1997, 6435 fitting / 3127 validation). Stage 1: a random-effects model of log10-transformed repeated HIV-1 RNA viral load since start of cART - the paper's final model, a linear spline with knots at 2 weeks and 3 months post-cART (time in months since the first dose), the intercept and all trajectory terms random at the patient level, and covariate interactions with the intercept and trajectory terms. The paper names no software and publishes no code (verified: the full text, the Europe PMC XML and the downloaded online Appendix contain no package, language or code statement), so the wrapper reimplements the model with nlme 3.1-166 and refits it per benchmark training fold (the paper's published HIV-specific coefficients are not transferable to the benchmark's generic marker, and the BIC search among fractional polynomials and 1-2-knot splines is not re-run: the final published spline is fitted directly - the spec records both routes and both differences). Stage 2: per future measurement the paper's prediction formula (online Appendix, after Taylor & Law 1998): predicted Y_iF = X_iF beta + Lambda_iF Omega_i^-1 (Y_i - X_i beta) with Omega_i = Z_i G Z_i^T + sigma^2 I, Lambda_iF = Z_iF G Z_i^T, the prediction error Omega_iF - Lambda_iF Omega_i^-1 Lambda_iF^T + (X_iF - Lambda_iF Omega_i^-1 X_i) var(beta) (X_iF - Lambda_iF Omega_i^-1 X_i)^T, with var(beta), G and sigma^2 from the fitted model. Stage 3: the published rule - 'suppression was a priori defined as a single viral load 200 copies/ml or less' (md:126-127) and patients are predicted suppressed when the predicted future trajectory reaches such a value 'within 6 months of starting cART' (md:220-223; 26 weeks absolute from the first dose, md:100-103). The wrapper writes risk = the predicted minimum of the future marker trajectory within the suppression window, in the marker's native scale (the quantity the rule thresholds; no probability exists natively - higher = a less suppressed predicted trajectory = more likely failing), and call = 1 when the patient is not predicted suppressed (observed value at the landmark above the cutoff AND the predicted trajectory never reaches it) - the benchmark's failure orientation of the paper's predicted-suppressed/not-suppressed call. The paper evaluates suppression-rule predictions at the 2/3/4-month clinic visits with diagnostic indices (Table 2: DOR 5.25/7.49/15.60 at 2/3/4 months) and draws prediction graphs with 95% prediction intervals; the wrapper does both internally (the prediction-error formula is implemented) but the benchmark carries the per-patient call and risk only. Differences from the paper (each recorded in README.md and run.json): the model and predictions are refitted per benchmark training fold rather than using the published HIV coefficient set; the paper's BIC model selection among fractional polynomials and splines is not re-run (the final published spline is fitted, and a spline segment with no support in the training data is dropped with its random term, recorded); covariates enter through the benchmark's cov_* columns with the paper's intercept-and-trajectory interaction structure (the paper's seven HIV-specific covariates - sex, age, ethnicity, exposure, first-line regimen type, pretreatment CD4 and VL category - arrive as generic columns, and the full-covariate published model is used when they are present; with none, the time-spline model alone is fitted - recorded); the suppression cutoff and horizon are the paper's published constants (200 copies/ml, 26 weeks) and the future time-point grid is not stated in the paper (a 0.25-month grid plus the spline knots and the horizon is used); the paper's handling of a below-detection first suppressed value ('replaced with the detection limit value', md:140-143) is applied to all below-detection draws with the benchmark's __lod value if present, else half the smallest positive training value (the numeric limit is not stated in the paper, '?'); the paper predicts only among patients not censored and not suppressed at the specified visit (abstaining), while the benchmark's universal per-patient call applies the rule to every patient with at least two informative draws by the landmark - a patient already suppressed at the landmark receives call = 0 rather than no call (recorded).

(md:143) on the FOUR raw 6-month post-treatment values - anti-PLA2R antibody status (positive >= 14 RU/mL vs negative reference, md:34, md:153), 24-h urine protein quantification (g/24 h), serum albumin level (g/L) and eGFR (ml/min-1.73 m2) - one-stage multivariable binary logistic regression of the 12-month NR label, all four terms retained (Table 3 multivariate column md:154-157: antibody positive OR 8.256 (2.793-24.407, p<0.001); 24-h urine protein OR 1.625 (1.223-2.159, p<0.001); albumin OR 0.876 (0.771-0.996, p=0.043); eGFR OR 0.987 (0.967-1.008, p=0.235 - kept despite p=0.235, no stepwise/backward removal described); model-level discrimination AUC 0.932 (95% CI 0.894-0.970, Figure 3, md:143); DeLong comparison with the paper's 1-month model Z=1.04, p=0.2984 (md:171)). NO coefficients/intercept, NO nomogram and NO cutoff are published (md:143, md:149-158, md:166), so the wrapper refits the paper's model on the benchmark training fold: a binary logistic regression (Newton-Raphson IRLS with backtracking, ridge-stabilised, raw values, complete case - the paper's 'Complete case analysis was performed... No imputation methods were applied', md:70) of the no_response outcome (the harness's reading of the paper's 12-month NR label - non-remission is neither CR nor PR, i.e. the non-responder class) on the four predictors taken from each patient's last draw at baseline_max_day < day <= landmark_day (the corpus convention of the paper's fixed 6-month time point; draws after the landmark never enter). risk = the fitted linear predictor (already failure-oriented: higher = more likely non-remission), p_no_response = sigmoid(risk) as the method's own probability of the paper's NR at 12 months; TxResBench converts the risk for progression, death and progressive_disease. methods.description: Binary logistic regression of disease control (DCR = best RECIST response CR, PR or SD lasting more than 6 months; SD under 6 months and PD are the failure class, Guida et al., J Transl Med 2022;20:193, N = 272 BRAF wild-type metastatic melanoma patients on first-line immune checkpoint inhibitors) on every marker passed, each entering as TWO variables - its baseline value continuous and its one-month difference Delta = T1 - T0 dichotomised at a cut-off - per the paper's two-variable and multivariable logistic analyses (md:103, md:243). The wrapper refits the published specification on the benchmark training patients: per marker, T0 = the marker's last value on or before the baseline day and T1 = its last value after the baseline and at or before the landmark (the paper's two fixed draws, baseline and before the subsequent cycle at 21/28 days, md:90/md:92); the Delta cut-off is re-derived per training fold from an ROC curve against the training patients' failure status - the paper's 'common and constant cut-off values' from ROC curves of the OS (md:92/md:101), with OS as the classification when the training data carry it and PFS otherwise (roc_outcome auto; the paper's optimality criterion is not stated, so Youden's J is the wrapper's documented choice); one multivariable logistic model of the failure-oriented response label enters every marker's baseline + Delta-indicator terms plus the cov_* clinical columns when the covariate track is present (the paper's age at diagnosis, sex, number of metastatic sites and basal LDH terms, md:103; with the track absent the wrapper fits the marker terms only, a documented fallback), reduced by stepwise selection on AIC (md:103; the direction, entry/exit thresholds and starting model are not published, so the wrapper's own both-directions-from-the-full-model implementation is documented). The fitted label is the harness outcome no_response (best RECIST response SD or PD), the closest harness analogue of the paper's DCR failure class - the harness cannot express the paper's 'SD lasting more than 6 months' rule (md:94), a documented difference; the wrapper fits P(no response) directly so the risk is failure-oriented by construction (the paper's Methods target 'the probability of a positive DCR', md:103; its Results text reads OR > 1 as 'a poorer DCR'/'risk of non-response', md:236/md:294 - the wrapper records the choice and reports the label-direction ambiguity, which the paper never resolves). The paper's per-parameter two-variable models (baseline + Delta, Table 5) are also fitted and their ORs, 95% Wald CIs and p-values written to run.json (the paper's reported output), while the per-patient risk is the final multivariable model's fitted probability (fallback chain: multivariable, then the most significant two-variable model, then the constant model - each recorded). The paper publishes no code (SAS 9.4 only, no procedure named; no code-availability statement), so the fit, coefficients and every probability are the wrapper's own. A patient without the T0/T1 pair of a marker term the final model uses, with a non-finite value for it, or - on the covariate track - with a missing or unseen-level covariate gets no prediction with the reason in note: the paper defines no imputation or fallback (a zero value is the harness's below-detection encoding and the paper reports no handling for it, '?').

methods.description: Per-patient probability of poor therapeutic effect (progression-free survival < 16 months) of anlotinib plus osimertinib in advanced non-small cell lung cancer with acquired resistance (EGFR T790M), from the multivariable binary logistic regression that the nomogram of Liu M, Wang W, Tang M, Li K, Zeng W, 'A predictive model for anlotinib-osimertinib efficacy in advanced NSCLC with acquired resistance: circulating tumor DNA and angiogenesis markers', Am J Transl Res 2025;17(10):8439-8453 (DOI 10.62347/HTAG4562; combination-therapy group n = 197 split 7:3, training n = 138 (71 better / 67 poor), test n = 59 (31 / 28); published AUC 0.912 training / 0.959 test; Hosmer-Lemeshow chi2 = 7.892, p = 0.444): 'Multivariate logistic regression was performed with PFS <16 months as the dependent variable. Biomarkers with P<0.05 in the inter-group comparison were included as independent variables in the analysis.' (md:285-289) on the six after-two-cycles (6-week) plasma predictors - ctDNA (ng/mL), VAF (%), the T790M mutation clearance rate derived as (baseline - post-treatment)/baseline (md:257-261), VEGF-A (pg/mL), VEGFR-2 (pg/mL), MMP-9 (ng/mL) - presented as a nomogram (Figure 3; 'A nomogram was developed using significant predictors identified through multivariate logistic regression', md:831-834) with a total score and five risk groups (low / intermediate / high / very high / extreme-risk, md:1100-1104). The paper publishes the six coefficients (Table 6: ctDNA B = 0.533, VAF B = 0.414, T790M clearance B = -1.605, VEGF-A B = 0.021, VEGFR-2 B = 0.017, MMP-9 B = 0.075) but NO intercept (Table 6 has no constant row, md:953-1015, '?'), NO analysis code (job.code = []; the analyses ran in SPSS 29.0, md:275-276, proprietary, no syntax published) and only two nomogram point anchors (ctDNA 5.35 ng/mL = 45 points, VAF 9.09% = 60 points, md:1095-1100). The wrapper therefore APPLIES THE PUBLISHED COEFFICIENTS - the paper's own score - and calibrates the own probability only: the unpublished intercept (md:953-1015, '?') enters the probability as the wrapper's benchmark-side mean-level calibration b0 = logit(training PFS < 16-months rate) - mean(published linear predictor) over the complete-case labeled training patients (the moment-based reading; the maximum-likelihood offset fit is unstable under the benchmark's folding and is not reproduced; the spec's new_patient_prediction.route alternative - the refit route with the per-fold P < 0.05 inter-group re-screening is recorded as a deviation but not implemented: the published model IS the six-predictor set, md:311-313, Table 6, and the published coefficients are the score, while a per-fold refit would replace the paper's fixed model by a fold-dependent fit silently absorbing the benchmark's marker units). The paper's own label - derived in the wrapper from the benchmark's PFS days/event as the 16-month split (16 x (365.25/12) = 487 days from treatment start; a patient censored before 487 days without an event has no label - the paper's censoring semantics at 16 months are not stated, md:196-199, '?') - enters only that intercept estimation, on the complete-case patients (the paper enrolled only patients with complete records, md:136-137). risk = the published linear predictor exactly (a monotone function of the paper's logit of the failure label; a function of the markers alone, so it is invariant to the benchmark's id/row-order/time-unit worlds; failure-oriented by construction), p_no_response = logistic(b0 + risk) as the method's own probability of the paper's failure label (the benchmark's response-probability slot; the p_event_H* columns are left empty - the paper's label is a fixed binary PFS split, not a landmark-conditioned event probability). No call is written: the paper publishes no model probability cutoff or total-score risk-group thresholds (md:1100-1104, '?'; the Table 7 cut-offs and the decision-pathway thresholds are the paper's separate per-marker rules and are NOT used, md:1023-1079, md:1305-1320). The wrapper takes exactly six markers (roles resolved from the marker names with a documented priority and positional fallback for unrecognized names, so the synthetic gate markers M1..M6 map to ctDNA, VAF, T790M, VEGF-A, VEGFR-2, MMP-9), the T790M clearance rate is derived in the fraction scale (0 = no clearance, 1 = full clearance, matching the paper's Table 7 best threshold 0.500) from the baseline and after-two-cycles T790M quantification, and the six features are each patient's last draw after the baseline and at or before the benchmark landmark (the corpus convention for the paper's fixed 6-week draw; a documented difference - the paper's schedule is exactly 6 weeks, md:241-244). A patient with no after-two-cycles draw, an incomplete six-marker panel, or no detectable baseline T790M quantification (the clearance formula divides by the baseline concentration, md:257-261) gets no prediction with the reason in note - the paper's complete-case enrolment and its unpublished fallback, '?'.
methods.licence: n/a for the model (the article, Am J Transl Res 2025;17(10):8439-8453, DOI 10.62347/HTAG4562, is published open access, but it publishes no analysis code, no code repository and no data- or code-availability statement - it ends at the reference list, md:1342-1616; the only software named for the analyses is SPSS 29.0, md:275-276, proprietary, with no published syntax; the nomogram-construction tool is not named, '?'); the wrapper is an original reimplementation in base R stats::glm plus the base image's TxrMethod helper, and no third-party code licence is asserted

required_markers.list_source: the fixed six-predictor list the published nomogram model IS DEFINED on (Table 6 md:953-1015; 'Our model incorporated 6 predictor variables in the final multivariate analysis.', md:311-313; entry rule 'Biomarkers with P<0.05 in the inter-group comparison were included as independent variables', md:287-289): after-two-cycles ctDNA (ng/mL), after-two-cycles VAF (%), the T790M mutation clearance rate (%) derived by the formula md:257-261, after-two-cycles VEGF-A (pg/mL), after-two-cycles VEGFR-2 (pg/mL), after-two-cycles MMP-9 (ng/mL). Five markers enter as their after-two-cycles (= 6-week = two-3-week-cycles, md:241-244) measured values; the T790M clearance rate is DERIVED inside the wrapper from the baseline and post-treatment values of the plasma T790M quantification (md:257-261), which is the third required marker. The standard ids are the benchmark-side mapping (the paper gives no id system; the ids follow the corpus conventions for a per-draw ctDNA amount, a per-draw panel-level VAF, a per-draw plasma T790M quantification and the plasma protein concentrations: cf. cox-early-kinetics, ctdna-ctc-ki67-combined, ctdna-turnover-weibull, rsf-cytokine-*). A dataset without any of the six measurands cannot run the model (the paper's model is exactly this six-feature set; no clinical covariate enters Table 6, md:287-289, md:524-531). The model is NOT defined on the paper's single-marker Youden-index cut-offs (Table 7: ctDNA 5.350 ng/mL, VAF 9.090%, T790M clearance 0.500, VEGF-A 217.870 pg/mL, VEGFR-2 221.480 pg/mL, MMP-9 74.400 ng/mL, md:1023-1079) and not on the clinical-decision-pathway thresholds (md:1305-1320) - those are the paper's separate single-marker rules

markers.name: total plasma circulating-tumour-DNA (ctDNA) concentration, ng/mL, from the capture-based plasma NGS panel ('After two cycles of treatment ctDNA' in Tables 4-7; NGS 'NextSeq 550, Illumina, USA' with an 86-gene panel, average depth 1000x, md:246-254) - the paper's ctDNA predictor, entered as its after-two-cycles (6-week) value (md:635-656, md:965-972). Corpus id convention for a per-draw ctDNA amount measured directly (cf. cox-early-kinetics 'cfDNA_ng_ml' for the Qubit cfDNA amount): the total ctDNA concentration series is distinct from the panel VAF and from detectability; the benchmark-side mapping must supply the amount itself, the wrapper never reconstructs it from components

per-plasma-draw panel-level ctDNA variant allele fraction (VAF, %) of the NGS panel's detected variants ('After two cycles of treatment VAF' in Tables 4-7; variant inclusion VAF >= 5% with Phred >= 30, coverage uniformity >= 95%, md:254-256) - the paper's VAF predictor, entered as its after-two-cycles value (md:973-980). The paper never states whether this VAF is the max/mean/other summary over the detected variants ('?'); the corpus id convention for a per-draw panel-level VAF summary (id 'ctDNA_maxVAF'; cf. ctdna-ctc-ki67-combined, combined-ctdna-risk-rule) is declared, and the wrapper does not recompute the summary from per-variant calls

EGFR T790M mutation quantification in plasma ctDNA per draw (allelic fraction/concentration; the paper's T790M 'concentration' in its clearance formula - 'clearance rate = (baseline concentration - post-treatment concentration)/baseline concentration x 100%' (md:257-261) - is not further defined,?). Corpus id convention for a per-draw plasma T790M quantification (cf. ctdna-turnover-weibull, plasma-genotype-monitoring 'EGFR T790M allelic fraction'): the wrapper derives the paper's T790M mutation clearance rate = (baseline - post-treatment)/baseline from this series (the ratio is scale-invariant, so any concentration/AF scale of the quantification works); the derived clearance rate is NOT itself a required marker

plasma vascular endothelial growth factor-A (VEGF-A) concentration, pg/mL, ELISA ('a multi-mode microplate reader (Synergy H1, BioTek Instruments, USA) and an Abcam kit', md:263-266) - the paper's VEGF-A predictor, entered as its after-two-cycles value (md:989-996). Corpus id convention for a plasma protein concentration (cf. rsf-cytokine-difference/rsf-cytokine-foldchange 'VEGFA'): the encoding gene symbol

plasma vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2 (VEGFR-2, KDR) concentration, pg/mL - the paper's VEGFR-2 predictor, entered as its after-two-cycles value (md:997-1004); the encoding gene is KDR (corpus plasma-protein convention)

plasma matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) concentration, ng/mL - the paper's MMP-9 predictor, entered as its after-two-cycles value (md:1005-1012); the encoding gene is MMP9 (corpus plasma-protein convention, cf. rsf-cytokine-snapshot 'MMP1' for MMP-1)

methods.description: Univariable binomial logistic regression of the RECIST 1.1 best response on the binary direction of change of tumor-informed ctDNA (Signatera, MTM/mL) from the baseline draw to the 3-4-week draw after anti-PD-1 based immune checkpoint inhibitor initiation in advanced-stage unresectable stage III/IV melanoma (Vincent et al., JCO Precision Oncology 2026, DOI 10.1200/PO-25-00254; 117 patients; Table 2: for ctDNA decrease (change <= 0, n = 76) vs increase (>0 change, n = 41, reference) OR 30.56 [95% CI 10.64-87.74] for disease control and 23.54 [8.58-64.57] for objective response, both P <.001). The paper fits the model TWICE - disease control (CR + PR + SD) and objective response (PR + CR) - with the direction as the only predictor ('using the change in ctDNA levels (decrease v increase) as the primary independent variable'; no covariate, no adjustment set, no selection), and fixes the exposure rules: change = ctDNA(3-4 weeks) - ctDNA(baseline), direction only (no magnitude cutoff), a net zero change and patients undetectable at both draws classified as decrease, and the increase group as the reference level. The paper prints no coefficients or intercept (only the ORs), names no analysis code (Stata 18 only), so the wrapper REFITS the two models on the benchmark training patients with base R stats::glm; the two paper labels are the complements of the harness's failure outcomes - disease control vs PD = progressive_disease (1 = PD) and objective response vs SD/PD = no_response (1 = SD or PD) - so fitting the complement label directly is the same model (the no_response OR per decrease is 1/23.54, the progressive_disease one 1/30.56). It writes the fitted P(no_response) as risk (the paper defines no per-patient probability; the disease-control model is fitted and recorded in run.json, and on the same binary exposure the two order every patient identically - only when the training data give no varying no_response label does the fitted P(progressive_disease) stand in for the risk, recorded in run.json) and the paper's direction call under the contract's failure orientation as call: 1 = ctDNA increase at 3-4 weeks (the paper's unfavorable group: 16.7% objective response / 26.7% disease control vs 80.8% / 88.5% in the decrease group), 0 = decrease - exactly the direction-only relchange-threshold rule (cutoff 0) the spec records as the paper's binary call. No p_* column is written (response-call group; the paper publishes no probability and TxResBench converts the risk). Baseline = the last ctDNA draw on or before the baseline day; on-treatment = the last draw in the 3-4-week window (days 21-28 by default, setting window_weeks [3, 4]); a patient without either is outside the paper's eligibility ('with at least two measurements... one at baseline... the other at 3-4 weeks') and gets no prediction with the reason in note; the benchmark's below-detection encoding (value 0) is read as undetectable per the paper's classification. The paper's percent-change category model (a three-level exposure) and its PFS/OS Cox analyses are separate methods and are not wrapped here.

College Station, TX: StataCorp LLC)' is named and no command, do-file, coefficients or code of it are used; this wrapper refits the specified model with base R stats::glm and relies on no paper function or package)

methods.description: A per-patient risk score for non-pCR (pathological complete response failure) after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in locally advanced rectal cancer, from the paper's combining predictive model - Wang Y, Yang L, Bao H, et al., PLoS Medicine 2021;18(9):e1003741: a multivariable logistic regression with non-pCR as the positive event, built by the paper's P-value selection cascade (features with P <= 0.1 in the univariable logistic regression enter the multivariable regression; only features with P <= 0.25 in the multivariable regression are kept), and the per-patient risk score = intercept + sum(b_feature x feature status) of the paper's reference 25. The paper publishes no analysis code and its coefficients live in S5 Table, which is not in the provided text, so the wrapper refits the published procedure on the benchmark training patients with base R stats::glm and writes the risk score (the linear predictor, higher = more likely non-pCR) and p_no_response = P(non-pCR) = logistic(risk). The paper's six features - baseline TP53/HRR/HMT mutation detection, T234_clearance (baseline highest-VAF mutation undetectable at all three pre-surgery draws), acquired mutation status, and the mrTRG grade 1-5 - come from a 422-gene ctDNA panel and the pre-surgery MRI and cannot be read out of the benchmark's marker interface (per-variant ctDNA calls are not curated marker ids and the detected HRR/HMT gene subsets are unpublished), so the wrapper derives the paper's feature types from whatever marker series it receives: per marker, the baseline detection status (the TP53/HRR/HMT statuses' role), persistent on-treatment non-detection (T234_clearance's role), detection at >= 2 on-treatment draws (acquired-mutation's role) plus the baseline and last on-treatment marker level and its relative change as the quantitative features (the role of the model's one ordinal covariate mrTRG); mrTRG-like per-patient clinical grades arrive as cov_* columns and enter numerically as given. Every mapping and the unpublished pieces (coefficients, mrTRG coding, no cutoff) are recorded in the README; a patient without a detectable baseline marker value (the paper's 89-of-103 model-cohort rule) or without the data a fitted feature needs abstains with the reason, never an invented score.

methods.description: Per-patient probability of NON-RESPONSE (stable or progressive disease, SD/PD vs CR/PR per iRECIST) to anti-PD-1 immunotherapy from the paper's day-28 multivariable logistic regression of Zhu Z, Jiang J, Cao M, Cao D, 'Early On-Treatment Expansion of Peripheral gammadeltaT Cells as a Noninvasive Biomarker of Response to Programmed Death-1 Inhibitor Therapy in Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer', Cancer Management and Research 2026:18, 624716 (DOI 10.2147/CMAR.S624716; n = 60 advanced NSCLC patients on nivolumab monotherapy 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks as second-line or later, 37 responders CR/PR / 23 non-responders SD/PD, md:100-111, md:184-185; extracted text cited as md:<line>): 'Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify independent factors associated with SD/PD.' (md:427) on the THREE raw day-28 values after treatment initiation (md:20-21) - day-28 serum CEA (ng/mL, ELISA), day-28 peripheral gammadelta T cell proportion (%, flow cytometry) and day-28 peripheral Th17 cell proportion (%, flow cytometry, intracellular IL-17) - all three entered and reported in the one model, Table 2 (md:460-476): day-28 CEA OR 1.183 (95% CI 1.011-1.385, P = 0.036); day-28 gammadelta T cells OR 0.164 (95% CI 0.040-0.663, P = 0.011); day-28 Th17 cells OR 0.073 (95% CI 0.015-0.362, P = 0.001) - higher day-28 CEA independently associated with a HIGHER likelihood of SD/PD, higher gammadelta T / Th17 proportions with a LOWER likelihood of non-response (md:428-431). No adjustment covariates, no interactions and no selection procedure are described; no intercept/coefficients, no per-patient probabilities and no cutoff are printed. Since the paper publishes no equation and no analysis code (job.code = []; only 'SPSS20.0 statistical software was used for data processing.', md:174), the wrapper refits the paper's model on the benchmark training fold: a binary logistic regression (Newton-Raphson IRLS with backtracking, ridge-stabilised) of the harness's no_response outcome (1 = SD/PD, the paper's label view: responders CR/PR vs non-responders SD/PD per iRECIST, md:135-137, md:146-151) on the three predictors taken from each patient's LAST finite draw at baseline_max_day < day <= landmark_day (the corpus convention for the paper's fixed day-28 time point; draws after the landmark and baseline values never enter), raw values, complete case with no imputation ('All enrolled patients completed the research and had complete paired peripheral immune data for the final analyses.', md:126-127). risk = the fitted linear predictor (failure-oriented: higher = more likely non-response, the paper's own 'developing SD/PD' direction, md:460), p_no_response = sigmoid(risk) as the method's own P(SD/PD) refitted on the training fold; TxResBench converts the risk for progression, death and progressive_disease. No call: the paper reports no probability cutoff for the regression (the ROC cutoffs of the same paper belong to its single-marker threshold rule, a separate method). A patient without the complete three-marker day-28 snapshot gets no prediction with the reason in note (complete case, no imputation); the wrapper refuses at fit when the training data give no no_response outcome (the paper's label is not observable), fewer than 10 complete-case patients carry it, or only one class is present (the paper's 60-patient / 37-23 split is the smallest sensible scale; a degenerate fit would not be the paper's model).

methods.description: Per-marker multiple logistic regression of the objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR) on ONE serum marker's change from baseline to cycle 2 of immune-checkpoint-inhibitor therapy (delta = cycle-2 value minus baseline value), categorized high (increase) vs low at the marker's optimal cut-off point, with a sex main effect and the second-order sex x marker interaction, reduced by backward elimination on the Bayesian Information Criterion (Pasello, Salizzato et al., J Transl Med 2024;22(1):194, DOI 10.1186/s12967-024-04920-6: 161 ICI-treated advanced melanoma/NSCLC patients, 13 serum cytokines; the change models report per-marker odds ratios for high vs low change: increases in IL-8 (cut-off 3.23 pg/ml, OR 0.36 [0.17-0.77]) and VEGF (45.0 pg/ml, OR 0.32 [0.15-0.69]) with a lower probability of ORR, increase in sPD-L1 (6.4 pg/ml, OR 0.40 [0.19-0.85]) with a lower probability of DCR; no significant interactions with sex for the changes - analyses run in RStudio and no code, package or coefficients are published, so the wrapper refits the published structure on the benchmark fold). For every fold the wrapper takes the marker's baseline draw (last value at day <= baseline_max_day) and its first on-treatment draw up to the landmark (the paper's cycle-2 draw, the first after the baseline cycle), derives delta = cycle2 - baseline, finds the outcome-specific cut-point on the training patients by maximizing the discriminative ability of the binary logistic model of that outcome's failure label (Harrell's-AUC reading of the paper's 'maximizing the discriminative capacity of the logistic model'; the 'minimax' criterion and the package are not stated), and fits the multiple logistic with the high/low change, sex (matched by name from the covariate track) and their interaction, kept or removed by BIC backward elimination. The paper's ORR model maps to the benchmark outcome no_response (best RECIST SD or PD vs CR/PR) and its DCR model to progressive_disease (PD vs CR/PR/SD); the wrapper refits each against the failure label (the same model class, signs flipped) and writes the fitted failure probability as risk, p_no_response and p_progressive_disease (the paper reports only cohort-level odds ratios). When the covariate track carries no sex column the wrapper fits the published structure without the sex terms (recorded as a deviation, as the benchmark's main track compares methods on the blood signal alone).

methods.description: Binary logistic regression of the response at the first CT scan (PD vs no-PD = PR or SD) on the continuous percent relative change of serum LDH from the baseline value, adjusted for the line of treatment (first vs second line and higher) - the sensitivity analysis of Diem et al. (Br J Cancer 2016) on 29 patients with metastatic melanoma treated with anti-PD-1 antibodies and a baseline LDH above the upper limit of normal. The paper publishes no coefficients, probabilities or code (results 'data not shown'), so the wrapper refits the model on the training patients with base R stats::glm (binomial, logit): the predictor is 100*(x1 - x0)/x0, x0 = last draw on or before the baseline day and x1 = last draw after it and by the landmark (the paper's pre-first-CT value), the adjustment terms are the cov_* columns of the patients table when covariates are given (with one 0/1 indicator of 'second line and higher', the paper's covariate; without them the wrapper fits the unadjusted model - the benchmark's default evaluation has no line-of-treatment column), and the label is the harness's PD vs no-PD outcome (progressive_disease, 1 = PD - the paper's positive class, so the risk column carries P(PD) under the identity mapping, declared in the README). It writes risk and its own p_progressive_disease; TxResBench converts the risk for the other outcomes. The paper's analysis set requires a baseline LDH above the ULN: the setting uln (default: no filter) restores that eligibility for data that carry a ULN or store LDH in ULN multiples; a patient without a baseline and an on-treatment draw, with a non-positive baseline LDH, or with a missing adjustment covariate gets no prediction.

methods.description: Binary multivariable logistic regression of the end-of-research treatment response - the paper's histologic liver NAS improvement by >=1 point vs no improvement (md:271; gold standard NAS 0-8, md:62), mapped onto the harness's failure-oriented no_response outcome (best response SD or PD = no improvement; the harness cannot express a histologic NAS label) - on the ABSOLUTE baseline-to-end-of-research changes (unit differences, delta = last value after the baseline and by the landmark minus the last value on or before the baseline day) of TWO non-invasive tests at a time, the two model instances of Cullinan, Vesterdal et al., JHEP Reports 2025;7:101432 (DOI 10.1016/j.jhepr.2025.101432): model (i) delta-sTREM2 + delta-PRO-C3 and model (ii) delta-sTREM2 + delta-HOMA-IR, each adjusted for treatment (active/placebo), cohort (Odense/Esbjerg), weight change, ALT and HOMA-IR (md:75; 'All logistic regression models accounted for treatment arm... and cohort heterogeneity...', md:268). The paper publishes no coefficients, no per-patient probabilities and no analysis code (only Stata 17 and R 4.2.2 are named, no package/function, md:75; data-only availability md:317), so the wrapper refits BOTH instances on the benchmark training patients with base R stats::glm (binomial, logit) - that fit is the wrapper's, not the paper's; the risk and p_no_response are the fitted P(no improvement) of the instance selected by the setting model_instance (default strem2_proc3, the paper's abstract/first-named combination; strem2_homair, its better-discriminating alternative (AUROC 0.79), selectable), the other instance's coefficients, AIC and training-fold AUROC are reported in run.json. The wrapper's probability is failure-oriented by construction - the harness outcome is no_response (1 = no improvement); the paper's positive class is improvement (its 'OR >1 indicates a decrease in a biomarker from baseline to EOS associated with higher odds of NAS improvement', md:75, reads in the wrapper as a decrease associated with lower odds of no improvement), and the mapping is declared in the README and run.json. Takes exactly three markers - sTREM2 (plasma ng/ml, Abcam ab224881), PRO-C3 (ng/ml, nordicPRO-C3) and HOMA-IR - resolving the paper's roles by name with a sorted-order fallback, and uses the covariate track when the benchmark passes one (covariates: optional - the benchmark's common arena runs covariates off and the native arena with a unit's full inputs; the paper's five adjustment terms are the mapping target cov_treatment_arm, cov_cohort, cov_weight_change, cov_ALT, cov_HOMA-IR, and the wrapper adjusts for the cov_* columns the dataset supplies, records which were used and never invents a term - a dataset omitting a channel, or the common arena's covariates-off evaluation, yields the narrower documented adjustment set). A patient missing a baseline or on-treatment value of either marker of the selected instance, or a covariate value, is outside the paper's complete-case analysis set ('Logistic regression (n = 140 with complete data)', md:75): no prediction, the reason in note, no imputation (the paper describes none; a below-detection value arrives as 0 with its __detected companion, and the wrapper uses the reported value - sTREM2 had no LOD violations, md:48, and PRO-C3's handling is not stated, '?'). Because the delta terms need exactly two draws (baseline + one on-treatment draw by the landmark), min_draws is 2, and the extra draws (3 months post-EOS Odense; surgery/control visit Esbjerg, md:41) never enter; the paper's fixed EOS window (6 months Odense, ~2.5 years Esbjerg, md:30) becomes the benchmark's last-draw-by-the-landmark pairing, and the design is the monitoring/congruent design of the paper (delta and label span the same baseline-to-EOS interval, no lead time, md:288). No cutoff or call is written - the paper reports AUROC and ORs only (md:75) - and the wrapper never substitutes another outcome for the label; degenerate folds get declared fallbacks (single-class label or all-constant predictors: intercept-only/constant model, recorded).

methods.description: Per-patient probability of pathological response failure - tumour regression grade TRG 2/3 (non-responder) vs TRG 0/1 (responder) - after conversion immunochemotherapy (chemotherapy + PD-1 antibody, 3-4-6 cycles) followed by radical gastrectomy in initially unresectable PD-L1-negative (CPS < 1) MSS locally advanced gastric cancer, from the multivariable binary logistic regression of Wang X, Jiang H, Liang M, et al., 'A Multi-marker model based on serum IL-10 predicts response to conversion immunochemotherapy in gastric cancer patients: a retrospective cohort research', BMC Gastroenterol 2025;25:621 (DOI 10.1186/s12876-025-04136-y; development cohort n = 153, 86 responders / 67 non-responders, AUC 0.748, no external validation): four predictors - hypertension history (binary), the 3-level restoration of tumour-associated carbohydrate antigens after treatment (>2 / N/A / <2 antigens normalized to within reference ranges; the six antigens AFP, CEA, CA125, CA199, CA724, CA242), the pre-treatment serum albumin (continuous) and the post-treatment serum IL-10 (continuous) - presented as an rms nomogram (md:99, md:259). The paper publishes no coefficients (Table 5 prints ORs (95% CI) and p only, md:209-226) and no analysis code (job.code = []; data-only availability md:349/md:396), so this wrapper refits the published four-predictor unpenalized binary logistic structure on the benchmark training patients with base R stats::glm; the printed Table 5 ORs (hypertension No vs Yes 0.470; restoration N/A 3.925 and <2 4.211 vs >=2; albumin 0.903; IL-10 0.873 per unit) are all consistent with the logit of NON-response (TRG 2/3) as the event, which is also the benchmark's failure orientation, so the wrapper fits P(no response) directly and risk = p_no_response = P(TRG 2/3) is failure-oriented by construction. Takes exactly eight markers (IL-10, albumin and the six antigens; roles resolved by name, positional fallback) and uses the benchmark covariate track when one is passed, matching the paper's hypertension predictor by name (a unit without the hypertension channel, or the benchmark's covariates-off common arena, yields the fitted four-marker model without it - recorded, never invented). The carbohydrate-antigen restoration derivation is the wrapper's, since the paper prints no per-antigen reference ranges (?): an antigen's reference upper limit is parameter ref_<antigen> when set, else the ref_quantile (default 0.95) quantile of that antigen's baseline values in the training fold (a benchmark-side decision, fitted on training patients only, recorded in run.json). The rms nomogram point scale (Fig. 7A) is not reproduced (a figure; the paper's point-to-probability mapping is not a published formula,?): the risk column carries the probability directly, and no call is written (no model probability cutoff is published; the ROC cutoffs of md:99 are the paper's evaluation statement with no values). A patient with an incomplete antigen panel, missing IL-10/albumin value, an unmatched hypertension value or a below-detection value under nondetect = 'abstain' gets no prediction with the reason in note.

methods.description: The week-4 sustained-virologic-response (SVR) nomogram of Thompson, Devine, Kattan, Muir (PLoS ONE 2014;9(8):e103370, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0103370: 522 genotype-1 chronic hepatitis C patients from the SPRINT-2/RESPOND-2/PROVIDE boceprevir + peginterferon alfa/ribavirin triple-therapy trials, modified ITT; development C-statistic 0.80 by bootstrap with 1000 resamples, external validation C-statistic 0.71 in the NCT01023035 anemia-management research): a multivariable binary logistic regression of P(SVR) - undetectable plasma HCV RNA 24 weeks after completion of therapy (12-week post-treatment measurement substituted when the 24-week-or-later value is missing; undetectable = lower limit of detection 9.3 IU/mL, TaqMan 2.0) - on the TW4 decline (the log10 change in plasma HCV RNA from baseline to treatment week 4, after the 4-week PR lead-in) plus HCV genotype 1 subtype (1b vs reference), gender (M vs reference), BMI, ribavirin starting dose (mg) and baseline platelet count, every continuous predictor a 3-knot restricted cubic spline; the authors' step-down selected exactly these six predictors (IL28B genotype and prior treatment experience were dropped, md:133) and the final linear predictor is published verbatim in Appendix S1 S1b (logit(P(SVR)) = -4.9007069 + 0.65603084*(gender = "M") + 0.17407306*bmi -... - 0.39397125*log.viral.base.tw4 -...), which the wrapper reproduces in run.json and README but does NOT hard-code: the published coefficients are the authors' fit on their non-public data (no data availability statement), the benchmark label is the response outcome (no_response = best RECIST SD or PD rather than CR/PR) at the benchmark's response assessment rather than SVR at 24 weeks post-completion, and the benchmark cov_* channels are dataset-dependent, so the wrapper refits the same published structure per benchmark fold - the logistic of the no_response (failure) label on the marker's log10 change baseline-to-landmark (last draw each side, draws after the landmark never enter) and the paper's five covariates as the cov_* channels the dataset carries (matched by name; a channel a dataset omits is recorded and the model falls back to the narrower set, never invented; covariates declared optional because the paper's named channels are dataset-dependent - the marker-only structure is the recorded fallback): continuous predictors as 3-knot restricted cubic splines with the harness/rms default placement (the training fold's 0.10/0.50/0.90 quantiles; the paper publishes its own sample's knots, the placement rule is not stated), gender coded male = 1 (M vs reference), genotype 1b indicator = 1. The wrapper writes risk and p_no_response = the fitted probability of no response (failure = 1 - P(SVR), the paper's P(SVR) flipped: the same model class, fitted directly on the benchmark failure label), and no call and no own survival probability (the paper publishes no cutoff and the model is not time-to-event - TxResBench converts the risk for the survival outcomes and progressive disease). The paper's model for the SVR label, the published logit verbatim, the fold's fitted coefficients, knots, the covariate-channel mapping with the imputation medians (the paper's MICE is realized as a deterministic single imputation - the training median per channel - since the number of imputations and the seed are not published), and every recorded deviation (refit vs published coefficients, last-draw-on-each-side change, quantile knot placement, log10 transform of the raw marker, LOD substitution for undetectable values, the benchmark's response label and landmark restriction, covariate channels omitted by a dataset) are recorded in run.json per fold.
