methods.description: Per-patient probability of TW8-response failure - plasma HCV RNA still detectable at treatment week 8 - in genotype 1 chronic hepatitis C treated with boceprevir plus peginterferon alfa/ribavirin (with a 4-week PR lead-in), from the multivariable binary logistic regression of Thompson AJ, Devine SJ, Kattan MW, Muir AJ (PLoS ONE 2014;9(8):e103370, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0103370; SPRINT-2 + RESPOND-2 + PROVIDE, TW8 model n = 856): the TW4 decline (log10 change in plasma HCV RNA from baseline to treatment week 4) plus race (Non-Black vs reference), baseline platelet count and ALT-to-ULN ratio, each continuous predictor as a 3-knot restricted cubic spline - the exact final model is published verbatim (Appendix S1 S1a, s001:4, linear predictor with the step-down-selected predictors of md:133, delivered as the paper's rms nomogram, C-statistic 0.88 development / 0.85 external validation). The paper publishes no analysis code (the R 2.14/Hmisc/rms/mice calls are never named, md:46) and no patient data, and the published coefficients belong to its own data, so this wrapper refits the published STRUCTURE on the benchmark training patients with base R stats::glm: the same four predictors, each spline as the Harrell 3-knot restricted cubic basis with the published knot values (the Appendix S1 formula's spline terms satisfy exactly that basis - verified against its printed coefficients), logit link, no penalization and no variable selection (the final step-down-selected set is published; re-doing the step-down would change the model). The fitted label is the harness outcome no_response (1 = SD/PD or responder = 0), the failure-oriented reading of the paper's TW8 response (1 = undetectable at week 8): the wrapper fits P(no response) directly, the sign-flipped linear predictor, so risk = p_no_response = P(detectable plasma HCV RNA at TW8 | covariates) is failure-oriented by construction; risk is converted by TxResBench for the other three outcomes. The paper's three non-marker covariates are matched to the benchmark's cov_* columns by name (params race_covariate / plt_covariate / alt_uln_covariate, then documented name patterns: a 0/1 race channel coded Black or Non-Black, a platelet-count channel, an ALT-to-ULN-ratio channel); covariates are declared optional with the corpus convention that a channel a dataset does not carry is recorded and never invented - without the channels the wrapper fits the published structure on the TW4-decline spline only (the marker-driven reading; recorded in run.json and README). The paper states no rule for the missing-data handling at the point of care (its MICE imputation details are not published,?), so a patient without a baseline and an on-treatment draw, with an undetectable marker value (non-detects arrive as value 0; the paper never states the numeric coding used in the log10 change, and its TW8-model sample's TW4 values run 24 IU/mL or more, Table 1, so undetectable TW4 values lie outside the published model's data range - the setting nondetect = 'lod' substitutes the draw's own <marker>__lod value when the dataset declares one) or with a missing matched covariate gets no prediction with the reason in note. The nomogram's total-point score is not written (the point mapping is a figure, not a formula,?); the risk column carries the transformed probability, the nomogram's own output after the points-to-probability scale.

methods.description: Per-patient odds of 48-week treatment failure (and the binary call 'detectable VL at the milestone -> predicted failure') from a UNADJUSTED univariate (single-predictor) binomial logistic regression of the binary 48-week treatment-failure label on ONE feature: the ON-TREATMENT HIV-1 viral load (VL) at week 12 or week 24 of lopinavir/ritonavir (LPV/r) monotherapy, entered either as the continuous VL (copies/mL) or dichotomised at the prespecified clinical cutoffs detectable = VL >400 copies/mL and VL >1000 copies/mL - Claassen CW et al., 'HIV Viral Dynamics of Lopinavir/Ritonavir Monotherapy as Second-Line Treatment: A Prospective, Single-Arm Trial', J Int Assoc Provid AIDS Care 2019 (DOI 10.1177/2325958218823209; 30 enrolled patients failing first-line NNRTI-based ART in Jos, Nigeria; cited as md:<line>): 'Univariate and multivariate logistic regression were used to calculate adjusted and unadjusted odds of treatment failure.' (md:64); 'Detectable VL (>400) at 12 weeks was strongly indicative of treatment failure at 48 weeks, with odds of either ITT failure (odds ratio [OR] = 8.75, P =.01) or OT failure (OR = 6.11, P =.02)...' (md:210); the clinical rule: 'a VL can be checked 6 months after starting LPV/r monotherapy, and if VL is detectable >400 copies, there may not be utility in continuing treatment without intensification.' (md:231). Published Table 3 (md:169-208, n = 30, OR and P only, no 95% CI, no coefficients, no intercept, no per-patient probability): VL >400 at 12 weeks OR 8.75 (P =.01, ITT) / 6.11 (P =.02, OT); VL >1000 at 12 weeks 5.68 (P =.04) / 5.50 (P =.03); VL >400 at 24 weeks 1.00 (no P, perfect separation, ITT) / 3.25 (P =.15, OT); VL >1000 at 24 weeks 1.00 (no P, ITT) / 8.33 (P =.04, OT); VL at 12 weeks continuous (per 1 copy/mL) 1.00 (P =.01, both labels); VL at 24 weeks continuous 1.00 (P =.01, OT; no P, ITT); all patients with a detectable VL at 24 weeks went on to be ITT failures (P not calculated due to collinearity, md:210). The paper prints NO fitted model, no Stata command, no coefficients and no intercept (Stata 13.1 is the only named software, md:66), so the wrapper REFITS the specified model on the benchmark training patients with base R stats::glm: logit(P(failure)) = b0 + b1*x with x = the milestone VL level (raw copies/mL - the paper never transforms the predictor, OR per 1 copy/mL, md:189/md:192) or x = 1 if the milestone VL > the prespecified cutoff (the >400 / >1000 instances, md:190-194); exactly ONE predictor, no adjustment covariate (the paper's unadjusted odds, md:64; the multivariate model was fitted but 'not displayed', md:214 - a different analysis, not this method). The benchmark's reading of the paper's 48-week treatment-failure label is the harness's response outcome no_response (1 = SD or PD / failed to respond = the failing class; the paper fits the same endpoint twice - ITT failure 21/30 md:123 and OT failure 14/30 md:136 - two codings of one binary label, which the harness's single response outcome cannot separate, recorded in run.json). It writes risk = the fitted P(no_response) (the paper's own 'VL at 12/24 weeks' continuous instance by default - the call of the method is the threshold rule, and a two-valued exposure would leave every patient below the cutoff with the same score; predictor = 'dichotomised' refits the paper's OR-8.75 instance, whose exposure is exactly the call, and is recorded in run.json) and call = 1 exactly when the milestone VL is detectable (> cutoff, strict boundary: suppression is '<400 copies/mL', md:59; the patient's risk and call are then consistent by construction). The paper's per-patient probabilities, intercept and coefficients were never published, so risk is a refit product whose ranking (not calibration) is the paper's association; the fitted OR with 95% CI and P are recorded in run.json, not claimed as the paper's Table 3 numbers. No p_* column (response-call group; TxResBench converts the risk). No survival reading: the label is a fixed 48-week binary endpoint, absolute from treatment start, not landmark-conditioned (md:59, md:64). A patient without a milestone draw (day > baseline_max_day and <= landmark_day - the wrapper reads the paper's fixed milestone as the benchmark's landmark day, 7*milestone_week) gets no prediction with the reason in note; the reference is treatment start (patients discontinued prior ARVs and began LPV/r at research entry, md:54).

methods.description: Per-patient probability of no pathological complete response (non-pCR) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (standardized EC*4-T*4, epirubicin 90 mg/m2 + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m2 every 3 weeks x 4, then docetaxel 100 mg/m2 every 3 weeks x 4) plus definitive surgery in luminal breast cancer (ER and PR expression >= 10%) - the five-predictor multivariable logistic nomogram of Zeng Y, Sun Y., BMC Women's Health 2026;26:263, DOI 10.1186/s12905-026-04440-z (201 patients, 72 pCR / 129 non-pCR, md:241-242): P(pCR) from TC_slope_std (z-scored linear slope of serial serum total cholesterol over the 8 draws taken two weeks after each 3-weekly cycle, mg/dL/week before z-scoring; multivariate OR 0.40 (0.25-0.64), p < 0.01), T stage (1-2 vs 3-4, OR 0.35), HER2 status (0 vs 1+/2+ ISH-, OR 0.39), Ki67 status (<20% vs >=20%, OR 2.28) and LDL_slope_std (z-scored LDL slope, OR 0.85); development AUC 0.816 (95% CI 0.758-0.874), optimism 0.0226, bootstrap-corrected AUC 0.7934 (500 resamples). The paper publishes no analysis code (SPSS 29.0 and R 4.5.1 named only, no package, md:223-224), no coefficients and no intercept (Table 2 prints ORs (95% CI) + p only, md:355-416), so the wrapper refits the published final five-predictor structure per benchmark fold with base R stats::glm - binomial logit of the harness's no_response outcome (best response SD or PD, or responder 0: the failure reading of the paper's pCR-vs-non-pCR label) on the two z-scored slopes plus the three clinical covariates resolved from the cov_* columns by name - and writes risk = p_no_response = P(no pCR) = 1 - P(pCR), failure-oriented by construction (TxResBench converts the risk for progression, death and progressive disease). The wrapper derives each patient's TC and LDL linear slope from the per-draw marker values (value ~ day, on-treatment draws after baseline_max_day and by the landmark, slope converted to mg/dL/week; the paper's draws are all on-treatment at two weeks after each cycle, md:193-195, so pre-treatment draws never enter), z-scores the slopes with the training-fold mean and SD (the paper's z-score reference distribution is not stated, '?', md:267-269 - the training-fold analysis set is the declared convention), and codes the three clinical categories to the paper's reference levels (T 1-2, HER2 0, Ki67 < 20% = 0; T 3-4, HER2 1+/2+ ISH-, Ki67 >= 20% = 1); a covariate channel a run omits (or the benchmark's covariates-off arena) is recorded and the model falls back to the narrower reading of the same binomial fit (two slopes, or slopes + the channels present), never invented - and a patient missing a slope (< 2 usable on-treatment draws of either lipid) or a value the fitted model uses gets no prediction with the reason in note (the paper's complete-case cohort, md:128-129; no imputation is described, '?'). No call: the paper publishes no probability cutoff (DCA's 40-80% net-benefit range, md:481-483, is utility, not a threshold); the nomogram's point-scale artifact and published ORs cannot be reproduced (ORs are rounded, no betas) and are reported verbatim in run.json; the paper's own accounts of the final model disagree (five predictors md:449-451 vs three in the Abstract md:36-37 vs Table 2's extra N row md:398-399) and the wrapper declares and fits the five-predictor reading.
methods.licence: n/a for the paper's model (the article - Zeng Y, Sun Y, BMC Women's Health 2026;26:263, DOI 10.1186/s12905-026-04440-z - is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, an article licence, and publishes no analysis code: the only software statement is 'SPSS 29.0 and R 4.5.1was used for statistical analyses.' md:223-224; the availability statement is data-only, md:790-792; the four MOESM supplements are tables/figures only, so no code licence can be asserted). The wrapper is an original reimplementation in base R stats::glm plus the contract helper TxrMethod of the base image; no third-party package is installed

methods.description: The two multiple logistic regression analyses of sustained virological response (SVR) of Rivero-Juarez A et al., PLoS ONE 2014;9(6):e99468, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0099468 (192 enrolled / 163 on-treatment HIV/HCV genotype-1 patients on pegylated interferon alpha-2a plus ribavirin; SVR = serum HCV RNA below the 15 IU/mL detection limit 24 weeks after completion of a 48- or 72-week course, 59/163; two models, Figure 2A with the day-28 RVR indicator and Figure 2B with the week-2 decline >=1.5 log IU/mL indicator, each adjusted for four binary baseline predictive factors: IL28B CC vs non-CC, liver fibrosis F3-F4 vs F0-F2 (METAVIR, or FibroScan >=11 kPa without a biopsy), HCV genotype 1a vs 1b and baseline HCV RNA >=600,000 vs <600,000 IU/mL; only the ORs are published, in Figure 2, md:125, and the exact variable list is not enumerated, md:43). The paper's reproducibility limits (no code - SPSS 18.0 only; OR values not retrievable from the text; the 1.5 log cutoff is the companion response-call rule's in-sample maximum-PPV cutoff, not a regression parameter, per the spec) mean the wrapper REFITS the paper's model-B structure per benchmark fold on the failure-oriented benchmark label no_response (best response SD or PD, or responder 0 - the complement of the paper's SVR); it selects model B, the paper's week-2 decline model (Figure 2B), and records that model A (the day-28 RVR) is not wrapped - both consume the same marker, the model is identical apart from the substituted indicator, and the paper's own aim is the week-2 time point. Two realizations of model B are fitted and recorded in run.json: the published exposure (binary week-2 decline >= indicator_cutoff, the Figure 2B indicator, whose ORs are the paper's reported output) and the risk model, whose exposure is the continuous week-2 decline magnitude (baseline log10 IU/mL minus the on-treatment-draw log10 IU/mL, positive = decline) - the paper's own predictive-accuracy quantity for the same relationship (AUROC 0.788 [0.703-0.869], md:97; Table 2's monotone PPVs, md:104-111), because a two-valued exposure leaves every patient in the below-cutoff group with the same score and the paper's evidence for the decline-SVR relationship is continuous; risk_model selects which exposure is written as the risk (default 'continuous', with the indicator model still fitted and its ORs recorded; 'indicator' is the faithful Figure 2B reading). Every run.json records per fold: the marker feature (baseline = last draw at day <= baseline_max_day, on-treatment = last draw at baseline_max_day < day <= landmark - the corpus convention of the fixed two-draw wrappers; the paper's week-2 draw is at 14 days and no rule is published for another draw schedule), the below-detection substitution (a value 0 draw becomes the paper's 15 IU/mL detection limit - the draw's own <marker>__lod row when present, else the training fold's smallest positive value; the paper's handling of its 7 unquantifiable week-2 patients, all of whom reached SVR, is not stated, '?'), the covariate channel mapping (the four baseline factors matched by name from the cov_* columns; a channel a dataset omits is recorded and the model is fitted on the remaining structure, never an invented substitute; IL28B columns are excluded from the other channels; missing per-patient values are imputed with the training median of the fit sample - the paper declares no missing-data handling for the absent 9.2% of IL28B genotypes, '?'), the coding of each factor (CC vs CT/TT; METAVIR >=3 or FibroScan >=11 kPa; 1a vs 1b; >=600,000 IU/mL vs below), the fitted coefficients with Wald ORs, 95% CIs and p-values, and every deviation. It writes risk and p_no_response = the fitted probability of no response (the paper's P(SVR) flipped: the same model class, fitted directly on the benchmark failure label) and no call and no own survival probability (the paper publishes no probability cutoff and the model is not time-to-event; TxResBench converts the risk for progression, death and progressive disease). A patient with no baseline draw, no on-treatment draw by the landmark, an empty/non-positive marker value after the detection-limit substitution, or a needed covariate that is missing and cannot be imputed gets no prediction with the reason in note - the paper defines no imputation or fallback.

methods.description: The per-patient biomarker growth slope of Campenni et al. (Clin Chem Lab Med 2026, aop, DOI 10.1515/cclm-2026-0757; 23 patients with advanced medullary thyroid carcinoma and confirmed structural disease, serum calcitonin, CEA, ProGRP and CA 19-9 every 3-6 months over a median 37 months): per patient, an ordinary least squares regression of the natural logarithm of the serum marker concentration on time - ln(marker) = beta0 + beta1 x time - over the available draws, so that beta1 is the proportional rate of change (growth slope). The paper evaluates the slope as a continuous risk score: ROC curves (AUC with bootstrap 95% CIs, 2,000 iterations) for structural progression vs non-progressive disease and for disease-related death vs surviving patients, and Kaplan-Meier PFS/OS with log-rank tests split at higher vs lower slopes (the split is not published, and the reported amplification is the PFS HR 3.8 (95% CI 1.4-10.2) of the higher ProGRP-slope group; ProGRP slope had the best discrimination, AUC 0.93 for death, 0.91 for progression). The wrapper is the fixed rule: it takes one serum marker (the paper fits the identical log-linear slope for each of its four markers separately; there is no multi-marker combination and no published threshold), uses the draws on or before the benchmark's decision day (the paper's primary analysis uses the entire follow-up retrospectively; at the benchmark's landmark only the draws up to it exist, and the paper's own sensitivity analyses recalculate the slope within therapy-defined windows), and writes as risk the slope in ln-units/month, the paper's scale - higher = faster growth = more likely failing. It writes no per-patient probability (the paper defines none - the deliverables are the per-patient slope and cohort-level AUC/log-rank/HR quantities) and no call (the paper publishes no threshold for the KM split, and the ROC evaluation is threshold-free); TxResBench converts the risk. It learns nothing from the training outcomes.

methods.description: The canonical log10-reduction threshold rule of Feng et al. (BMC Gastroenterology 2014;14:47, DOI 10.1186/1471-230X-14-47; NCT01140997): among 32 genotype 1b chronic hepatitis C patients (16 SVR / 16 non-SVR) completing 48 weeks of peginterferon-alpha (90/135/180 ug weekly) plus ribavirin and 24 weeks of follow-up, serum HCV core antigen (ARCHITECT HCVcAg, quantitative chemiluminescent microparticle immunoassay, fmol/L; nonreactive below 3.0 fmol/L) was drawn at 24/48/72/96/120/144 h, and the per-patient delta HCVcAg = log10(baseline) - log10(144-h value) in log10 fmol/L (md:38) was ROC-analysed against the week-72 SVR label (HCV RNA <50 IU/mL 24 weeks after cessation, md:43): AUROC 0.913 (0.799-1.000) at 144 h (best of 0.835/0.814/0.870/0.866/0.879/0.913 at 24/48/72/96/120/144 h and 0.853/0.823/0.719 at weeks 4/8/12), with two cutoffs both derived in the same sample at quartiles 0.25/0.75 (md:162) - 0.976 ('the optimal combination of AUROC, PPV and NPV', md:83; sensitivity 0.952, specificity 0.700, PPV 0.913, NPV 1.000) and 1.096 (sensitivity 0.762, specificity 0.800, PPV 1.000, NPV 0.769; Table 2, md:96-100): 'at the 144 h time point it will be unlikely that patients will have a delta HCVcAg lower than 0.976 and those patients with a delta HCVcAg of more than 1.096 will be likely to achieve SVR' (md:83); absolute (non-delta) levels have no predictive power (md:106). The wrapper takes the serum HCVcAg series (one marker, fmol/L), computes baseline = the marker's last draw on or before baseline_max_day and the on-treatment draw = the marker's last draw after baseline_max_day and at or before the benchmark's landmark (the paper's fixed 144-h draw = day 6; a landmark at day 6 reproduces the paper exactly, at any other landmark the rule is evaluated at the decision day - the corpus fixed-pair convention), delta = log10(baseline) - log10(on-treatment), and writes risk = -delta (the failure direction: higher = more likely failing; the paper's delta is kept in the extra column delta_hcvcag), call = 1 = treatment judged failing (SVR unlikely: delta < 0.976, the paper's primary 'optimal combination' cutoff) vs 0 = likely SVR, plus the extra column call_1.096 (the paper's PPV-1.000 operating point: failing iff delta < 1.096); no probability is written (the paper defines none per patient; TxResBench converts the risk). Declared readings (recorded, never hidden): a nonreactive (<3.0 fmol/L, md:38/md:160) on-treatment value enters as the assay floor 3.0 fmol/L - delta is then a lower bound, so the likely-SVR call is guaranteed whenever the bound clears the cutoff, and when it does not the patient is abstained (call undetermined, note); a nonreactive baseline draw abstains (no quantitative reference; none in the paper's cohort, md:56); the boundary reads delta < 0.976 as the failing call per md:83 with Table 2's cutoff semantics (the paper's 'more than 1.096' prose for the second cutoff is recorded verbatim); the cutoffs were derived in the authors' own 32-patient sample (quartiles 0.25/0.75, no split, validation.type 'none') and are treated as the published constants - nothing is learned from the training outcomes (fitted false); the paper's Table 2 operating points are not reconcilable with the 16/16 SVR split (recorded in run.json, near-degenerate separation is a benchmark finding), and its other internal inconsistencies (0.976/1.096 'both a NPV and PPV of 1.000' in md:162/md:171; Table 4's 'delta HCV Ag >= 1 log' row) are recorded verbatim, never silently resolved.

(md:48); SPSS is proprietary commercial software, no SPSS procedure (e.g. the SPSS ROC procedure) is named, no syntax/request file and no analysis code is published anywhere (job.code = []; extraction code_url null, availability_statement null; no data/code availability statement in the md); this wrapper implements the rule from the Methods/Results text and Tables 2-4; nothing was substituted or downloaded)

required_markers.list_source: Feng B, Yang R-F, Kong F-Y, et al., BMC Gastroenterology 2014;14:47, DOI 10.1186/1471-230X-14-47: the method IS defined on the serum HCVcAg concentration itself - 'The ARCHITECT HCVcAg (Abbott Diagnostics, Wiesbaden, Germany)... was used to quantify HCVcAg' (md:38), the feature is 'log10 reduction of serum HCVcAg levels between other time points and baseline' (md:38), the operating points are AUROC/sensitivity/specificity/PPV/NPV of the delta and of the absolute levels ('the absolute values of HCVcAg levels had no predictive power on SVR', md:106) and the reported values are in fmol/L ('Mean baseline viral load and HCV antigen levels were 6.33 +/- 0.88 log10 IU/mL and 3.66 +/- 0.49 log10 fmol/L', md:56). LOINC 54914-7 ('Hepatitis C virus core Ag [ACnc] in Ser by IA', quantitative, immunoassay) is the vocabulary's quantitative serum HCV core antigen term; LOINC defines no Mass/volume term for HCV core antigen (the ACnc [arb'U]/mL property is the standard way the numeric immunoassay result, fmol/L in the manufacturer's units, is recorded; cf. the CA125 LOINC 10334-1 Units/volume convention of the ca125 wrappers), and the qualitative presence term (LOINC 79189-7) is not this quantity - a unit matching only the qualitative HCV core Ag presence/absence does not measure the fmol/L concentration the log10 reduction needs

methods.description: The landmark proportional-hazards cure (LPHC) model of Xie, Huang, Li, Tsodikov & Bhalla, Ann. Appl. Stat. 18(4) 2024, 2796-2817 (DOI 10.1214/24-aoas1906): at the landmark, a promotion-time proportional-hazards cure model is fitted on the patients still event-free, with the event clock reset to the time since the landmark, S(t | L) = exp(-exp(beta0 + z'psi) F0(t)) with a nonparametric baseline cumulative hazard F0 and covariates z = baseline covariates plus the baseline and the most current (last observation carried forward) marker values; the flexible-hazards (gamma) part of the sibling LFHC model is removed, so the proportional-hazards assumption is required for every covariate (the paper's CML model has no X covariates). The model's own conditional probability of the event by each horizon (1 minus the conditional survival, conditioning on being event-free at the landmark) is written as risk (first horizon) and as p_progression_H<h> / p_death_H<h>, one LPHC per learned survival outcome, shared when the outcome data coincide. The paper's other output, the conditional cure probability, has no column in the benchmark predictions table: it is summarised in run.json. The wrapper fits with fhc::fhcmodel with gamma_variable = NULL (the package's documented PHC variant) on the residual clock as paper eq. (6) requires; the published curedynpred::pred_landmark_model cannot produce the LPHC conditional survival at all (its survival branch errors when gamma_variable = NULL) and fits on the original time scale, so the survival is computed by the wrapper from the fit's baseline cumulative hazard; when the marker terms are degenerate or the fit fails it falls back to a Cox model of the post-landmark clock, recorded in run.json.

methods.description: The per-patient risk classification of Garrido et al., LungBEAM (Cancer Med 2021;10:5878-5888, DOI 10.1002/cam4.4135; 110 stage IV EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients on first-/second-generation EGFR-TKI): the slope of the post-baseline plasma MAF (BEAMing, %) of the patient's EGFR sensitizing mutations (ex19del and/or L858R) - defined as the mean change in MAF value, computed on the post-baseline draws on or before the decision day - is classified by SIGN into a two-group call: positive slope (progressively increasing MAF) = treatment failing (the paper's high-risk class, HR for progression 3.85 [2.01-7.36]), negative or null slope = not failing. The wrapper writes the slope as risk (higher = increasing MAF = failing) and the 0/1 call, and no probability (the paper defines none per patient; TxResBench converts the risk). The population needs a baseline plasma sensitizing-mutation detection (78/110, md:284-286); the paper's analysis cohort further required at least four post-baseline samples (68/78, md:469-471) - a survivorship restriction the wrapper records as a difference and does not impose (it scores a baseline-detected patient from two post-baseline draws). The paper's slope formula ('mean change in MAF value', md:252-254) and the combination of co-detected sensitizing mutations are not defined and no analysis code is published; the wrapper's declared readings (least-squares slope on day, per-draw quantitative sum of the sensitizing series, below-detection values kept as 0) are recorded in run.json and the README, and the method is declared marker-specific (required_markers: EGFR ex19del / EGFR p.L858R, match min_fraction 0.8).

methods.description: Tree-based gradient-boosted Cox landmark model (Super Learner base learners M2, M4 and M6 of van Gerwen et al. 2026, arXiv:2602.19761, for dynamic predictions in primary biliary cholangitis): at the landmark time t the patients still at risk (T_i > t, with the landmark as time zero) form R(t); the covariates X are the baseline variables plus the longitudinal biomarkers at t, obtained either by one-stage landmarking (last value carried forward; M2, the default) or by two-stage landmarking (the per-marker linear-mixed-model predicted expected trajectory at t; M4 linear time, M6 natural cubic splines with 3 degrees of freedom); the Cox partial log-likelihood is then boosted with mboost::blackboost (bstop = 500, step size nu = 0.025, regression-tree sub-base learners of all covariates and their two-way interactions at the mboost package defaults: maxdepth 2, minsplit 10, minbucket 4, mincriterion 0), and the number of iterations is chosen by 5-fold cross-validation of the negative partial log-likelihood (bopt, the paper's early stopping); the conditional survival probability pi(u | t) comes from the Breslow estimator exp(-H0(u) exp(psi_hat(X))). The wrapper fits one such boosted landmark model per survival outcome the training data give (progression and death), writes 1 - pi(h | L) as the outcome's own probability by the horizon day, writes the boosted log-hazard psi_hat as its risk (higher = worse), and abstains with a note only for a patient it cannot score. methods.description: The multivariate ROC classifier of Diaz et al. (Molecular Oncology 2022, doi 10.1002/1878-0261.13216): a binary classifier of response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy (Miller-Payne grades 4-5 vs 1-3) in triple-negative breast cancer, on the two plasma bile acids glycohyocholic acid and glycodeoxycholic acid at the presurgery sample. The paper ran it in the 'Biomarker Analysis' panel of the MetaboAnalyst 4.0 web platform, whose underlying functions are the companion package MetaboAnalystR 2.0.0 (github xia-lab/MetaboAnalystR, tag v2.0.0). The wrapper re-expresses that code path with the exact packages it calls: the preprocessing MetaboAnalystR applies (probabilistic quotient normalization against a reference sample, generalized log base 2, autoscaling - the paper's 'normalization by a QC reference sample, logarithmic transformation, and autoscaling'), the Monte-Carlo cross-validation of PerformCV.test (stratified 2/3 train by the smallest class, nRuns default 100, per-run AUC via ROCR and accuracy at the 0.5 call, mean AUC with a 2.5-97.5% quantile CI exactly as GetCIs returns it), and Predict.class's classifier, by default e1071::svm(type='C', kernel='linear', probability=TRUE) with randomForest::randomForest(ntree=300) available behind the classifier setting. The paper names no code URL, so this is a re-expression of the named software module, not a reproduction of a published analysis script. Per patient the predictor is the two peak areas at the equivalent of the paper's t2 sample: the last on-treatment draw on or before the landmark; the label is the harness failure outcome standing in for the paper's response group (no_response = SD or PD; when it is absent, progressive_disease, else the event-by-horizon label of the first horizon, the paper's same-procedure-on-another-label reading), and because the benchmark measures failure, the wrapper codes the failure class as class 1 - the flip of the paper's class-1-is-responder labelling - so risk is P(failure) from the classifier's calibrated probability and call is the paper's 0.5 threshold in the failure orientation. At fit the whole training cohort goes through the paper's MCCV evaluation (recorded in run.json) and the classifier is then refitted on the full training data (the package's only new-patient route, mSetObj$dataSet$new.data semantics) and saved; at predict the saved model scores each patient's t2 draw and writes risk = P(failure), call = (risk > 0.5); a patient without an on-treatment draw carrying both markers by the landmark gets no prediction, with the reason in note. The paper's data and QC reference sample are not published, so the PQN reference is the per-feature median of the training t2 values (recorded), MetaboAnalystR is not installed in the image (its Imports - xcms, MSnbase, Rserve and others - are not distributable in a method image) and which of the two classifiers produced the reported AUC is not stated (the wrapper's default is the paper's named SVM-linear, the RF setting is available).

methods.description: The two-branch early-treatment-benefit call of Thomsen et al. (Ther Adv Med Oncol 2020, DOI 10.1177/1758835920918472; 123 first-line mCRC patients on capecitabine + oxaliplatin + bevacizumab; no published analysis code, the rule is prose in the paper's Data management, md:48): after the first treatment cycle a patient is 'low-level methylated ctDNA' (LctDNA - the paper's benefit face: PFS median 9.2 vs 6.7 months, HR 0.48, p = 0.0005; OS median 25.4 vs 13.5 months, HR 0.50, p = 0.0001; 55 (45%) of 123) or 'high-level methylated ctDNA' (HctDNA - all other patients, 'stable, increasing, or slightly decreasing values'). LctDNA = a level of zero at baseline (digit zero, Table 1: 16 patients) OR a level decreasing to one with zero included in its 95% CI (Poisson statistics, reported per draw by QuantaSoft) at T1; T0 and T1 are the two fixed protocol draws ('Plasma samples from all patients were collected at baseline (T0) and after the first treatment cycle (T1)'), which the wrapper reads as the last draw on or before baseline_max_day and the last draw after it up to the landmark (the cycle length in days is not printed, so the paper's cycle-1 draw maps to the benchmark's standard two-slot reading, the same convention as the other two-draw ctDNA rules in this repository). The benchmark contract carries NO per-draw 95% CI (the long frame has the value and the __detected/__lod companions only), so the wrapper evaluates the paper's CI condition exactly when per-row ci_lo/ci_hi columns are present (zero in CI = ci_lo <= 0 <= ci_hi), and otherwise on the benchmark's own encoding of a zero level (value 0, or __detected 0: zero is necessarily within the 95% CI of a zero measurement); a still-detected (nonzero) T1 level after a decrease is HctDNA - the paper's 'slightly decreasing values' class - and no Poisson CI is invented; the degradation is stated in the fit record. It writes the T1 level (log1p) as risk (the quantity the L/H boundary is about; higher = more likely failing), the 0/1 call (1 = HctDNA = treatment judged failing, 0 = LctDNA) and no probability of its own (TxResBench converts the risk); a patient without both draws gets no prediction, with the reason in note. The KM/log-rank cohort validation of the paper (medians, HRs) is not per-patient output and is not produced by the wrapper.

methods.description: The longitudinal discriminant analysis (LoAD) on two per-group Bayesian linear mixed models, as used by Wu et al., Hepatology International 2025;20(1):31-45 (the ANCHOR randomized trial: predict HBsAg loss at week 96 under Peg-IFN-based combination therapy from serial serum quantitative HBsAg; DOI 10.1007/s12072-025-10977-2) and implemented there with the mixAK package version 5.4 (the paper's only software statement, md:55; construction process in the online supplement, Method section). The one continuous blood marker is modelled as a Bayesian linear mixed model with a random intercept and a random slope on time and no fixed effects - Log(marker)_ij = mu_g,i + gamma_g,i * t_j, bivariate normal (mu, gamma) (the supplement's 'multilevel linear mixed models'; anchored on the paper's log10 IU/mL table convention) - fitted separately in the outcome group that reached the endpoint (group-1: HBsAg loss at week 96) and the group that did not (group-0) by Gibbs MCMC in mixAK::GLMM_MCMC (two chains, 1000 burn-in + 1000 kept iterations per chain as the supplement states, the package's automatic weakly-informative priors); a patient with serial history y up to the decision day is allocated by Bayes' rule P(G = g | y) = omega_g P(y | theta_g) / sum_h P(y | theta_h) with the group prior weights omega, computed per observation by mixAK::GLMM_longitDA v1 (marginal density over the random effects, the supplement's P(y | theta_g); the package's per-visit cumulative-history probabilities). The wrapper's risk is the posterior probability of the failure group (the paper's 'unfavorable' group-0) at the patient's last visit at or before the landmark, and its call thresholds that probability at the Youden index of the training ROC (the paper states no cutoff). The wrapper retargets the paper's HBsAg-loss endpoint to the benchmark's failure labels exactly as the paper retargets the LoAD scheme to its endpoint: the two groups are the training patients' labels of the primary outcome (no_response, else progressive_disease, else the first event-by-horizon label of progression or death; fitted per fold on the training labels only), so risk is oriented to failure and own_outputs carry no probability - TxResBench recalibrates the risk per outcome. Wrapper differences from the paper (the paper prints no call: which mixAK function v1 vs v2, omega values, seed, cutoff, and visit window used are all outside the supplement; the Gut 2024 reference of the scheme is the GOLDEN model of Fan et al., DOI 10.1136/gutjnl-2024-332182) are detailed in the README: the marginal density over the random effects is used (the supplement's Bayes-rule term), omega is the training group proportion, the time axis is days since the first dose (the supplement's t in weeks is the same linear model up to the scale of the slope), negatives clamp to 0, and values at or below zero (the benchmark's non-detect encoding) are replaced by half the smallest positive observed training value (the paper states no rule).

methods.description: The Multilayer Perceptron (DeepSurv-style) baseline of the SHERLOC framework of Mamann et al. (bioRxiv 2026.06.04.730097) for overall survival from the landmark: the patient's longitudinal ctDNA profile is flattened into one vector (in the paper, 17 gene-level ctDNA VAFs + 4 panel-level aggregated features = 21 channels x T = 4 clinical timepoints baseline to C4D1 = 84 features), batch-normalized, passed through one fully connected bottleneck layer whose hidden dimension is half the input (84 -> 42) with sigmoid activation; the compressed vector is fused with per-timestep representations of a frozen genomic-interaction encoder (MLP pretrained with the Cox partial-likelihood on solid-biopsy VAF data, frozen after pretraining, 2 dimensions per timestep; the paper uses the external MSK-CHORD cohort, 22,068 patients) and with baseline clinical covariates, all batch-normalized before concatenation; the concatenation is dropped out at 0.4 and passed to a single linear layer with sigmoid output whose value is the Cox log-risk fed to pycox's CoxPH, trained by the negative log-partial likelihood (lr 0.005, batch 50, up to 256 epochs, early stopping patience 20, 20% validation split). The wrapper refits it per survival outcome of the training data (death first - the paper's OS, then progression), rebases the outcome times to the benchmark's landmark (the paper's OS from the final on-treatment ctDNA collection), resolves the vector to the patient's visits up to the landmark (baseline slot = last baseline visit, then the most recent on-treatment visits, at most n_timepoints = 4 slots; the paper's evaluability rule requires all configured timepoints, md:1404-1408) and writes the paper's native outputs: the sigmoid log-risk (risk, monotone in the Cox log-risk) and per-horizon failure probabilities from the Breslow baseline-hazard survival curve. The frozen genomic-interaction encoder cannot be reproduced as published (MSK-CHORD is not redistributed, scripts/data/msk_chord/README.md:1-17), so the wrapper pretrains the same MLP architecture on the training cohort itself - the paper's transfer-learning step is replaced by an in-cohort pretraining (recorded deviation); the marker set is data-driven (the paper derives its channel count from the data, d_input = train_ds[0][0].shape[0], train_DL.py:287-289), so the wrapper takes whatever markers a unit carries as the channels.

methods.description: The molecular PD detection rule of Xia S et al., Transl Lung Cancer Res 2019;8(6):1016-1028 (DOI 10.21037/tlcr.2019.12.09; 8 stage IV EGFR T790M+ lung adenocarcinoma patients on osimertinib 80 mg qd, AURA17 sub-cohort; 85 longitudinal plasma samples; 168-gene Lung Plasma capture panel, 273 kb, 10,000x, variant calling by proprietary computation algorithms, md:317-335; blood at baseline before osimertinib initiation and longitudinally every 30-40 days until radiologic RECIST v1.1 PD, md:352-358): molecular PD = 'the emergence of new mutations or significant increase in allele fraction (AF) of existing driver mutations' (md:679-681, repeated md:996-1001; Figure 4 legend: 'new mutations or significant increases in allele fraction of existing mutations', md:856-858). The rule is applied per patient on the serial per-marker AF draws up to the benchmark landmark: EVENT A (emergence) = a marker's detection state goes from undetected in every earlier draw of that patient to detected in a later draw (any draw up to the landmark; a first detection without a prior undetected observation of the marker is no emergence evidence); EVENT B (increase) = a marker that was detected at the patient's baseline draw (an existing mutation; the paper prints no driver list - in its cohort the existing drivers are the EGFR-sensitizing mutation (maxAF 4.00-6.29% in 7/8 patients) and P4's TP53 at 4.95%, md:558-561 - so the wrapper evaluates the patient's baseline-detected markers, with the configurable driver_markers list to restrict them) has its AF rise by at least increase_ratio (default 1.0 = any strict rise: 'significant' is never quantified in the paper - no threshold, no fold change, no statistical test, '?'; the >1.5x-from-baseline reading of the same rule in the variant paper S2021 (tlcr-20-371, md:119) is recorded and available as a setting, never the default) compared with its reference value (default baseline = the patient's pre-treatment draw, the corpus convention for a from-baseline increase and the reading of group-3 'reached the maximum level of twice as much as the baseline level at radiological PD', md:645-647; alternative references previous/nadir exposed). Call = 1 when event A or event B fires, else 0 (molecular PD = treatment judged failing; the paper's cohort result: 5 of 8 patients, average lead time 1.9 months before radiologic PD, Table 2 md:860-898 - the lead time is a retrospective validation statistic, not reproduced). The wrapper's risk - the quantity the increase arm thresholds, per the contract's rule-writing convention - is the geometric mean over the markers of their per-marker max AF rise factor value(t)/reference (a factor from an undetectable state is measured against the patient's smallest positive value of that marker, else the training minimum positive, the corpus convention for a rise from 0; a marker with no factor contributes none; the no-factor case is the neutral 1; higher = the existing mutations rose more = treatment more likely failing; no emergence-only extra signal is added to the risk - event A carries the call, the paper's per-patient scalar is its binary call). It writes no probability (the paper defines none; TxResBench converts the risk). A patient with no draw of any marker on or before baseline_max_day, or no on-treatment draw by the landmark, gets no prediction with the reason in note.

methods.description: The MR PD prediction model of Xia S et al., Transl Lung Cancer Res 2019;8(6):1016-1028 (DOI 10.21037/tlcr.2019.12.09; 8 stage IV EGFR T790M+ lung adenocarcinoma patients on osimertinib 80 mg qd, AURA17 sub-cohort, NCT02442349; 85 longitudinal plasma samples from baseline before osimertinib initiation every ~30-40 days until the radiologic RECIST v1.1 PD evaluation; methylation by brELSA(TM) bisulfite libraries and a custom lung-cancer panel covering 80,672 CpG sites / 1.05 Mb, md:198-245; no published analysis code): a per-sample 'MR model score' built in steps I-VI (md:265-316) - (I) drop MBs with no significant difference from background methylation, (II) t-test weighted methylation scores of each MB between the patient's tumor and adjacent-normal tissue, (III) rank them descending and take the top 1,000 (significant increase) and bottom 1,000 (significant decrease), (IV) per-MB ctDNA z-score against the healthy-control MB mean/SD (196 controls, md:543-544), (V) weight = z x |tissue weighted score|, (VI) score = mean(weighted top 1,000) - mean(weighted bottom 1,000) - and a per-patient PD call on 'the significant elevation of MR' across the serial score trajectory (md:901-905: PD predicted in all 6 evaluable patients prior to radiological PD, average lead time 3.0 months, as early as 5.6 months; P2/P3 not evaluable - no adequate tissue, md:614-617, NA not FALSE). The wrapper implements the score from per-MB per-draw ctDNA methylation frequencies plus the two reference blocks the score needs, delivered as fixed features of the same measurements table (per-MB tissue weighted score rows and per-MB healthy-control mean/SD rows - the paper's tissue t-test and the 196-control reference are upstream/non-reproducible and not re-computed or invented); the 'significant elevation' threshold and reference draw are never quantified in the paper ('?'), so the wrapper thresholds the score's rise against the patient's own running minimum (exposed as parameters, plus baseline/previous references) with the literal reading of an unquantified 'significant': any strict rise (elevation_ratio 1.0). risk = the largest elevation factor (the quantity the rule thresholds), call = 1 = MR-model PD = treatment judged failing; when the reference blocks are absent (the benchmark's generic scalar-marker worlds), the wrapper evaluates the same elevation rule on the per-draw panel methylation level (the unweighted mean of the MB markers, the paper's 'methylation level', Figure 3 blue line) and records the reduction in run.json.

methods.description: The end-of-therapy (EOT) peripheral-blood MRD status stratification of Kater et al. (J Clin Oncol 2019;37(4):269-277, MURANO, fixed-duration venetoclax-rituximab in relapsed/refractory CLL; the venetoclax-rituximab arm analysis): the MRD status at the EOT visit (approximately month 24, at venetoclax cessation) is classified into uMRD (< 10^-4, the iwCLL-recommended cutoff), L-MRD (10^-4 to < 10^-2) and H-MRD (>= 10^-2) in the 130 patients who completed 2 years of venetoclax without progression, and that 3-level status is tested against disease progression (PD, per iwCLL criteria) after EOT by Fisher's exact test: PD occurred in 2 (2.4%) of 83 uMRD, 3 (13.0%) of 23 L-MRD and 11 (78.6%) of 14 H-MRD patients (P <.001); two further single-cohort analyses are the Kaplan-Meier PFS from venetoclax cessation over the 130 completers (6-month PFS 92%, 12-month PFS 87%) and the Kaplan-Meier time to conversion from uMRD to detectable MRD among the 83 uMRD-at-EOT patients (58 [70%] sustained uMRD, 25 [30%] converted). The wrapper takes one marker - the per-draw MRD status at the EOT visit, either the 0/1/2 category (the benchmark input per the per-method spec) or the quantitative MRD fraction, which it classifies with the paper's thresholds (value_scale 'auto' distinguishes the two at fit) - and writes the value at the EOT visit (the last draw on or before the landmark, the benchmark's stand-in for the ~month-24 visit) as risk (higher = more likely failing, matching the 2.4% / 13.0% / 78.6% PD rates) and call = 1 for H-MRD, the group the paper flags ('patients with H-MRD are better managed by continuing venetoclax'); the paper defines no per-patient probability, so TxResBench converts the risk. At fit the three paper analyses are recomputed on the training patients and reported in run.json: the exact Fisher-Freeman-Halton 3 x 2 test with the per-category PD table (patients without an EOT MRD status are excluded, like the paper's 10 of 130), the cohort KM PFS from the EOT landmark (at the benchmark horizons and at the paper's 6- and 12-month points), and the uMRD -> MRD+ conversion KM from the post-landmark draws of long_full.csv; the same Fisher test is reported for each cov_* column when covariates are passed (the paper's other Table 1 factors).

methods.description: The MRD-based risk stratification rule of DCOG ALL10 (Pieters et al., J Clin Oncol 2016, newly diagnosed childhood ALL, 778 children): after courses IA and IB (TP1, TP2 ~day 79) the PCR-detected MRD level (EuroMRD real-time quantitative PCR, fraction of leukemic cells) plus four MRD-independent criteria assign each patient standard risk (SR), medium risk (MR) or high risk (HR). SR requires all of: cytomorphologic CR day 33, MRD-negativity at TP1 and TP2 (target quantitative range/sensitivity 10^-4, i.e. below 10^-4), no MLL-AF4 rearrangement, no prednisone-poor response, no CNS/testicular involvement; HR requires at least one of: (TP1 MRD >= 5 x 10^-4 or unknown and TP2 MRD >= 5 x 10^-4), MLL-AF4, poor prednisone response, no CR day 33; everyone else - including patients with inconclusive or missing MRD data - is MR, and children with Down syndrome are never HR. The wrapper takes the two protocol time points on the benchmark clock (TP1 = first draw after baseline_max_day up to the landmark, TP2 = the last, the paper's day-79 decision day) and the five criteria as cov_* columns named by the settings (0/1 each; a missing criterion or a value outside 0/1 is unknown and can never confirm SR or trigger HR, so the patient falls to MR unless the MRD criterion says HR). It writes the TP2 MRD level as risk (the decision-day quantity the criteria threshold; an MRD level of 0 or below 10^-4 is an undetectable/negative result, the benchmark's not-detected convention) and call 1 when the group is HR (treatment judged failing), 0 otherwise; no probability is written, TxResBench converts the risk. A patient with no MRD level at TP2 gets no prediction with the reason in note (the paper's 'MRD classification not feasible' case). Unlike the paper: the EuroMRD per-patient target-coverage requirement is upstream assay information the benchmark does not carry (the wrapper reads the level the data provides), the paper's 'TP1 or unknown' clause is implemented for a patient with a single on-treatment draw (TP1 unknown, that draw is TP2), and the Down-syndrome exclusion applies to known DS only.

methods.description: The MRD-status-based survival stratification of Zabaleta et al. (Am J Hematol, DOI 10.1002/ajh.27526; 201 relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma patients treated with T-cell redirecting immunotherapy - cilta-cel, ide-cel, ARI0002h, teclistamab, talquetamab, elranatamab): from the serial next-generation-flow (NGF) bone-marrow MRD statuses (negative at 10^-6 vs positive) and the serological CR status per the 2016 IMWG criteria the patients are grouped as (a) MRD-negative by best MRD response - negativity at one or more assessments - vs MRD positive (patients without an MRD assessment counted positive in ITT analyses, md:32; 117/201 negative, md:82), (b) MRD kinetics three groups - sustained (>= 2 consecutive negative results, n = 60) vs transient (negativity followed by MRD resurgence, n = 26) vs persistent MRD positive, md:32/md:89 - and (c) the four CR x MRD groups CR/MRD- (N = 88), NoCR/MRD- (N = 26), CR/MRD+ (N = 11), NoCR/MRD+ (N = 69), md:107; the groups are compared by Kaplan-Meier (two-sided 95% CI) with the log-rank test and univariate Cox for PFS and OS from treatment initiation plus a seven-covariate multivariate Cox (prior lines, CAR T vs TCE, ISS, cytogenetic risk, EMD, CR, MRD status; adjusted HRs 0.22 PFS / 0.34 OS, md:102) and landmark analyses at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months (md:36, md:84; the published reference: two-group PFS HR 0.11, 95% CI 0.07-0.16, median PFS 20 vs 3 months, median OS NR vs 7 months, md:84; kinetics 1-year rates 10%/65%/93% PFS and 32%/92%/98% OS, md:89; four-group medians 29/10/8/3 and NR/19/34/7 months, md:107). The wrapper takes two markers (markers[0] = the per-draw BM NGF MRD status, markers[1] = the per-draw 2016-IMWG CR status; roles by marker name, else value type, else position), derives the per-patient group labels from the draws up to the call's landmark (the paper's months 1/3/6/12 stand at the benchmark's landmark day; a patient must have a baseline draw and a draw during treatment, the benchmark's convention) and writes the four-level CR x MRD group as risk (0 = CR/MRD-, 1 = NoCR/MRD-, 2 = CR/MRD+, 3 = NoCR/MRD+, higher = more likely failing - the paper's own ordering) and call = 1 when the MRD status is positive (treatment judged failing); TxResBench converts the risk, the paper defines no per-patient probability. At fit the paper's whole analysis is recomputed on the training patients and reported in run.json (per-patient group labels, per-group KM with 95% CIs, medians, 1-year rates, log-rank tests, univariate and multivariate Cox HRs, the landmark analysis at the call's landmark and the published results as the reference). Differences from the paper, all recorded in the README: the benchmark's fit data hold only patients whose outcome is still open at the landmark, so the from-treatment-initiation estimates are the landmark-conditioned versions; the four landmark months are one analysis per benchmark call; the MRD-marker detection call and its threshold are resolved at fit from the training values (the marker's __detected rows, a 0/1 status, the value-0 convention, or a quantitative level split at the paper's 10^-6 - with a documented training-median stand-in for an uncalibrated input); the single-negative residual of the kinetics classification is counted in the persistent group (the paper leaves it unexplained); the CR covariate of the multivariate model is the wrapper's second marker and the multivariate model is only fitted when cov_* columns matching the paper's five covariates are passed.

methods.description: The univariate diagnostic-test evaluation of Schmidt et al. (PLoS ONE 2015;10(2):e0118195, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0118195; 36 prospectively enrolled advanced NSCLC/SCLC patients, 31 first-line, standard platinum-based therapy or TKI, mSHOX2 measured blinded to the clinical data): the RAW plasma mSHOX2 PMR value (percent methylation reference, relative to ACTB, md:186-188, md:377-378) at one fixed blood draw is used as a diagnostic test for the RECIST v1.1 re-staging response after three therapy cycles (19 non-responders vs 12 responders among the 31, md:27-28), evaluated by a receiver operating characteristic curve per draw with the AUC - baseline 0.593, blood draw 1 (the first on-treatment draw, 7-10 days after therapy start) 0.844, rising to 1.000 at blood draw 7 (Fig. 2, md:429-435, md:444-445). The paper defines no operating cutoff, no per-patient call and no probability; the wrapper therefore writes risk = the raw PMR value at the named draw (no change score, ratio or log transform; the identity projection) - higher = non-response-favorable (responders' median dropped 4.06% at baseline to 0.62% at draw 1 vs non-responders' 26.45% to 6.86%, md:367-372) - for the paper's analysis set only: patients whose baseline PMR is at or below 1% (7 of 31; 'assumed to be the level of technical/biological variance', md:214-215) get no score, with the reason in `note` (the paper defines no fallback), as do patients without a baseline draw or without the named on-treatment draw by the landmark. It writes no call and no probability of its own (TxResBench converts the risk); nothing is learned from the training outcomes (a fixed rule - no code is published, only the environments SPSS 21 and R, md:198-199, so the rule is quoted from the text) and the per-draw ROC/AUC evaluation is the benchmark analysis's, not the wrapper's.

methods.description: The four-class molecular response criteria of Yi et al. (Signal Transduct Target Ther 2021;6:251, DOI 10.1038/s41392-021-00662-9; 125 patients with HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer receiving first-line capecitabine + docetaxel then maintenance capecitabine, CAMELLIA NCT01917279; serial plasma ctDNA before the first treatment and at every two cycles): a per-patient call at the first tumor evaluation (~cycle 2) from the serial plasma ctDNA mTBI (molecular tumor burden index, %, the paper's own per-draw index = the mean mutant allele frequency over the N unique variants of the patient's whole plasma series; the index's computation from variant-level data is feature construction the curated marker carries). The rule as printed: mCR = mTBI reduced to zero during treatment; mPR = mTBI decreased by at least 80% vs the baseline if the baseline mTBI is >= 1.0% (the 80% derived from the ROC analysis in this sample, AUC 0.98), else (baseline < 1.0%) by at least 50%; mPD = mTBI increased by at least 80% vs the lowest mTBI value, or - if the lowest mTBI < 2 - an absolute increase of at least 0.1 vs the lowest mTBI value; mSD = the change in mTBI does not qualify as mPR or mPD. The paper's validation is agreement with CT-based RECIST 1.1 (50.9%, 85/167 samples; sensitivity 88.5% for CT PR/CR, 87.5% for CT PD) and longer PFS (median 9.7 vs 6.8 months, HR 2.43) and OS (64.7 vs 33.5 months, HR 2.48) for molecular responders than non-molecular responders. The wrapper takes one marker (the per-draw mTBI in percent; the per-draw detectability state comes from the marker's <marker>__detected companion rows when present, else a value above 0 counts as detected), reads the baseline draw (the last draw on or before baseline_max_day) and the evaluation draw (the last draw after it and at or before the landmark - the benchmark's decision day; the paper's named cycle-2 visit has no benchmark channel), and applies the rule in the order the four classes are printed (mCR, mPR, mPD, mSD; a documented reading - the paper does not state the order for conflicting conditions). It writes risk = the percent change of the mTBI from the baseline draw to the evaluation draw ((v1 - v0)/v0 x 100, the quantity the mPR branch thresholds; higher = increase = more likely failing) with the documented categorical value -100 for mCR and +100 for the mPD absolute-branch case with an undetectable baseline (cf. the de novo-detection convention of the ctDNA response criteria), and call = 1 for mSD/mPD (the paper's non-molecular responders - its survival comparison is molecular responders vs non-molecular responders - the contract's 'treatment judged failing') and 0 for mCR/mPR; it writes no probability (the paper defines none; TxResBench converts the risk). A patient with no baseline draw, no evaluation draw by the landmark, or a required draw whose detected value is not a positive finite number gets no prediction with the reason in note; a marker undetectable at the baseline and at the evaluation draw is the paper's mCR zero state (call 0), but gets no risk score - the percent change vs the baseline is undefined there.

methods.description: Per-patient probability of pathological complete response failure (residual disease at surgery after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy) from three peripheral blood transcriptomic immune scores before and after one treatment cycle - the unpenalized binomial logistic regression (the paper's 'GLM function in R', md:196) of Sun X, Ocampo AA et al. (Sci Transl Med 2026, DOI 10.1126/scitranslmed.aec2358; I-SPY2, trained on the 59-patient Chemo+Pembro 'pembro4' arm, separately on the Chemo arm, validated on 59 dostarlimab-treated patients): Response ~ Clinical subtype + Early Treatment 19-gene T cell score|TNBC + Baseline 19-gene T cell score|HR+BC + Baseline TCR Shannon + (Early Treatment - Baseline) Leukocyte chemotaxis score|HR+BC. The model's features are a baseline (T0) 19-gene T cell composite score (HR+ BC), an early-treatment (T1, after one cycle) T cell composite score (TNBC), a baseline TCR Shannon diversity index (both subtypes) and the T1 - T0 difference of the leukocyte chemotaxis score (HR+ BC), with clinical subtype (HR+ BC vs TNBC) as the main effect and stratifier of the subtype-specific terms. The paper publishes no analysis code, no coefficients and no per-patient probabilities ('?', candidate spec code status), so the wrapper refits the published structure per benchmark fold with base R stats::glm, with the subtype-specific terms rendered as interactions with a 0/1 TNBC indicator (the paper's '|TNBC'/'|HR+BC' notation is not valid R formula syntax); risk = p_no_response = P(residual disease) = 1 - P(pCR), fitted directly, so it is failure-oriented by construction; call = 1 (treatment judged failing / predicted no pCR) at the training fold's ROC-optimal cutoff, the paper's procedure for its immune-signature high/low split (md:98; the preprint's numeric cutoffs 0.45 Chemo+Pembro / 0.19 Chemo apply to the paper's own sample and are recorded in run.json, not reused). The three immune scores are precomputed inputs (their derivation - the 19-gene list in Fig. 5C, the composite-score arithmetic, the chemotaxis gene set - is not published); the wrapper is defined for the three-feature panel (markers: 3, required_markers all) and abstains with the reason in note for a patient missing the subtype's features or a known clinical-subtype channel, rather than impute or drop; the clinical subtype is declared as an optional covariate per the benchmark convention (analysis-plan 8: the common arena runs covariates off; the native arena passes a unit's full inputs), so the wrapper resolves the subtype channel from the cov_* columns by name (params subtype_covariates) and fits the paper's subtype-stratified design when it is present - when a run passes no subtype channel the wrapper fits the pooled reading of the same design (the four immune terms, no subtype mask) and records it: the paper's model needs the subtype, and no subtype is ever invented (documented degradation, never claimed as the paper). Differences from the paper: the model is refitted (no published coefficients), T1 is the benchmark's landmark-truncated last on-treatment draw (the paper's fixed one-cycle T1), the harness's no_response label is the failure complement of the paper's pCR vs RD label, and the DRFS survival application of the high/low call is out of scope.

methods.description: The per-patient ctDNA-dynamics risk rule of Oliveira et al. (npj Breast Cancer 2021;7:19, 45 evaluable metastatic HR+/HER2-negative breast cancer patients on CDK4/6i + ET, paired baseline (C1D1) and C2D1 Guardant360 v2.11 74-gene plasma ctDNA): mutations with VAF >= 0.4% at the baseline or the on-treatment draw (the union; patients with none are ctDNA-low) get a per-mutation VAFR = VAF_C2D1/VAF_C1D1 (VAF 0 for single-timepoint variants), the ratios are capped at 0.1 minimum (undetected or < 0.4% at C2D1) and 10 maximum (new at C2D1), and the patient's mVAFR is the arithmetic mean of all VAFRs, grouped mVAFR-low (<= 0.3) / mVAFR-medium / mVAFR-high (>= 1.0) - the high group had the worse PFS (vs low: aHR 0.31, 95% CI 0.09-1, p = 0.049; mVAFR continuous aHR per 1-unit increase 2.07, p = 0.008), while baseline/on-treatment VAF and delta-VAF were not associated with PFS. The wrapper takes every marker passed as one mutation of the panel (per-mutation VAF features; __detected/__lod companions are stripped), reads the baseline as the last draw on or before baseline_max_day and the on-treatment draw as the last draw in (baseline_max_day, landmark_day] (the paper's fixed C1D1/C2D1 pair mapped onto the benchmark's landmark day frame, the 'last draw before the landmark' reading of the other landmark wrappers; the paper defines no rule for later draws), writes risk = mVAFR (higher = worse) and call 1 for the mVAFR-high group (0 otherwise - the benchmark's binary collapse of the paper's three-level call, native per-patient probability none, so TxResBench converts the risk), and abstains with a note for the ctDNA-low patients (no qualifying mutation; the paper's separate category, no mVAFR defined) and for missing baseline/on-treatment pairs. The wrapper learns nothing from the training outcomes; the paper's Cox analyses and the Fig. 2e regrouping (mVAFR-low + ctDNA-low combined, aHR 0.25) are validation, not fitted here. Differences from the paper (each with its reason, and the unresolved readings flagged) are in the README: '0.1 as minimum' (Methods) vs 'fixed VAFR values of 10 or 0.1' (Discussion) - the wrapper defaults to the floor reading and records it; the cap 10 applies to new-at-C2D1 mutations only (no stated cap for a baseline-tracked ratio above 10); exactly 0.3 -> low / exactly 1.0 -> high (the printed groups leave 0.30-0.31 and 0.99-1.00 gaps); the alternative mVAFR_log score is available as score_metric 'logmean' (log of the capped ratios, same cutoffs); value_to_pct maps VAF units to the paper's percent scale.

methods.description: The per-patient NAT ctDNA-response call of George et al. (EMBO Molecular Medicine 2026, DOI 10.1038/s44321-026-00447-z; NeoCircle substudy of SCAN-B, NCT02306096; 136 early breast cancer patients on neoadjuvant treatment (NAT), median 11 plasma timepoints per patient, range 6-14, md:54): the variable 'NAT ctDNA-response' 'was defined as either complete clearance of ctDNA at end-NAT (i.e., being end-NAT ctDNA-) or partial ctDNA clearance, defined as a decrease in ctDNA TF by at least 50% from baseline to the end-NAT timepoint and with a decreasing TF trend from the prior timepoint to the end-NAT timepoint.' (md:135) - a responder is end-NAT ctDNA-negative, or the end-NAT ctDNA tumor fraction (TF, %) is at most half the baseline TF AND the TF fell from the prior (mid-NAT) draw to the end-NAT draw; everything else is a NAT ctDNA-non-responder (13.1% of the cohort, md:9; the paper's worked example of the trend condition: P09322 was 'end-NAT ctDNA+ with an increase from mid-NAT to end-NAT and thus classified a NAT ctDNA-non-responder', md:161 - a plain >=50% decrease threshold could have called him a responder). The wrapper takes exactly one marker - the per-draw ctDNA TF (%) from the patient's tumor-informed personalized SV fingerprint multiplex dPCR assay (Pathlight, SAGA Dx Inc, up to 16 SVs FFPE / up to 8 SVs FF research test, md:99/md:276; LOD 0.00052% TF at 95% certainty, md:101) with its per-draw detection status (the assay's 'proprietary thresholding algorithm', md:276, arriving as the marker's <marker>__detected rows) - and, per patient with a baseline draw (the last draw on or before baseline_max_day; the paper's 'baseline plasma timepoint, taken at the time of diagnostic biopsy prior to any therapy', md:114), an end-NAT draw (the last draw before the landmark; the paper's end-NAT = 'the final timepoint after the last administration of NAT and prior to surgery', md:124) and a prior mid-NAT draw (the draw immediately before end-NAT, md:135/md:232), writes: risk = the relative change (x_end - x0)/x0 of the ctDNA TF from baseline to end-NAT - the quantity the 50% threshold applies to, with an undetectable end-NAT TF entering as the reported 0 (a full drop, -1.0; higher = more likely failing); call = 1 = NAT ctDNA-non-responder (treatment judged failing), 0 = NAT ctDNA-responder; and nat_ctdna_response = the paper's variable (1 = responder = call 0). No probability is written (the paper defines none per patient, so TxResBench converts the risk per outcome); the paper's validation layer - Kaplan-Meier/log-rank/Cox hazard ratios on breast cancer-free interval and overall survival (DATECAN-defined, md:283) and the Fisher's-exact recurrence/death tables (md:281) with HR 9.4 (95% CI 3.8 to 23.7) / HR 11.9 (3.9 to 35.9) for non-response vs response (md:135) - is the paper's group-association analysis of the call, not part of it, and is recorded in run.json as reported. Nothing is fitted (fitted false: the 50% cutoff is the definition's constant - 'at least 50%', inclusive, md:135 - not a training estimate; the variable is introduced as 'an exploratory analysis', md:135, with no derivation described, so the provenance is '?'). Declared readings of the paper's open points (each also in run.json): the prior draw = the last draw strictly before the end-NAT draw (which draw when several mid-NAT draws exist is not stated, '?'); the trend is compared on the reported TFs (the paper's log2(tf + 1e-8) transform, md:285, is monotone, so the sign is identical); the benchmark's landmark stands in for the end-NAT assessment (the paper's draws are numbered by three-weekly cycle, md:232); a patient whose baseline is ctDNA-negative (14/136 = 10.3%, md:114) gets no prediction - the 50% decrease divides by the baseline TF and the paper defines no rule for these patients (the letter of md:135 would call an end-NAT ctDNA- patient a responder regardless of baseline, recorded and not acted on: no score is invented), as does a patient without the prior draw (the trend condition is undefined; the wrapper does not silently degenerate to the 2-draw clearance/50% rule); the boundary is inclusive (a 50% decrease satisfies 'at least 50%'). The paper publishes no analysis code, so the wrapper implements the rule (spec candidates/nat-ctdna-response.yaml) from the Methods/Results text.

methods.description: The low/high serum neopterin status rule and its two-group survival analysis of Siemiatkowska A, Bryl M, Kuznar-Kaminska B, Kosicka-Noworzyn K, Pruszynski P, Golda-Gocka I, Glowka FK, 'Low serum neopterin early indicates durable benefits of atezolizumab and pembrolizumab therapy in advanced lung cancer' (Sci Rep 2025;15, DOI 10.1038/s41598-025-97792-9; 103 advanced NSCLC stage IIIB/IV patients of the Polish national drug program - 59 on first-line pembrolizumab 200 mg Q3W, 44 on first/second-line atezolizumab 1200 mg Q3W, 20 of them on concurrent chemoimmunotherapy - prospective two-centre, serum at baseline and at the end of cycles 1-4, Feb 2019 - Aug 2023). The rule: per patient, serum neopterin (NEO, nM, validated HPLC-FLD/UV) is read at the end-of-cycle-3 (NEO.3) and end-of-cycle-4 (NEO.4) pre-dose draws of the Q3W schedule and compared with the two ROC-derived cutoffs of the paper, which were derived in-sample against the long-term-benefit label (disease control CR/PR/SD lasting >= 12 months from treatment start; 23 vs 80 patients): 'Low-NEO status was defined as serum neopterin concentrations <= 71.65 nM at the end of the 3rd cycle (NEO.3) and <= 66.84 nM at the end of the 4th cycle (NEO.4).' (md:203) - low-NEO status = NEO.3 <= 71.65 nM AND NEO.4 <= 66.84 nM (AND conjunction, boundaries inclusive per '<='); all other patients (either draw above its cutoff) are high-NEO status. The cutoffs: NEO.3 71.65 nM (AUC 0.664, 95% CI 0.541-0.772, p < 0.05, sensitivity 80.0%, specificity 60.0%) and NEO.4 66.84 nM (AUC 0.747, 95% CI 0.612-0.853, p < 0.001, sensitivity 88.2%, specificity 69.2%) (md:193); the ROC optimality criterion is not named ('the best cut-offs', md:97) and no AUC is reported for the combined AND rule (md:193). The status was evaluated by Kaplan-Meier with log-rank tests and by univariable and stepwise multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression (p < 0.05 entry / p > 0.1 elimination; only univariable-significant variables entered): low-NEO status vs high-NEO status PFS HR = 0.327 (95% CI 0.171-0.625, p < 0.001, the only retained PFS factor), TTF adjusted HR = 0.450 (95% CI 0.244-0.829, p < 0.05) with patient's sex (adjusted HR = 1.818, 95% CI 1.033-3.201, p < 0.05) and objective response (adjusted HR = 0.387, 95% CI 0.186-0.804, p < 0.05); KM medians PFS 17.3 (95% CI 6.3-41.7) vs 5.9 (4.4-7.3) months and TTF 16.3 (6.3-29.7) vs 5.5 (4.4-6.5) months; OS was NOT significantly affected by NEO status (log-rank p = 0.0742; the paper's OS multivariable model has no NEO term) (md:53, md:99, md:200, md:203, md:205). The wrapper writes risk = the larger of the two on-treatment draws in the paper's cutoff units, max(NEO.3 / 71.65, NEO.4 / 66.84) - the wrapper's reading of 'the quantity the rule thresholds' for a two-cutoff AND rule, per the corpus conventions (the stronger-arm threshold-unit risk of combined-ctdna-risk-rule and the AND-rule threshold-unit combination of psa-deep-response-combined); higher = worse (the paper's high-NEO group has the shorter PFS/TTF), risk <= 1 is exactly the low-NEO side and risk > 1 the high-NEO side - and call = 1 for high-NEO status (risk > 1; either draw above its cutoff; the paper's high-risk group, treatment judged failing) and 0 for low-NEO status (risk <= 1; both draws at or below their cutoffs). No probability is written: the paper defines no per-patient survival probability or risk score (its quantities are the group HRs, KM medians and log-rank p), so TxResBench converts the risk per outcome. Nothing is learned from the training outcomes (fitted false): the cutoffs were derived in the authors' own 103-patient sample by ROC analysis against the long-term-benefit label (md:97, md:193) and no derivation code is published (MedCalc 22.019, md:101), so they are treated as published constants (params cutoff_neo3_nm / cutoff_neo4_nm, the corpus published-constant convention; a benchmark may override them). The two on-treatment draws are mapped by the corpus fixed-pair convention: NEO.4 = the marker's last draw after baseline_max_day and at or before the landmark, NEO.3 = the marker's last draw after baseline_max_day strictly before that NEO.4 draw (a landmark at the paper's end-of-cycle-4 day - ~day 84 under Q3W, the paper prints no day number, md:38/md:44 - reproduces the paper's draws exactly; at any other landmark the rule is evaluated at the decision day and draws after the landmark never enter); baseline, NEO.1 and NEO.2 are descriptive/non-discriminating and never enter the call (md:178, md:183, md:219, md:252). A patient without both on-treatment draws (the wrapper needs at least three draws including the baseline, min_draws 3), or with a non-finite or negative value at either draw, gets no prediction with the reason in note (the paper states no imputation or fallback; 400 of up to 515 planned samples were assessed, md:178, and the n = 39 all-five-sera / dose-delay-<=-3-days analysis of md:252 is a sensitivity check, not an inclusion rule). A below-detection-limit value (benchmark encoding: 0 with a <marker>__detected row of 0) counts as a measured 0 and scores as low on that draw: the paper's calibration range starts at 12.5 nM and all 400 results were within it (md:85, md:178), no NEO non-detect convention is published, and the corpus below-threshold convention for raw-value rules (cf. scd8-roc-cutoff-subgroup) applies - recorded, not invented. The fit report records the paper's cohort-level association results as printed (ROC operating points, KM medians, log-rank p, Cox HRs) plus the wrapper's own UNIVARIABLE KM/log-rank/Cox of the call on the training fold for the harness's progression and death outcomes (the paper's TTF has no harness outcome; the paper's stepwise multivariable TTF model and its covariates are association-analysis quantities, not part of the per-patient call, and are recorded as printed).

methods.description: The per-patient low/high-NEO status call of Siemiatkowska A, Kuznar-Kaminska B, Bryl M, et al., 'Low serum neopterin early indicates durable benefits of atezolizumab and pembrolizumab therapy in advanced lung cancer' (Sci Rep 2025;15:13078, DOI 10.1038/s41598-025-97792-9; 103 advanced NSCLC patients - stage IIIB/IV, Polish national drug program - 59 on pembrolizumab 200 mg Q3W, 44 on atezolizumab 1200 mg Q3W, 20 on concurrent chemoimmunotherapy, prospective two-centre research, samples Feb 2019 - Aug 2023): serum neopterin (NEO, nM, validated HPLC-FLD/UV) was measured at baseline (NEO.0) and at the end of cycles 1-4 pre-dose (NEO.1-NEO.4, md:44/md:73); the on-treatment NEO levels were consistently lower in patients with long-term benefits (disease control CR/PR/SD lasting >= 12 months from the start of treatment, md:55), reaching significance at the end of the 3rd and 4th cycles (NEO.3 medians 58.8 vs 77.8 nM, p < 0.05; NEO.4 52.9 vs 77.6 nM, p < 0.005; md:183); ROC analysis against the long-term-benefit label derived the cutoffs 71.65 nM (NEO.3; AUC 0.664, 95% CI 0.541-0.772, p < 0.05, sensitivity 80.0%, specificity 60.0%) and 66.84 nM (NEO.4; AUC 0.747, 95% CI 0.612-0.853, p < 0.001, sensitivity 88.2%, specificity 69.2%) (md:193), and 'Low-NEO status was defined as serum neopterin concentrations <= 71.65 nM at the end of the 3rd cycle (NEO.3) and <= 66.84 nM at the end of the 4th cycle (NEO.4).' (md:203) - the boundary-inclusive AND rule; high-NEO status = every other patient (md:205). The stepwise univariable/multivariable binary logistic regression of the >= 12-month benefit label confirmed low-NEO status as the only retained factor (p < 0.05 entry / p > 0.1 elimination; the other univariable-significant factors - NSCLC subtype p < 0.05 and objective response p < 0.001, Table 2 - were not retained), OR = 11.70 (95% CI 3.24-42.28, p < 0.001) (md:195); the paper's KM/log-rank/Cox survival analyses are the companion spec neo-roc-status-cox. The wrapper writes risk = the raw NEO.4 value (nM) of the pair - the quantity the 66.84 nM cutoff thresholds, the decision-time read; higher = worse (high-NEO status: median PFS 5.9 vs 17.3 months, md:200) - and call = 1 for high-NEO status (> 71.65 nM at NEO.3 OR > 66.84 nM at NEO.4 = treatment judged failing, the paper's ~12x lower-odds group) and 0 for low-NEO status (both draws at/below their cutoffs); it writes no probability (the paper reports only the group OR; no per-patient probability or risk score is defined - spec output.projection - so TxResBench converts the risk). The pair is mapped by the corpus fixed-pair convention: NEO.3/NEO.4 = the marker's second-to-last / last draw after baseline_max_day and at or before the landmark (the paper's end-of-cycle-3/4 draws of the Q3W schedule, ~days 63/84; the paper prints no day numbers, md:38/md:44) - a landmark at the paper's end-of-cycle-4 day reproduces the paper's pair exactly, at any other landmark the rule is evaluated at the decision day, and draws after the landmark never enter (the same convention as scd8-roc-cutoff-subgroup's single end-of-cycle-2 draw, extended to the two-draw pair; cf. ctdna-dynamics-two-group / ldh-interval-ratio-threshold). The cutoffs are published constants (params neo3_cutoff_nm / neo4_cutoff_nm, overridable): they were derived in the authors' own sample by ROC analysis (the optimality criterion is not named - 'the best cut-offs', md:97 - and MedCalc 22.019, md:101, publishes no code), so the derivation is not re-run on benchmark data and nothing is learned from the training outcomes (fitted false; the corpus published-constant convention); the paper's OR, ROC operating points, per-cycle medians and Table 2 screening are recorded in the fit report as printed, not fitted and not per-patient outputs. A patient without two usable on-treatment draws by the landmark gets no prediction, with the reason in note (the paper's complete case: 400 of the up-to-515 planned samples assessed, md:178; the counts of patients with both draws and the per-group low/high-NEO n are not printed, '?'; no imputation is described): min_draws is 3 (baseline + the two on-treatment draws of the pair - the paper needs no baseline for the call, but a patient with fewer than two on-treatment draws cannot be scored and the contract's draw count starts from the baseline). A below-detection-limit value (the benchmark's 0 with a <marker>__detected row of 0) enters as the reported 0 and scores low (0 <= both cutoffs; the corpus below-threshold convention for raw-value rules - the paper's calibration range starts at 12.5 nM and all 400 results fell inside it, md:85/md:178 - so no value below the range is described and no non-detect convention is published); a negative value is not a measured concentration and also abstains the patient. No covariates are taken (the paper's Table 2 screening covariates belong to the evaluation logistic, whose OR is recorded as printed - the per-patient rule itself is marker-only).
