methods.description: The naive Bayes classifier of pCR occurrence that Huang et al. (Scientific Reports 2020;10:12555, doi:10.1038/s41598-020-69345-9) fitted in STATISTICA 13.0 (md:157) to predict pathological complete response (pCR = ypT0N0 in the TME specimen, md:128-129) after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in 236 patients with locally advanced rectal cancer (56 pCR / 180 non-pCR, Table 1 md:338-344) - one of the five forecasting models of the authors' comparison ('An NBC model can be used to efficiently develop classification tools for various health domains and transform complex clinical problems into clear, precise, and predictive models.', md:75-76 - the paper's only description of the classifier). Its predictors are the risk factors significant (P < 0.01) in the authors' univariate logistic regression (md:170-174): the post-CRT serum CEA category (<=2 vs >2 ng/mL; the cutoff follows the cohort median 2.2 ng/mL, md:165-167) plus 15 clinical variables (gender, age, tumour location, chemotherapy regimen, clinical T, clinical N, TNM stage, tumour grade, anemia, diarrhea, urinary symptoms, dermatitis, leukopenia, RT dose, RT-surgery interval); in the benchmark these arrive as the marker's last on-treatment draw before the landmark (the paper's single post-CRT measurement ~6-10 weeks after CRT, md:132-133) and the cov_* clinical columns (covariates optional: the benchmark's main track runs without the covariate track, when the wrapper fits the classifier on the marker category alone - the paper's clinical variables are not representable - and with the track on the 15 clinical variables are resolved from its cov_* columns by name, params covariate_columns, encoded per the paper's Table 1 categories). The paper publishes no code (STATISTICA is proprietary, md:157; availability is data-only, md:737-738), so the wrapper refits the publication's described classifier with scikit-learn's GaussianNB - per-class Gaussian class-conditional densities on a diagonal covariance (conditional independence given the class), empirical class priors, var_smoothing added to every class variance - fitted on the training patients whose harness outcome no_response (best RECIST SD or PD - the closest benchmark analogue of the paper's non-pCR residual-tumour class, md:128-129) is known; the wrapper fits P(no response) directly, so risk = p_no_response is failure-oriented by construction, the flip of the paper's stated P(pCR) (md:138-139). Everything the paper leaves unspecified - the distributional assumption, smoothing, the class-prior handling, the feature encoding, and the classification probability cutoff behind its reported indices (all '?' per the spec) - is the wrapper's documented choice, made once and recorded in run.json and the README; no scikit-learn default is presented as a paper fact, and the paper's published NBC cohort indices (Table 3: training n=165 sens 0.91/1-spec 0.49/acc 0.75/AUROC 0.50, testing n=71 0.90/0.85/0.78/0.51; Table 4 validation n=34 0.90/0.53/0.80/0.63, md:513-519/549-555/594-600) are recorded in run.json as reported, not fitted. A patient without both a baseline draw (day <= baseline_max_day) and a post-baseline marker draw before the landmark, or (with the covariate track on) with a missing or unparseable value of a used covariate, gets no prediction with the reason in note - the paper's cohorts were complete-case by its inclusion criteria (md:93-99) and it defines no imputation.

methods.description: The support vector machine (SVM) classifier that Huang C-M, Huang M-Y, Huang C-W, et al., Scientific Reports 2020;10:12555, doi:10.1038/s41598-020-69345-9, fitted in STATISTICA 13.0 (md:157) to predict pathological complete response (pCR = ypT0N0 in the total mesorectal excision specimen, md:128-129) after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in 236 patients with locally advanced rectal cancer (56 pCR / 180 non-pCR, Table 1 md:338-344): 'An SVM model constructs multidimensional hyperplanes that separate the 2 classes while maximizing the margin between the 2 classes; it uses kernel functions and can discriminate between non-linearly separable classes.' (md:71-75), 'the dependent variable was the probability of pCR' (md:138-139). Its 16 inputs are the risk factors significant (P < 0.01) in the authors' univariate logistic regression (md:170-174): the post-CRT serum CEA category (<=2 vs >2 ng/mL; cutoff 2 ng/mL from the cohort median 2.2 ng/mL, md:165-167) plus 15 clinical variables (gender, age, tumour location, chemotherapy regimen, clinical T, clinical N, TNM stage, tumour grade, anemia, diarrhea, urinary symptoms, dermatitis, leukopenia, RT dose, RT-surgery interval); in the benchmark these arrive as the marker's last on-treatment draw before the landmark (the paper's single post-CRT measurement ~6-10 weeks after CRT completion, before surgery, md:132-133) and the cov_* clinical columns; covariates are declared optional because the benchmark's datasets carry the clinical track or not - with the track the wrapper fits the paper's full 16-variable model, without it (the benchmark's covariate-free mode) it fits the post-CRT CEA category alone, a recorded fallback (run.json records which model was fitted), not one the paper defines. The paper publishes no code (STATISTICA is proprietary; availability is data-only, md:737-738) and never states the kernel, the kernel parameters, the soft-margin penalty, the solver, the feature encoding or the classification probability cutoff (all '?'), so the wrapper refits the described maximum-margin classifier on the benchmark training patients with scikit-learn's SVC (kernel rbf, C 1.0, gamma 'scale', Platt-scaled probabilities, all WRAPPER choices recorded in run.json and the README - no scikit-learn default is presented as a paper fact; the paper states only 'it uses kernel functions', md:73-75). The wrapper fits P(no response) directly on the harness outcome no_response (best RECIST SD or PD - the benchmark label standing in for the paper's non-pCR residual-tumour class; the harness cannot carry the pathological ypT0N0 label, a recorded difference), so risk = p_no_response = the SVM's calibrated probability of no response and is failure-oriented by construction, the flip of the paper's stated P(pCR) (md:138-139). The paper's published cohort indices (Table 3: training n=165 sensitivity 0.91/1-specificity 0.57/PPV 0.85/NPV 0.57/accuracy 0.64/AUROC 0.73, testing n=71 0.90/0.82/0.85/0.71/0.85/0.74, md:506-512/md:542-548; Table 4 validation n=34 0.91/0.76/0.86/0.72/0.71/0.76, md:587-593, averaged over the paper's 1,000 random 70/30 splits, md:150-152) are recorded in run.json as reported, not fitted. A patient without both a baseline draw (day <= baseline_max_day) and a post-baseline draw before the landmark, or incomplete on a covariate of the fitted model, gets no prediction with the reason in note - the paper's cohorts were complete-case by its inclusion criteria (md:93-99) and it defines no imputation.

methods.description: The paper's TabPFN pipeline for predicting pathological treatment response to neoadjuvant pembrolizumab in resectable locally advanced HNSCC (Bandaru et al., J Clin Invest 2026, DOI 10.1172/JCI196284; NCT02641093, 68 patients, 185 cfDNA WGS samples, analysis set 58 patients / 151 samples): given a plasma cfDNA sample's genome-wide region-level motif diversity score (rMDS) - the normalized Shannon entropy of 5'-end 4-mer motif frequencies per nonoverlapping 500 kb autosomal bin - the sample's rMDS vector is z scored across its bins (pandas std, ddof=1, a zero standard deviation becomes 0), regressed on the batch covariates (cfDNA isolation date, WGS library prep date, collection institute; sum contrasts, no intercept, patsy 0.5.6) with the training failure label preserved as a covariate (the coefficients for the batch design are removed, the preserved label's are not). Covariates are optional in the benchmark contract: when the covariate channel is passed the design is fitted exactly as the paper's; when it is absent - the common arena runs covariates off - the batch design block has no levels to contrast and batch_correct returns the z-scored matrix unchanged with an empty beta: no batch term is fitted or subtracted (the paper's batch-correction step is skipped; the preserved label is never subtracted by construction), a documented degradation of the paper's three-covariate design, the training draws are balanced by downsampling the majority class to the minority count (sklearn.utils.resample, no replacement, random_state=42, then shuffled with sample(frac=1, random_state=42)), reduced by TruncatedSVD(n_components=6, random_state=42), and classified by TabPFNClassifier with all package defaults (tabpfn 2.0.8: n_estimators=4, softmax_temperature=0.9, balance_probabilities=False, average_before_softmax=False, random_state=0, model_path='auto' - the pretrained checkpoint is bundled in the image because the container has no network; n_jobs=-1 is capped to the call's threads). The patient-level output uses the most recent draw on or before the landmark (the paper's fixed visit priority Adj Wk 1 > Day 0 > Screen is chronological in its cohort, so the day axis gives the same rule; the code also falls back to a screen-only draw and the wrapper scores any draw it is given). The wrapper writes risk = P(failure) = 1 - the paper's predicted probability of being a responder, and call = 1 when risk > 0.5 - the paper's 'Responder if probability >= 0.5 else Non-Responder' decision rule, complement-identical. Published validation: 100 repeated 10-fold patient-level CV mean AUC 0.99 +/- 0.05, leave-one-institute-out 0.89 +/- 0.12, and 100 x 10-patient pre-holdout 0.69 +/- 0.19; the batch-correction coefficients were refit on the training fold only in the pre-holdout analysis and the wrapper does that in every fold (the paper's CV/LOIO batch fit used the whole analysis set including the test samples).

methods.description: A univariable time-dependent Cox model of progression-free survival (PFS2, RECIST 1.1) from ONE serial tumour-burden marker entered as a single linear time-dependent covariate, after Beddowes et al. (bioRxiv 2023, published Mol Oncol 2025): each patient's marker draws open intervals in a counting-process frame Surv(start, stop, status), the value of each draw is carried to the next draw or the outcome (survival::coxph, no spline, no threshold, no covariates), and the paper's deliverable is the per-marker hazard ratio and concordance index used to compare which tumour-burden measure (ichorCNA, t-MAD, z-score; the maximum NGTAS VAF; CA15-3) best tracks plasma tumour burden. The wrapper fits that model on the training patients (the whole pre-outcome history, as the paper does; PFS learned first, else overall survival) and writes as risk the fitted model's linear predictor at the landmark - the transformation of the last marker value at or before the landmark - which TxResBench converts into the benchmark's probabilities: the paper itself reports only the cohort-level hazard ratio/c-index and defines no per-patient score, so the per-patient projection is the wrapper's (documented as such in the README). Marker transforms follow the paper's per-measure choices (raw values; params.transform, default none, may be set to log or sqrt for CA15-3-like or VAF-like measures).

methods.description: The memory-to-effector CD8+ T cell transition rule of Sander et al. (Oncotarget 2016;7:7586-7596, DOI 10.18632/oncotarget.7210; here FE2016; relapse-preventive HDC/IL-2 immunotherapy in 84 non-transplanted AML patients in first complete remission, Re:Mission NCT01347996; peripheral blood PBMC at C1D1 and C1D21 of ten 21-day cycles; subset frequencies by flow cytometry, gating CD45RA+/CCR7+/CD45RO+/CCR7-): a patient is transition-positive when the frequency of CD8+ TEM cells (%) decreased AND the frequency of CD8+ Teff cells (%) increased simultaneously between the C1D1 and C1D21 draws ('A patient was considered transition-positive by the occurrence of a reduction of TEM cells (%) and a simultaneous induction of Teff cells (%) during the first treatment cycle.', md:37; 18/44 analyzable patients = 41%, md:70); the two groups were compared on LFS and OS by the log-rank test, and the association was quantified by univariate and multivariate (age, number of induction courses) Cox regression (Table 1: transition vs LFS HR 0.19 [0.07-0.50] p = 0.001 and vs OS HR 0.13 [0.03-0.59] p = 0.008 univariate; 0.17 [0.06-0.47] p = 0.001 and 0.12 [0.02-0.54] p = 0.006 multivariate, md:55-56; the text prints p < 0.001 / p = 0.002, md:70 - an unresolved discrepancy). The wrapper takes exactly two markers (markers[0..1], identified by name as the TEM and Teff frequencies where the names say so, else by sorted order - markers[0] = TEM, markers[1] = Teff, the corpus convention of the fixed-list wrappers; the gate's M1/M2 arrive in this order) and pairs, per marker, the last draw on or before baseline_max_day (C1D1) with the last draw after it and at or before the landmark (the C1D21 draw at a day-21 landmark; draws after the landmark never enter). The call is the paper's definition in the failure direction: call = 1 (transition-negative, treatment judged failing) when TEM did not strictly decrease or Teff did not strictly increase; transition-positive is call 0. The risk is the quantity the conjunction thresholds - risk = max(TEM(x1) - TEM(x0), Teff(x0) - Teff(x1)) in percentage points: negative exactly for transition-positive, higher = the worse unmet favourable direction (TEM rising or Teff falling by more). It writes no probability (the paper defines no per-patient probability; the HRs and KM curves are cohort-level association statistics - TxResBench converts the risk), nothing is learned from the training outcomes (fitted false: the rule and both direction cutoffs are fixed by the printed definition, cutoff 0 on each direction), and a patient without a scorable baseline/on-treatment pair of both markers gets no prediction with the reason in note (the paper's 44 analyzable patients of 81 with blood samples, md:70, md:155; no imputation is described). Differences from the paper: the direction conditions are read strictly (an exactly equal TEM or Teff frequency is not a reduction/induction; the paper does not state the equal case, '?'); the paper's C1D21 evaluation is the landmark's last draw (at a later landmark the same direction rule is evaluated as of the decision day); the single-direction per-subset calls (Table 1 'Reduction TEM' / 'Induction TEFF') and the median single-time-point splits are separate methods (recorded as variant-of relchange-threshold and the median-split-survival family in the method catalog), not this rule.

(md:153); the software used for the log-rank/Cox analyses is not named anywhere (md:167, md:169); nothing was substituted or downloaded - this wrapper implements the rule from the Methods and Results text)

methods.description: The Temporal Transformer variant of the SHERLOC framework of Mamann et al. (bioRxiv 2026.06.04.730097) for overall survival from the landmark: the patient's longitudinal ctDNA profile is read as a matrix X in R^{T x C} (in the paper, T = 4 clinical timesteps BL to C4D1, C = 21 channels: 17 gene-level ctDNA VAFs + 4 panel-level aggregated features), each timestep being one token carrying the C channels; the matrix is batch-normalized along the timestep axis, and a single-head scaled dot-product self-attention over the T timestep tokens (Q = W_q(x), score = QK^T/sqrt(q), softmax, score@V, W_o; q = v = d_hidden = int(C/2)) produces the temporal representation, which is fused with per-timestep representations of a frozen genomic-interaction encoder (MLP pretrained with the Cox partial likelihood on solid-biopsy VAF data, frozen after pretraining, 2 dimensions per timestep; the paper uses the external MSK-CHORD cohort, 22,068 patients) and with baseline clinical covariates; the concatenation is dropped out at 0.4 and passed to a single linear layer with sigmoid output whose value is the Cox log-risk fed to pycox's CoxPH, trained by the negative log-partial likelihood (lr 0.005, batch 50, up to 256 epochs, early stopping patience 20, 20% validation split). The wrapper refits it per survival outcome of the training data (death first - the paper's OS, then progression), rebases the outcome times to the benchmark's landmark (the paper's OS from the final on-treatment ctDNA collection), resolves the sequence to the patient's visits up to the landmark (baseline slot = last baseline visit, then the most recent on-treatment visits, at most n_timepoints = 4 slots; the paper's evaluability rule requires all configured timepoints, md:1404-1408) and writes the paper's native outputs: the sigmoid log-risk (risk, monotone in the Cox log-risk) and per-horizon failure probabilities from the Breslow baseline-hazard survival curve. The frozen genomic-interaction encoder cannot be reproduced as published (MSK-CHORD is not redistributed, scripts/data/msk_chord/README.md:1-17), so the wrapper pretrains the same MLP architecture on the training cohort itself - the paper's transfer-learning step is replaced by an in-cohort pretraining (recorded deviation); the marker set is data-driven and the paper's gene/panel split is not recoverable from the benchmark's flat marker list (the code concatenates the two branches before the single BatchNorm/attention, so the wrapper feeds all channels as one vector, d_agg_input = 0 - recorded).

methods.description: The week-3 TIE-cell expansion rule of Valpione et al. (Nature Cancer 2020, DOI 10.1038/s43018-019-0022-x), first-line checkpoint-inhibitor therapy in metastatic melanoma. TIE cells are CD27-/CCR7- cells in the CD3+/CD8+/CD45RO+/CD45- gate, quantified by FACS on PBMC as the percentage of CD8+ memory T cells (the TIE ratio); the paper's rule is the difference between the W3 (week 3, after one cycle of CPI) and T0 (pre-treatment) values - 'Deltas were calculated as the difference between W3 and T0 values' - and an increase of >0.8 percentage points at W3 is W3 TIE expansion, which segregated DC (week-12 RECIST 1.1 best response including late responders) from PD patients (training sensitivity 0.94, specificity 0.79, accuracy 0.87, AUC 0.85; validation sensitivity 0.82, specificity 1, accuracy 0.90, AUC 0.92); patients without W3 TIE expansion had HR 3.7 (95% CI 1.12-11.9, P=0.032) for death. The wrapper takes one marker, the TIE % of CD8+ memory T cells per patient per draw; its T0 value is the last draw on or before baseline_max_day (the paper's pre-treatment draw) and its W3 value is the draw after the baseline, at or before the landmark, whose day lies inside week3_days +/- week3_window_days (default 21 +/- 7 days: the paper's week 3 after one cycle of a q3w regimen, no day numbers printed) closest to week3_days, ties going to the later draw; draws outside that window (week 9, week 12) never enter the rule, because by week 9 TIE cells no longer discriminated DC from PD. It writes risk = delta-W3TIE in percentage points itself (the quantity the cutoff thresholds; higher = more TIE expansion, the paper's favourable direction - the decision orientation is carried by call), call 0 = W3 TIE expansion (delta > expansion_cutoff, the paper's favourable group) and call 1 = no expansion (delta <= expansion_cutoff, the paper's HR 3.7 group, treatment judged failing) - the paper prints '>0.8%', so a delta of exactly 0.8 is not expansion - and no probability: the paper defines none and TxResBench converts the risk. The cutoff is the paper's published operating threshold, so the wrapper learns nothing from the training outcomes; a patient without a baseline draw or baseline value, without a draw in the week-3 window by the landmark, or with a missing week-3 value gets no prediction with the reason in note (the paper's TIE cohort is the 50 patients with paired T0/W3 TIE measurements; no fallback is stated). A TIE value of 0 is a valid measurement (the delta is then the W3 value: the rule is an absolute difference, no division or log), and the paper's group-level HR is an association statistic of the call, not part of it.

methods.description: The Bayesian hierarchical piecewise-linear trajectory model with the nadir-based alarm-threshold rule of Zhou et al. (ESMO Open 2022;7(2):100417, DOI 10.1016/j.esmoop.2022.100417 - plasma Tie2 trajectories identify vascular response criteria for VEGF inhibitors across biliary tract, colorectal and ovarian cancers): per biomarker (vascular pTie2 + epithelial pCK18/CA125) and per patient, a Bayesian hierarchical piecewise-linear model of the log2 biomarker concentration vs treatment time, C(t) = alpha + S(tinf-t)*beta*t + S(t-tinf)*(beta*tinf + gamma*(t-tinf)) + eps, is fitted by MCMC: t_inf (per-patient inflection point, uniformly distributed between 21 days after treatment start and 21 days before progression, bounded here by the patient's last observed draw day) is the VEGFi-resistance onset and the earliest sign of tumour progression; beta/alpha and gamma/alpha components form a two-group slope mixture with Bernoulli membership E1/E2 (responding vs non-responding trajectories) and population priors as given in the origin research (Jayson et al., Nat Commun 2018;9:4672, reference 9 of the paper; the paper's sampler is WinBUGS 1.4 - the wrapper implements the model itself with Metropolis-within-Gibbs, documented). The trained model drives the appendix's generic rule: prediction of tumour progression when the percentage change of the biomarker vs the nadir recorded prior to the time point exceeds the alarm threshold at a time point at least 45 days after treatment; the published thresholds are a 40% pTie2 increase from nadir (vascular progressive disease, vPD) and a 50% pCK18 increase from nadir; the vascular and epithelial predictions are co-modelled into one combined progression prediction (the combination detects significantly more patients than either biomarker alone, P < 0.001 - implemented as the union, since an AND combination would detect fewer). The wrapper's benchmark outputs: risk = the posterior mean of the model-predicted log2 concentration of the vascular biomarker at the landmark day (the model's own inference of the concentration at a given time during treatment, a use the appendix states; higher pTie2 = vascular progression = treatment escape; the paper defines no per-patient risk so TxResBench converts it to probabilities), call = the co-modelled nadir-alarm state at the landmark (1 when either biomarker has crossed its threshold at a time >= 45 days, 0 otherwise), and the paper's cohort-level results are reported at fit in run.json. The wrapper differs from the paper where the benchmark clock demands it: the PFS-21 inflection bound is replaced by the data-observed bound (the true progression time is unavailable at prediction), the model is fitted to the landmark history (the benchmark's decision point) rather than the full trajectory to progression, the MCMC uses far fewer iterations than the paper's 3 chains x 50,000 + 100,000, and the alarm rule runs on the benchmark's observed draws at their days rather than the paper's monthly 30 +/- 5-day pseudo-trial scheme (the pseudo-trial scheme is the threshold-inference machinery; the published thresholds are used as given).

methods.description: The pTie2-defined vascular response criteria of Zhou C, O'Connor J, Backen A, Valle JW, Bridgewater J, Dive C, Jayson GC ('Plasma Tie2 trajectories identify vascular response criteria for VEGF inhibitors across advanced biliary tract, colorectal and ovarian cancers', ESMO Open 2022;7(2):100417, DOI 10.1016/j.esmoop.2022.100417; 124 ABC-03 patients, 92 ICON7 ovarian, 70 Travastin CRC): the per-patient classification of the change in plasma Tie2 (pTie2) between the pre-treatment value and the value during the first 9 weeks of a VEGFi-containing regimen into vascular complete response (vCR), vascular partial response (vPR) and vascular no response (vNR). The paper deconvoluted the log2-scale pTie2 changes of the cediranib-treated ABC patients into two Gaussian distributions (a placebo/cytotoxic-like one with unchanged-to-elevated pTie2 and a drug-induced-reduction one; t-test P = 2.7 x 10^-14) and set the three classes at the 95% confidence intervals of the two distributions: 'patients who had at least a 24% reduction in pTie2 over 9 weeks of treatment were deemed to have had a vCR. Patients whose plasma pTie2 concentrations increased by 7% or more had vNR, while the rest had a vPR.' (md:68); CRC (Travastin/bevacizumab): vCR = 30% reduction or more, vNR = 4% increase or more (md:77). Paper's validation (group-level, not the call): vCR patients (21, 38% of the cediranib arm) had median OS 18.8 vs 14.3 (vPR/vNR) vs 12.1 months (placebo) and PFS 8.8 vs 7.5 vs 8.0 months; multivariable Cox OS HR 0.49 (95% CI 1.102-3.752, P = 0.023) vCR vs placebo and PFS RMST ratios 0.73 (P = 0.012, vCR vs vPR/vNR) and 0.77 (P = 0.001, vCR vs placebo) (md:70; Table 1: 38/36/25 ABC, 47/29/24 CRC). The wrapper is a fixed rule (fitted false): risk = the per-patient percentage change 100*(x1-x0)/x0 (the quantity the paper thresholds; equivalently 100*(2^dlog2 - 1), the log scale of md:41 converted to the paper's percent wording - the reported pair 12% <-> 0.16 log2 confirms the identity), higher = more likely failing; call = 1 for vPR and vNR (NOT a vCR - the paper's primary contrast 'patients with vCR and other groups', md:70) and 0 for vCR; the native three-class call (0 = vCR, 1 = vPR, 2 = vNR) is written as the extra numeric column vascular_response_class. The published 24%/7% thresholds are the defaults (params vcr_reduction_pct / vnr_increase_pct); the CRC 30%/4% set is documented in the README and selectable via the same params. The wrapper never refits the two-component Gaussian mixture (no fitting algorithm, component variances, mixing weights or fitted component parameters are published - spec runtime.randomness, new_patient_prediction.route) and learns nothing from the training outcomes. A patient without a pre-treatment draw, without a draw in the 9-week window, or with a non-positive pTie2 value (the benchmark's below-detection 0 convention; the paper reports no below-detection handling for the ELISA) gets no prediction, with the reason in note; draws after the 9-week window never enter the change.

methods.description: The time-to-PSA-nadir (TTPN) threshold rule of Wong CH-M, Ko IC-H, Leung DK-W, et al. (Prostate 2025;85:30-39, DOI 10.1002/pros.24797): 131 consecutive patients with de novo metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (Hong Kong Prostate Cancer Research Group Database, 2016-2022) treated with upfront intensification (ADT plus docetaxel or an androgen receptor signalling inhibitor), landmark analysis at 6 months post-ADT. Per patient the time from treatment start to the lowest serum PSA recorded after treatment initiation (the nadir) is documented in months, and the patient is called by that time: TTPN >= 6 months vs < 6 months - the TTPN >= 6 months group had better outcomes on the 123 landmark-eligible patients (median PFS 26.6 vs 19.8 months, HR 0.78; median OS 75.1 vs 61.8 months, HR 0.69, p = 0.072; CSS NR vs 61.8 months, HR 0.57, p = 0.082; md:74; the KM/log-rank/Cox association is not part of the rule). The wrapper is a fixed rule (learns nothing from the training outcomes): the nadir = the minimum serum PSA over the on-treatment draws (after baseline_max_day) up to the benchmark landmark (the paper's design allows an any-time nadir, md:140, but the benchmark call uses no draws after the call day), TTPN months = the nadir day / month_days (365.25/12 = 30.4375; the paper documents TTPN in months, md:36), call 1 = TTPN < ttpn_months (the paper's worse-outcome class) and 0 = TTPN >= ttpn_months (inclusive as printed, md:36), with risk = -TTPN months so higher = more likely failing (the quantity the rule thresholds is TTPN, which the contract orients toward failure; the un-negated TTPN is recorded in run.json), and no probability (TxResBench converts the risk). A patient with no measured on-treatment PSA by the landmark gets no prediction, with the reason in note. The paper publishes no analysis code (data-on-request only), so the rule is implemented from the Methods/Results text.

methods.description: The per-patient molecular progressive disease (mPD) call at the C3 landmark of Anees et al. (J Liquid Biopsy 2026;13:100477; two independent prospective immunotherapy cohorts, AHN n=72 + NORTH n=70, combined n=142): blood was collected pre-treatment (C1D1), C2D1 and C3D1, the Northstar Response assay (BillionToOne, tumor-naive methylation-based CAP/CLIA laboratory-developed test, >500 tumor-hypermethylated differentially methylated regions with paired plasma and buffy coat sequencing) reports a Tumor Methylation Score (TMS) per draw, and a patient is mPD if a clinically reportable TMS increase is called on the pair pre-treatment baseline -> C2D1 or on the pair C2D1 -> C3D1 (md:191-193); mPD then stratified PFS (AHN HR 7.0, 95% CI 3.3-14.9, C-index 0.69; NORTH applied without modification HR 5.9, 2.7-13.0, C-index 0.69) and OS (HR 6.2 / 3.2) in both cohorts. The increase call is the assay's statistical test per its cited ref [32] (Ye et al., Sci Rep 2025;15:5869): each time point is modeled as normal around its TMS with a CV-derived SD, the pair difference is normal with SD = sqrt(sd1^2 + sd2^2), and an Increase call requires the pair's relative TMS change >= +15% AND the log2 likelihood ratio of >= 15% vs < 15% greater than 3 (Decrease symmetric at <= -15%); otherwise No Change, and both draws below the calling threshold = Below Quantifiable Range (never an Increase, so never mPD - the M2026 md does not print that classification). The assay publishes no code and its CV-regression fit parameters and the M2026 research's exact calling threshold are not printed (assay revision unspecified), so the wrapper declares its reproducible readings in place of them: a constant per-draw relative SD (cv, default 0.10 = the assay's published <10% CV at 1% tumor fraction, md:174-178) with the published pair-SD formula, the likelihood ratio as the posterior odds under the published normal evidence model with a flat prior (the paper prints no formula), the relative change measured against the preceding timepoint, below-calling-threshold draws floored at the threshold when the dataset declares it (the marker's <marker>__lod row, else the calling_threshold setting; the ref [32] value 120 is applied only on the TMS scale) and otherwise treated as not evaluable. The wrapper writes risk = the largest per-pair relative TMS change (0 = no change, negative = decrease; the quantity the rule thresholds, so higher = more likely failing) and call = 1 for mPD (the paper's worse-PFS/OS group), 0 otherwise; no probability is defined by the paper and none is written (TxResBench converts the risk). Only the landmark window's draws are used (baseline + the first two on-treatment draws up to the benchmark landmark; the paper's longitudinal first-increase-over-all-serial-draws application and its KM/Cox and RECIST analyses are validation and are not part of the call), nothing is fitted (fitted false), and a patient with no evaluable pair gets no prediction with the reason in note.

methods.description: The combined tumor-uninformed ctDNA (TUCA) change rule of Cheng H et al., Cancer Innovation 2025;4:e70014 (DOI 10.1002/cai2.70014; 57 platinum-resistant recurrent ovarian cancer [PROC] patients on pegylated liposomal doxorubicin [PLD, 40 mg/m2, Q4w, 6 cycles] or PLD + apatinib [250 mg po qd], NCT04348032): the rule combines two per-marker change rules at the draw before the third cycle of treatment - component A (TP53 mutation change, md:168): favorable = TP53 mutation negative during treatment or positive with a >= 80% decrease from baseline; unfavorable = baseline-negative turning positive, or positivity that was stable / increased / decreased < 80%; component B (chromosomal-instability [CNA] change of the I score, md:182): favorable = CNA negative (I score < 14) during treatment or an I-score decline of more than 27.8 from baseline; unfavorable = baseline-negative turning positive, or positivity that increased or declined <= 27.8; combination (md:189): unfavorable TUCA change = unfavorable component A OR unfavorable component B; favorable TUCA change = favorable component A AND favorable component B. In the paper's 49 patients with baseline and before-third-cycle samples (35 cohort A + 14 cohort B; 30 no clinical benefit [nCB] / 19 clinical benefit [CB]) a favorable TUCA change before the third cycle predicted the best overall response (RECIST) with 90.0% sensitivity (27/30) and 63.2% specificity (12/19) and was associated with longer PFS (HR 2.88, 95% CI 1.56-5.30, log-rank p = 0.0008; mPFS 9.2 vs 3.6 months; multivariate Cox p = 0.005). The wrapper takes exactly two markers (the per-draw TP53MAF and the per-draw chromosome-instability I score; identified by marker name, positional fallback), applies the two component rules at the benchmark's baseline/landmark draw pair (the paper's fixed baseline -> before-third-cycle pair; the paper prints cycle labels, no day numbers), writes call = 1 for an unfavorable TUCA change (treatment judged failing) and risk = the number of unfavorable component calls (0, 1 or 2 - the paper defines no per-patient scalar; its output is the combined 2-level call, so the wrapper reports the two components' joint state that the AND/OR combination thresholds), and abstains when either component's value pair is missing. Nothing is fitted: the thresholds are the paper's fixed values (80%, 14, 27.8, all derived in the paper's sample), the training outcomes are never read.

methods.description: The paper's methods 2 and 3, 'Two consecutive increments' (van Delft et al., Heliyon 2022;8(10):e10932; NSCLC immunotherapy, non-response at 6 months, the paper calls them '2x increased BL' and '2x increased PL'): per measurement of one serum tumour marker (the paper fits each of CYFRA 21.1, CEA, CA-125, NSE and SCC separately, with per-marker thresholds) the increment relative to a reference value is evaluated - the reference is the BASELINE value for method 2, the PREVIOUS MEASUREMENT value for method 3 (the rule parameter `reference`), and the test is an increment when the change from the reference is at least the reference-level times the test-condition threshold (Figure 1B: 'An increment if dx >= Baseline x Threshold' / 'dx > X1 x Threshold'; the paper's '2x' names are the theta = 1 case). A patient is called a non-responder when two consecutive measurements both exceed an upper threshold of relevancy (UTR), or when the largest LTR-gated increment among measurements at or above a lower threshold of relevancy (LTR) exceeds the test-condition threshold (positive test results for measurements below the LTR are ignored; the logical-test outcome is used at an upward UTR crossing). The three thresholds (test condition, UTR, LTR) are fitted on the training cohort to maximize sensitivity at 95% specificity (the paper's anchor), with the paper's data cleaning (consecutive measurements less than 5 days or more than 30 days apart are excluded, and a baseline measurement with more than 2 values in the window is required; min_draws 3). The wrapper writes the largest LTR-gated fractional increase as risk (the quantity the rule thresholds, higher = failing, positive when the measurement exceeds the reference) and the 0/1 call, and no probability (the paper defines none; the benchmark converts the risk). It takes one marker and the draws on or before the landmark as the observation window; the paper's exact test-condition expression, threshold search and boundary conventions are not published - the reading of Figure 1B, the search grid and the tie-breaks are documented in the README and run.json.

methods.description: The two-population exponential tumour-evolution model predicting per-patient waiting time to treatment failure (Khan et al., Cancer Discovery 2018; PROSPECT-C phase II metastatic colorectal cancer on cetuximab; DOI 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-17-0891). The paper publishes no analysis code and never states the fitting algorithm ('?' in the spec: the model is given as mathematics in the Results and the Methods subsection is absent), so the wrapper implements the model as stated: N(t) = ns*e^(-lambda_s*t) + nr*e^(lambda_r*t) (Eq. 1) is fitted to the serial tumour-burden marker (CEA is proportional to N(t), per patient, and R(t) = nr*e^(lambda_r*t) (Eq. 2) to the serial cfDNA RAS-pathway mutant fractional abundance; rates per week; per-patient deterministic fit, no mixed effects, no population parameters, (no survival model). The fitted parameters (response rate lambda_s, relapse rate lambda_r, initial resistant frequency nr/N) are plugged back into Eq. 1 and the equation is solved for the time t at which N(t) is 72.8% larger than N(t = 0) (ratio 1.728: RECIST v1.1's 20% increase in lesions diameter = 72.8% increase in volume) - the predicted waiting time to treatment failure, validated by the paper against the observed RECIST v1.1 progression time (percent error, Fig. 5J/5K and Supplementary Fig. S15). Markers by order: markers[0] = the tumour-burden marker (CEA role, fitted by Eq. 1), markers[1] = the cfDNA fraction of one resistant RAS-pathway sub-clone (fitted by Eq. 2); the paper fits each sub-clone independently (patient 1007: KRAS G12D 0.303/week, KRAS Q61H 0.122/week), so one sub-clone is passed at a time. Fits require >=3 detected time points by the landmark, and the refit is repeated on the accumulating draws (the paper's updates-with-new-draws use; risky at the benchmark landmark). The wrapper writes the reciprocal of the predicted waiting time as risk - per week, higher = sooner predicted relapse = more likely failing, the contract's risk direction - and the native outputs as extra numeric columns (predicted_waiting_time_weeks, lambda_s_per_week, lambda_r_cea_per_week, initial_resistant_frequency, lambda_r_cfdna_per_week, predicted_waiting_time_cfdna_weeks; the cfDNA route plugs the cfDNA-fit relapse rate into Eq. 1 with the CEA fit's lambda_s and initial frequency, the paper's plasma-forecasting reading). A fitted model that never reaches the RECIST threshold (no relapse rate or no resistant population; e.g. a monotonically declining burden) gets risk 0 - the model's own deterministic answer, no relapse within the fitted dynamics - with the reason in note; the paper reports waiting times only for patients who initially responded and does not describe this case. A patient with <3 detected draws of the tumour-burden marker by the landmark, or an undetectable baseline draw (value 0 with a <marker>__detected row of 0, else value <= detection_threshold), gets no prediction, with the reason in note. Since the paper does not publish the fit, the wrapper's deterministic choices are documented in the README: log-residual nonlinear least squares over a grid of starts spanning the paper's parameter ranges (initial resistant frequency 0.03%-95%; lambda_s, lambda_r in [0, 1]/week), ties (squared residuals within 1e-12 of the best) broken toward the largest initial resistant frequency f and then the largest lambda_r - an exactly exponential trajectory is thus the pure exponential (f = 1, lambda_r = the log-slope) and constant data gives lambda_s = lambda_r = 0.

methods.description: Tissue-independent per-timepoint WBC-filtered ctDNA detection (Leal et al., Nature Communications 2020; 50 resectable gastric-cancer patients on perioperative chemotherapy, matched cfDNA + baseline WBC targeted deep sequencing of 58 cancer driver genes at >30,000x): a patient's ctDNA is DETECTED at a plasma draw when at least one tumor-specific variant survives the assay's six-criteria somatic-mutation filter (including criterion (iii): not identified in the patient's matched baseline WBC sequencing at the level of one distinct read) - and is further supported by the paper's Bayesian tumor-vs-hematopoietic derivation probability per variant (binomial read-count likelihoods, tumor-derived model theta_WBC = 0 vs hematopoietic model theta_WBC = theta_cfDNA, Beta(2.4,340) prior, prior odds 1, P = PO/(1+PO)), computed for every mutation identified by cfDNA but not by WBC. WBC-filtered ctDNA positivity was the paper's worse-outcome group (preoperative EFS HR 3.0, 95% CI 1.3-6.9, p = 0.012; postoperative EFS HR 21.8, 95% CI 3.9-123.1, p < 0.001), and unfiltered cfDNA mutations did NOT predict recurrence (p = 0.76). The benchmark contract has no channel for the per-variant read counts, variant annotations or matched baseline WBC evidence the six criteria and the binomial model consume (the proprietary VariantDx caller is not available either), so the benchmark receives the pipeline's per-draw output - the WBC-filtered per-draw detectability state as the marker's <marker>__detected companion and the tumor-specific ctDNA level (mutant allele fraction, %) as the marker value; the wrapper applies the paper's per-draw patient rule at the last on-treatment draw on or before the landmark and writes call = 1 (ctDNA detected, treatment judged failing) and, as risk, the marker's value at that draw (higher = more ctDNA = failing). It writes no probability: TxResBench converts the risk.

methods.description: The Weka neural-network (fully connected MultilayerPerceptron) regressor for the per-patient time to cure of chronic HCV infection during DAA therapy from Churkin A et al., 'Machine learning for mathematical models of HCV kinetics during antiviral therapy', Math Biosci 2022;344:108756, doi:10.1016/j.mbs.2021.108756: the learner ('neural network (Multilayer Perceptron [39]) regressor', md:92) maps the on-treatment log10 HCV RNA viral loads at the fixed sampling days 0, 1, 7, 14, 28 (standard scheme, reported 0.95% average relative error) or the economized days 0, 14, 28 (reported 4.2%) to the continuous time to cure, and is trained once on 30,000 in-silico patients generated with the analytically solved two-equation HCV kinetic model (parameters uniform: V0 5-7.5 [log10], e_p 0.9-0.999, c 6-22/day, delta 0.1-1.5/day, md:92) so that it 'can immediately provide the predicted time to cure' for new patients (md:105); the published training table (Zenodo 4771147 = mathbio-bgu/Machine-Learning-HCV-Biphasic-Model@5fa4832, artificial_dataset.csv, GPL-3.0) is carried in the image and our wrapper re-trains the model on all 30,000 instances at fit (the paper's 9.7% real-patient run trains on all 30,000 and tests on the 266 real patients) and applies it at predict unchanged, so it never learns from the benchmark's training outcomes (fitted: false; the paper's in-silico augmentation replaces outcome learning). The paper names no Weka version, no MLP settings and no architecture ('?' - the training was a GUI run and the published tutorial documents only the RandomForest walk-through), so the wrapper pins Weka 3.8.5 and its release defaults (one hidden layer of (5+1)/2 = 3 sigmoid units, learning rate 0.3, momentum 0.2, 500 epochs, validation threshold 20, no decay, attributes and class normalized to [0,1], seed from the call), documented as a re-creation, not the published run (the paper's reported 0.95%/4.2%/9.7% relative errors are recorded as reported, not fitted; a Weka 3.8.5 default run on the published data gives about 2.5% relative absolute error on the paper's 66%-34% split). Per patient the wrapper builds the fixed-day feature vector by last-observed-value carry-backward (V0 = the last draw at or before the baseline day; each Vd = the last draw at or before the fixed day, draws beyond the landmark never used) and takes the log10 of the lab-reported IU/mL values (the published columns are log10; the harness value is the lab value, so the wrapper takes the log10 and never twice), and writes risk = the predicted time to cure (the model's native output, in the paper's day scale: higher = longer to cure = treatment judged failing; the gate's conversion turns it into the per-outcome probabilities). A patient with no baseline draw, with no on-treatment draw by the landmark, or whose fixed-day vector rests on a below-detection value (log10 undefined for value 0/negative) gets no prediction with the reason in note, and a landmark before the last sampling day limits every fixed day to the draws by the landmark (the paper defines no missing-day or below-detection fallback, '?').

methods.description: The Weka random forest regressor ('random-forest-decision-tree regressor', md:92, md:101) that Churkin et al. (Math Biosci 2022;344:108756, DOI 10.1016/j.mbs.2021.108756) used to predict the per-patient time to cure of chronic HCV infection during DAA therapy from serial on-treatment HCV RNA: the published model maps the five numeric attributes V0, V1, V7, V14, V28 (log10 HCV RNA, IU/mL, at days 0, 1, 7, 14, 28 of the treatment; the economized protocol keeps days 0, 14, 28) to the numeric class time_cure, patients' time until the virus is eliminated; the tutorial published with the data (Zenodo 4771147) documents the fit as Weka Explorer -> Classify -> trees -> RandomForest -> Start with no option set, so the wrapper runs weka.classifiers.trees.RandomForest (Weka 3.8.5) from the command line with the version's GUI defaults plus the run's seed, the published 30,000-patient in-silico ARFF schema as the internal feature format, and it fits on the benchmark training patients (the paper's 266-real-patient fit scenario; its 30,000-in-silico alternative training source is recorded, not substituted). The benchmark has no cure time, so the wrapper regresses the same fixed-day vector on the treatment-failure time (pfs_time where the progression outcome is learned, else os_time; a no_response label when the data carry no time outcome), and writes risk = the negated predicted failure time (days): the model's native per-patient output is a predicted duration, a shorter one means the treatment is more likely failing, exactly the paper's own time-to-cure axis ('longer to cure = worse') reversed for the benchmark's failure-oriented risk; no probability is written (the paper reports no per-patient values, only the test-set average relative errors 29% and 9.7%), so TxResBench converts the risk per outcome. The mapping of each patient's irregular draws onto the paper's fixed-day columns is by the draw closest to each protocol day (V0 = the last baseline draw), values are logged once to the paper's log10 scale (never twice), the below-detection state (value 0 with a __detected = 0 row) substitutes log10 of the assay's detection limit (the marker's __lod rows or params.nondetect_log10), and a patient without a baseline draw or without an on-treatment draw of the marker by the landmark gets no prediction with the reason in note (the paper's schemes are complete 5- or 3-point vectors; it defines no imputation - min_draws 2 is the paper's minimum information, and the economized 3-point scheme is its stated minimum protocol, md:101). The paper's settings (Weka version, all RandomForest options) and its exact 66%-34% split (the caption's '34% (98 instances)' does not match 0.34 x 266) are unpublished/self-inconsistent; every wrapper choice (defaults, scheme, substitution, target mapping) is made once, recorded in run.json and the README, and never presented as a paper fact - the paper's reported numbers (29%, 9.7%, the tutorial's 1.4%, the neural network's 0.95%/4.2%) are recorded as reported, not reproduced.

methods.description: The XGBoost ensemble classifier of durable clinical benefit (DCB = confirmed absence of progressive disease or death within 6 months of therapy initiation) of Anagnostou, Hurwitz, Connal et al. (JITC 2022) for patients with metastatic NSCLC on immune-checkpoint-inhibitor-containing therapy: a gradient-boosted decision tree classifier on 25 features built from the peripheral CBC-with-differential values (absolute neutrophil count, absolute lymphocyte count, eosinophil fraction, neutrophil fraction, lymphocyte fraction) at baseline (day of first treatment), 4 weeks and the first radiographic follow-up, the derived relative changes of these subsets (ratios to the baseline value), the derived NLR = ANC/ALC at those timepoints and the relative NLR changes, plus (when covariates=True) the cov_* columns standing in for the paper's patient features, tumor characteristics and treatment history. The wrapper re-implements the paper's training regime verbatim (10-fold CV feature selection, 100 iterations, final model = ensemble of 100 models) because the paper publishes no code and no hyperparameters; every unstated value is an xgboost package default or a documented wrapper choice. The label is the paper's DCB dichotomy derived from the training PFS (event within dcb_days = 183 days of the first dose = no durable benefit; event-free past the window, or no event by it, = DCB; patients whose 6-month status is unknown - censored before the window end - are not used). risk and p_no_response carry the fitted P(no durable benefit), failure-oriented, under the declared mapping (the paper's DCB label is a 6-month PFS-based benefit dichotomy, not a RECIST SD/PD call; it is the benchmark's closest response outcome, and the spec records the projection cost for the survival outcomes, whose probabilities TxResBench converts from the risk). Missing values are not imputed: they travel to the trees' built-in missing path (the paper is silent on missing draws); a patient without a baseline draw or without a draw during treatment by the landmark gets no prediction with the reason in note.

methods.description: The predictive signature of Harel, Lahav, Jacob et al. (J Immunother Cancer 2022;10:e004582): a binary XGBoost classifier of resistance to ICI-based therapy in advanced (stage IIIB-IV) NSCLC, evaluated at the 3-month RECIST time point (responder = SD/PR/CR, non-responder = PD), on the final published four features - the plasma levels of CXCL10 (IP-10) and CXCL8 (IL-8) at the T1 draw (2-6 weeks after commencement of treatment), log2-transformed, plus sex and age (md:64, md:100, md:102). The paper's output is the resistance probability with the call at 0.5 (>=0.5 = predicted non-responder), and publishes no code, no XGBoost binding/version and no hyperparameters, so the wrapper refits the published final model with the canonical Python xgboost (moderate documented defaults - the paper states no hyperparameters, '?'; overridable) on the benchmark training patients: risk = the fitted P(PD) - the paper's resistance probability, an identity mapping into contract 2.0's failure orientation - together with the method's own p_progressive_disease and the 0.5-threshold call; the paper's upstream per-protein selection pipeline (508-protein panel, T0/T1/FC features, 300 models per feature, BH FDR < 0.15, forward selection) is not re-run because it needs the RayBiotech panel - the wrapper takes the published signature as the model (declared in required_markers). The paper's model includes age and sex; the benchmark's pilot passes no covariate track, so the benchmark track is the paper's own published age/sex-excluded sensitivity model (AUC 0.76 all patients / 0.65 monotherapy, md:104) while a covariate track that resolves age and/or sex (method_params aliases; 1 = male) refits the published four-feature model - both recorded in run.json. Values at or below zero (the harness's below-detection encoding) are replaced by half the smallest positive training value of the marker before log2 - the wrapper's mapping of the paper's below-LOD-to-LOD rounding (per-protein LODs are not published), and a patient without a complete T1-window feature vector (no draw in days 14-42, an unmeasured value, or a missing resolved covariate) gets an empty risk and the reason in note: the paper defines no imputation. The harness no_response outcome (SD or PD) is not the paper's dichotomy - the paper counts SD as a response - so no model is fitted for it and TxResBench converts the risk.

methods.description: The per-marker Youden-index (ROC) optimal cut-off stratification of Yan C et al., 'Time-spatial analysis of T cell receptor repertoire in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma patients treated with combined radiotherapy and PD-1 blockade', Oncoimmunology 2022;11(1):2025668 (DOI 10.1080/2162402x.2022.2025668; PMID 35036077; phase Ib NCT03222440, 19 locally advanced ESCC patients on definitive SIB-IMRT 60 Gy + camrelizumab 200 mg q2w; 18 baseline + 16 on-treatment tumor tissues, 15 pairs, 18 paired peripheral CD8+ T-cell samples): one per-patient TCRB CDR3 repertoire metric is read at its named draw (baseline, the day before the first dose; or on-treatment, after 40 Gy radiation and 2 rounds of camrelizumab = at 4 weeks of RT; or as the two-draw change) and dichotomised at 'the best cutoff of Kaplan-Meier survival analysis... calculated by the Youden index of the ROC curve' (md:106) into two strata, compared by Kaplan-Meier OS and PFS with two-sided log-rank tests (significance 0.05, md:106); no Cox model, no hazard ratio and no per-patient probability is reported for any repertoire feature (md:106, md:133-170). The paper publishes no cut-off value (each is printed in the figures only, '?'), no analysis code and no ROC class label ('?' - the only binary labels with published strata are the RECIST 1.1 objective-response groups of md:128), so the wrapper re-derives the cut-off per training fold from the objective-response label (ROC label param, fallback to the OS event indicator - recorded as wrapper choices, not the paper's, and recorded in run.json). The published directions (carried by the wrapper per marker, spec output.projection.loses) are: high baseline peripheral-CD8+ (BLC) TCR Shannon index -> better OS and PFS (Fig. 2c); high BLC clonality -> worse OS and PFS (Fig. 2d); high 'patient-specific'-clonotype percentage in baseline tumors (BLT) -> shorter OS and PFS (Fig. 3g); higher percentage expansion of persistent intratumoral clonotypes -> longer OS and PFS (Fig. 4c); low total frequency of the top 100 clones in BLC -> longer OS (Fig. 5b); higher BLT low-frequency (<=0.01%) clonotype proportion -> better OS (Fig. 5d); higher BLT high-frequency (>=0.1%) and medium-frequency (0.01-0.1%) proportions -> worse OS (Fig. 5e, Supplementary Fig. 10); higher TRBV20-1 frequency in on-treatment peripheral CD8+ T cells (RTC) -> better OS (Fig. 5h); higher increase in tumor-vs-peripheral Morisita-Horn overlap -> improved PFS (Fig. 6b). The baseline-feature panels are the paper's 'landmark analysis' (landmark point printed in the figures only, '?'); the wrapper conditions on the benchmark landmark for every panel and records the deviation. The wrapper writes risk = the feature value oriented to failure (the value itself for markers where high is worse, its negation where high is better - the quantity the rule thresholds, made monotone toward failure), call = 1 for the worse stratum, and the training-fold per-group Kaplan-Meier event probability by each horizon as p_progression_H<h> / p_death_H<h> (group-level: the paper's curves are group-level, no per-patient probability is defined); a patient without the required draw(s) or with a missing value gets no prediction with the reason in note. The paper names no analysis package (only SPSS v.21.0, mislabelled 'STATA', and R 4.1.0, md:106), so the wrapper reimplements the stated analyses in base survival 3.7-0 - a candidate implementation, not a paper fact.

methods.description: Fixed-cutoff stratification of a norm-referenced biomarker Z score at the index (first on-treatment) serum sample into the two groups the paper compares by per-group Kaplan-Meier curves and a Cox proportional-hazards model with the clock starting at the index sample - Maleska Maceski A et al., 'GFAP and NfL as predictors of disease progression and relapse activity in fingolimod-treated multiple sclerosis', Brain 2026; DOI 10.1093/brain/awaf433 (420 fingolimod-treated RMS patients, 130 PIRA events): elevated = Z score > cutoff (sGFAP > 0.75 versus <= 0.75, md:179; sNfL > 1 versus <= 1, md:182 - the cutoffs are fixed a priori from the control distribution, 77.3% / 84.1% of controls below, supp.txt:223-225), and the two groups are compared for the time to the first event from the index sample (md:66). The wrapper takes the one marker the benchmark passes - the norm-referenced Z score at the index sample (the paper's reference-model output; the wrapper does not recompute it, see the README) - the marker's last on-treatment draw up to the benchmark landmark as the index value, forms the group at the fixed cutoff (default 0.75, the sGFAP instance; 1.0 for the sNfL instance), and on the training fold fits one per-group Kaplan-Meier curve per survival outcome the training data give (progression from PFS, death from OS) on the residual clock with the patients event-free at the landmark, plus the paper's cohort-level diagnostics (per-group KM medians, log-rank, univariable Cox HR and continuous-Z Cox HR, and the adjusted Cox when covariates are passed). It writes the Z score as risk (higher = the treatment is more likely failing; the paper's pairs are focus-specific - sGFAP->PIRA and sNfL->relapse are the significant instances, sNfL->PIRA and sGFAP->relapse are null, md:179/md:184), the two-group call (1 = elevated), and the training-fold group KM event probability by each horizon as the model's own p_progression_H<h> / p_death_H<h>. A patient without an on-treatment marker draw up to the landmark gets no prediction, with the reason in note. The paper's continuous-Z, both-biomarker and absolute-cutoff instances are reported as diagnostics, not separate outputs. No package is named by the paper for the KM/Cox analysis (md:78 names only R 4.3.1; supp.txt:217 names no package), so the wrapper is its own reimplementation in base survival 3.7-0 - a candidate implementation, not a paper fact.
